Display: Terminal HUD 'PoT 30b 41% · →16:00 63% · ETA ~10:40'; Clean label tooltip only, so the Clean face is unchanged.
Ledger: when the horizon is not 'Bars', trials store hT and f_step uses t.bars >= t.hT (1455).
proposals.risk: Future-time projection uses the symbol session; holidays are unknown, so the ETA is shown as approximate. Requires TIME-1.

proposals.title: Replace fixed killzone affinity with a clock-consistent learned affinity; continuous hysteresis
proposals.rationale: f_kzAff (597-602, applied at 1941) boosts session and PD pools by 5-20% in fixed killzones regardless of distance. A random walk on the volatility clock already reproduces 'London raids Asia / NY raids London'. In FX the Asian range is respected more than random (both sides broken 37.7% observed vs 48.9%). With TIME-1 the multipliers double-count timing and bias the ledger.
proposals.spec:
Input kzAffMode: 'Learned', 'Fixed (legacy)' or 'Off'; default Off until the ledger has 40 outcomes.
Learned: 18 cells (kz at snapshot 0-5 × source class {session 3-5/8-10, PD/PW 6-7, other}). Outcomes come from ict_liq ICT-1 candidate probes (or DOL trials) scored against the clock-aware pBase. lift = ((k+2)/(e+2))/((K+2)/(E+2)), shrunk with w = n/(n+40), bounded [0.85, 1.15], applied at 1941 instead of f_kzAff.
Hysteresis (976): hystEff = hyst * clamp(sqrt(clkL*H/fwdV), 1, kzHx): stickier when the coming bars are expected to be quiet; falls back to the binary rule without the clock.
proposals.risk: Learning noise with few outcomes (shrinkage and bounds). Some users prefer the ICT narrative, so 'Fixed (legacy)' stays available.

proposals.title: Midnight open as a candidate target ('Target: MO'), ledger-gated
proposals.rationale: The only time anchor with a measured excess over a random walk: RTH revisit 65.6-68.0% across 9,226 days vs 52-61% on the clock. It is strongly distance-dependent and early (median 09:41-09:48). Traders use it as a draw; the engine only uses it as confluence (1931).
proposals.spec:
New kind 8 OPEN, a magnet rather than liquidity: touched on touch; side recomputed each bar from the price's position; price = top = bottom = midOpen with 0.10*atr depth. src 11 MO (optional src 12 08:30 open, src 13 weekly open). Created when f_sessOpen fires for sessMid; expires at 16:00 or on touch.
Pillars: proximity/reach (clock-aware); freshness from the session open; confluence as usual; density 0.35 + 0.30 when the overnight direction disagrees with the gap (that subgroup revisits 77-82%). Ledger group 4 'OPENS' (stats arrays of size 6). Clean code 'MO'.
proposals.risk: The kind enum is used in many helpers: f_newLevel side logic (1085), touched (624), isLiquidity/isArray, grp (636), f_levelName/f_shortName, and the delivAt crop (1566). A mechanical but wide change.

proposals.title: Manual scheduled-event input (FOMC/CPI/NFP) that scales the volatility clock
proposals.rationale: Pine has no economic calendar. The clock learns only the average 08:30/10:00 bump, yet the FOMC hour runs 5.2x normal and CPI 2.1-2.7x, and both are known in advance. Reachability into the event should reflect that.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_POT): evOn (bool), evT = input.time(...) (UNIX timestamp), evX (variance multiplier, default 3.0), evMin (window minutes, default 60). In f_fwdVar, cells whose projected time falls inside [evT, evT + evMin) get their variance multiplied by evX. The HUD and tooltip show '⚑ EVENT' while the window lies inside the horizon.
proposals.risk: User input errors; a stale event if left on (auto-ignore once evT + evMin has passed).

proposals.title: IPDA 20/40/60-day extremes and 60-day equilibrium as registry sources for the HTF objective
proposals.rationale: These are the ICT 'big liquidity' map for swing horizons. They are cheap to add, and the ledger can test them; evidence is weak, so they enter through the registry and tiers, not fixed weights.
proposals.spec: One request.security(syminfo.tickerid, f_tfSafe('D'), [ta.highest(high,20)[1], ta.lowest(low,20)[1], ... 40 ..., ... 60 ...], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on). Push to extReg when a value changes (f_changed): src 14/15/16 '20D/40D/60D H|L', tiers 0.70/0.78/0.85. Anchor with f_anchorScan (1141) or f_barAtTime (1191). Add the 60-day equilibrium to the confluence anchors (1931). They feed the HTF objective (1984-1989) naturally.
proposals.risk: Overlap with PWH/PWL and HTF pivots (handled by de-duplication and the tier upgrade). One more request (limit 40). Avoid the dynamic history index inside security (max_bars_back): request prices only and anchor on the chart.

proposals.title: Equity-index late-session continuation term in the draw vector, ledger-gated
proposals.rationale: The measured opposite of the Judas narrative. For SPY the first half-hour (and the 12th half-hour) return predicts the last half-hour (R² 1.6-2.6%, OOS 1.2-1.7%; Gao et al. JFE 2018). The effect is absent in FX and commodities. It is a small but real tilt for late-session target choice.
proposals.spec: Input toggle (default off) for equity-index symbols. Between 15:00 and 16:00 NY: mR = clamp((close - rthPrevClose)/rthSd, -1, 1), where rthSd comes from the clock's RTH variance and rthPrevClose is captured at session.islastbar_regular. Add wR*mR (wR = 0.15) to drawD (1894). Grade with TIME-2's per-killzone EDGE and auto-disable if the lift is <= 0 after 40 outcomes.
proposals.risk: Symbol classification; the RTH previous close on futures; small effect size.

result.summary: I found no evidence that market structure predicts which side's liquidity is taken first, and an original test on three markets agrees. Five independent studies: 44 SMC detectors on S&P 500 stocks never beat random entry (Tangirala). 15,817 MSS signals had an edge ratio of 0.97-1.13 whether or not displacement was present (Nordman). The mechanised 2022 model was within ±0.05R before costs on 12 markets (IvanSetuper). The textbook CHoCH+FVG reversal read should be faded (Mahadzva). The AMD model carries no information beyond the daily trend regime (Taylor). For the original test I replicated the engine's f_structure on 1H, ≈4H and ≈D bars plus the engine's draw vector D, on NQ, gold and EURUSD hourly data (≈2 years each), and asked which side of close ± 1.5 ATR is touched first within 30 bars. D called it right 49.9% / 51.6% / 50.4%, inside random-walk controls (47-53%). An 11-feature logistic learner did worse than a coin out of sample. Yet the draw pillar is the heaviest score weight (30), counter-draw targets get ×0.5, and selection is draw-side first. On most charts this pushes targets to the farther side and flips them on noise. The top proposal therefore measures D's skill online and scales its influence by it. The sweep read in liqEvt is mis-signed. Raids that close back inside were followed by continuation 52.6% of the time (n = 1,402), not reversal. Breakouts that hold against the HTF swing bias reversed 56% of the time (n = 381); with the bias they continued 53%. ICT's own MSS is defined inside an HTF bias ('if you're bearish…'), so it is a trend-resumption signal; tested as a reversal it scored 45.6-50.5%. Which pool is hit first is geometry: the race from the weak extreme to the protected extreme matched gambler's-ruin odds within 2 pp. The engine already has that race math (f_race/f_raceH) but shows it only in the Terminal view, so the Clean label should show it. f_structure's dealing range is the last pivot high and low; ICT's range is [protected, weak] of the current leg. The engine computes both (protH/protL are returned but unused, legH/legL are not returned), so a two-line fix corrects premium/discount, htfEQ and structural invalidation. OTE, MMXM ladders, CISD and the 2022 model add no forecastable edge, so they stay out of scoring.

concepts.name: Swing points (3-candle vs N-candle fractal)
concepts.definition: ICT swing high = 3 candles, the middle has the highest high (a lower high on each side), confirmed when the 3rd candle closes. N-fractal of strength p: p lower highs on each side, known p bars late (Williams p=2; LuxAlgo SMC 50 swing / 5 internal). Pine: ta.pivothigh(high,p,p), value refers to bar t-p; tie handling is undocumented, so hand-code (strict left, >= right) if equal highs matter.
concepts.dolRole: Unswept swings are where stops rest; the next unswept swing on each side is the nearest candidate draw. Larger p gives fewer, larger pools with more lag.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Stops cluster beyond obvious levels (Osler; see ict_liq.md E1-E3), but the swing size/label adds little beyond distance (ict_liq.md E6).
concepts.engineNotes: Chart pivots pivLen=5 (lines 90, 879-880) are 5 bars late, so a swing taken within 5 bars never becomes a pool or sweep event; MTF pivots biasLen=3 (708-710). No 3-candle STH.

concepts.name: STH / ITH / LTH hierarchy
concepts.definition: STH = 3-candle swing; ITH = STH with lower STHs on both sides (or the high made rebalancing an imbalance); LTH = ITH with lower ITHs on both sides, usually a daily level (ICT 2022 Ep.12). Breaking an ITL is 'a significant break in market structure'.
concepts.dolRole: The order of the swing approximates pool size; the ITH/LTH above is the objective and the ITL is protected.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitions only (ICT lectures).
concepts.engineNotes: Proxied by timeframe tier f_tierW (506-516: chart .25, STF .45, HTF .65); no nested ITH/LTH (ict_liq.md ICT-8 proposes it).

concepts.name: Break of structure (BOS)
concepts.definition: Candle close beyond the last swing in the trend direction (continuation). Settings that change the label: swing size, wick vs close, minimum break distance.
concepts.dolRole: Implies continuation toward the next swing pool in the trend direction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Negative: Tangirala SSRN 7483658, 44 detectors incl. BOS/CHoCH on 496 stocks, none beat random entry. Original test: engine structure components 50-52% directional accuracy.
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure upBrk/dnBrk close-based, protected extreme re-armed at each BOS (746-759); chart BOS for OBs at 1542-1547.

concepts.name: Change of character (CHoCH)
concepts.definition: First close through a swing against prevailing structure; swing CHoCH needs a close through the protected extreme of the last leg, internal CHoCH through the last minor swing.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed reversal toward opposing liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mahadzva SSRN 7430998: CHoCH+FVG reversal read should be faded (EURUSD H1 p=0.019). Head-and-shoulders (a CHoCH-type pattern): profitable for 2/6 FX pairs and dominated by filter rules (Chang & Osler 1999); 5-7%/yr in 1990s US stocks via negative momentum (Savin et al. 2007).
concepts.engineNotes: Swing CHoCH via protH/protL (760-773); internal ibias flips on any close through the last pivot (749-753); the Clean bias table falls back to ibias (2299-2305).

concepts.name: ICT market structure shift (MSS)
concepts.definition: Bearish: price runs an old high (a wick is enough), then closes (preferably with displacement) below the short-term low formed BEFORE the run, within a few bars. Defined inside an HTF bias ('if you're bearish…'), i.e. the end of a counter-trend retracement. Algo: on a BSL sweep capture the last 3-candle swing low; the first close below it within 8 bars is the MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Intraday bias toward the opposite pool (the 2022-model target); per ICT, a with-HTF resumption signal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Negative. Nordman: 15,817 MSS, edge ratio 0.97-1.13, displacement adds nothing. Original test: MSS reversal right 45.6% (n 171), 50.5% with displacement (n 97). Taylor: trend-aligned reads 62-71% vs against 25-30%.
concepts.engineNotes: No sweep→MSS sequence; sweeps (1579-1582) and structure (708-782) are independent. Proposed only as an alert with a measured follow-through rate (ICTS-6).

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.definition: Energetic one-sided move. Operational forms: body ≥ k·ATR (1.0-2.0) and body/range ≥ 0.6, or a two-candle leg, or the move leaves an FVG, or body ≫ 20-bar average body.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed to validate an MSS and imply continuation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman: no improvement to MSS at 5m/15m/1h/1d. Original test: displacement momentum 48.3-50.8% directional accuracy.
concepts.engineNotes: dispUp/dispDn (897-904) is good as an FVG/OB quality gate, but it also gets 20% of D (wM 0.20, line 156; half-life 12) with no measured skill; ICTS-1 would scale it by skill.

concepts.name: Change in state of delivery (CISD)
concepts.definition: Body close back through the open of the first candle of the last consecutive down-close (up-close) series into a swept extreme; fires earlier than an MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Entry trigger only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics found.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed by a target engine.

concepts.name: Protected (strong) vs weak extremes
concepts.definition: In bullish swing structure the low that started the leg (broke structure) is protected/strong; the running leg high is weak (liquidity until taken). Mirror in bearish structure.
concepts.dolRole: Weak extreme = structural target (HTF objective); protected extreme = invalidation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Original race test: weak-before-protected first-touch frequency matched gambler's-ruin geometry (NQ .628 vs .648, gold .624 vs .646; random-walk null −0.002±0.025): no edge beyond geometry, but the geometry is calibrated.
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure computes protH/protL (755-773) and legH/legL (729-730). protH/protL are returned at 782 but never used (only 923-925); legH/legL are not returned; f_invalidation uses the nearest opposing pool instead (1343-1365).

concepts.name: Dealing range and premium/discount
concepts.definition: The range of the last meaningful leg; structure-consistent form = [protL, legH] in bullish bias, [legL, protH] in bearish; premium above 50%, discount below.
concepts.dolRole: From discount the draw is the premium old high (buy discount → premium liquidity).
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT doctrine; long-horizon evidence favours continuation near highs (George & Hwang, see ict_pd.md); Fibonacci depth has no special level (Tradeify).
concepts.engineNotes: rngH/rngL (727-779) = last pivot high / last pivot low, extended while broken, so after any lower high the range becomes an internal swing. Feeds htfEQ (968), the Terminal P/D (2323-2333) and the f_invalidation fallback (1354).

concepts.name: Structure-derived draw vector (bias → DOL side)
concepts.definition: Engine D = (0.5·sV + 0.2·displacement + 0.3·liqEvt)/1, with sV = 0.5·htfBias + 0.3·stfBias + 0.2·exeIB; |D| ≥ 0.35 sets the draw side.
concepts.dolRole: Decides which side's liquidity the DOL is chosen from.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Original test (NQ/gold/EURUSD 1H): D 49.9/51.6/50.4% first-touch accuracy; gated D 52.0/50.4/50.2%; 11-feature logistic learner 48.0/47.8/49.6% out of sample. Only gold at 120 bars reached 53-55%.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed weights (lines 155-162, 1892-1898). The draw pillar is the largest weight (wDraw 30, line 145), ctrMult 0.5 (162), side-first selection with 2× hysteresis (1964-2035). No skill measurement.

concepts.name: Sweep outcome read (hold vs reject)
concepts.definition: After a pool is traded through: HOLD = close beyond the zone; REJECT = close back inside the level; NEUTRAL otherwise.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: hold → continuation to the next same-side pool; reject → reversal to opposing liquidity (turtle soup / 2022 model).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Original pooled test: REJECT → continuation 52.6% (n 1402; 51-53% at 12/30/120 bars); HOLD against HTF swing bias reversed 56% (n 381); HOLD with bias continued 53.2% (n 423). Mahadzva: 65/66 folds continuation; ict_liq.md E6: reversal 39-44%.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 1579-1582: HOLD = +1 continuation, REJECT = −1 reversal, fixed. REJECT has the wrong sign; HOLD ignores HTF alignment.

concepts.name: Market maker buy/sell model (MMXM)
concepts.definition: Original consolidation → staged run into a sell-side objective (engineering liquidity) → smart money reversal (sweep + MSS) → retrace of the whole path, taking interior consolidations/short-term highs nearest first, ending at the original consolidation; −2 to −2.5 SD projections beyond. Void on a close back through the swept extreme.
concepts.dolRole: After the SMR, a target ladder of interior pools in order.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published test; its core (sweep→MSS reversal) tested ≈ coin flip.
concepts.engineNotes: Implicitly approximated: lower highs are BSL pools and proximity picks the nearest draw-side one after D flips. No SMR detector; rejected for scoring.

concepts.name: ICT 2022 mentorship model
concepts.definition: HTF bias and draw → raid of an obvious pool (killzone) → displacement close through the pre-raid STH/STL (MSS) → entry on the FVG retrace → stop beyond the raid → target the opposite pool, partials at the nearest swing.
concepts.dolRole: Target = the opposite liquidity pool after the raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: IvanSetuper open-source test, 12 markets Feb 2021-Aug 2025: within ±0.05R before costs on every timeframe; after costs 1m −0.25R (41,541 trades), 5m −0.08R, 15m −0.04R.
concepts.engineNotes: Pieces exist (liqEvt 1579-1582, D flip 1895-1899, opposite-side selection 1964-2035). The sequence is not coded; rejected for scoring.

concepts.name: Turtle soup
concepts.definition: New 20-day low below a prior 20-day low ≥ 4 sessions old; buy stop just above the old low (Connors-Raschke); ICT version uses discount context and a later MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Claims a reversal to opposite liquidity after a false break.
concepts.evidenceNotes: See ict_liq.md. Original data: reject sweeps of 5-bar pools lean toward continuation (52.6%); the age filter was untested.
concepts.engineNotes: Sweeps read at 1579-1582 with no age/context filter (covered by ict_liq.md ICT-2).

concepts.name: Optimal trade entry (OTE 62-79%)
concepts.definition: Entry band at 62-79% retracement (70.5% sweet spot) of the displacement leg, ideally in discount and overlapping an FVG/OB.
concepts.dolRole: Entry location; for the draw only geometry: deeper pullback = nearer protected low, farther old high.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Tradeify ES/NQ daily (100 legs): continuation odds fall monotonically 33.3% (23.6%) → ~20% (61.8%) → 13.5% (78.6%), no Fibonacci bump; median continuing depth 60.4%.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed; geometry is already in the race/PoT models.

concepts.name: ITH/LTH and the HTF weak extreme as targets
concepts.definition: Once the ITL forms after the first STL raid, the ITH/LTH above (the HTF leg's weak extreme) is the objective.
concepts.dolRole: HTF objective / ERL target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT doctrine; tier labels add little beyond distance (ict_liq.md E6).
concepts.engineNotes: STF/HTF pivots reach the registry only after biasLen HTF bars + [1] (≈4 days on D) (1779-1789, hValid 780-781); the current HTF leg extreme is invisible until then; the HTF objective is ranked without proximity (1984-1989).

concepts.name: HTF trend regime / trend persistence
concepts.definition: Trend state from HTF swing structure or EMA distance (e.g. daily EMA20 ±0.5%); weak trends persist from ~30 min to ~1 year, strong ones revert.
concepts.dolRole: The only structure-family variable with consistent (small) directional information; it sets which side's draw is likelier.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012 (58 futures, all positive TSMOM); Schmidhuber 2021/2025 (universal, small coefficients); Taylor: AMD direction explained by regime (aligned 62-71%). Original: HTF bias 50.8-52.4% at 30 bars, gold 53.7% at 120 bars.
concepts.engineNotes: Empirical PoT surface split by htfBias regime (f_bump line 1531, f_empPoT index line 1286); htfBias also carries 0.5 of sV (1892).

concepts.name: First-passage race (which pool is taken first)
concepts.definition: P(target at distance a is hit before an opposing level at distance b) for Brownian motion with drift; driftless = b/(a+b); with a horizon H via eigen-expansion.
concepts.dolRole: Directly answers 'which liquidity next' once two candidate pools are known.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mathematical result; original calibration on NQ/gold within 2 pp of geometric prediction; the engine also corrects it with its own ledger (f_raceAdj).
concepts.engineNotes: f_race/f_raceH (447-482), f_invalidation (1343-1365), f_raceAdj (1367-1371) shown as WIN≤H only in the Terminal HUD; absent from the Clean label (2225).

concepts.name: Directional-change overshoot scaling law
concepts.definition: After a reversal of threshold δ is confirmed, price extends on average ≈ δ beyond the confirmation point before the next reversal; for a random walk the overshoot is exponential with mean δ (median 0.70δ, P(≥δ)=0.37).
concepts.dolRole: Prior for how far a new leg runs (P(extension ≥ x) ≈ e^(−x/δ)); per-chart persistence meter (ratio > 1 = trending).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Glattfelder-Dupuis-Olsen 2011 (13 FX pairs, ~3 orders of magnitude). Original: gold 1.39 vs RW 1.19±0.04, NQ 1.29 vs 1.17±0.06, EURUSD 1.14 vs 1.11±0.07; leg direction predicted first touch only 47-56%.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed: the empirical PoT surface already learns excursion distributions per regime.

concepts.name: AMD / Power of 3 session model
concepts.definition: Asia accumulation range, London false break of one side (sweep + close back), NY delivery to the opposite Asia extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Target = opposite side of the Asia range after a London raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Taylor arXiv 2610.35887: no information beyond the daily trend regime; 57% of targets were delivered before the NY entry window.
concepts.engineNotes: Killzone affinity: London raids Asia ×1.20, NY raids London ×1.20 (f_kzAff 597-602); no regime conditioning (out of this domain).

concepts.name: Structure-shift alerts
concepts.definition: Alert on an HTF swing-bias flip and on an execution MSS after a sweep, ideally with the chart's measured follow-through rate.
concepts.dolRole: Workflow support; tells the trader when the draw narrative changed.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Edge evidence negative (MSS ≈ coin); value is UX and transparency.
concepts.engineNotes: Alerts exist for new DOL, iFVG, sweep and draw flip only (2077-2094).

proposals.title: Draw-skill gate: measure the draw vector online and scale the draw pillar, counter-draw penalty and side-first selection by its measured skill
proposals.rationale: The draw pillar is the largest score weight (30), counter-draw targets get ×0.5, and selection is draw-side first, all assuming D knows the direction. All external tests (Tangirala, Nordman, IvanSetuper, Mahadzva, Taylor) and the engine replica (D 49.9-51.6% on NQ/gold/EURUSD) say it barely does on most charts, though it sometimes does (gold 53-55% at 120 bars). A fixed weight is wrong both ways and makes targets jump sides on noise. Measuring the skill lets each chart decide, and the ledger can compare before and after.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_FLOW): dSkill=true, dSkK=1.5 ATR, dSkEvery=5 bars, dSkFull=0.56 (accuracy for full weight), dSkPrior=60 pseudo-probes at 50%, dFloor=0.25. TYPE DProbe{float up, float dn, int bar0, int dS, int sS, int mS, int lS, int hS} after Trial (~396). STATE (after 1079): var array<DProbe> dq; var array<float> skN/skK (5 cells: 0 D, 1 structure sV, 2 displacement mV, 3 liqEvt, 4 htfBias); var float drawRho=1. Helpers after STATE: f_skill(c) = (skK[c]+0.5*prior)/(skN[c]+prior); f_skBook(c,s,y) books when s != 0. ENGINE step 2b (after the Trial loop ~1557): for each probe with bar_index>bar0: u=high>=up, d=low<=dn; if exactly one, y=±1 and book all five cells, then remove; if both or bar_index-bar0>=H, remove unbooked. Step 14 (after dirSide, line 1895; sV and mV in scope): every dSkEvery bars and if dq.size()<128, push DProbe(close±dSkK*atr, bar_index, dirSide, int(math.sign(sV)), int(math.sign(mV)), int(math.sign(liqEvt)), htfBias). drawRho = dSkill ? max(dFloor, clamp((f_skill(0)-0.5)/(dSkFull-0.5),0,1)) : 1. int dirSel = drawRho>=0.5 ? dirSide : 0. Step 17 (1948): pass drawD*drawRho to evaluate(), so the draw pillar shrinks to 0.5 and ctrMult fires only on a strong scaled D (line 692). Step 19: use dirSel in elig/useCtr/ctrHold/curElig/activeCtr and the INVALIDATED ghost. drawFlip alert requires drawRho>=0.5. UX: Terminal DRAW row 'skill 51% (n 812) ×0.25'; Full panel per-component skills; data-window plot of drawRho. Cost ≤128 probes × O(1) per confirmed bar; no request.security.
proposals.risk: The probe label (symmetric ±k ATR first touch) is a proxy for direction skill, not the actual targets; the ledger EDGE still measures target-level impact. It needs ~300 bars of probes before the gate moves (5,000-bar history gives ~900). The 'Draw Direction' feature becomes mostly neutral on charts without skill; the 0.25 floor keeps it visible.

proposals.title: Correct the sweep-outcome mapping in liqEvt: a hold against the HTF swing is a failed breakout, a close back inside is not a reversal
proposals.rationale: Line 1581 maps HOLD → continuation (+1) and REJECT → reversal (−1). Pooled over three markets: REJECT → continuation 52.6% (n 1,402; 51-53% at 12/30/120 bars); HOLD against the HTF swing bias reversed 56% (n 381) and against the EMA regime 62% (n 155); HOLD with the bias continued 53.2% (n 423). This agrees with Mahadzva (continuation in 65/66 folds, fade reversal reads), Taylor (against-trend reads 25-30%) and ict_liq.md E6. The current mapping adds a wrong-signed term to 30% of D.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_FLOW): swHoldW=0.5 (holds with HTF, continuation), swFailW=0.5 (holds against HTF, failed breakout), swRejW=0.0 (closes back inside; measured slight continuation). Replace lines 1579-1582: if hit and lv.isLiquidity(): hold = side==1 ? close>lv.top : close<lv.bottom; rej = side==1 ? close<lv.price : close>lv.price; c = hold ? (htfBias==side ? swHoldW : htfBias==-side ? -swFailW : 0) : rej ? swRejW : 0; liqEvt := clamp(liqEvt + c*side*tier, -1, 1). This is the static prior for ict_liq.md ICT-2's learner; when ICT-2 lands, add HTF alignment {with, against, none} to its cells. ICTS-1's component skill f_skill(3) reports whether liqEvt helps on the chart.
proposals.risk: Low: the weights are inputs and the effect is bounded by wL (0.30) and tier. The sample is one 2-year window; the learner should take over.

proposals.title: 'Which pool first': show the calibrated first-touch race against the opposing pool in the Clean label
proposals.rationale: The user's question is which liquidity price reaches next. Structure cannot call the side, but the race between two known pools is geometry plus drift: the original test matched gambler's-ruin odds within 2 pp on NQ and gold. The engine already computes it (f_race/f_raceH 447-482, ledger-corrected by f_raceAdj 1367-1371) but shows it only as WIN≤H in the Terminal HUD.
proposals.spec: f_invalidation (1343-1365) also returns the opposing level index: track oppI in the loop and return [inv, d/risk, p, oppI]. Update both destructurings with distinct names: line 1428 [inv, rr, pR, oI0] and line 2127 [i0, i1, i2, i3]. Input showRace=true (G_DOL). Clean label (2225): append '\n1st: ' + str.tostring(invWin*100,'0') + '% vs ' + oppTag, where oppTag = i3>=0 ? f_shortName(pool.get(i3).kind, pool.get(i3).src) : '−1.5 ATR'. Optional dotted thin line at the opposing pool's near edge to xR (1 extra line object). Tooltip explains 'touched before the opposing pool, among races decided within the PoT horizon, corrected by this chart's first touches'. Already graded by raceSt (line 1079).
proposals.risk: One extra label line (toggleable). When no opposing pool is within maxATR the fallback barrier is 1.5 ATR, so the tag must say so.

proposals.title: Return ICT's dealing range from f_structure: [protected extreme, weak extreme] of the current leg
proposals.rationale: rngH/rngL are the last pivot high and low, so after any internal lower high the 'range' shrinks to a sub-swing. That corrupts the Terminal premium/discount %, the htfEQ confluence anchor and the f_invalidation fallback, and every dealing-range proposal in the companion studies (ICT-4, ICTPD-4/7) depends on it. The engine already computes the correct pair (protH/protL, legH/legL).
proposals.spec: In f_structure after the bias update (before lines 776-779): float drH = bias==1 ? legH : bias==-1 ? protH : rngH; float drL = bias==1 ? protL : bias==-1 ? legL : rngL. Return drH[1], drL[1] in place of rngH[1], rngL[1] (line 782); tuple shape unchanged, so no call-site edits. Semantics: bull = [strong low, weak high (running high since the last BOS, re-armed at line 758)]; bear mirror; neutral falls back to the old range. protL is defined at the first BOS (protL := legL), and legH >= close, so there are no na holes. Registry prominence uses these only as magnitudes (1783-1789). Non-repainting: same [1]+lookahead_on read.
proposals.risk: htfEQ values change, so some confluence scores shift; P/D readouts read more 'premium' right after breaks. No compile risk beyond one function.

proposals.title: Structural anchors: protected-swing invalidation option and weak-extreme tag on the HTF objective
proposals.rationale: ICT/SMC traders put risk beyond the protected low and aim at the weak high. f_invalidation uses the nearest opposing pool (often an inner pool), so the Terminal R:R / WIN% / EV describe a different trade. The race test shows weak-before-protected odds follow geometry: this is semantic alignment, not edge.
proposals.spec: Input invMode = ['Nearest Opposing Pool', 'Protected Swing (Exec)', 'Protected Swing (STF)'] (G_DOL). In f_invalidation, when the mode is protected and tgt.side equals that TF's swing bias: sw = side==1 ? exeProtL : exeProtH (or stf*); if sw is on the correct side of close and |close-sw|/atr <= maxATR, then inv = sw - side*buf, else the current rule (exeProt* already returned at 923-925; with ICTS-4, exeRL/exeRH equal them in trends). Step 19 (1984-1989): if the HTF objective is within eqTol·atr of htfRH (htfBias==1) or htfRL (−1), append '· WEAK H/L' to its label. Terminal: one dotted 'PROT' line at the exec protected level. The ledger's raceSt then grades the trader's actual stop logic.
proposals.risk: Wider stops show lower R:R (honest). Small code surface.

proposals.title: Structure-shift alerts (HTF swing flip, execution MSS after a sweep) carrying the chart's measured follow-through rate
proposals.rationale: ICT users want to be told when the HTF swing bias flips and when an MSS prints after a raid, but MSS reversal reads tested at 45.6-50.5% (Nordman ≈1.0 edge ratio, 2022-model ≈0R). Each alert should therefore carry the chart's own measured follow-through instead of an implied promise.
proposals.spec: Global series: stlP = ta.pivotlow(low,1,1), sthP = ta.pivothigh(high,1,1); var lastStl/lastSth, mssDir, mssLvl, mssTill, mssEvt. Step 3: on a REJECT liquidity hit, arm mssDir = -side, mssLvl = side==1 ? lastStl : lastSth, mssTill = bar_index + mssWin (input 8). Each confirmed bar: update lastStl/lastSth; mssEvt = 0; if bar_index <= mssTill and the close crosses mssLvl in mssDir, set mssEvt = mssDir and disarm. Follow-through: probe cell 5 in ICTS-1 = sign of the last MSS while younger than H. htfShift = barstate.isconfirmed and htfBias != htfBias[1] and htfBias[1] != 0 (non-repainting via the [1]-offset request). alertcondition(htfShift, 'HTF Structure Shift', …) and alertcondition(mssEvt != 0, 'Execution MSS', …) after line 2094; alert() text 'MSS ▼ after BSL sweep · follow-through 46% (n 171)'. Terminal row STRUCT.
proposals.risk: Alert noise on low timeframes; mssWin and an optional displacement gate reduce it. Adds a few var states only.

proposals.title: Register the HTF/STF weak extreme in the external registry before pivot confirmation
proposals.rationale: The current HTF leg's extreme, the textbook HTF objective, enters the registry only after biasLen HTF bars plus the [1] shift (≈4 days on D, ≈16 h on 4H); until then it is at best a tier-0.25 chart pool. Benefit is correct labelling and HTF tier/freshness, since evidence says tier adds little beyond distance.
proposals.spec: f_structure also returns legH[1], legL[1], legHT[1], legLT[1] (legHT/legLT = time updated when legH/legL set a new extreme). Each tuple grows 12→16, total ≈64 of the 127-element request limit (limitations.md line 275). Step 10 (1779-1789), confirmed bars, for HTF and STF: if htfBias==1, htfLegH is unswept on the chart and (htfLegH-close)/atr >= minDistATR, call f_pushExt(extReg, htfLegH, true, 2, f_barAtTime(htfLegHT, anchorMax), prom, hmH); mirror for bias −1 / legL; same for STF with src 1. f_pushExt dedups/upgrades by price and f_mergeLiq folds it into an existing chart pool. A later higher high: the step-4 raid check removes the old entry and the new one registers when price leaves.
proposals.risk: More registry churn and possible near-duplicates (handled by dedup). Four more tuple elements per request call. Low forecasting value per E6.

concepts.name: Race geometry (gambler's-ruin first passage between opposing pools)
concepts.definition: Price x between an upper level U and a lower level D. Driftless: P(U before D) = (x−D)/(U−D). With drift μ and volatility σ, k = 2μ/σ², a = U−x, b = x−D: P = (1−e^{k·b})/(e^{−k·a}−e^{k·b}). The h-bar truncated version is f_raceH. For the previous candle, U=H1, D=L1, x=C1 (decision at the close) or x=open (decision at the next open, open inside the range).
concepts.dolRole: The single strongest predictor of which liquidity is taken next. It is the right prior for the side choice and for the probability, and every other bias feature should be judged as excess over it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study, race.py] Ruin accuracy 70-81% on 17 combinations (e.g. S&P D 0.702, NASDAQ W 0.788, NQ 1H 0.761, S&P D from the open 0.756). Out-of-sample, adding ICT/CRT/CLV/trend/pivot features changes accuracy by ≤ ±2 pp. On daily equities the raw ruin probability is overconfident at the extremes (close-through up: P 0.73 vs geometry 0.83) and needs a fitted slope.
concepts.engineNotes: f_race 447-464 and f_raceH 466-482 exist and are correct, but they are used only in f_invalidation (1334-1365) for the target-vs-stop race. The side choice at 1891-1897 and 1975 ignores them.

concepts.name: Previous-candle range states and base rates (PDH/PDL taken, both, inside)
concepts.definition:
Candle t−1 vs t−2:
- close-through up: H1>H2, L1≥L2, C1>H2
- sweep-reject up (bear CRT): H1>H2, L1≥L2, C1≤H2
- close-through down / sweep-reject down (bull CRT): mirror
- inside: H1≤H2, L1≥L2
- outside, by where it closes
'Taken' = traded through, strict >/<.
concepts.dolRole: Gives base rates and timing for HTF prior-candle liquidity. At least one prior extreme is taken within 1 candle 79-93% of the time and within 2 candles 92-99%. Both are taken 8-12% of the time; inside 7-21%.
concepts.evidenceNotes:
[this study, prevcandle.py, nr.py]
- S&P D: H1 51.3%, L1 44.6%, both 9.0%, inside 13.0%, ≥1 side 87.0%; either within 2 days 97.0%.
- NQ 1H: 51.1 / 46.1 / 11.6 / 14.5%.
- External: ES PDH or PDL touched 90.3% (Elite Trader, 168/186 days); edgeful NQ opening inside the prior NY range → one side tagged 75%; edgeful SPY inside days → PDH 52%, PDL 40%, both 15.3%.
concepts.engineNotes: PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL exist as levels (f_rangeTrack 807-833, 945-961) with exact anchors. There is no candle class, no prior close, no 4H/1H prior candle, and no which-first probability or base-rate readout.

concepts.name: ICT daily bias rule (close through PDH → PDH+ next; swept and closed back inside → opposite side)
concepts.dolRole: The practitioners' standard answer to 'is today a PDH or a PDL day'. It picks the side of the next draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Bias side first among decided within 3 candles: real 0.69-0.76 vs shape-shuffle null 0.68-0.76 (S&P D 0.688/0.710, NQ 1H 0.727/0.739, NASDAQ W 0.763/0.758). That is pure geometry. As a hard rule it is right 64-73%, below ruin geometry at 70-81%. edgeful YM: PDH broken → green session 67%/81%, which is consistent with geometry and drift.
concepts.engineNotes: Not part of D (1891-1894). This is correct as a fixed term, because the evidence shows no information beyond geometry. It should enter only as a learned feature (BIAS-1) and as an informational class (BIAS-3).

concepts.name: Candle Range Theory (CRT)
concepts.dolRole: A popular rule for choosing the next draw: after a sweep and reclaim, target the opposite extreme of the range candle.
concepts.engineNotes: There is no CRT detector. Sweeps feed liqEvt at 1580-1582 with REJECT = reversal, the CRT reading, which the evidence contradicts. Recommendation: informational event and alert only (BIAS-3, BIAS-7), never a hard target rule.

concepts.name: Turtle Soup / Oops / smash day (sweep-and-reverse of external liquidity)
concepts.definition:
- Turtle Soup: a new 20-day low where the prior 20-day low is at least 4 days old, then a trade back above it → long (mirror for shorts).
- Oops: the open gaps beyond the prior day's extreme, then price trades back to it.
- Smash day: the close is below the prior day's low; buy if the next day trades above the smash-day high; exit at the first profitable open.
concepts.dolRole: A reversal draw after external liquidity is raided: the opposite side becomes the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study, turtle.py] Turtle Soup excess over geometry: −0.13 to +0.08, mostly ≤ 0 (S&P D bull −0.105, n=58; NQ 1H −0.02/−0.04). External: smash-day longs on the S&P 2014-24 had an 80% win rate and PF 6.94, but index shorts were weak (RogueQuant). This matches daily-equity mean reversion after closes below the prior low (+7 to +15 pp toward the high vs geometry). It is asset-specific.
concepts.engineNotes: Raids of any pool feed liqEvt (1580-1582) with no age requirement; induceBar (892-895) feeds density. Nothing more is needed beyond making the raid-outcome sign learned (BIAS-4).

concepts.name: Open-relative bias (midnight / true day open / weekly open)
concepts.definition: Price above the period's opening price → bullish period, so the draw is the period or prior-period high (mirror below). Anchors: the 00:00 NY open, the 18:00 futures open, the Sunday weekly open. It is evaluated at a decision time (e.g. 08:00, or after Monday/Tuesday).
concepts.dolRole: An intraday or intraweek side filter for PDH/PDL or PWH/PWL.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study, openrel.py] 'Above weekly open → PWH first' is right 0.515-0.636 vs ruin geometry 0.721-0.805 (S&P and NASDAQ 1999-2018, about 180-370 weeks per case). Adding the open sign to calibrated geometry: OOS Brier unchanged (0.1777 vs 0.1780, etc.), weight −0.03 to −0.21. EURUSD midnight-open samples (21-92 days) are inconclusive.
concepts.engineNotes: Midnight/London/NY opens are used only as confluence anchors (964-966, 1931). That is correct. Do not add them to D.

concepts.name: Order-flow / structure bias vector D (MTF swing bias + displacement + raid outcomes)
concepts.dolRole: Decides the eligible side, the draw pillar (30% weight) and the ×0.5 counter-draw penalty, so it dominates the side choice.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sibling ict_struct results: the engine D's OOS accuracy on symmetric ±1.5 ATR first passage is 0.488-0.543 and htfBias alone 0.502-0.522, the same as random-walk controls. [this study, race.py] Pivot-bias logistic weight is about 0 on 12/13 datasets. [this study, sidesel.py] D-first vs geometry: −4 to −10 pp first-touch accuracy, −2 to −7 pp hit-within-H on NQ/GC/EURUSD 1H and S&P/NASDAQ D.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed weights at 1892-1894, gate 1895, draw pillar 691, ctrMult 692-693, eligibility 1975 and 1998-2005. This is an unvalidated prior with coin-flip skill that overrides geometry. Fix: D := calibrated race probability with learned features (BIAS-1, BIAS-2).

concepts.name: Raid outcome sign (sweep HOLD = continuation, REJECT = reversal)
concepts.definition:
After a pool is traded through on a confirmed bar:
- HOLD = the close stays beyond the zone → continuation;
- REJECT = the close is back inside the level → reversal.
Engine: evt = ±1, tier-weighted, half-life 24.
concepts.dolRole: Feeds D's 30% liquidity-event component, so it pushes the next-draw side after every raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CRT/Turtle Soup are at or below geometry. [this study] Swept equity highs are retaken more than the null (+5 to +9 pp). AMD on NQ: direction follows the trend regime, not the sweep (a bearish London sweep in an uptrend was correct only 24.8%, n=153). Sibling E7: swept levels predict continuation in 65/66 fold selections.
concepts.engineNotes: 1580-1582: REJECT pushes D toward reversal. Set the REJECT weight to 0 by default and learn its sign (BIAS-4). This complements ict_liq ICT-2.

concepts.name: Dealing-range position / premium-discount / close-location value
concepts.definition: pos = (x − rangeLow)/(rangeHigh − rangeLow) of the HTF dealing range (ICT: buy in discount toward the premium draw). The previous-candle version is CLV = (C1−L1)/(H1−L1).
concepts.dolRole: Prior-candle CLV is the most predictive single feature for which prior extreme is taken first (through geometry). HTF dealing-range position is a premium/discount prior.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] The CLV coefficient dominates every logistic fit (+2.3 to +4.7 when the decision is at the close). Quintiles on the S&P D: lowest CLV → P(H1) 0.206 / P(L1) 0.741; highest → 0.753 / 0.210. Premium/discount as an ICT prior: see ict_pd ICTPD-7 (mixed evidence).
concepts.engineNotes: Premium/discount % is shown in the Terminal panel only (2324-2333); htfEQ/dayEQ are confluence anchors (967-968). It should enter the side model as geometry (the race) plus a learned HTF-position feature (BIAS-1, x7).

concepts.name: Trend regime (daily close vs EMA20 ±0.5%)
concepts.definition: Uptrend if close > EMA20·(1+0.5%), downtrend if close < EMA20·(1−0.5%), otherwise ranging. Sensitivity was tested at EMA 10-50.
concepts.dolRole: Conditions every sweep or bias signal. In the AMD study it carries all the directional information.
concepts.evidenceNotes: AMD paper (arXiv 2610.35887, NQ 2022-26): trend-aligned correct 62-71%, opposed 25-30%, BH-significant. [this study, cells.py] Excess over geometry is only ±2-4 pp and changes sign: S&P D uptrend −3.6 pp (mean reversion); S&P W +2.2 pp; NQ 1H +1.5/−1.2 pp. The evidence is mixed overall and regime-specific.
concepts.engineNotes: No EMA regime. Add it only as a learned feature (it could be computed on the chart from HTF closes, or proxied by HTF range position) inside BIAS-1.

concepts.name: Momentum vs mean reversion; breakout continuation vs sweep reversal (by asset and timescale)
concepts.definition: Breakout: close beyond the N-bar extreme (N=20) → continuation. Sweep: wick beyond and close inside → reversal. Time-series momentum works at 1-12 months; at shorter horizons the regime depends on the market.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether a close-through level is the next draw's origin (continuation) or a magnet back (reversion), i.e. the sign of the side adjustment.
concepts.engineNotes: The empirical PoT surface (1526-1532, f_empPoT 1285-1301) captures drift per htfBias regime. Because htfBias has about zero skill, the split mostly costs sample (BIAS-6). There is no breakout-state feature; add it as a learned feature.

concepts.name: Contraction → expansion (Crabel NR4/NR7/inside day)
concepts.definition: NR4/NR7: the narrowest range of the last 4/7 candles. Inside day: as in the taxonomy. Premise: contraction is followed by expansion, so trade the break of the narrow candle's extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Timing and 'both sides' risk: after a narrow candle both prior extremes are near and both are often taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes:
[this study, nr.py]
- P(next range > 20-bar median) after NR7 is 0.26-0.45, lower than the 0.48-0.50 base on every dataset, so the expansion claim is false in absolute terms (volatility clusters).
- P(next candle takes both prior extremes) after NR7 is 0.16-0.29 vs base 0.08-0.14 (about 2×, which is geometry).
concepts.engineNotes: coilScore (886-889) feeds level density only. Do not add an expansion prior. The 'both sides' probability belongs in the BIAS-3 readout.

concepts.name: AMD / Power of 3 (London sweep of the Asia range → NY delivery to the opposite side)
concepts.definition: Asia range 19:00-00:00 ET. London (02:00-05:00) breaches one extreme by δ (10 NQ points) before 04:00 and closes back inside before 05:00. NY (09:40-10:30) delivers to the opposite Asia extreme. Bilateral breaches are excluded.
concepts.dolRole: The intraday session version of CRT, used to pick the NY-session draw.
concepts.engineNotes: Killzone affinity f_kzAff 597-602 (London ×1.20 on Asia pools) handles timing. The direction should come from the learned side model, not from the sweep. Timing details are in ict_time.md.

concepts.name: Weekly profile templates
concepts.definition: Named weekly shapes: the low or high of the week forms Mon/Tue in trending weeks, midweek reversal, consolidation then Thursday reversal, and so on.
concepts.dolRole: Which of PWH/PWL is taken first, and on which day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Covered by ict_time.md 1.10: the arcsine law explains most of the 'high/low forms early' effect. As a side predictor it reduces to the PWH/PWL race. [this study, openrel.py] ruin geometry 72-80% vs the open rule 52-64%.
concepts.engineNotes: No template logic. Not recommended beyond the PWH/PWL race readout (BIAS-3 with tfH = W in Swing mode).

concepts.name: Side-level ('which side first') accuracy ledger
concepts.definition: Every few bars, record the best buy-side and sell-side finalists, the geometric race probability and the model probability. Resolve on the first trade-through (same-bar both = ambiguous; none within H = undecided). Score prequentially with Brier, log-loss and accuracy against geometry and against the legacy D.
concepts.dolRole: Measures and learns the side forecast itself, the core 'which liquidity next' question, rather than only 'did the chosen target get hit'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Methodological need shown by X10 (arXiv 2611.12141: a sign-randomised null reproduces about 95% of apparent skill) and by this study's null results. The engine's own EDGE metric is already distance-matched, which is good, but it does not test the side.
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger (1426-1499) grades only the active DOL's hit within H against f_potBase (1314-1322). Add SideTrial records and calibration (BIAS-1).

concepts.name: Multi-timeframe bias table (structure)
concepts.definition: For each of HTF/STF/EXE: swing bias from BOS/CHoCH (f_structure), or internal bias while the swing is undecided, shown BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL.
concepts.dolRole: Traders read it as the directional forecast and align entries with it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The sibling study and this one show swing/pivot bias has about zero skill for the next draw (0.49-0.54; logistic weight about 0). It is shown with no accuracy attached.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean 2293-2305, Terminal 2321-2336. Keep the look (reference product), and add measured skill in shading and a tooltip (BIAS-5).

concepts.name: HTF previous-candle probabilities for 4H/1H (CRT on 4H, P4H/P1H extremes)
concepts.definition: The previous candle of each mode timeframe (D/4H/1H in Day Trading mode): its high, low, close and class. The within-period race between the prior high and prior low uses f_raceH with the bars remaining in the period.
concepts.dolRole: Gives 'daily/4H bias' as P(prior high first), P(prior low first) and P(neither), and supplies 4H CRT targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Geometry 70-81% (race.py); base rates in prevcandle.py; class lift about 0. Practitioners use the 4H CRT heavily.
concepts.engineNotes: Only D and W ranges are tracked (945-961). Add f_candleTrack(timeframe.change(tf)) for tfH/tfS/tfE; no new request.security is needed (BIAS-3).

proposals.title: Side ledger with an online-calibrated side model P(BSL finalist before SSL finalist)
proposals.rationale: The core forecasting question (which side first) is currently neither measured nor modelled. Geometry predicts it at 70-81%, and every tested bias feature adds ≤ ±2-4 pp with a market-specific sign. The engine should start from geometry and let features earn weight on the chart, scored prequentially, which makes every bias claim self-measuring.
proposals.spec:
1. Add a Level field `scoreND`, set in evaluate. Save `mPre = this.mult` before the ctrMult test (692), then set scoreND = clamp(100·(raw − wDraw·draw/wSum)·mPre). This is needed because track() resets mult to 1 at 659.
2. New step 14b, inCalc bars only, after sV/mV (1892-1893) and before drawD:
   - finalist per side = the pool level with max scoreND and 0 < distance ≤ maxATR·atr; fall back to the nearest extReg entry;
   - up = nearEdge of the up finalist, dn = nearEdge of the down finalist;
   - pGeo = f_race(up−close, close−dn, potSig, potMu).
3. Features x[9] = [1, logit(pGeo), sV, mV, liqHold, liqRej, prevHTF rule (BIAS-3), HTF range position 2·(close−htfRL)/(htfRH−htfRL)−1, HTF CRT flag].
4. pUp = sigm(w·x), with w initialised to the prior w0 = [0,1,0,…] (pure geometry).
5. Every sp = max(1, round(H/5)) bars push SideTrial{up, dn, pGeo, pMod, x, bar0}; cap 64.
6. New step 2b resolves trials: high>up xor low<dn → learn; both → ambiguous; neither by H → undecided.
7. Learning: online logistic SGD with shrinkage to w0: w += η((y−p)x − 0.01(w−w0)), η = 0.05/√(1+n/200).
8. Prequential stats: Brier of the model, of geometry and of the legacy D; accuracy; undecided and ambiguous counts.
9. UX: Terminal row 'SIDE BSL 63% · skill +2.1% · n 412'; Full view lists the learned weights; Clean view puts it in the target tooltip.

Pine v6:
- UDT SideTrial with an array<float> field (docs: fields may reference collections);
- globals sdW, sdW0, sideT, sdSt, pUp in STATE (~1080);
- helpers f_dot and f_sideLearn after f_raceAdj (~1372); they use f_sigm and f_logit (484-490);
- no new request.security; cost O(pool + trials·9) per bar.
proposals.risk: SGD noise at small n (mitigated by shrinkage to geometry and a decaying η; show n). Overlapping trials make the effective n smaller (spacing sp). Feature collinearity is handled by the logistic form. Finalist choice must exclude draw influence (scoreND with mPre), otherwise it becomes circular.

proposals.title: Draw Source = calibrated side probability (D := 2·pUp − 1), legacy structure vote kept as an option
proposals.rationale: An engine-like simulation shows that selecting the side by a structure vote (≈ engine sV, gate 0.35) instead of by race geometry costs 4-10 pp of side accuracy and 2-7 pp of hit-within-H on NQ/GC/EURUSD 1H and S&P/NASDAQ daily. Keeping draw-side-first (the decision history) but changing what the draw is fixes this. The draw pillar becomes P(this side first).
proposals.risk: Targets may be nearer on average (the race favours the near side); the minDistATR taper and minScore limit trivially close picks. Side churn as geometry moves is mitigated by the 2-bar challenger, the 2× side-flip hysteresis (2013-2016) and the persistence rule. The legacy look stays available via the 'Structure Vote' option.

proposals.title: Previous-candle module for HTF/STF/EXE: class (close-through / CRT / inside / outside) + P(prior high first), P(prior low first), P(neither)
proposals.rationale: It answers the trader's daily-bias question with honest numbers. Geometry gives 70-81%; class labels are shown with their measured lift, usually about 0. It also supplies features to BIAS-1 and CRT events to BIAS-7. The engine already tracks PDH/PDL but not the class, the prior close, the 4H/1H prior candle, or any probability.
proposals.spec:
1. New f_candleTrack(bool isNew) in SERIES-STATE FUNCTIONS after f_rangeTrack (833).
   - var state: running h0/l0/o0, previous h1/l1/c1 (c1 = close[1] at the change) and h2/l2.
   - Returns [h1, l1, c1, o0, h0, l0, cls], cls ∈ {1 close-through up, 2 bear CRT, −1 close-through down, −2 bull CRT, 0 inside, ±3/4 outside by close}.
2. Call it three times at global scope with timeframe.change(tfH), (tfS) and (tfE); each call site has its own var state; no request.security.
3. While both prior extremes are untaken this period:
   - pU = f_raceH(h1−close, close−l1, potSig, potMu, hRem) and pD = f_raceH(close−l1, h1−close, potSig, −potMu, hRem);
   - hRem = (time_close(tf) − time)/(chart seconds·1000);
   - pNone = 1 − pU − pD.
4. Calibration per (TF, class): n, k, Σp of 'high first | decided', booked at period end from the first-touch flags, using the prediction made at the period's first bar. Shift with δ = logit((k+20p̄)/(n+20)) − logit(p̄), the f_raceAdj pattern (1367-1372).
5. UX: Clean table stays 2 columns with a tooltip per Bias cell ('Prev D: swept high, closed inside (CRT↓) · P(PDH first) 41% · P(PDL first) 47% · neither 12% · class lift +1% (n 212)'). Terminal gets a 'PREV' row group.
6. Optional (off by default): push the STF/EXE prior-candle extremes into extReg as new src codes.
proposals.risk: Session-boundary conventions differ (18:00 futures day vs RTH vs midnight); expose the day source. Class samples are small (about 1/day on D), so shrinkage keeps values at geometry until data accrue. Tooltip-only UX preserves the reference look.

proposals.title: Raid outcome: split liqEvt into HOLD and REJECT; REJECT carries no direction by default (learned in BIAS-1)
proposals.spec:
- Replace `var float liqEvt` with `var float liqHold` and `var float liqRej`, both decayed with liqHL at 1535.
- At 1581-1582: HOLD → liqHold += side·tier; REJECT → liqRej += −side·tier (same sign convention as now).
- Input rejW = input.float(0.0, 'D · Raid Rejection Weight', −1..1, tooltip '0 = evidence default; 1 = classic ICT reversal reading').
- Legacy D uses liqHold + rejW·liqRej. The Calibrated draw (BIAS-1) learns both signs as features x4 and x5.
- Complements ict_liq ICT-2 (post-sweep outcome learner); implement them together.
proposals.risk: On some markets rejections may carry a reversal signal; the learned weight in BIAS-1 recovers it. The default change alters legacy D behaviour, which the README should note.

proposals.title: Bias table with measured skill: keep BULLISH/BEARISH text, shade and annotate by measured lift over geometry
proposals.rationale: Traders read the bias table as a forecast, but swing/pivot bias has about zero skill for the next draw (sibling 0.49-0.54; logistic weight about 0). Showing the measured lift keeps the reference look while removing false confidence, and the numbers are measured by construction.
proposals.spec:
- For each TF row, the BIAS-3 period bookkeeping also stores that row's bias at the first bar of each period: n, k = 'prior high first | decided' when BULLISH (mirror for BEARISH), and Σ pGeo.
- lift = k/n − p̄geo; se = √(Σp(1−p))/n.
- Clean (2297-2305): same words; the text colour has full alpha if lift > 1.5·se, otherwise alpha 60; tooltip 'when bullish, prior high taken first 61% (geometry 58%, n 140)'.
- Terminal (2321-2336): add a SKILL column.
- Input 'Bias Skill Shading' (default on).
proposals.risk: Dimmed cells may look broken to users expecting the reference look (hence the toggle). Small n on HTF rows: show n.

proposals.title: Empirical PoT surface: choose the regime key (pooled vs htfBias split, optionally prev-HTF-class) by held-out Brier
proposals.rationale: f_bump/f_empPoT (1531-1532, 1285-1301) split the reach surface three ways by htfBias, which has about zero measured skill. The split mostly cuts the sample per row to about a third and adds PoT noise. Regime effects of ±2-4 pp are market-specific (cells.py, AMD paper), so let the chart decide.
proposals.spec:
- At step 0 (1526), before f_bump for the window that just completed:
  - for d ∈ {0.5, 1, 2} ATR and each side, compute the pooled prediction Σ_r S_r(d)/Σ_r n_r and the split prediction S_{r*}(d)/n_{r*}, with r* from htfBias[H];
  - score both against the realized reach (fwdHi − close[H])/aH ≥ d (mirror for down) and accumulate the two Brier scores (2 floats per (d, side)).
- In f_empPoT: use the split row only if BrSplit < BrPool − 0.002 after ≥ 300 windows, else pooled.
- Optional alternative key: BIAS-3 prev-HTF class groups (up-close/bull-CRT, down-close/bear-CRT, other).
- Report the choice in the Terminal Full view.
proposals.risk: A small per-bar cost (6 surface interpolations). Choosing on in-sample Brier could overfit marginally; the margin and minimum window count limit that. Interacts with ict_time TIME-1/TIME-2 (clock-aware PoT), so coordinate.

proposals.title: HTF candle-close event alerts (CRT / close-through) carrying calibrated odds and measured class lift
proposals.rationale: CRT and close-through events are what many traders wait for. An alert that states the engine's calibrated probabilities (e.g. P(sweep high retaken first) 59%) gives workflow value without encouraging the overconfidence the evidence warns about.
proposals.spec:
- On timeframe.change(tfH) or timeframe.change(tfS) with cls ∈ {±1, ±2} from BIAS-3:
  alert('DOL Engine ▸ ' + tfLabel + ' ' + clsText + ' · P(prior high first) ' + pU + ' · P(prior low first) ' + pD + ' · class lift ' + lift + ' (n ' + n + ')', alert.freq_once_per_bar_close).
- Plus alertcondition(htfCandleEvent, 'HTF Candle Event', ...).
- Input 'Alert · HTF candle events', default off; limited to tfH and tfS to avoid spam.
proposals.risk: Alert fatigue on low timeframes (limited to HTF/STF). Users may still read CRT as a signal; the message shows the lift, typically about 0.

concepts.name: Swing point detection (pivot vs leg vs zigzag)
concepts.definition: ta.pivothigh(len,len): H[len] is the extreme of a symmetric 2*len+1 window, confirmed len bars late (engine pivLen 5, MTF biasLen 3). LuxAlgo SMC 'leg': a bearish leg starts when H[size] > highest(H,size) of the following bars, and the swing high is emitted when the leg flips (swing 50, internal 5, EQ 3); highs and lows alternate. py-smc: symmetric window, consecutive same-type swings reduced to the more extreme one. PyIndicators recursive fractals: depth 1/2/3 = short/intermediate/long term.
concepts.dolRole: Swings are the liquidity pools (BSL above swing highs, SSL below swing lows); hierarchy (short vs intermediate vs long term) ranks them.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definition choices; no study shows one pivot rule forecasts better. Tie behaviour of ta.pivothigh is undocumented in the v6 reference.
concepts.engineNotes: 879-880, 709-710. No alternation, which is correct for liquidity. Tight double tops inside one pivot window give one pivot (no EQx2). Hierarchy is missing (ICT-8).

concepts.name: BOS/CHoCH confirmation (body vs wick), internal vs swing
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: first close crossing the pivot level (crossover(close, level)), each pivot breaks once; CHoCH if the prior trend was opposite, else BOS; internal (5) breaks are ignored when the internal level equals the swing (50) level; optional wick-comparison confluence filter. py-smc: 4-swing patterns with close_break=True by default. openalgo: close by default, wick optional.
concepts.dolRole: Sets bias/draw side and order-block creation; ICT uses MSS to end a retracement.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Structure direction is about a coin flip for which side is taken first (49.9-51.6%, ict_struct 2.2); 44 SMC detectors incl. BOS/CHoCH do not beat matched random (SSRN 7483658).
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure 708-782 (ibias on close through the last pivot; swing bias via protected extremes); chart BOS 1542-1547. Matches the open-source consensus and the reference product's body-break rule.

concepts.name: Strong/weak extremes (trailing extremes)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: top = max(top, H) since the last swing high, updated every bar; 'Strong High' if the swing trend is bearish, else 'Weak High' (the likely target); mirror for lows.
concepts.dolRole: The weak extreme is the open-source 'next target' on the trend side; the strong extreme is the invalidation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner convention; the race between weak and protected extremes matches gambler's-ruin geometry (ict_struct).
concepts.engineNotes: legH/legL and protH/protL tracked 713-774 and returned at 782, but the weak extreme is not a pool and protH/protL are unused (ICTS-4/5/7).

concepts.name: Premium/discount zones
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC from trailing extremes: premium [0.95*top+0.05*bottom, top], equilibrium band [0.525*bottom+0.475*top, 0.525*top+0.475*bottom], discount [bottom, 0.95*bottom+0.05*top].
concepts.dolRole: ICT: target buy-side from discount, sell-side from premium.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No intraday evidence; long-horizon literature favours continuation near highs (ict_pd).
concepts.engineNotes: Display only (Terminal ZONE 2327-2332), dayEQ/htfEQ as confluence anchors 967-968 (ICTPD-7).

concepts.name: Order block detection
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: on a structure break, the extreme candle (lowest low for bullish) between the broken pivot and the break bar, excluding high-volatility bars (range >= 2*ATR(200) or cumulative mean range; v2 swaps parsed high/low so they cannot be chosen); up to 100 stored. py-smc: lowest-low candle between last swing high and break. ICT: last down-close candle before displacement.
concepts.dolRole: Candidate imbalance target (PD array) and breaker source.
concepts.evidenceNotes: OBs revisited 73.7% vs 73.7% for random zones at the same distance (Nordman, 10,986 touches, via ict_pd).
concepts.engineNotes: 1663-1748: last down-close at or before the leg low within obLook 20, with a quality gate and a revisit skip. No volatility exclusion or height cap, so a capitulation candle can form a multi-ATR OB (SMC-5).

concepts.name: Order block mitigation modes
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo v2 input Close vs High/Low (default High/Low): removed when the source crosses the far edge. py-smc: wick (default) or body through the bottom turns the OB into a breaker. openalgo: removed at first touch.
concepts.dolRole: Decides when an OB stops being a valid target or flips to a breaker.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Convention only.
concepts.engineNotes: As a target: Touch/CE/Full delivery (delivIn 123, 1566-1577); validity via obTrk breaks 1651.

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows (EQH/EQL) thresholds
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: separate pivot length 3, compared with the previous EQ pivot only, tolerance 0.1*ATR(200). LuxAlgo free DOL: 0.1 ATR, pool moves to the outermost swing. PyIndicators internal zones: 0.25*ATR(14). openalgo Radar: compare with the 5 previous swings. py-smc: 1% of the whole dataset range (non-causal).
concepts.dolRole: Equal levels mark resting stop clusters; practitioners rank them as a higher-tier draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Distance-matched test across 8 markets: EQ adds <1 pp beyond distance (ict_liq E6).
concepts.engineNotes: f_findLiq/f_mergeAt 1090-1137, eqTol 0.10*ATR(14) at 1522. Uses fast ATR, so tolerance shrinks in quiet sessions (SMC-5).

concepts.name: Buyside/sellside liquidity clusters
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo BSL/SSL (PyIndicators port): zigzag of pivots (len 7); on a new pivot, scan older same-side swings newest-first, stop at the first swing beyond the band, count swings within an ATR(10)-scaled band; a pool needs >=3 swings; level = mid of the cluster; breach zone x2.3.
concepts.dolRole: Larger clusters are larger stop pools; the outermost is the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics published.
concepts.engineNotes: Stacked pools: outermost is the draw, inner pools are inducement (f_stackSide 1230-1251, inner x0.70 at 684-685).

concepts.name: Liquidity visits / touch counts (Liquidity Swings)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo Liquidity Swings: pivot 14; zone = wick extremity (H to max(O,C) of the pivot bar) or full range; each later bar overlapping the zone adds 1 to count and its volume, until a close beyond the zone (crossed); filter by min count or volume.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioners treat a heavily visited level as more relevant; for the DOL question the sign (more likely broken vs more likely bounce) matters.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Chung & Bellotti 2021 (arXiv 2101.07410): bounce probability rises with prior bounces and beats a shuffled control; it decays to 0.5 after about 350-900 min on EURUSD (e.g. b_prev=4: a=0.402***, b=-0.00179*, N=505).
concepts.engineNotes: tests 650-658 add +0.35 each (max 6) to magnitude at 682, a positive sign with no decay; gap>0 at 654 skips exact touches, contradicting README line 66 (SMC-3).

concepts.name: Liquidity sweep classification
concepts.definition: PyIndicators/LuxAlgo Liquidity Sweeps: wick sweep = H > level and C < level (once per level); outbreak-and-retest = close beyond, then a later wick back through with a close on the original side; levels retired on a close through. Pure price action variant: wick through a recursive-fractal pivot without a close beyond; max age 2000.
concepts.dolRole: Distinguishes a raid (stops taken, then reversal or continuation) from a run; feeds draw direction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Continuation after sweeps dominates in several studies (ict_liq E6/E7/E9, ict_struct 2.2).
concepts.engineNotes: 1580-1582 HOLD/REJECT mapping into liqEvt, disputed (ICTS-2, ICT-2). The removal rule (strict trade-through, 623-624) is right.

concepts.name: Fair value gap detection and filters
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: L > H[2] and C[1] > H[2] with an auto threshold (middle bar body% > 2 * cumulative mean of absolute body%). TradingFinder filters: Very Aggressive (candle 3 extends beyond candle 2), Aggressive (+ candle 2 not small), Defensive (+ large body-dominated candle 2, candles 2-3 in direction), Very Defensive (+ no doji at candles 1 and 3). py-smc: optional join_consecutive.
concepts.dolRole: Imbalance targets and waypoints (ICT IRL).
concepts.evidenceNotes: FVGs revisited 73.0% vs 72.9% for random levels (Nordman, 38,114 returns); about +5 pp short-lived reaction (ict_pd 2.1).
concepts.engineNotes: 907-913, 1868-1887: size >= 0.15 ATR plus a quality gate >= 0.45; stricter than most open-source scripts.

concepts.name: FVG mitigation modes
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC deletes on a wick full fill (L < bottom); py-smc mitigates at first touch; TFlab offers proximal / 50% / distal; LuxAlgo dynamic FVG shrinks the box as it fills.
concepts.dolRole: When an imbalance target counts as delivered.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Fill ladder statistics in ict_pd (ICTPD-3).
concepts.engineNotes: delivIn Touch/CE/Full with partial-fill cropping 1566-1577; the active DOL counts a touch.

concepts.name: Inversion FVG (iFVG)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo IFVG: an FVG whose whole gap is closed through against its bias flips role; gaps filtered by an ATR multiplier; last N pairs shown; retest signals by wick or close; a zone is cleared once it is itself mitigated.
concepts.dolRole: Continuation retest zones on the way to the DOL (reference product usage).
concepts.evidenceNotes: S&P daily test: iFVG retests hold 38% vs 38% for random (via ict_pd); no edge.
concepts.engineNotes: 1598-1644: inversion and cleanup match. No slow-ATR width filter and no show-last-N per side, which clutters low TFs (SMC-6); no retest event (ICTPD-8).

concepts.name: Breaker blocks
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo Breaker Blocks with Signals (PyIndicators port): zigzag with older low C, high D, newer low E where E < C (old low taken), then the first close above D (MSS); the breaker is the first up-close candle scanning from D back to C (optionally body, or 2 candles); mitigated on a close below the bottom; cancelled on a close between centre and bottom before entry.
concepts.dolRole: A failed OB that becomes the opposite PD array after liquidity is taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics; arrays are near-random as magnets (E3).
concepts.engineNotes: 1646-1661 builds breakers only from OBs whose own origin swept a 20-bar extreme (tookL 1691/1706/1734/1747). The open-source template is given in the report section 5 for ICTPD-2.

concepts.name: Killzones and session pivots
concepts.definition: TFO ICT Killzones & Pivots defaults (NY time): Asia 2000-0000, London 0200-0500, NY AM 0930-1100, NY Lunch 1200-1300, NY PM 1330-1600; session high/low pivots extend until mitigated (swept); most recent only by default; optional opens at 00:00, 06:00, 10:00, 14:00.
concepts.dolRole: Session extremes are classic intraday draws (London raids Asia, NY raids London).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Timing evidence is in ict_time.
concepts.engineNotes: Sessions at 107-109 (NY AM 0930-1200), killzones at 223-226, registry until swept 1591-1596, 1800-1809. No NY Lunch or PM session pools (TIME-3).

concepts.name: Previous day/week highs and lows
concepts.definition: Prior completed period extremes; LuxAlgo SMC v1 reads them via request.security on daily/weekly high and low with lookahead on.
concepts.dolRole: Top-tier external liquidity (LuxAlgo DOL tiers W 4 > D 3).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Old highs and lows show strong S/R reactions (ict_pd 2.4).
concepts.engineNotes: Computed on the chart with exact print bars (f_rangeTrack 807-832, 945-961, 1790-1799); more precise than the common request.security pattern.

concepts.name: Volume profile LVN/HVN detection
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo Volume Profile with Node Detection: a peak is a row above the N neighbouring rows on each side (N as % of rows), a trough is the mirror; plus a minimum share-of-max threshold. LuxAlgo Liquidity Levels/Voids: profile between consecutive swings (length 47, 27 rows); a void is below 21% of max; filled when price crosses its midpoint.
concepts.dolRole: Thin-volume paths are crossed fast and HVNs stall price, which helps decide if a target is reachable.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner consensus only (NinjaTrader, Quantower); Quantower notes LVNs can become accepted.
concepts.engineNotes: Rolling 1H profile 1384-1414; LVN = run below 0.30*peak excluding tails (2250-2286); path cost 1416-1424, 1945-1947. The absolute cut marks shoulders, not troughs (SMC-7).

concepts.name: Naked (virgin) POC
concepts.definition: A prior session's point of control that price has not traded through since that session ended.
concepts.dolRole: Practitioners treat unrevisited POCs as magnets/targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 84-87% revisited within 5 days on gold/ES/BTC (n about 962-1034); by distance <0.5 ADR 82%, 0.5-1 ADR 59%, 1-2 ADR 32%; no random baseline, distance-confounded.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed; could be measured by the candidate ledger (ICT-1) if added later.

concepts.name: Draw-on-liquidity target selection (open-source tools)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo free DOL: score = tier / ATR distance (W 4, D 3, session/EQ 2, gap 1.5, swing 1), bias side first with fallback, minor pools expire after 500 bars. AGPro planner: 0-100 per side from quality, proximity, trend and freshness, with a balanced state when sides are close. Liquidity Draw: volume-weighted side imbalance >= 55%, target locked on bar close until reached, stop broken or N bars. MQLSoftware: draw % = empirical hit rate of past draws in the same bucket (score x distance x alignment), shown as provisional while n is small.
concepts.dolRole: Directly the forecasting problem: which pool next, how stable, how likely.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published validation of any of these selectors.
concepts.engineNotes: Richer scoring and hysteresis in 1964-2035. Missing: commitment/lock mode (SMC-2) and an outcome-calibrated displayed probability (SMC-1).

concepts.name: Displayed probability calibration
concepts.definition: Show the probability as the observed hit rate of comparable past targets (or a model shifted by it), with the sample size, marked provisional while thin.
concepts.dolRole: Answers 'how likely' honestly for the user's chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard calibration method; raw PoT errors measured up to 2x by hour (ict_time E18).
concepts.engineNotes: f_potModel 1303-1311 is a random-level model; ledger per-family outcomes (stN/stK 1066-1067) only feed f_calMult (1376) and f_raceAdj (1367).

concepts.name: Drawing management (time anchoring, object reuse)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo anchors boxes with xloc.bar_time and pre-allocates 'show last N' objects, updating them with set_* on the last bar. Docs: xloc.bar_index reaches at most 10,000 bars back and 500 forward; max_bars_back is at most 5000; time(tf, bars_back=-1..-500) gives the expected future timestamp, session-aware on time-based charts.
concepts.dolRole: Visual fidelity of origin-anchored zones (the reference look) and realtime smoothness.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Engineering item, grounded in the Pine v6 docs; no market evidence applies.
concepts.engineNotes: max_bars_back(time,5000) at 37 and f_x clamp at 404-405 break origin anchors beyond 5,000 bars (1-minute charts); delete and recreate of all DOL drawings each tick at 2132-2141 (SMC-4).

concepts.name: Liquidity voids (large low-overlap candles)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo BSL/SSL voids: three-bar gaps wider than ATR(200), drawn as zones price tends to revisit.
concepts.dolRole: Imbalance targets and fast-travel paths.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Covered in spirit by ICTPD-10 (merging consecutive FVGs).

proposals.title: Ledger-calibrated PoT: the displayed probability learns from the engine's own past targets
proposals.rationale: The Clean label's PoT is a random-level distance/volatility model (f_potModel 1303-1311). The ledger knows how often selected targets of each family were actually hit (stN/stK) but only uses that to nudge scores and race odds. Raw PoT is off by up to 2x by hour of day (ict_time E18). An open-source DOL tool (MQLSoftware) shows its probability as a bucketed empirical hit rate with n. Outcome calibration corrects all residual biases at once (time, family, selection effect).
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_POT): potCal bool (default true), potK float 20 (shrinkage). Trial (375-395): add pShow (raw f_potModel at open; this is TIME-2's pMod if TIME-2 lands) and pCal (calibrated at open, using only earlier outcomes). State: stPS array<float>(5) = sum of pShow per [grp0..3, ALL]; brSt array<float>(3) = [n, sum (y-pShow)^2, sum (y-pCal)^2]. Helper after f_raceAdj (1371): f_potCal(p, g): gg = stN[g] >= 10 ? g : 4; if n >= 10: pb = stPS[gg]/n; dl = logit((stK[gg] + potK*pb)/(n + potK)) - logit(pb); return min(0.95, sigm(logit(p) + dl)). f_openTrial (1426): pShow = f_potModel(d, side, potMu*side), pCal = f_potCal(pShow, lv.grp()). f_book (1461): accumulate stPS per group and the Brier sums. Use f_potCal at 2067 (activePoT) and 2184 (secondary targets), so the minPoT filter and announcement use the calibrated value. Clean label unchanged, with '~' while n < 30; tooltip shows raw vs calibrated and n; Terminal PoT row shows 'cal n'; Full view row 'PoT CAL Brier raw .231 -> cal .214 · n'. There is no feedback loop because trials open independently of minPoT (2038-2045).
proposals.risk: Noisy offsets early, with roughly 50-150 trials per family on 5,000 bars; mitigated by kappa=20 shrinkage and the ALL fallback. Calibration lags setting changes, but history recomputes on input change. Capped at 95%.

proposals.title: Target commitment mode (Locked until resolved) with a switch-rate metric
proposals.rationale: Open-source DOL tools commit to a target (Liquidity Draw locks on bar close until reached, stop broken or N bars; AGPro reports 'balanced' instead of forcing a side). The engine re-ranks every confirmed bar with hysteresis, so a trader using the DOL as an H-bar plan can see it move ('targets jump around'). Locking also makes the displayed target identical to the graded ledger trial.
proposals.spec: Input commitIn ['Adaptive' (default), 'Locked'] in G_SCORE. State: lockInv float, nSw int, nSwBars int. Selection step 19 (2016-2020): locked = commitIn=='Locked' and curI>=0 and bar_index-activeSince < H and close still on the target side of lockInv. If locked, pick := curI; else the existing logic runs. While locked the INVALIDATED ghost does not fire; on release by an invalidation close the existing ghost path applies; optional '⌛ EXPIRED' reason. On commit (2030-2035): [lkInv, lkRR, lkP] = f_invalidation(activeLv); lockInv := lkInv; count switches (nSw) when both old and new ids are >= 0 within inCalc. Re-arm after H if the same target is still best (activeSince := bar_index, recompute lockInv); the ledger opens a fresh trial automatically. Full view: 'SWITCH x /100b'; Clean tooltip 'locked · k/H bars'. A/B: toggling the input recomputes history, so HIT %, EDGE and switch rate are compared on identical bars.
proposals.risk: A locked target can go stale after a sharp opposite move; bounded by the invalidation close and the H expiry. Default stays Adaptive.

proposals.title: Tests with the right sign: count exact touches, decay with recency, neutral default weight
proposals.rationale: Near-misses add +0.35 each (max 6, up to about 7 score points) to pool magnitude (682). Evidence (Chung & Bellotti 2021) shows more prior bounces raise the chance of another bounce, decaying over hours. Under the engine's strict trade-through sweep rule a bounce is not a hit, so the positive weight favours levels less likely to be taken within H. Liquidity Swings counts visits as interest, not as a break predictor. Bug: gap>0 (654) excludes exact touches, contradicting README line 66.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_LIQ): wTest float default 0.0, range -0.35..0.35 (step 0.05); tauT float default 60 bars. Level: add testW float. track (650-658): if gap >= 0 and gap <= testATR*atrV (debounce >= 3 bars kept), then testW := testW*exp(-(bar_index-lastTest)/tauT) + 1, tests += 1, lastTest := bar_index. evaluate (682): replace 0.35*min(tests,6) with wTest*min(testW*exp(-(bar_index-lastTest)/tauT), 6) and wrap x in max(0, x). Keep the T-tag display. If ICT-1's candidate ledger is built, register testsEff as a learned feature and drop wTest. Measure by toggling wTest and comparing CHART LIQ and EXT LIQ family EDGE in the Full view (2410-2418).
proposals.risk: On instruments where repeated tests precede breaks (stop accumulation), a neutral default under-weights them until measured; the input allows a positive weight.

proposals.title: Time-anchored, persistent drawings (xloc.bar_time plus a session-aware future edge)
proposals.rationale: The reference look anchors each zone at its origin candle. xloc.bar_index objects reach at most 10,000 bars back and need a time buffer that max_bars_back caps at 5000, so the engine clamps anchors to 4,999 bars (f_x 404-405, max_bars_back 37). On 1-minute charts PWH and older HTF FVG zones start at the wrong candle. LuxAlgo uses xloc.bar_time. Pine v6 time(timeframe.period, bars_back=-N) returns the expected, session-aware future timestamp (-1..-500), so the right edge can be time-based too. The engine also deletes and recreates every DOL drawing on each tick (2132-2141).
proposals.spec: Add int anchorT to Level, Ext and Zone, set at creation: chart pivots time at the anchor bar (return it from f_anchorScan); FVG time[1]; OB time[obI]/time[obJ]; HTF FVG hfT; MTF pivots htfPvHT/stfPvHT; extend f_rangeTrack and f_sessTrack (807-863) to return hiT/loT. Pass it through f_pushExt and f_newLevel. Compute rT = time(timeframe.period, bars_back = -extBars) at global scope; draw the DOL box, glow lines, tether, label, iFVG boxes, ghosts and LVN boxes with xloc=xloc.bar_time (left = anchorT, right = rT) so all right edges align. Fallback when not chart.is_standard: keep the bar_index path. Persistence: var box/lines/label for the DOL set created once and updated with set_* on barstate.islast; hide with transparency; keep delete/recreate only for variable-count extras.
