proposals.title: Composite value area and value state (POC/VAH/VAL; inside / probe / accepted) as infrastructure and Terminal UX
proposals.rationale: Needed for AMT-2 bits 17-19 and for AMT-4, and gives AMT traders the expected 'are we in value?' context at near-zero cost. Explicitly not a target source (POC/VA edges have no reach edge) and not a directional bias (value migration has no information beyond distance).
proposals.spec: G_LVN inputs: useVA=true, vaPct=70 (50-90), showVA=false; needVP (979) becomes showLVN or usePathVP or useVA. State (1052-1057): var float vpPOC, vpVAH, vpVAL; var int vaPos, vaRun. In step 15, rebuild when (usePathVP or useVA) on newHour, h1Lower or an empty cache. After vpCum: pI = vSm.indexof(vSm.max()); tot = vSm.sum(); while acc < vaPct/100*tot and (lo>0 or hi<nR-1), add the larger neighbour (ties go to the upper row); vpPOC = vLo+(pI+0.5)*vStep, vpVAH = vLo+(hi+1)*vStep, vpVAL = vLo+lo*vStep. Value state once per hourly close (h1C on newHour for charts below 1H, close for charts at or above 1H): p = cH>vpVAH ? 1 : cH<vpVAL ? -1 : 0; vaRun := p!=0 and p==vaPos ? vaRun+1 : p!=0 ? 1 : 0; vaPos := p. UX: Terminal row 'VALUE ▲ ACCEPTED ABOVE (4h) · POC x · VA a-b' and data-window plots; optional POC (solid) and VAH/VAL (dotted) lines from f_x(lvB.first()) to xR, drawn only within maxATR of close. Clean style unchanged.
proposals.risk: VA edges differ between platforms; the tooltip must say 'composite 1H, 48 rows' so users do not compare them with a TPO VA. A while loop of at most 48 iterations once per hour is negligible.

proposals.title: Extended-acceptance damping: mildly penalise targets further from value after 3+ closes beyond value
proposals.rationale: After ≥3 consecutive hourly closes beyond the composite VA, targets further from value are hit 3.8-6.0 pp less than random in 5 of 6 depth×side cells (z up to -3.0); targets back toward value are at baseline. This contradicts the AMT 'acceptance → continuation' folklore and matches the mean-reverting close-vs-VA logit sign. It reduces over-extended continuation targets late in a move.
proposals.spec: G_FLOW inputs: accN=3 (1-12), accM=0.95 (0.7-1.1). In the multiplier loop (1939-1948): if useVA and vaRun >= accN and lv.side == vaPos, multiply lv.mult by accM. Register as AMT-2 bit 19 so the learned lift replaces accM. Requires AMT-3.
proposals.risk: May fight the draw vector D in strong trends, but ×0.95 is small next to the draw pillar (weight 30). Significance is mixed, so it should stay learnable.

proposals.title: LVN troughs as rejection barriers: invalidation anchor, barrier-count feature, honest LVN display
proposals.rationale: LVN troughs reject price more than random levels (+3.2 pp, z 2.9 at 1 ATR) and targets behind thin paths are reached less often, yet the engine treats LVNs as accelerators and draws them without meaning. Using LVNs as barriers puts invalidations behind real rejection zones and gives users correct semantics.
proposals.spec: Adopt SMC-7 trough detection (strict local minimum over ±N rows, depth ≥ lvnProm×peak, tails excluded) in step 15 into var array<float> lvnPx and lvnHalf. Barrier feature: nBar = number of troughs strictly between close and lv.nearEdge(); register as LVN_BARRIER in the ledger (learned lift only, no default multiplier). In f_invalidation (1343-1365), when no opposing pool lies within maxATR, prefer the nearest opposite-side LVN trough at 0.5-1.5 ATR (inv beyond its far edge plus buf) before the execution swing or the 1.5 ATR fallback, behind an input invLVN=true. Display (2250-2287): draw troughs, limit them to maxATR from close, and add a tooltip explaining rejection or fast pass. Race stats (WIN≤H, avg R) measure the invalidation change.
proposals.risk: Troughs are coarse with 48 rows over 120h. Changing invalidation alters R:R readouts, so it sits behind an input. The stop-placement benefit was not tested directly.

proposals.title: Poor (flat) key-level extremes count as equal highs/lows (eqCount) for PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL/session H/L
proposals.rationale: Flat session extremes are slightly more likely to be traded through: +1.6 pp overall (z 1.1), +5.7 pp at 2-4 ATR (z 1.9), rising with the touch count (1 → -2.1, 4+ → +4.4 pp). Chart swings already get EQ density, but key-level trackers keep only the extreme, so the levels traders call 'poor highs' get no credit.
proposals.spec: Add a float tol argument (eqTol*atr, computed at global scope) to f_rangeTrack and f_sessTrack, plus var int hiN/loN and hiLast/loLast. Reset to 1 on a new period or when high exceeds hi+tol. Increment when high >= hi-tol and bar_index-hiLast >= 3, mirroring the 652 test tracker; a new high within tol keeps the count. Emit oHiN/oLoN. Add int eqN to Ext (365-372) and pass it in f_pushExt at 1793-1809. On materialisation (1848) set ne.eqCount := max(ne.eqCount, eqN-1). The label shows EQx2 and the tooltip says 'flat (poor) high'. Register as AMT-2 bit 20.
proposals.risk: Minimal: density saturates through 1-exp(-x). Signatures change at 5 call sites (945-950). The evidence is only marginally significant.

result.summary: Microstructure research strongly supports the engine's geometry. Stops rest just beyond obvious extremes and round numbers: Osler found 14.3% of stop-buys at 01-10 above a "00" against 6.9% at 90-99. Take-profits rest at the round (9.3% exactly at 00). Stops are placed a median 0.43% from the market and live a median 0.46 days. Original tests on 7 datasets (5,631 pivot-pool sweeps) show that sweeps which close back inside penetrate a median 0.23 ATR (q80 0.52). The engine's 0.20 ATR zone is close to that, but its 0.10 ATR invalidation buffer is beaten by 78.5% of rejected sweeps. Moving the stop deeper does not change expectancy (25,195 simulated races: mean R −0.004 to −0.020); it only trades R for win rate. Pool-size proxies (equal prints, tests, age, round numbers) do not change which pool is taken or what happens after the sweep; only prominence relates to a slightly larger post-take run (+0.15 ATR at 10 bars, about 2.3σ). The best size model is therefore small: tier, prominence and stack, with equal-print and test weights at 0 and learned per chart, as in WYK-1/WYK-2. Sweep depth and close class carry no directional information at 3, 10 or 30 bars. Every trade-through is followed by a symmetric volatility burst (+24% excursion at 3 bars, gone by 30), which fits Osler's 15-minute-to-2-hour cascades and the 30-minute crypto liquidation cascades: a timing effect, not a direction effect. The clearest structural gap: 60.8% of rejected-sweep wicks are re-taken within 5 bars, before a pivLen-5 pivot could register them, so the engine never offers them as targets or as the 'beyond the sweep high' invalidation (proposal OF-1). Round numbers are not magnets on hourly/daily bars (mixed sign across datasets). Sweep wicks stop short of a round number beyond a pool about 4 pp more often than at an arbitrary price, and price that reaches a coarse round number passes it +3.3 pp more often. So zones should be capped at the round and stops placed beyond it, with no score bonus; this amends sibling ICT-3. The engine's ×0.85 high-volume-path penalty is unsupported. `request.footprint` exists but would lock the script to Premium users, and delta/absorption and crypto liquidation heatmaps have no bar-level validation, so they are P3, logged and graded by the ledger only. Ops note: Firecrawl reported this account's credits are running low (daily MCP credits refresh in about 23 h).

concepts.name: Stop-loss clustering beyond obvious levels (the physical pool)
concepts.definition: Protective and breakout stops rest just beyond recent swing extremes: BSL above highs, SSL below lows. They form a band, not a single price. Osler: stop-loss orders sit a median 0.43% (mean 0.91%) from the market at placement, stay outstanding a median 0.46 days (mean 3.42), and are larger than take-profits (median $3.24m vs $2.12m).
concepts.dolRole: Defines WHERE the draw is: the band just beyond the most obvious unswept extremes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003/2005 (RBS order book, about 9,700 orders); Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004 (S/R coincides with book depth); Osler 2000 (published S/R predicts trend interruptions, effect lasts at least 5 days).
concepts.engineNotes: BSL zone [P, P+0.20 ATR] (1762), SSL mirror (1774); strict trade-through = swept (623-624).

concepts.name: Take-profit / limit clustering at round numbers and front-running
concepts.definition: Take-profits and limits bunch exactly at 00/50, stops just beyond (01-10). Algorithms post one tick ahead of clusters. Coarse round step = smallest {1,5}x10^k at or above one daily ATR.
concepts.dolRole: Round numbers just beyond a pool cap the sweep wick (take-profit barrier). Stops beyond the round fuel the pass once price reaches it. Round numbers are not magnets at bar resolution.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong for order placement: Osler (take-profits 9.3% at 00; reversals 58-60% vs 55-57%), Bhattacharya et al. 2012 (imbalance flips at round numbers), Lallouache & Abergel, Jung & Lee 2026 (more depth, no extra depth-adjusted stickiness). This study: the magnet edge (round minus control) is mixed in sign across 7 datasets (−4.5 to +10.9 pp). Sweep wicks pass a round just beyond the pool about 4.2 pp less often than an arbitrary level (about 3σ). Once price is at a coarse round, it passes 77.3% vs 74.0% (+3.3 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: No round-number logic anywhere. Sibling ICT-3 proposes a bonus and zone extension; this study's evidence says cap the zone at the round and give no bonus by default.

concepts.name: Stop cascades (running the stops)
concepts.definition: Crossing a stop cluster turns stops into same-direction market orders: price accelerates for minutes to hours, then partially reverts over days. Predatory-trading theory predicts an overshoot followed by reversal.
concepts.dolRole: The inner pool of a stack accelerates price into the outer pool (outermost = draw). Mostly informs timing, not direction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2005: extra move after crossing a round vs an arbitrary level of +0.0057% to +0.0235% at 15 min to 2 h, negative at 1-2 days. CFTC: stops execute more on volatile days. Crypto: 88% of forced selling within 30 min; open interest clears 25-70%.
concepts.engineNotes: Stack logic (1230-1251, inner pool ×0.70 at 684); the liqEvt raid read (1580-1582) uses fixed signs that siblings dispute.

concepts.name: Stop-zone depth (stop band)
concepts.definition: pen = (sweep-bar high − P) / ATR[1]. Core band = [P, P + q50], outer edge = q80, both learned from REJECT sweeps only. Pooled: q50 0.233 and q80 0.518 ATR (daily equities 0.16-0.19, hourly FX/NQ/GC 0.23-0.27). HOLD sweeps: q50 0.74 ATR.
concepts.dolRole: Correct zone drawing, invalidation placement and sweep classification. Does not change which pool is taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study, 7 datasets, 2,504 REJECT sweeps: P(pen > 0.10 ATR) = 0.785, P(> 0.20) = 0.553, P(> 0.50) = 0.210. Consistent with Osler's 01-10 stop band.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed zoneATR 0.20 (93, 1520). Invalidation buffer 0.10 ATR (1344) is inside the band for 78.5% of rejected sweeps.

concepts.name: Invalidation beyond the stop-hunt band
concepts.definition: The stop sits past the q80 sweep depth of the opposing pool instead of 0.10 ATR beyond it.
concepts.dolRole: Honest R:R and win readout. The trader sees the stop-hunt exposure.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study, 25,195 simulated races: buffer 0.10 → win 41.8%, loss 42.8%, mean R −0.004. Buffer 0.75 → 44.6%, 35.5%, −0.020. Stop-then-target share of losses falls from 16.3% to 11.9%. Expectancy is invariant (martingale), so this is a trade-off, not an edge.
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation 1343-1364 uses a fixed 0.10 ATR buffer and offers no band option.

concepts.name: Pool size growth with time and touches
concepts.definition: Microstructure claim: more watchers means more stops (tier, prominence, touches, equal prints, age). Proposed size model = 1 − exp(−(1.2·tier + 0.8·min(1, prom/3) + 0.45·min(stack, 2))), with equal-print and test weights at 0 by default and learned. Freshness flat with a slow decay.
concepts.dolRole: Tie-breaker magnitude only. Size proxies do not predict which pool is taken next at bar resolution.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bounce memory rises with prior bounces but decays in hours (Garzarelli 2014; Chung & Bellotti: EURUSD reaches p = 0.5 at about 350 min for 1 bounce, about 900 min for 4). Stop life is a median 0.46 days. This study: eq ≥ 1 re-take −1.4 ± 1.9 pp, tests ≥ 2 +2.0 ± 1.2 pp. Prominence high vs low: K10 extension +0.21 vs +0.06 ATR. Sibling WYK: no reach effect for eq, tests, coil or age.
concepts.engineNotes: Density adds 0.9·eqCount + 0.35·min(tests,6) (682). Freshness ramps up with age, as if stops accumulate (671).

concepts.name: Pool decay after a sweep and liquidity at the fresh extreme
concepts.definition: A trade-through fills stops between P and the wick; residual stops remain beyond. New stops form beyond the new wick at once.
concepts.dolRole: The sweep wick is an immediate new target and the natural invalidation level.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: 60.8% of REJECT wicks are re-taken within 5 bars (52-82% by dataset), before a pivLen-5 pivot exists; only 38.3% ever become pivots. Re-take edge vs null: +4.3 ± 1.0 pp at K = 3, +0.2 pp at K = 30. Residual after pokes ≤ 0.05 ATR: +2.6 ± 1.6 pp (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Binary removal on trade-through (1583-1589) is correct. New extremes become pools only via ta.pivothigh/low after pivLen bars (1753-1776).

concepts.name: Sweep vs breakout classification
concepts.definition: At the sweep-bar close (BSL): POKE = close < P and pen < 0.05 ATR; REJECT = close < P; PROBE = P ≤ close < P + q50·ATR; ACCEPT = close ≥ P + q50·ATR (q50 is about 0.25 ATR, the same as ICT-2's HOLD threshold).
concepts.dolRole: Labels, alerts and ledger cells. Depth adds no directional forecast at bar resolution.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: re-take and throwback edges are within ±2.6 pp of the null in every depth bucket at K = 3, 10 and 30. P(REJECT | depth bucket) = 91 / 85 / 76 / 59 / 44 / 18%. Volume does not modulate outcomes (WYK §2.6). Continuation is the base case (ICTS-2, BIAS-4).
concepts.engineNotes: HOLD = close > lv.top, REJECT = close < lv.price, fixed ±tier into D (1580-1582). Depth is not used.

concepts.name: Post-sweep volatility burst (timing of stop runs)
concepts.definition: For 3-10 bars after any pool trade-through, excursions in BOTH directions exceed the distance-matched null.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: the next pools on both sides become reachable sooner for a few bars. Matters for short-horizon PoT and ETA.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: K = 3 re-take +4.1 ± 0.6 pp, throwback +3.2 ± 0.6 pp, excursion +0.145 ± 0.018 ATR (+24%). K = 10: +9%. K = 30: about 0. Osler: cascades last 15 min to 2 h. Crypto: 88% within 30 min.
concepts.engineNotes: PoT and race use the slow 50-bar potSig (915-916). No event-conditioned volatility.

concepts.name: Absorption, exhaustion, icebergs, delta divergence
concepts.definition: Absorption = aggressive volume beyond the level with no progress, then a close back inside (BSL: positive delta in the rows above P). Exhaustion = a delta spike, then volume dries up. Iceberg = displayed size refilled at one price. Pine v6 has request.footprint (delta, POC, imbalance rows), but a script calling it is usable only on Premium/Ultimate plans. A lower-TF signed-volume proxy works for everyone.
concepts.dolRole: Confirmation labels at sweeps. No validated forecasting role at bar scale.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Frey & Sandås: icebergs attract matching market orders. Cont et al.: order-flow imbalance has a contemporaneous linear impact. Heston et al.: liquidity reversals last under 1 h. Crypto 15-min reversal after taker-driven moves is worth 1.3 bp. A vendor claim says CVD divergence has no directional edge vs random bars. No bar-level evidence.
concepts.engineNotes: Volume is used only in the 1H volume profile (978-1009).

concepts.name: Liquidity holes and thin volume paths
concepts.definition: Large price changes come from book gaps. Bar proxy: vf = mean volume-profile volume between price and target / profile mean.
concepts.dolRole: Small reachability modifier.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Farmer et al. 2004 (mechanism). This study: thin path (vf < 0.6) +1.3 to +3.6 pp, depending on lookback. Thick path (vf > 1.4) −1.5 to +1.4 pp, so a penalty is unsupported.
concepts.engineNotes: Multipliers ×1.10 thin / ×0.85 thick at 1947. The thick penalty lacks evidence.

concepts.name: Crypto liquidation levels (leverage-implied clusters)
concepts.definition: Long liquidation ≈ entry·(1 − 1/L + mmr), short ≈ entry·(1 + 1/L − mmr). Heatmap model: ΔOI > 0 per bar at hlc3, split long/short, projected to 10/25/50/100× tiers with weights, binned, decayed, and deleted when crossed.
concepts.dolRole: Mechanical forced-order pools on leveraged crypto perps: an optional extra level source.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanics are moderate: BitMEX liquidated traders averaged 60× leverage; daily forced liquidations were 3.51% (long) / 1.89% (short) of OI; Oct 10, 2025 saw about $19bn liquidated. No published hit-rate or magnet test of heatmap clusters exists, and vendors admit no sequence information.
concepts.engineNotes: No open-interest feed or liquidation source. Sibling competitors study set this aside.

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows as pooled stops
concepts.definition: Two or more prints within a tolerance (0.10 ATR) form one pool, with stops beyond the OUTERMOST print.
concepts.dolRole: Location of the pool. Not a size multiplier.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kavajecz & Odders-White define support as a low reached at least twice. Equal pools are not taken more often (sibling E6: under 1 pp; WYK eqtest). This study: post-sweep path unchanged.
concepts.engineNotes: f_mergeAt moves to the outermost print and skips same-candle prints (1104-1131). Correct, but over-weighted in density (682).

concepts.name: Tests (touches without taking)
concepts.definition: A bar within 0.30 ATR of the pool without trading through, at least 3 bars after the previous test.
concepts.dolRole: HF bounce memory makes a bounce, not a break, more likely in the short run. Neutral at bar scale.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Garzarelli and Chung & Bellotti: memory decays within hours. This study: tests ≥ 2 give +2.0 ± 1.2 pp (n.s.). WYK: no reach effect.
concepts.engineNotes: 0.35·min(tests,6) adds magnitude (682). The weight should be 0 by default and learned.

concepts.name: Stop hunting / predatory trading as the DOL premise
concepts.definition: Pushing price through a known cluster to fill size against triggered orders.
concepts.dolRole: Justifies drawing to the obvious pool. The intent is untestable.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brunnermeier & Pedersen 2005 (theory); Osler cascades (mechanism). No evidence about intent.
concepts.engineNotes: This is the engine's core premise; no change needed.

proposals.title: Instant sweep-wick pools: register a rejected sweep's wick as BSL/SSL at bar close
proposals.rationale: Stops form beyond every fresh extreme at once. 60.8% of rejected-sweep wicks are re-taken within 5 bars, before a pivLen-5 pivot can register them, so the engine misses the most obvious level on the chart. For a counter-target, it also cannot place the invalidation 'beyond the sweep high'.
proposals.spec: Input useWick (G_LIQ, default true). Add bool wick to Level (after induce, 340) and Trial (after liq, 389). In step 3 (1564-1589), inside `hit and lv.isLiquidity()`: if REJECT (side == 1 ? close < price : close > price), set the local flag wkH or wkL. New step 4b after the registry drop (never push while step 3 iterates): if not f_mergeLiq(pool, 0, high, 0, eqPx, (high-llR)/atr, 1.0, false, bar_index, -1, -1), create f_newLevel(nextId, 0, 0, high+wPx, high, high, bar_index, bar_index, coilScore, indScore) with wick = true and prom set; mirror for SSL. The later pivot merge at the same bar is the same print, so no eqCount (f_mergeAt 1112-1114). tag() appends ' · WICK'. Ledger: f_openTrial passes wick; f_book updates wkSt = [n, hits, ΣpBase]; the Full view shows 'WICK POOLS hit vs base'. Hit rule unchanged; non-repainting (confirmed bars only).
proposals.risk: More near-price candidates, contained by the minDistATR taper and the 2-bar hysteresis. Its expected edge over the distance baseline at H = 30 is about 0, so its value is coverage and correct invalidation, not extra hit rate.

proposals.title: Measured stop band: learned zone depth, sweep classes, invalidation-buffer option (absorbs ICT-7)
proposals.rationale: Rejected sweeps penetrate a median 0.23 ATR (q80 0.52), and the depth varies by market and timeframe. The fixed 0.20 zone and 0.10 invalidation buffer are beaten by 78.5% of rejected sweeps. A deeper buffer leaves expectancy unchanged (it trades win rate for R), so the honest fix is to show the band, offer the choice, and classify each sweep.
proposals.spec: zoneATR default 0.25 becomes the prior. Inputs zoneLearn (true) and invBufM ['Tight', 'Beyond Stop Band']. STATE before 1082: var array<float> penRej, var float bandQ50/bandQ80, var int swCls. In step 3, push pen = (high − P)/atr[1] for REJECT sweeps (cap 300) and set the class POKE (< 0.05) / REJECT / PROBE (close beyond < q50) / ACCEPT. At 1520: bandQ50/80 = percentile_linear_interpolation(50/80) once n ≥ 30, else the prior; wPx = clamp(bandQ50, 0.05, 0.60)·atr. f_invalidation 1344: buf = Tight ? 0.10·atr : clamp(bandQ80, 0.10, 1.0)·atr. Bar-close sweep alert with class and depth. Terminal line 'STOP BAND q50 · q80 (n)'. ICT-2/ICTS-2 use bandQ50 as holdATR and do not split cells by depth. Measured by band coverage of about 80% and an A/B on raceSt WIN / avgR / PF.
proposals.risk: Survivorship is handled by using REJECT sweeps only. Thin histories fall back to the prior. A deeper buffer lowers the displayed R:R, which is honest.

proposals.title: Evidence-based pool-size model: tier + prominence + stack, equal-print and test weights learned (with WYK-1/WYK-2)
proposals.rationale: Pool size = how many participants reference a level. Equal prints, tests and age change neither reach nor the post-sweep path at bar resolution. Prominence is the only proxy with a measurable post-take effect. The current density gives 0.9·eqCount + 0.35·tests and a maturation ramp, a systematic bias of 5-15 points.
proposals.spec: In evaluate (681-683): x = 1.2·tier + 0.8·min(1, prom/3) + 0.45·min(stack, 2) + eqW·min(eqCount, 2) + tstW·min(tests, 3); dens = 1 − e^−x. Inputs eqW = 0.0 and tstW = 0.0 (G_SCORE, with an evidence tooltip). Liquidity freshness flat: 0.5^(age/(4·halfLife)) (WYK-2). Round numbers add no size. Keep the EQx/T tags in the HUD as facts. Measured by A/B vs the Classic density on overall EDGE and the CHART LIQ / EXT LIQ rows. With ICT-1's candidate ledger, eqCount and tests become learned features.
proposals.risk: Markets where touches do precede breaks lose that weight until the user or ledger raises it. Overlaps WYK-1, so implement once.

proposals.title: Round-number layer, evidence-calibrated: cap zones at rounds, put stops beyond rounds, no score bonus by default (amends ICT-3)
proposals.rationale: Order clustering at rounds is well documented. On bars it is geometry, not a draw: round numbers are not magnets (mixed sign); sweep wicks stop short of a round beyond the pool (−4.2 pp, about 3σ); a coarse round, once reached, is passed +3.3 pp more often. ICT-3's zone extension past the round contradicts this.
proposals.spec: Inputs rnMode ['Off', 'Auto', 'Manual'], rnMan, rnConf (false). Daily step from atrD = atrSlow·sqrt(86400/chartS): e = 10^floor(log10(atrD)), m = atrD/e, step = m ≤ 1 ? e : m ≤ 5 ? 5e : 10e. This gives EURUSD 0.01, NQ 500, gold 100, S&P 50. timeframe.change('D') is evaluated at global scope. Zone cap at 1762/1774/1848 and in OF-1: if a round R lies in (P, top), set top := R (mirror for SSL). f_invalidation: if a round lies within bandQ80 beyond the opposing pool, inv := R ∓ 0.05·atr. Push round anchors into the confluence list (1931) only if rnConf. Trial.rn feature with rnSt = [n, hits, ΣpBase] in the Full view.
proposals.risk: The auto step can be wrong on exotic symbols; Manual overrides it. Must be coordinated with ICT-3 to avoid double counting.

proposals.title: Volume-profile path cost: small thin-path bonus, drop the HVN-wall penalty
proposals.rationale: A thin path helps reach by +1.3 to +3.6 pp (unstable). A thick path shows −1.5 to +1.4 pp, so the engine's ×0.85 (worth 4-6 points, able to flip a selection) is unsupported.
proposals.spec: At 1947: lv.mult *= vf < 0.6 ? vpThin : vf > 1.4 ? vpThick : 1.0. Inputs vpThin = 1.05 and vpThick = 1.00 (G_SCORE, with an evidence tooltip). Optional feature stat for targets with vf < 0.6. Measured by A/B on overall EDGE.
proposals.risk: Negligible.

proposals.title: Post-sweep volatility state for short-horizon readouts (ETA, PoT by session end, race)
proposals.rationale: For 3-10 bars after any trade-through, both sides are more reachable (+24% excursion at 3 bars, +9% at 10). The 50-bar potSig misses this. It matters for horizons of 10 bars or less, and little at H = 30.
proposals.spec: State: var int lastSwp (set on any liquidity hit in step 3); var float vbIn and vbAll = EWMAs of (high−low)/atr[1] for bars 1-3 after a sweep and for all bars. vbF = clamp(vbIn/vbAll, 1, 1.6). sigEff = potSig·(1 + (vbF−1)·0.5^((bar_index−lastSwp)/3)), used in f_pot/f_raceH only for horizons of 10 bars or less (TIME-4 / ETA). Ledger check: calibration of pBase for trials opened within 3 bars of a sweep vs the rest.
proposals.risk: Low: bounded and fast-decaying. Effect on the H = 30 PoT is about +2% on σ.

proposals.title: Order-flow tags at sweeps from a lower-TF delta proxy (zero default weight, logged and graded)
proposals.rationale: Traders want absorption and delta confirmation, and competitors filter sweeps by LTF delta. There is no bar-level evidence of directional value, so it is added as a label and ledger cell only. request.footprint must not go into the main engine, because only Premium/Ultimate users can use a script that calls it.
proposals.spec: Input useDelta (false). ltfD = timeframe.from_seconds(max(60, int(timeframe.in_seconds()/12))). [ltO, ltC, ltV] = request.security_lower_tf(syminfo.tickerid, ltfD, [open, close, volume], ignore_invalid_timeframe = true), one extra unique request. On sweep bars, sum signed intrabar volume overall and beyond P. Tags: ABSORBED (REJECT and side·dBey > 0.2·vAll), EXHAUSTED (|dAll| < 0.1·vAll on a range above 1.5 ATR), DRIVEN (ACCEPT and side·dAll > 0.3·vAll). Shown in the OF-2 bar-close alert and used as ICT-2 learner cells with prior weight 0.
proposals.risk: A sign proxy is not true aggressor delta; FX has tick volume only. Intrabar limits are 100-200k, which covers about 8,000+ bars at 12 intrabars per bar. Users may over-trust the tags.

proposals.title: Crypto estimated liquidation levels as an optional, ledger-graded registry source
proposals.rationale: Forced liquidations are the largest mechanical stop pools on leveraged perps. No study validates heatmap clusters as targets, so the source is off by default and judged only by the ledger.
proposals.spec: Inputs useLiqMap (false) and oiSym (input.symbol; empty means try ticker+'_OI'). oi = request.security(sym, timeframe.period, close[1], lookahead_on, ignore_invalid_symbol = true). On confirmed bars with ΔOI > 0: entry hlc3, long share 0.6/0.4 by candle direction, tiers (10, 25, 50, 100) with weights (.35, .30, .20, .15), mmr 0.005. Add mass to map<int,float> bins of 0.25·atrSlow (capped at 400 keys). Scale by oi/oi[1] when ΔOI < 0; decay with a half-life of about 3 days; delete bins that are crossed. Every 5 bars, push local maxima at or above the 90th percentile within maxATR via f_pushExt with a new src 8 (tierW 0.50, names 'LIQ H' / 'LIQ L'). Per-source ledger stat.
proposals.risk: Model error (unknown leverage mix and long/short split), single-exchange OI, symbol-format variance and extra complexity. Ship only if the ledger shows an edge.

result.summary: The engine's closed-form PoT maths is correct, and its inputs are the weak point. I ported f_pot, f_race and f_raceH to Python: they match Monte Carlo within discretisation bias, and the log-space reflection term and the Numerical Recipes erfc are sound. On 6 CME futures (about 1.2M level-windows per horizon, causal walk-forward), the analytic PoT built on ta.stdev(Δclose,50) and a 0.5×50-bar drift is badly over-confident: calibration slope 0.66 (ideal 1.0). The drift term is the largest error. Removing it cuts log-loss by 3.7% at H=30 and 7.1% at H=60. A driftless random-walk simulation shows the same harm (+5.4% log-loss). Races match the martingale value b/(a+b) within 1.2 percentage points over about 28k races per cell. The default Empirical model is well calibrated (ECE 0.004) but no better than knowing the base rate at each distance: it ignores time of day and volatility state. ES 5-min variance is 4.7× the daily mean at 09:30 ET and 0.20× at 23:30 ET. A seasonal, range-based, mean-reverting horizon-variance forecast (volatility time) fixes this: with a simple calibration it beats an oracle base-rate-by-distance table by 1.5% Brier skill at H=30 and 3.6% at H=60 on 5-min data. Vol-time ETA also ranks actual time-to-touch positively (rank correlation +0.11 to +0.22, versus −0.09 for constant σ). The cheapest robust gain is a volatility-state (or session) dimension in the existing sUp/sDn surface with partial pooling: it improved log-loss on every clean symbol at every horizon tested (5-min, 1-hour, 1-min) and stayed calibrated. Close-based events need the Broadie–Glasserman–Kou shift (0.5826·σ_bar); touches judged on highs and lows correctly do not. Finally, the displayed PoT is never graded: Trial has no pPot field, so there is no Brier score, reliability diagram or recalibration of the headline number. The 95% cap also sits inside the model (proximity scoring, baseline) instead of only on display.

concepts.name: One-barrier first passage (reflection principle) with drift
concepts.definition: X_t=μt+σW_t, barrier d>0, horizon h bars: P(touch)=Φ((μh−d)/(σ√h))+exp(2μd/σ²)Φ((−μh−d)/(σ√h)); driftless 2Φ(−d/(σ√h)) ('touch ≈ 2× finish-beyond'). In volatility time replace σ²h by the integrated forecast variance V: P=2Φ(−d/√V). Edge cases: d≤0→1; compute the exp term in log space.
concepts.dolRole: Core 'how likely within H' number for any target; also feeds proximity/reachability scoring.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Textbook result; verified against Monte Carlo (f_pot 0.3173 vs MC 0.3051 with expected discrete bias; 0.3613 vs 0.3600). Options practitioners use the 2×delta rule.
concepts.engineNotes: f_pot lines 434-444 correct, overflow-safe via f_expPhi 420-429; but caps at 0.95 internally and is fed noisy σ/μ (see drift, σ concepts).

concepts.name: Two-barrier race (finite horizon) and martingale invariance
concepts.definition: P(+a before −b)=(1−e^{kb})/(e^{−ka}−e^{kb}), k=2μ/σ²; driftless b/(a+b), which holds for ANY continuous martingale (optional stopping) regardless of stochastic vol or seasonality. Finite-horizon via eigen-expansion: P_h=P_∞−e^{μa/σ²}Σ(σ²nπ/L²)(−1)^{n+1}sin(nπb/L)e^{−(λ_n+ν)h}/(λ_n+ν), λ_n=σ²n²π²/(2L²), ν=μ²/(2σ²).
concepts.dolRole: Which liquidity is taken next (nearest BSL vs SSL), and target-before-invalidation (WIN≤H).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory strong; our data: 6 futures, 5-min, ~28k decided races per (a,b) cell, empirical P(up first) within 0.4-1.2 pp of b/(a+b) (e.g., a=1,b=2: 0.658 vs 0.667).
concepts.engineNotes: f_race 447-462 and f_raceH 466-482 mathematically correct (MC-verified), but f_invalidation 1343-1364 injects the noisy drift potMu; no nearest-BSL-vs-SSL 'next pool' race exists; f_raceAdj 1367 ledger shift is good.

concepts.name: Discrete-monitoring continuity correction (Broadie–Glasserman–Kou)
concepts.definition: When a barrier is checked only at discrete times Δt apart (e.g. bar closes), use the continuous formula with the barrier shifted away by β·σ·√Δt, β=−ζ(1/2)/√(2π)≈0.5826. For bars: d_close=d+0.5826·σ_bar. Not applicable to high/low touches (bar extremes ≈ continuous path max).
concepts.dolRole: Probability that price CLOSES beyond a pool (body-close break/BOS, iFVG inversion) vs merely wicks it (sweep).
concepts.evidenceNotes: BGK 1997 Math. Finance; our data 5-min H=30: realised close-beyond 0.453, continuous formula mean 0.583, BGK 0.517; log-loss 0.626→0.586; same on 1-hour (0.558→0.507) and 1-min (0.618→0.583).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent for touches (touched() at 623-625 uses highs/lows); no close-beyond probability anywhere (needed for sweep-vs-break and body-close bias logic).

concepts.name: Time-to-touch distribution (ETA)
concepts.definition: Driftless: P(T≤t)=2Φ(−d/(σ√t)) (Lévy); with drift inverse Gaussian f(t)=d/(σ√(2πt³))exp(−(d−μt)²/(2σ²t)). Conditional median given touch within H solves F(t)=½F(H); in vol time use cumulative forecast variance V(t).
concepts.dolRole: WHEN the target is likely to be reached (bars and clock time; 'this session' probability).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Our 5-min test (H=60, 6 symbols, 15-24k hits per k): rank corr(actual T, predicted median) const-σ −0.09 vs vol-time +0.11/+0.16/+0.22 at 1/2/3 ATR; coverage of median 0.45-0.47 (vol-time).
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2116-2126: median bars-to-hit of past DOL hits within ±0.5 ATR of current distance; ignores time of day / vol state; no quantiles or clock time.

concepts.name: Range-based volatility estimators (Parkinson, Garman–Klass, Rogers–Satchell, Yang–Zhang)
concepts.definition: Per-bar variance proxies: Parkinson (H−L)²/(4ln2); GK ½(H−L)²−(2ln2−1)(C−O)²; RS (H−C)(H−O)+(L−C)(L−O); YZ σ_o²+kσ_c²+(1−k)σ_RS², k=0.34/(1.34+(n+1)/(n−1)). Add gap² (O−C₋₁)² for opens/rolls; winsorise roll gaps.
concepts.dolRole: Lower-noise σ for PoT and proximity scoring; faster adaptation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Efficiency vs close-to-close: Parkinson ≈5.2, GK ≈7.4, RS ≈6, YZ up to 14 (7.2-8.2 at n=20); Alizadeh-Brandt-Diebold 2002. Our data: alone (no seasonality) only small gains (p_yz LL 0.5875 vs 0.5891 at H=30) — the big gain needs vol time.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig=ta.stdev(chg, potLen=50) line 916 (close-to-close, equal weights).

concepts.name: Intraday volatility seasonality and volatility time
concepts.definition: Multiplicative model r_{t,n}=σ_t·s_n·Z/√N (Andersen–Bollerslev). Estimate s²_b by bucket means of variance proxy / slow level (15-min UTC buckets), then horizon variance V_H=Σ_{j=1..H} s²_{b(t+j)}·[L_slow+φ^j(L_fast−L_slow)]; PoT=2Φ(−d/√V_H).
concepts.dolRole: The same distance is far more reachable when the next H bars include the NY open than overnight; drives both PoT and ETA.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Andersen-Bollerslev 1997 S&P futures |r| 0.095%→0.055%→0.105% U-shape; crypto peak 16-17 UTC. Ours: ES 5-min 09:30 ET bucket 4.67× daily mean, 23:30 ET 0.20× (24× variance range). Vol-time analytic (calibrated) BSS vs oracle-by-distance +1.5% (H=30), +3.6% (H=60) on 5-min; no gain at 30-minute clock horizon (1-min H=30).
concepts.engineNotes: Killzone multipliers affect scoring only (README); PoT horizon is a flat H bars with a 50-bar σ.

concepts.name: Volatility clustering forecast (EWMA / GARCH-lite / HAR)
concepts.definition: EWMA σ²_t=λσ²_{t−1}+(1−λ)r²; GARCH term structure E[σ²_{t+j}]=L̄+φ^j(σ²_t−L̄); HAR cascade of daily/weekly/monthly RV.
concepts.dolRole: Forecasts how volatile the next H bars will be, not the last 50.
concepts.evidenceNotes: RiskMetrics λ=0.94 daily/0.97 monthly; Corsi 2009. Ours: deseasonalised log-range ACF ES 0.63 (lag 1), 0.27 (1 day). Ablation: seasonal-only flat level (p_cl) LL 0.6003 vs seasonal×clustering 0.5659 at H=30.
concepts.engineNotes: Flat ta.stdev window, line 916; atrSlow exists (875) but only for ejection.

concepts.name: Drift estimation and short-horizon predictability
concepts.definition: μ̂ = mean of n bar changes has SE σ/√n; in an H-bar first-passage formula with weight w it shifts the standardised barrier by w√(H/n)·Z (0.39·Z at H=30, n=50, w=0.5). Shrink (positive-part James–Stein) or set 0.
concepts.dolRole: Directional tilt of PoT/race; if noisy it randomly favours one side and double-counts the Draw pillar.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018: best intraday predictor R²=1.6%. Ours: engine analytic LL 0.6115 vs no-drift 0.5891 (5-min H=30), 0.6220 vs 0.5776 (H=60), 1-hour 0.6154 vs 0.5835, 1-min 0.5848 vs 0.5613; driftless-RW simulation: drift raises LL 5.4%, slope 0.83.
concepts.engineNotes: potMu=ta.sma(chg,50)*driftW (917, driftW default 0.5 at 185) used in evaluate 665, f_potModel 1303/2067/2184, f_invalidation 1361-1363.

concepts.name: Fat tails / stochastic-vol mixture / jumps
concepts.definition: PoT(d)=E_σ[2Φ(−d/(σ√h))]: a vol mixture lowers near-level and raises far-level touch probability vs Gaussian; jumps add overshoot (Kou–Wang double-exponential). Standardising distance by horizon σ collapses empirical curves.
concepts.dolRole: Correct probabilities for far targets (HTF objective, PW levels) and near ones.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Perelló et al. 2011 (6 futures, tick): Wiener under-estimates x≳σ_t, over-estimates x≲0.1σ_t. Ours: analytic at k=6 ATR 0.118 vs realised 0.150 (5-min H=30); Osler 2005 stop cascades.
concepts.engineNotes: Empirical surface captures it inside the grid (≤15 ATR); beyond-grid fallback (1292-1293) uses the Gaussian analytic.

concepts.name: Variance ratio (trend vs mean reversion)
concepts.definition: VR(q)=Var(q-bar return)/(q·Var(1-bar)) ≈1+2Σ(1−j/q)ρ_j; VR<1 mean-reverting (far levels less reachable than √H implies).
concepts.dolRole: Scales reachability of far levels per symbol/regime.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Lo-MacKinlay 1988. Ours at q=30-60: ES 0.96, NQ 1.02-1.05, CL 1.00-1.03, GC 0.84-0.87, YM 0.91-0.94 → √H scaling acceptable; residual absorbed by empirical surface.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed explicitly once the empirical surface is kept; no engine change proposed.

concepts.name: Empirical excursion surface (MFE/MAE) with overlap-aware sample size
concepts.definition: For each closed H-bar window, up/down max excursion from the start close normalised by ATR, bucketed (0.25 ATR); survival counts give empirical PoT; overlapping windows' effective n = n/VIF.
concepts.dolRole: Symbol-specific, regime-specific reach probabilities and reach bands.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ours: engine-style surface ECE 0.004, slope 0.99 (well calibrated). Measured VIF/H 0.21-0.83 (ES/CL 5-min), so the engine's 0.6H divisor is reasonable.
concepts.engineNotes: sUp/sDn 1059-1062, f_bump/f_surv/f_empPoT 1265-1300, update 1526-1532; conditions only on HTF regime.

concepts.name: Volatility-state / session conditioning with partial pooling
concepts.definition: Split surface rows by vs=tercile of q=√V_H/(ATR√H) (or 6×4h UTC sessions); shrink cell to parent: p=(nE_c p_c+m p_parent)/(nE_c+m), m=30.
concepts.dolRole: Adds 'when' resolution to PoT at fixed ATR distance while keeping calibration.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ours: LL 0.5015→0.4962 (H=12), 0.5636→0.5538 (H=30), 0.5614→0.5478 (H=60), all 6 symbols better, ECE ≤0.004; 1-hour H=12 0.5268→0.5086 (all 6); 1-min H=30 0.5517→0.5484 (all 3). Session split gets most of the gain; ATR14/ATR200 alone almost none. Efron-Morris 1975 shrinkage.
concepts.engineNotes: Only the 3-row HTF-regime split exists (f_empPoT 1284-1300).

concepts.name: Bayesian blending of model and empirical rates
concepts.definition: Beta-binomial posterior mean (k+m·p0)/(n+m) with the analytic model as prior of strength m pseudo-observations; nEff=n/(0.6H).
concepts.dolRole: Stable PoT during warm-up and in sparse cells.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard conjugate Bayes; also used by Garzarelli et al. and Chung-Bellotti for bounce probabilities.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potModel 1303-1311 (priorM=30); correct form, but the prior carries the drift noise and the cap.

concepts.name: Calibration and proper scoring of displayed PoT
concepts.definition: Brier, log-loss, Murphy decomposition REL−RES+UNC, 10-bin reliability/ECE, calibration slope; recalibrate with Platt σ(a+b·logit p) (online SGD) or isotonic (≥1000 samples); skill vs random-level baseline.
concepts.dolRole: Makes the headline PoT trustworthy and folds the engine's measured edge (pools vs random levels) into it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005; Murphy 1973; ours: Platt on vol-time analytic slope 0.89→1.01, ECE 0.062→0.024, LL 0.5659→0.5557 (5-min H=30).
concepts.engineNotes: Trial (375-391) has pBase and pRace but no pPot; f_book 1461-1499 never grades the displayed PoT. f_raceAdj does this for races only.

concepts.name: Liquidity levels vs random levels (stop clustering, S/R memory)
concepts.definition: Stops/take-profits cluster at salient levels; take-profits reverse trends and stops accelerate them once crossed; bounce probability rises with prior bounces and decays with time.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why real pools deviate from random-level PoT; the ledger edge measures the deviation that should calibrate PoT and race.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003 JF (~9,700 orders), Osler 2005 JIMF; Garzarelli et al. 2014 p(bounce)>0.5 vs shuffled ≈0.5; Chung-Bellotti 2021: 1-bounce levels decay to 0.5 at ~350-minute windows, 4-bounce at ~900.
concepts.engineNotes: Ledger EDGE vs distance-matched random level exists (2375-2389, f_potBase 1314) but is not fed back into displayed PoT.

concepts.name: 95% probability cap
concepts.definition: Product spec caps the displayed PoT at 95%; mathematically a near level's true PoT approaches 1 and should not be capped inside models or baselines.
concepts.dolRole: Display convention only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Spec convention, not an empirical claim.
concepts.engineNotes: Cap inside f_pot 444 and f_potModel 1310; evaluate divides by 0.95 (665); f_potBase 1314-1322 blends a capped analytic → baseline biased low for very near targets.

proposals.title: Remove the raw 50-bar drift from every analytic probability
proposals.rationale: potMu=0.5·SMA(Δclose,50) is mostly noise (shifts the standardised barrier by ≈0.39 sd at defaults), double-counts the Draw pillar, and is the largest single source of over-confidence.
proposals.spec: Set μ=0 in f_pot calls in evaluate (line 665), f_potModel (1304, called at 2067/2184), f_invalidation (1361-1363), so f_raceH races reduce to the martingale value b/(a+b) with horizon truncation. Change driftW default to 0.0 (line 185) or remove it; if kept, use positive-part James–Stein shrinkage μ_eff=μ̂·max(0,1−(σ²/n)/μ̂²). Directional information continues to flow through the HTF-regime rows of the empirical surface, the Draw pillar, and the ledger (f_raceAdj; QPOT-04). Measured on 6 CME futures: log-loss 0.6115→0.5891 (5-min H=30), 0.6220→0.5776 (H=60), 1-hour 0.6154→0.5835, 1-min 0.5848→0.5613; races match b/(a+b) within 1.2 pp.
proposals.risk: Slightly slower reaction in persistent trends; mitigated by the regime-split surface and Draw pillar. Changes which near-equidistant level wins the proximity pillar.

proposals.title: Volatility-time horizon variance V_H (range-based, seasonal, mean-reverting) for analytic PoT and reachability
proposals.rationale: Volatility varies about 24× in variance across the day on ES; a flat 50-bar σ cannot tell 'H bars into the NY open' from 'H bars overnight'. A vol-time forecast gives the analytic model real resolution and calibration.
proposals.spec: Variance proxy x=max(0,½(H−L)²−(2ln2−1)(C−O)²)+(O−C[1])², winsorised at 25× slow level. Buckets binSec=max(900,chartS), NBK=86400/binSec, seasonOn=timeframe.isintraday and chartS<14400, b=(hour(time,'UTC')*3600+minute(time,'UTC')*60)/binSec. On confirmed bars: slow EWMA R (half-life min(2000, 5 days of bars)); sSum[b]+=x/R, sCnt[b]+=1; s²_b=bucket mean / mean of seen bucket means (maintained incrementally). Deseasonalised Lf=EWMA(x/s²_b, hl 30), Ls=EWMA(x/s²_b, hlS), φ=0.5^(1/30). Walk future bars j=1..H on the clock (time+j*chartS*1000), skip buckets with sCnt=0, cumulative V(j)=Σ s²_b(j)(Ls+φ^j(Lf−Ls)) into var array vCum (also used by QPOT-05/07). Analytic PoT=f_erfc(d/sqrt(2·V_H)); proximity reach uses it uncapped. Keep mutable scalars in var arrays (functions cannot := globals). Place series after line 917, state after 1080, helpers in STATE HELPERS, update in engine step 0 (~1524). Input 'PoT Volatility' [Vol-time, Close-to-close]. Measured: analytic LL 0.6115→0.5659 (5-min H=30) uncalibrated; with Platt +1.5% BSS (H=30) and +3.6% (H=60) vs an oracle base-rate-by-distance; 1-hour H=12 +2.7%.
proposals.risk: Gains need H×timeframe ≥ ~1-2 h (no gain at a 30-minute horizon on 1-min); weekend/holiday buckets approximated; roll gaps must be winsorised (GC 1h data broke it). Loop ≤ H+2·NBK·binSec/chartS per confirmed bar, well within 500 ms.

proposals.title: Add a volatility-state (or session) dimension to the empirical surface with partial pooling
proposals.rationale: The default Empirical PoT is calibrated but no better than knowing distance; conditioning on volatility state/time of day gives resolution while keeping calibration. It was the only variant that never lost to the engine on a clean symbol.
proposals.spec: vs∈{0,1,2} from ln q, q=√V_H/(atr√H), using EWMA mean m and sd s of ln q (half-life ~2000): vs=lnq<m−0.43s?0:lnq>m+0.43s?2:1 (O(1) terciles). Without QPOT-02, use vs = 4-hour UTC session bucket (6 states). Resize sUp/sDn to 9*NB1 (regime*3+vs); bump with vsSer[H] next to htfBias[H] (1530-1532). In f_empPoT compute cell p_c and parent p_p (sum of the regime's 3 rows) and return p=(nE_c·p_c+30·p_p)/(nE_c+30), nE=n/(0.6H), then the existing analytic blend; apply the nMin gate to the parent; f_reachD reads the parent. Measured mean LL: 0.5015→0.4962 (H=12), 0.5636→0.5538 (H=30), 0.5614→0.5478 (H=60) on 5-min, all 6 symbols better, ECE ≤0.004; 1-hour H=12 0.5268→0.5086; 1-min H=30 0.5517→0.5484.
proposals.risk: Sparser cells warm up slower (pooling handles it); memory 1,098 ints per side, negligible.

proposals.title: Grade and recalibrate the displayed PoT in the accuracy ledger
proposals.rationale: The headline PoT is never checked against outcomes, and the engine's measured edge (selected pools vs random levels) never reaches the number the trader sees. Calibration is directly measurable by the ledger.
proposals.spec: Add float pPot to Trial (375-391) and set it in f_openTrial (1426) to the PoT shown at that bar close. In f_book (1461) accumulate Σ(p−y)², Σ log-loss and 10 reliability bins (var arrays rbN/rbP/rbY) per family and ALL; Brier skill vs pBase = 1−Σ(p−y)²/Σ(pBase−y)². Online Platt in var array calW=[a,b,n]: x=logit(p), z=σ(a+b·x), η=1/(30+n), a+=η(y−z), b+=η(y−z)x, clamp a∈[−1.5,1.5], b∈[0.5,1.5], apply when n≥30 (or intercept-only δ=logit((K+20P̄)/(N+20))−logit(P̄) like f_raceAdj). Show 'PoT 64% (cal 58%)' and a Terminal row 'PoT CAL · Brier .201 vs base .215 · slope 0.92 · n 140'; Full view adds a reliability strip. Measured: Platt on vol-time analytic slope 0.89→1.01, ECE 0.062→0.024, LL 0.5659→0.5557.
proposals.risk: Overlapping trials make the effective n small; use a conservative step size and the cluster blocks already in cluSt. The calibration map can drift if the regime changes; Robbins–Monro steps keep it adaptive.

proposals.title: Volatility-time ETA quantiles and 'PoT this session'
proposals.rationale: Traders need WHEN as well as IF; the current ETA ignores time of day and is close to uninformative. Vol-time ETA ranks the actual time-to-touch positively.
proposals.spec: Using vCum from QPOT-02: F(j)=2Φ(−d/√V(j)); ETA50/ETA80 = first j with F(j)/F(H) ≥ 0.5/0.8 (binary search over H floats, μ=0). Clock label time+ETA·chartS·1000 (skipping closed buckets as in the path walk). 'PoT this session' = 2Φ(−d/√V_eod), V to the session end (17:00 ET CME, 00:00 UTC crypto, input-selectable). Replace the etaHit block (2116-2126) on the HUD: 'ETA ~14b (≈10:35) · today 78%'. Ledger: for hits store T and ETA50; show coverage share(T≤ETA50) (target 50%). Measured rank corr(T, ETA): const-σ −0.09 vs vol-time +0.11/+0.16/+0.22 at 1/2/3 ATR; coverage 0.45-0.47.
proposals.risk: Holiday/weekend schedules approximate; label as approximate. Cost shares the QPOT-02 loop.

proposals.title: 'Next liquidity taken' race readout (nearest BSL vs nearest SSL) with ledger tilt
proposals.rationale: The literal forecast 'which pool is taken next' is a two-barrier race whose driftless value b/(a+b) is model-robust; ledger deviations from it measure genuine liquidity magnetism for the symbol.
proposals.spec: At bar close find the nearest unswept kind≤1 pool above (distance a) and below (b). p_up=f_raceH(a,b,σ_eff,0,H)/(f_raceH(a,b,σ_eff,0,H)+f_raceH(b,a,σ_eff,0,H)), σ_eff=√(V_H/H) (≈b/(a+b)). Ledger: var array nxSt=[n, upWins, Σp]; open one record per new pair and resolve when either pool is swept; logit shift as in f_raceAdj. Terminal row 'NEXT ▲ BSL 62% · ▼ SSL 38%'; optional alert when one side ≥ 70%. Can also enter selection as a tie-breaker between draw-side candidates. Measured: random-level races within 1.2 pp of b/(a+b) (≈28k per cell).
proposals.risk: For pools very close to price the race resolves in 1-2 bars (show only when both a,b ≥ minDistATR). Adds one more panel row.

proposals.title: BGK close-beyond probability: show sweep vs break
proposals.rationale: Liquidity raids are wick events and breaks are close events; the continuous formula over-states close-beyond by ~13 pp, while the BGK shift is a closed-form fix.
proposals.spec: P_close(d)=2Φ(−(d+0.5826·σ_bar)/√V_H), σ_bar=√(V_H/H) (or the current bucket's seasonal σ). For liquidity targets show 'PoT 71% · close-thru 52%'; P_touch−P_close bounds the chance of a wick-only raid within H. Optionally use it as the expectation for body-close breaks in the bias table. Calibrate with the QPOT-04 Platt layer. Measured: 5-min H=30 realised 0.453, continuous 0.583, BGK 0.517, LL 0.626→0.586; 1-hour H=12 0.558→0.507; 1-min 0.618→0.583.
proposals.risk: Inherits the level bias of the vol-time model unless calibrated; extra HUD text.

proposals.title: Adaptive stacked PoT (online logistic of empirical surface + vol-time analytic)
proposals.rationale: The best log-loss in the 5-min test came from letting the data weight the empirical surface and the vol-time model per symbol.
proposals.spec: Every confirmed bar store [logit p_emp, logit p_vt] for 7 distances × 2 sides in a ring buffer of H+1 rows (≤451×28 floats); when the window from t−H resolves, take an AdaGrad step on w=[w0,w1,w2]; after ≥3,000 samples show PoT=σ(w0+w1·logit p_emp+w2·logit p_vt), otherwise the QPOT-03 surface. Input 'PoT Model' gains 'Adaptive'. Measured: LL 0.5503 (H=30) / 0.5412 (H=60) vs engine 0.5639/0.5617 (BSS +2.5%/+4.1%); learned vol-time weight 0.66-0.86 on equity indices, 0.3-0.4 on CL/GC; worse than the plain surface on data with roll gaps.
proposals.risk: Fragile on corrupted data and during warm-up; extra memory and per-bar work; keep it optional behind QPOT-03.

proposals.title: Consistency fixes: display-only 95% cap, live remaining time, fat-tail fallback, gap winsorising
proposals.rationale: The cap leaks into scoring and the EDGE baseline; the live bar uses a full H; beyond-grid levels fall back to a Gaussian that under-states far touches.
proposals.spec: Return uncapped values from f_pot/f_potModel; apply math.min(0.95, p) only for activePoT display, HUD, alert text and the minPoT filter (2065-2067, 2240); drop the /0.95 in evaluate (665); f_potBase (1314-1322) uncapped so near-target baselines are unbiased. On realtime bars use horizon H−1+(time_close−timenow)/(time_close−time) for live PoT. Beyond the grid (1292-1293) use a two-component variance mixture p=½·2Φ(−d/(0.8σ_H))+½·2Φ(−d/(1.17σ_H)) (same mean variance, kurtosis ≈3.4) or widen bStep. Winsorise the variance proxy at 25× slow level. Evidence: Perelló et al. 2011 (Wiener under-estimates far targets); ours k=6 ATR 0.118 analytic vs 0.150 realised.
proposals.risk: Minimal; display unchanged except more accurate near-target scoring.

result.summary: The academic evidence says price levels act as small barriers that fade over hours. They are not magnets. Osler (2000) found published FX support and resistance levels stopped trends 60.8% of the time, against 56.2% for arbitrary levels, and kept working for at least 5 days. Garzarelli et al. (2014) and Chung & Bellotti (2021) found that a level that has held more often is more likely to hold again, and that this decays within hours. My replication on 1-minute futures (6 symbols, about 80k approaches, against a shuffled no-memory series) confirms it. On arrival, a level holds 4.9 to 7.5 points more often than a memory-free level, rising with the number of prior holds, in all 6 symbols. It is strongest when the last hold was under 15 minutes ago (+7 to +9 points). After about 4 hours the sign flips: levels price comes back to break more often than chance (-3 to -5.5 points in all 6 symbols). On 1-hour bars the effect depends on the asset (gold strongly positive, ES and NQ negative), so no fixed prior is justified there. In the engine's own terms (strict trade-through within 30 bars, against a random level at the same distance), pools are slightly sticky at -2 points. The engine's test count adds nothing (3 or more tests: -7 points), and pools untouched for more than 12 hours are reached less often (-7.5 points). That contradicts both the monotone test bonus (line 682) and the freshness ramp (line 671). The most robust new finding is path crowding. A target is reached less often for each unswept same-side pool between price and it: -1.2, -1.5, -3.5 and -6.1 points on 1-minute bars, and -0.1, -6, -10 and -29 points on 1-hour bars. This holds inside the engine's 0.75-ATR stack window too, so the engine's preference for the outermost pool (inner pools x0.70 and a stack bonus) points the wrong way. Stop cascades after a pool is swept are small at bar resolution (+1.1 points still beyond the level versus arbitrary levels), and larger for 4-12 hour old pools (+5.1 points at 120 minutes), in line with Osler's 15-minute to 2-hour cascade window. Round numbers, prior-day highs and lows, and the timing of daily highs and lows are mostly geometry or already covered by sibling studies. The 52-week high and all-time high are the best-documented anchors in finance but are missing from the engine; their value at intraday horizons is untested.

concepts.name: Support/resistance barrier: bounce vs penetration on arrival
concepts.definition: Osler 2000: a level is hit when the bid or ask comes within 0.01% of it; a bounce means the rate is still on the near side 15 minutes later; the control is 10,000 sets of arbitrary levels. Garzarelli 2014: price sampled every tau = 45-180 s; the stripe width is the mean absolute increment at scale tau; a bounce means price enters the stripe and leaves on the same side; b_prev is the number of prior bounces. Chung & Bellotti 2021: rolling-window max/min, zone width gamma = mean absolute change, bounces = half the boundary crossings. Engine terms: pivotLen-5 pool, stripe 0.35 ATR, penetration = strict trade-through.
concepts.dolRole: Gives P(through | arrival) for a liquidity pool. Under the engine's strict sweep rule a bounce at the level is a missed target, so this conditions the last-mile PoT and the race against the opposing pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2000: published levels 60.8% vs arbitrary 56.2% (DEM 54.9 arbitrary vs 56.6-62.0 for the firms; JPY 57.3 vs 60.7-66.5; GBP 56.3 vs 58.8-63.0), effective for at least 5 business days, firms' strength ratings useless (https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/epr/00v06n2/0007osle.html). Garzarelli 2014: p(b|b_prev) above 0.5 and rising, p<0.0001 at 45-90 s, not significant at 180 s (https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.5197). This study, 1-minute futures: excess bounce +4.9/+6.8/+6.8/+7.3/+7.5 pp for b_prev 1-5+, z 7-19, positive in 6 of 6 symbols.
concepts.engineNotes: PoT (f_pot 434-445, f_empPoT 1284-1301, f_potModel 1303-1311, live readout 2067) depends only on distance and volatility and does not know the level's history. As price reaches the level it tends to 95%, even for a pool that has just held three times.

concepts.name: Level memory decay (macro/micro) and sign flip for stale levels
concepts.definition: Bounce probability in excess of a no-memory null, as a function of time since the last bounce. Fit from this study's 1-minute data: E(b,dt) in pp = (7 + 0.75*min(b-1,4))*exp(-dt/400) - 8*(1 - exp(-dt/400)), with dt in bars on a 1-minute chart. The zero crossing is at about 260 bars (about 4 hours).
concepts.dolRole: Tells the engine whether a nearby pool will hold (fresh) or break (stale) when price arrives, and over what time window a level's history still matters.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Chung & Bellotti: EURUSD 1-bounce level decays to 0.5 at about a 350-minute window and a 4-bounce level at about 900 minutes; BRENT 1-bounce falls below 0.5 beyond about 300 minutes; micro-decay logit slope -0.0018/min at b_prev=4 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.07410). This study: excess +7 to +9 pp under 15 minutes, +3 to +5 pp at 1-4 h, -3.0 to -5.5 pp at 4 h or more in all 6 symbols, -7 to -15 pp beyond 12 h for multi-bounce levels. On 1-hour bars the effect is asset-specific (GC +17.7 pp, ES -5.9, NQ -7.3).
concepts.engineNotes: Freshness (671) ramps up as pools 'mature', then decays with a 600-bar half-life measured in bars; no bounce timestamp is kept. lastTest is only used for 3-bar spacing (650-658).

concepts.name: Test count (touches without a take)
concepts.definition: Engine rule: a bar within 0.30 ATR of the pool that does not trade through it, at least 3 bars after the previous test (track 650-658). Academic equivalent: b_prev, the number of prior bounces.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore holds that tests either 'add resting stops' (more attractive) or 'weaken the level'. The evidence supports neither: tests predict a short-term bounce, not more frequent sweeps.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study (engine terms, H=30, 1-minute): reach edge for 0/1/2/3+ tests is -2.0/-1.9/-2.1/-7.3 ± 3.6 pp. Siblings found no effect on 1H/daily bars (WYK section 2.4). No quantitative support was found for 'each touch weakens the level'; a vendor PDF claims hold rates stay flat (75/73/76/79%) and is unverified.
concepts.engineNotes: Density x includes +0.35*min(tests,6) (682), a monotone bonus with no support; exact touches are skipped because of gap>0 (654).

concepts.name: Path crowding (unswept same-side pools between price and target)
concepts.definition: nIn = number of live, unswept same-side liquidity pools strictly between price and the target's near edge, with a 0.1-ATR margin. The quantity tracked is the target's reach within H, relative to a random level at the same distance.
concepts.dolRole: A strong predictor of whether a far target is reached: every intermediate pool is a small barrier and/or a sign of a counter-trend staircase. It also bears directly on which pool of a stack to choose.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: on 1-minute bars nIn 0/1/2/3+ gives -1.2/-1.5/-3.5/-6.1 pp (n about 74k); on 1-hour bars -0.1/-6.0/-10.3/-29.3 pp. Inside the engine's 0.75-ATR stack window the outer pool is -2.0/-5.2 pp (1m) and -6.1/-20.6 pp (1H). Consistent with S/R levels coinciding with order-book depth (Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004) and interrupting trends (Osler 2000). Likely confounded with trend.
concepts.engineNotes: f_stackSide (1230-1251) marks inner pools; evaluate gives inner x0.70 (684-685) and the outer pool +0.45*stack (682), the opposite of the evidence. Nothing counts pools on the path; the only path cost is volume-profile based (1945-1947).

concepts.name: Stop-loss clustering and post-break cascades
concepts.definition: Stops sit just beyond levels (Osler 2003: stop-buys 14.4% at 01-10 above a '00' vs 7.4% at 90-99) and take-profits sit at them (9.3% exactly at 00). After a cluster is crossed, the extra move vs an arbitrary crossing (MVCR - MVRV) is +0.27 to +2.35 hundredths of a percent over 15 minutes to 2 hours, and is gone or reversed at 1-2 days (Osler 2005).
concepts.dolRole: Says what happens after a pool is taken: whether the next pool in the same direction becomes more likely (continuation), and for how long.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003/2005 are strong for FX round numbers (sibling ict_liq E1/E2). This study: after a pivot's trade-through, price is still beyond the level +1.1 pp more often than after an arbitrary grid-level cross at 30 and 120 minutes (z about 2); median 120-minute return +0.25 vs -0.01 ATR; pools aged 4-12 h show +5.1 pp (z 3.3).
concepts.engineNotes: The raid outcome feeds liqEvt (1580-1582), weighted by tier only, with a decay in bars (liqHL 24 bars, 159/1535): 24 minutes on a 1m chart but 4 days on 4H, whereas the evidence points to 15 minutes to 2 hours and to older pools.

concepts.name: Round-number psychological barriers
concepts.definition: Barrier tests on M-digit frequency and on shifts in the conditional mean and variance near round numbers (Donaldson & Kim 1993; De Grauwe & Decupere 1992; Aggarwal & Lucey 2007). Order-flow imbalance at round numbers (Bhattacharya, Holden & Jacobsen 2012). Orders placed one tick ahead of clusters (Lallouache & Abergel 2014).
concepts.dolRole: Round numbers slow price on approach and can trigger acceleration once crossed; a sweep wick tends to stop short of a round number just beyond a pool. They do not attract price.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Barriers found in USD/JPY but weak in USD/DEM; gold yes, silver no. Jung & Lee 2026: round levels hold more resting liquidity but do not hold prices longer once depth is accounted for (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34787). Sibling bar-level tests: coarse rounds passed +3.3 pp more often once reached, mixed sign as magnets, sweep wicks pass a round just beyond a pool -4.2 pp less often.
concepts.engineNotes: No round-number logic. Siblings ICT-3 and OF-4 specify an evidence-calibrated version; no new proposal here.

concepts.name: 52-week high/low and all-time high anchoring
concepts.definition: Nearness = price / 52-week high (George & Hwang 2004). Crossing the 52-week extreme (Huddart et al. 2009). Approach and breakthrough effects on implied volatility (Driessen et al. 2013). Recency of the 52-week high (Bhootra & Hur 2013). Index at the 52-week high vs the historical high (Li & Yu 2012).
concepts.dolRole: Widely watched extremes act as barriers on approach (volatility compresses) and as continuation triggers once broken. They are natural higher-timeframe objectives in Swing mode.
concepts.evidenceNotes: George & Hwang: winner-minus-loser 0.45%/month (t=2.00) to 1.23%/month (t=7.06). Li & Yu: 52-week high predicts higher returns, historical high lower. Huddart: volume spikes when the extreme is crossed. Driessen: implied volatility falls on approach and rises by more than 1 vol point after a breakthrough (2011 working-paper figure). Bhootra & Hur: about 0.70%/month for recency. All at daily to monthly horizons, mostly in stocks; intraday reach is untested.
concepts.engineNotes: Registry sources are PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL, sessions and HTF/STF pivots only (1778-1822, f_tierW 506). There is no 52-week, all-time or N-day anchor; siblings ICTPD-5 and TIME-8 cover 20/40/60-day extremes.

concepts.name: Prior-high/low (trading-range) breakouts
concepts.definition: Trading-range break: buy when price exceeds the max of the previous n = 50/150/200 days (0% or 1% band), sell on a break of the min (Brock, Lakonishok & LeBaron 1992). Intraday opening-range breakout beyond the opening range (Holmberg et al. 2013).
concepts.dolRole: Breaking a prior extreme in the direction of the higher-timeframe trend is the continuation case. Breakout edges decay once published and rarely survive costs intraday, so a breakout alone is not a target signal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brock et al.: significant on the DJIA 1897-1986; Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999: no out-of-sample advantage after 1986. MNQ 2021-25 walk-forward: no OHLCV family passes; ORB long T=0.88 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04004). ICT AMD on NQ: no information beyond the daily trend regime, right 62-71% with the trend and 25-30% against (https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35887).
concepts.engineNotes: PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL and session highs and lows are registry pools (944-961, 1797-1822) and the draw vector D uses HTF structure (1891-1899). The tier ranks are hand-set; Osler found published strength ratings useless, so learned weights are preferable.

concepts.name: Trend vs reversion timescales
concepts.definition: Safari & Schmidhuber 2025: markets mean-revert below about 30 minutes; weak trends persist from about 30 minutes (strongly from a few hours) to about 1-2 years; strong trends revert; trend persistence peaks at 3-12 months.
concepts.dolRole: Reconciles bounces at levels over minutes with breakouts that continue over hours. The draw vector should work on the trending scale and level stickiness on the reverting scale.
concepts.evidenceNotes: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.16772 (futures tick data plus centuries of daily and monthly data).
concepts.engineNotes: D uses HTF structure (correct scale); level stickiness is not modelled at all.

concepts.name: Conditional magnets (option pinning, price-limit magnet)
concepts.definition: On expiration dates optionable stocks close near strikes (Ni, Pearson & Poteshman 2005), and S&P 500 futures are pinned toward strikes (Golez & Jackwerth 2012). Prices accelerate toward a price limit (Cho et al. 2003).
concepts.dolRole: The only well-documented cases where a known level attracts price. Both require a hedging or limit mechanism, which generic support/resistance levels lack.
concepts.evidenceNotes: JFE 78(1) 2005; JFE 106(3) 2012; J. Empirical Finance 10, 2003.
concepts.engineNotes: Needs open-interest data that Pine does not provide; not proposed.

concepts.name: Timing of daily highs and lows
concepts.definition: Arcsine law: the time of a Brownian maximum on [0,T] has density 1/(pi*sqrt(t(T-t))). In business time (the intraday U-shaped volatility clock) the open gets even more mass. ES: the 09:30 15-minute segment holds 17.2% of highs of day vs a uniform 3.7%.
concepts.dolRole: Explains when extremes form (the timing of the draw). It is a variance-clock effect, not a property of levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sibling ict_time E4/E5/E15 and Andersen & Bollerslev 1997/98; the statistics are reproduced by an arcsine-plus-clock random walk.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed killzone affinities (f_kzAff 597-602) and killzone hysteresis; addressed by siblings TIME-1 and TIME-5.

concepts.name: Probability the previous day's high/low is exceeded
concepts.definition: For a driftless walk, P(H1 before L1) = (C - L1)/(H1 - L1). Empirical next-day rates: PDH taken 51.3% (S&P) and 55.4% (NASDAQ), PDL 44.6% and 46.5%, either 87-91%. Highs and lows are cointegrated and the range has long memory (Caporin et al. 2013).
concepts.dolRole: Base rates for PDH/PDL targets. The engine's volatility-scaled PoT already captures this geometry; there is no previous-day 'magnet'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sibling bias_dol section 2.1 (descriptive base rates); Caporin, Ranaldo & Santucci de Magistris, JBF 37(12) 2013.
concepts.engineNotes: PoT via f_potModel (1303); base rates are not displayed (sibling BIAS-3).

concepts.name: Level depth mechanism (why levels hold)
concepts.definition: Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004: support = the lowest bid reached at least twice (equal lows); support/resistance levels coincide with peaks in order-book depth; limit orders do not cluster there afterwards. Latent-liquidity models (Bouchaud et al.) give memory over several timescales.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why pools are sticky and why crowding on the path matters, while equal highs and lows are not bigger magnets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 84% of level-depth series cointegrated at 5%; significant for 49-73% of stocks (RFS 17(4) 2004).
concepts.engineNotes: Equal highs/lows merge to the outermost print (f_mergeAt 1111-1131) and get a density bonus of 0.9*eqCount (682); no stickiness or barrier term.

proposals.title: Path-crowding prior and a neutral stack rule
proposals.rationale: The most robust level effect found: a target's reach falls with each unswept same-side pool between price and it. It is monotone on 6 futures at both 1m and 1H, and present inside the engine's own 0.75-ATR stack window, where the engine currently prefers the outer pool and penalises the inner one.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_SCORE, after line 152): stackMode = input.string('Neutral', options ['Neutral','Outermost (ICT)']) and crowdW = input.float(1.0, 0-2). Add Level field int nIn. In step 16, after f_stackSide (1927), run an O(n^2) loop (n<=40, inCalc bars only): for each lv, count o.isLiquidity() and o.side==lv.side and o.id!=lv.id whose nearEdge lies strictly between close and lv.nearEdge() with a 0.1*atr margin. Prior ratios f_crowdPrior(k) = [1.00, 0.97, 0.92, 0.82] for nIn 0/1/2/3+. In STATE add var arrays crK and crE (size 4), filled in f_book from a new Trial field nIn0 (set in f_openTrial). f_crowdMult(k) = clamp(((crK[k] + 20*prior[k])/(crE[k] + 20)) / ((crK[0] + 20)/(crE[0] + 20)), 0.6, 1.1). In step 17, before evaluate: lv.mult *= pow(f_crowdMult(min(nIn,3)), crowdW). When stackMode=='Neutral', evaluate (682-685) drops 0.45*stack from density x and skips the inner x0.70; keep the STK tag. Live PoT: f_sigm(f_logit(pot) + log(f_crowdMult)), capped at 0.95. If ICT-1 probes exist, register nIn as a probe feature instead. Add a Full-view row 'CROWD 0/1/2/3+ edge'.
proposals.risk: Changes a visible ICT convention (the outer pool as the draw); mitigated by the option and a ledger A/B. Trend confounding (a counter-trend staircase) could double-count with the counter-draw penalty; learning the ratio from the ledger rather than fixing it limits this.

proposals.title: Two-stage ledger: ARRIVE vs THROUGH-given-ARRIVE, with a per-chart S/R memory table
proposals.rationale: Support/resistance research measures what happens at the level (Osler, Garzarelli, Chung & Bellotti), while the engine's ledger records only 'hit within H'. Splitting the two tells the trader whether the engine picks places price actually goes and whether those places break once reached. It also learns each chart's S/R memory, which is needed because the 1H evidence differs by asset.
proposals.spec: Input arrGam = 0.35 ATR (G_ACC); this equals the 0.5 x mean|dClose| stripe. Trial fields: bool arr, float gam, pArrB, pThrB, int mb (memory bucket 0-8 = (nB>=3?2:nB>=2?1:0)*3 + (dt<tau/4?0:dt<tau?1:2)). In f_openTrial (1426): pArrB = f_potBase(max(d - g, 0)) and pThrB = clamp(f_potBase(d)/pArrB, .01, .99); the ratio S(d)/S(d-g) from the existing empirical surface is the exact random-level (Osler arbitrary-level) baseline, so no new state is needed. In f_step (1434): arr := arr or high >= edge - gam (mirror for sell-side), set before hit. In f_book (1461): arN/arK/arE and, for arrived trials, thN/thK/thE[9]. Terminal Full view: 'ARRIVE 71% (rand 66%) · THRU|ARR 58% (rand 74%) · MEM cell edge'. Show cells only at n>=20. Feeds ACAD-3.
proposals.risk: Cells fill slowly because only the active DOL is graded (about 1 trial per H bars); ICT-1 candidate probes would speed this up 10-30x. No effect on selection.

proposals.title: S/R memory state per pool and a last-mile barrier PoT (replaces the wrong-signed test bonus)
proposals.rationale: At the level the live PoT tends to 95% whatever the level's history. On charts of 5m or less, a pool that has just held repeatedly is 7-11 pp less likely to break on this approach than a memory-free level, while a pool price returns to after a long absence is 3-8 pp more likely to break (6 of 6 symbols, consistent with Garzarelli and Chung & Bellotti). This also replaces the test bonus at 682 with quantified, recency-signed priors (amends SMC-3).
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_LIQ): memTau = 400 bars and memW = -1 (auto: 1 on charts of 5m or less, 0 above, because 1H evidence is asset-specific). Level fields: nB = 1 (the formation counts as the first bounce), lastB = bornBar, inZ = (distance <= arrGam*atr at creation), form = inZ. In track (650-658), with inside = high >= price - g: if not inZ and inside then inZ := true; else if inZ and not inside then { if not form: nB += 1 }; form := false; inZ := false; lastB := bar_index; tests := nB - 1. Pure helper f_memE(b, dt) = ((7 + 0.75*min(b-1,4))*exp(-dt/memTau) - 8*(1 - exp(-dt/memTau)))/100. In LIVE READOUTS only (2064-2068), because f_potModel and f_potBase are declared after evaluate and cannot be called from it: pMod = f_potModel(d); pArr = f_potModel(max(d-g,0)); pThrR = f_potBase(d)/f_potBase(max(d-g,0)); eMem = w*f_memE(nB, bar_index - lastB), blended with the ACAD-2 cell when n>=20; pThr = clamp(pThrR - eMem, .02, .99); activePoT = min(.95, f_sigm(f_logit(pMod) + pArr*(f_logit(pThr) - f_logit(pThrR)))). With eMem = 0 this equals today's readout. Remove 0.35*min(tests,6) from density at 682 and add nothing back, since reach within H barely depends on fresh memory. Tooltip shows 'B3 · last 12 bars · barrier -9 pp' or 'STALE · breaks +5 pp'; optional bar-close alert 'Approaching fresh barrier' when pArr > 0.8 and eMem > 0.06.
proposals.risk: The decay constant was calibrated on 1-minute bars (in bars); 5m-1H charts are untested, which is why the prior is off above 5m and the ledger learns. Per-bar cost is O(1) per pool.

proposals.title: Stale-pool raids: continuation weight by pool age, decay in clock time
proposals.rationale: Osler's stop cascades last 15 minutes to 2 hours, but liqHL = 24 bars means 24 minutes on a 1m chart and 4 days on 4H. Post-break continuation is concentrated in pools that were 4-12 h old (+5.1 pp still beyond the level at 120 minutes, z 3.3, median +1.1 ATR), while young pools show about zero. Complements ICTS-2 and BIAS-4, which fix the sign mapping.
proposals.spec: Input liqHLm = 90 minutes. Each confirmed bar: liqEvt *= pow(0.5, chartS/60/liqHLm) (chartS is defined at 307). Raid weight at 1580-1582: evt * tier * clamp(0.5 + 0.5*(bar_index - nz(lastB, bornBar))*chartS/60/240, 0.5, 1.5), so pools more than 4 h past their last interaction weigh up to 1.5x. Measure with the ICTS-1 draw-skill gate or the BIAS-1 side ledger (side hit-rate A/B).
proposals.risk: On 4H and above a 90-minute half-life makes the raid term almost vanish within a bar. That matches Osler (no effect at 1-2 days) but shifts the draw vector's weight to structure. Single data window.

proposals.title: 52-week and all-time extremes as anchor pools
proposals.rationale: The best-documented anchors in finance (George & Hwang, Li & Yu, Huddart et al., Driessen et al., Bhootra & Hur) are absent from the engine. They act as barriers on approach and continuation triggers when broken, and are natural HTF objectives in Swing mode. Siblings ICTPD-5 and TIME-8 cover 20/40/60-day extremes but not these.
proposals.spec: One extra request: [h52, l52, ath, atl] = request.security(syminfo.tickerid, f_tfSafe('D'), [ta.highest(high,252)[1], ta.lowest(low,252)[1], ta.max(high)[1], ta.min(low)[1]], lookahead = barmerge.lookahead_on); ta.max is documented in reference/ta.md:973-978 as the all-time high from the chart start, and [1] with lookahead_on does not repaint. Use 365 sessions for crypto. New src codes 8 (52W) and 9 (ATH/ATL), with f_tierW 0.95/1.0 and names '52W H/L', 'ATH', 'ATL'. Push with f_pushExt when f_changed(h52) and so on, anchored by f_anchorScan or else bar_index - anchorMax. The registry keeps them until raided and the HTF objective picks them up. Optional and ledger-gated: within 1 ATR scale potSig by 0.9 (approach compression); after a close beyond, add +0.2 to D on that side, decaying with liqHL. Measure via the family edge for src>=8.
proposals.risk: Low: on intraday charts these levels usually sit outside maxATR and stay dormant. The intraday value is unproven (the evidence is daily to monthly, mostly stocks).

result.summary: I tested trend, range and compression regimes on 23 series (six CME futures at 5m/15m/1H, NQ/GC/EURUSD hourly, S&P/NASDAQ/GOOG daily). Each test also ran on a sign-flip null that keeps the bar ranges and volatility clustering but removes any direction between bars. Trend/range labels (ER, ADX, CHOP, rolling Hurst) do not persist: a window's reading has about zero correlation with the next window's (ER −0.04..+0.01, CHOP −0.13..0.00, Hurst −0.08..+0.01). The classic thresholds fire on random data about as often as on real data (ER20≥0.4 on 18-22% of null bars intraday, ADX≥25 on 35-49%, CHOP≈50 for a random walk). Volatility state does persist (corr 0.5-0.8). No trend measure improves which-side-first out of sample beyond the gambler's-ruin race geometry (OOS log-loss changes between −0.25% and +1.0%). In efficient trends the geometry already points to the with-trend pool 76-82% of the time, so 'the draw continues in trends' is mostly geometry. Choosing the side by an engine-like structure D costs 9-12 pp of first-touch accuracy intraday. Gating D by efficiency (ER20≥0.40 and D agrees with the ER direction) recovers the geometry result within 0.2 pp; gating by ADX≥25 still loses 2.5-3.5 pp. PoT drift worsens log-loss in every regime, including efficient trends, so a 'trend regime' should never switch drift back on. Ranges do not raise the chance that both sides get raided, nor make pools more magnetic. Volatility compression does both, measured in ATR units on 15m/1H (reach ≥3 ATR 0.50→0.39 on 1H and 0.46→0.33 on 15m, from compressed to expanded). That effect comes from volatility clustering and mean reversion, carries no direction, is absent on 5m, and is replicated by the null. Pools printed while price was coiling are no more magnetic. After a sweep, 'holds = continuation, rejects = reversal' is false in every intraday regime (symmetric race ≈0.50). Counter-trend pools in efficient trends are touched about 5 pp less than the null on 1H and daily only, which supports a mild scoped penalty (×0.85), not ×0.50. The literature agrees: fast trend-following has collapsed on small-tick index and FX futures since 2009, intraday forecasts fail preregistered tests, and VR/Hurst estimates are noise in chart-length windows. Proposed design: key the PoT surface on volatility state, build a cheap two-axis classifier (efficiency for gating and honest reporting, volatility for probability) with a regime-split ledger, gate D by efficiency, scope the counter-draw penalty, and add a graded stop-run readout.

concepts.name: Kaufman efficiency ratio (ER) and signed ER
concepts.definition: ER_n = |C_t − C_{t−n}| / Σ_{i=t−n+1..t}|C_i − C_{i−1}| ∈ [0,1]; sER_n = (C_t − C_{t−n})/Σ|ΔC| ∈ [−1,1]. Kaufman's KAMA uses n=10, fast 2, slow 30. Practitioners use ER≥0.4-0.6 for trend and ER<0.2-0.3 for chop. Under a Gaussian random walk ER_n ≈ |Z|·√(π/(2n)): for n=20 the mean is ≈0.22 and P(ER≥0.40)≈15%. Guard a zero path; use close-to-close changes so gaps count.
concepts.dolRole: A gate deciding when a directional draw is allowed to steer target selection. It describes the last n bars; it does not forecast the next window.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Next non-overlapping window corr −0.04..+0.01 (null −0.03..+0.03). P(ER20≥0.4) is 17-22% real vs 18-22% null intraday. Adding sER to ruin geometry worsens OOS log-loss by 0.01-0.66%. As a gate it is useful: D gated by ER≥0.40 and agreement matches geometry within 0.2 pp, while ungated D loses 9-12 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: No ER in the engine. coilScore (886-891) is a related overlap ratio used only in density.

concepts.name: ADX / DMI (Wilder)
