concepts.definition: +DM = H_t−H_{t−1} if that move is greater than L_{t−1}−L_t and greater than 0 (−DM is the mirror). ±DI = 100·RMA(±DM,14)/RMA(TR,14). DX = 100|+DI−−DI|/(+DI+−DI). ADX = RMA(DX,14). ADX>25 = trend, <20 = no trend; +DI>−DI gives the direction. The double RMA gives about 27 bars of memory.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore trend filter for preferring with-trend liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] ADX≥25 holds on 42-50% of real bars vs 35-49% on the direction-free null. Gating D by ADX≥25 loses 2.5-3.5 pp first-touch vs geometry intraday. +DI−−DI adds −0.25%..+0.30% OOS log-loss. Practitioner tests: no added value to Donchian (oxfordstrat); gains only from skipping chop (algolab 2026).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; do not add it as a gate.

concepts.name: Choppiness Index (Dreiss)
concepts.definition: CHOP_n = 100·log10(ΣTR_n/(HH_n−LL_n))/log10(n), n=14. Above 61.8 = chop, below 38.2 = trend (Fibonacci conventions). For a random walk ΣTR/(HH−LL)≈√n, so CHOP≈50.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore 'range regime' marker (both sides raided, edges magnetic).
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Next-window corr −0.13..0.00. High CHOP does not raise distance-matched P(both pools taken): 1H 0.436 vs low-CHOP 0.540, 5m flat, 15m replicated by the null. Daily inconclusive (raw 0.28 vs 0.13, but the OOS logit is 3.2% worse). No pool-magnet effect (high CHOP −0.005/−0.019/−0.023/+0.015 vs null).
concepts.engineNotes: coilScore (886-891) is a CHOP-like overlap ratio feeding density (683, 687) at pool birth. Pools printed while coiling are not more magnetic (−0.005..−0.018 vs null −0.002..−0.020).

concepts.name: Hurst exponent (R/S, DFA, VR-implied)
concepts.definition: Var(r_q) ∝ q^{2H}. H=0.5 is a random walk, H>0.5 persistent, H<0.5 anti-persistent. VR-implied: H ≈ 0.5 + ln VR(q)/(2 ln q). Rolling estimate in this study: q=4, w=96 bars. Lo-MacKinlay SE of VR ≈ √(2(2q−1)(q−1)/(3qT)) ≈ 0.19, so the Hurst SE ≈ 0.07.
concepts.dolRole: Folklore classifier of trending vs mean-reverting regime.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Mean 0.47-0.48 on real and null alike. A random walk is labelled H>0.55 on 20-22% of bars and H<0.45 on 35-38%. Next-window corr ≈0. No reach or side information. Literature: R/S is biased in short samples (Kristoufek 2012); estimator variance is large (Barunik & Kristoufek 2012); local Hurst is scale-dependent (Bartolozzi et al. 2007).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Variance ratio test (Lo-MacKinlay)
concepts.definition: VR(q) = Var(q-bar returns)/(q·Var(1-bar)), with the heteroskedasticity-robust z*. VR>1 means positive autocorrelation (trend), VR<1 means reversion.
concepts.dolRole: A diagnostic of whether a market trends or reverts at a scale; possible regime switch.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong as a test: weekly equal-weighted CRSP autocorrelation 0.30 in 1962-85, random walk rejected (Lo & MacKinlay 1988). At intraday DOL scales, FX, commodities and crypto are random-walk-like and SPY lag-1 reversal is magnitude-only (arXiv 2606.29591). The VR test cannot reject a random walk for most of 61 instruments (arXiv 2610.11028). As a rolling classifier: none.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed in Pine.

concepts.name: Volatility state: compression/expansion (ATR5/ATR100, BB-width percentile, NR4/NR7, TTM squeeze)
concepts.definition: volr = ATR(5)/ATR(100), or a z-score of ln(ATR5/ATR100) against a slow EWMA with tercile cutoffs ±0.43σ. BB squeeze: 4σ20/SMA20 at a ~120-bar low or low percentile. TTM squeeze: BB(20,2σ) inside KC(20,1.5·ATR) ⇔ 2σ20 < 1.5·ATR20 with a common basis; it 'fires' when it exits. NR4/NR7: range is the smallest of the last 4/7 bars (Crabel).
concepts.dolRole: Sets how far price travels in ATR units over H bars, and so PoT, proximity reach, and the risk that both sides (target and stop) get run. It carries no direction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Persistence corr 0.49-0.80. Reach ≥3 ATR within 30 bars by compressed/normal/expanded tercile: 1H .50/.43/.39 (OOS −0.53%), 15m .46/.45/.33 (−0.92%), 5m flat (seasonality dominates). P(both pools within K) OOS −0.97% (1H), −2.95% (15m). Pool touch vs random level: compressed +0.03, expanded −0.06..−0.10. The null replicates it (vol clustering). No which-side information. QPOT-03 finds lower log-loss on 6/6 symbols. HAR persistence is strong in the literature (Corsi 2009).
concepts.engineNotes: Only atrE = max(ATR14, ATR200) for ejection gates (874-878). The PoT surface (1060, 1284-1301, 1530-1532) is keyed on htfBias, not volatility. Proximity reach (665) uses the analytic f_pot.

concepts.name: Realised vs implied volatility ratio (variance risk premium)
concepts.definition: VRP = IV² − E[RV²] (e.g. VIX² vs realised 5-min variance). RV/IV > 1 marks stress regimes.
concepts.dolRole: Possible stress-regime flag for wider reach and trend days in index futures.
concepts.evidenceNotes: It predicts equity index returns at monthly-quarterly horizons (Bollerslev, Tauchen & Zhou 2009); nothing documented at DOL (intraday) horizons. In Pine it needs an index-specific implied-vol symbol (CBOE:VIX), so it is not generic.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended: not generic and outside the horizon.

concepts.name: Time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen) and fast trend-following
concepts.definition: sign(past 1-12 month excess return) predicts the next month. Fast variant: EWMA(τ) − EWMA(4τ) normalised by its own dispersion, clipped ±2.
concepts.dolRole: Would justify a persistent directional draw if trends persisted at DOL horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong at 1-12 months across 58 futures, with partial reversal after 1 year (JFE 2012). Fast trend after 2009: Sharpe 0.84→0.12 (τ=5d) up to 0.70→0.40 (τ=50d); on small-tick contracts (equity index, FX) 'completely degraded'; large-tick 1.0-1.2 (Kurth et al. 2026, ~100 futures). [this study] sign(trend)×forward 30-bar return is not significant in any regime or family.
concepts.engineNotes: Outside DOL horizons; the structure component of D (1892) assumes a persistence the data do not show.

concepts.name: Trend-strength nonlinearity (weak trends persist, strong revert; Safari & Schmidhuber)
concepts.definition: Trend strength φ_T = Σ w_T(n)·R̂(t−n) with Σw²=1 (standard-deviation units). Next return ≈ b·φ + c·φ³, with b>0 and c<0 from about 30 min to a few years. Below about 15-30 min weak trends revert.
concepts.dolRole: Would modulate continuation probability by trend strength (persist when weak, fade when stretched).
concepts.evidenceNotes: 14 years of futures tick data and 30 years daily; small coefficients (arXiv 2501.16772; 2006.07847). [this study] Adding φ24 and φ24³ to geometry worsens OOS log-loss by 0.08-1.00%; the samples are too small to resolve effects that size.
concepts.engineNotes: Not worth fixed rules; at most a learned feature (REG-6).

concepts.name: Intraday momentum (first half-hour → last half-hour)
concepts.definition: The return over the first 30 minutes of the session predicts the last 30-minute return (Gao, Han, Li & Zhou 2018).
concepts.dolRole: Late-session draw direction for index futures.
concepts.evidenceNotes: SPY 1993-2013: R² 1.6% in-sample, 1.2% out-of-sample, stronger on high-volatility and high-volume days. A practical walk-forward on MNQ 2021-25 finds 0 of 14 OHLCV momentum families pass (arXiv 2605.04004). Zero of 160 forecast cells beat no-change at 5-120 min on ES/NQ (arXiv 2611.12141).
concepts.engineNotes: Covered by sibling TIME-9 as a ledger-gated feature; not a regime-classifier input.

concepts.name: Short-term reversal / microstructure mean reversion and the LeBaron effect
concepts.definition: Sub-hour reversal from bid-ask bounce and temporary imbalance. Lag-1 autocorrelation that is magnitude- rather than sign-driven. LeBaron effect: serial correlation is lower when predictable volatility is high and higher with unexpected volatility.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why short-horizon 'trend' labels fade; would argue for a conditional continuation weight.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka 2010; SPY ρ(1)=−0.081 is magnitude-driven (sign test p=0.11), and FX, commodities and crypto are random-walk-like (arXiv 2606.29591); LeBaron effect intraday in S&P futures (Bianco, Corsi & Renò 2008). Trends are more profitable in low volatility (Kurth et al. 2026). [this study] ER≥0.4 with-trend excess by volatility is inconsistent across families (small n).
concepts.engineNotes: No action beyond REG-6 learned features.

concepts.name: Claim C1: in trends opposite-side liquidity holds and the draw continues
concepts.definition: In an efficient trend (ER20≥0.40 with direction sign(sER)), the with-trend pool is reached before the counter-trend pool more often than distance alone implies, and counter-trend pools are less likely to be touched.
concepts.dolRole: The justification for draw-side-first selection and the counter-draw penalty.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] In efficient trends geometry already points with the trend 76-82% of the time (null 78-83%); mean P(with-trend first) 0.62-0.65. With-trend excess beyond geometry: only 1H ER≥0.4 +6.1±2.5 pp (null −0.4) clears 2σ, out of about 20 gates × 4 families. Counter-trend pool touch vs random level: 1H −6.7±2.7 pp (null −1.5), D −6.7±4.1 (null −1.7), 5m/15m about 0. Engine-like D-first loses 9-12 pp first-touch intraday vs geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: D (1891-1895) gates selection (1975) whenever |D|≥0.35 in any regime; ctrMult 0.50 (162, 692-693) halves counter-draw scores; ⚠ COUNTER-DRAW label (2029, 2237). That over-applies a weak, regime-limited effect.

concepts.name: Claim C2: in ranges both sides get raided
concepts.definition: In low-efficiency or high-CHOP regimes, P(both the nearest BSL and SSL are taken within H) and pool magnetism exceed what distance and volatility imply.
concepts.dolRole: Would justify range-edge bonuses, expecting stop runs at both edges, and draw-neutral selection in ranges.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Distance-matched P(both): ER and CHOP add nothing OOS on 1H, 5m or 15m; 1H high-CHOP 0.436 vs low-CHOP 0.540 (opposite of the claim). The two-sided effect comes from volatility compression instead (OOS −0.97% 1H, −2.95% 15m), and the null replicates it. Inside ranges, which edge goes first is pure geometry (sibling WYK-3).
concepts.engineNotes: No range regime in the engine. Use WYK-3's draw-neutral range handling and REG-5's volatility-based stop-run readout, not a range bonus.

concepts.name: Claim C3: compression precedes expansion (squeeze breakouts)
concepts.definition: After NR4/NR7, an inside bar or a BB/TTM squeeze, the next move is large and tradeable on the break of the narrow range.
concepts.dolRole: Timing and magnitude of the next raid; direction is claimed from the squeeze momentum or the break.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Magnitude in ATR(14) units: true on 15m/1H (reach ≥3 ATR 0.50 vs 0.39; 0.46 vs 0.33), from volatility clustering and mean reversion; the absolute next range is smaller (sibling: NR7 next range > median only 26-45%). Direction: none (squeeze and NR states add nothing to which-side-first). TTM squeeze has no published quantitative test (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Add as volatility state (REG-1, REG-5), never as a draw input.

concepts.name: Claim C4: a raid that holds means continuation, one that rejects means reversal, by regime
concepts.definition: After price trades through a pool: if the bar closes beyond it, expect continuation; if it closes back inside, expect reversal; with trend alignment as a modifier.
concepts.dolRole: Feeds liqEvt into D (30% weight in D).
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Symmetric ±1 ATR race from the sweep close, hold vs reject: 5m 0.507/0.510, 15m 0.508/0.510, 1H 0.497/0.509. Aligned with an efficient trend: 5m 0.538±0.014 vs null 0.487, but 15m 0.542 (null 0.538) and 1H 0.521 (null 0.514) do not replicate. Daily all-sweeps 0.539±0.016 vs null 0.497.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt sign rule at 1579-1582; sibling BIAS-4 already proposes removal; regime does not rescue it.

concepts.name: PoT drift conditioned on regime
concepts.definition: The analytic first-passage touch probability with per-bar drift μ = driftW·SMA(ΔC,50) toward the level, versus μ=0, or drift only when ER≥0.4.
concepts.dolRole: Tilts PoT and proximity reach toward the trend side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Log-loss is worse with drift in every regime. ER≥0.40: 1H 0.614 vs 0.590, 5m 0.694 vs 0.669, 15m 0.686 vs 0.653, D 0.504 vs 0.503. All bars: +1.2-3.9%. Drift only in ER≥0.4 does not rescue it. Consistent with QPOT-01 (1.2M windows).

concepts.name: Empirical PoT regime key (HTF bias rows vs volatility rows)
concepts.definition: The excursion survival surface S[r][j] is split into 3 rows per side. Today r = HTF swing bias with/neutral/against; alternative r = volatility state compressed/normal/expanded, bumped with the state at window start.
concepts.dolRole: Makes the headline PoT and the random-level baseline pBase regime-aware.
concepts.evidenceNotes: [this study] Trend keys (ER, CHOP, ADX, Hurst) change reach by |ΔLL| ≤ 0.17%; the volatility key gives −0.3..−0.9% at 15m/1H. QPOT-03: every one of 6 symbols improves, ECE ≤ 0.004. Sibling studies: htfBias ≈ no directional skill.

concepts.name: Markov-switching / HMM regimes
concepts.definition: Latent states with their own mean and variance and a transition matrix (Hamilton 1989). Variants combine volatility MSR with an adaptive MA for a 4-state trend × volatility split (Pomorski & Gorse 2022).
concepts.dolRole: A principled latent-regime probability for modulating draw and PoT.
concepts.evidenceNotes: In-sample segmentations are convincing; no documented out-of-sample intraday directional value. The volatility part is captured by the persistent volatility state. Trend states are not persistent at DOL horizons in this study.
concepts.engineNotes: Feasible in Pine as a 2-state forward filter but not recommended; an O(1) volatility z-score plus ER covers the useful part.

concepts.name: Regime-split accuracy (per-regime ledger)
concepts.definition: Grade every asserted DOL by the regime at assertion. E class: RANGE/MIXED/TREND-WITH/TREND-AGAINST (target on or against the trend side). V class: COMPRESSED/NORMAL/EXPANDED. Report hit%, EDGE = (K−ΣpBase)/n and z = (K−ΣpBase)/√ΣpV per class.
concepts.dolRole: Lets each chart show whether regime matters for the engine's picks, instead of assuming it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A stratified version of the engine's existing, sound distance-matched baseline method. It measures claim C1 directly through the TREND-AGAINST cell.
concepts.engineNotes: Ledger is split only by family (stN/stK/stPE/stPV, 1461-1499; Trial 375-395).

proposals.title: Volatility state replaces HTF bias as the regime key of the empirical PoT surface; proximity reach uses the blended PoT
proposals.rationale: Trend keys carry no information about ATR-scaled reach. Volatility state does (reach ≥3 ATR 0.50→0.39 on 1H, 0.46→0.33 on 15m; OOS −0.5..−0.9%) and is persistent (corr 0.5-0.8). Splitting by an uninformative key only divides the sample. This merges QPOT-03 and BIAS-6 and is the regime-aware pool-scoring change the data support.
proposals.spec: Input vsKey ['Volatility','HTF Bias','None'] (G_POT). SERIES: vLn = math.log(nz(ta.atr(5)/ta.atr(100),1.0)). STATE: var float vMu=na, var float vVar=0.04, var int vState=1. Engine step 0 (confirmed bars, before 1526): aV=2/2001; dv=vLn−nz(vMu,vLn); vMu:=nz(vMu,vLn)+aV·dv; vVar:=(1−aV)(vVar+aV·dv²); vz=(vLn−vMu)/√vVar. Hysteresis: enter at ±0.43, leave at ±0.30, giving vState 0/1/2. Global UDF f_rows(int bias,int vs) returns [rU,rD] via if/else (Volatility→[vs,vs], None→[1,1], else [bias+1,1−bias]). Replace 1530-1532 with [rU,rD]=f_rows(htfBias[H],vState[H]); f_bump(sUp,rU,…); f_bump(sDn,rD,…). f_empPoT takes the row from f_rows(htfBias,vState) instead of bias (1284-1301); f_potModel and f_potBase (1307, 1318) and f_reachD calls (2112-2115) follow. evaluate (665): reach = f_potModel(dist, side, 0.0)/0.95 instead of analytic f_pot with drift. On ≤5m charts prefer QPOT-02's vol-time q (or QPOT-03's session buckets) as the vState input, because the plain ATR ratio is flat there. O(1) per bar; no new request; confirmed-bar state, so no repainting.
proposals.risk: The EWMA needs about 500 bars to settle (vState=1, the pooled row, until then). The PoT can still miss on 5m without the vol-time input. Old saved settings change meaning; the surface rebuilds on load.

proposals.title: Two-axis regime classifier (efficiency × volatility) with a regime-split ledger and panel row
proposals.rationale: Users expect regime awareness. The data say trend/range labels describe the past window and rarely change outcomes, so the honest feature measures per chart whether regime matters. It is also the reporting layer for REG-3/4/5, and the TREND-AGAINST cell tests claim C1 directly.
proposals.spec: Inputs (new group 'Regime'): erLen 20, erTrend 0.40, erRange 0.15. Each tooltip states that about 1 bar in 5 reads as trend on random data. SERIES: erPath = math.sum(math.abs(ta.change(close)), erLen) (length is series int per the reference); erS = erPath>0 ? (close−close[erLen])/erPath : 0; erA = |erS|; gE = clamp((erA−0.25)/0.20,0,1). STATE: var int eState, updated on confirmed bars: erA≥erTrend → int(math.sign(erS)); erA<erRange → 0; else hold the previous value while erA ≥ erTrend−0.08, otherwise 0. vState comes from REG-1; an optional sqz flag (2·ta.stdev(close,20) < 1.5·ta.atr(20)) is for display only. Ledger: Trial (375-395) gains int eCls and int vCls, set in f_openTrial (1426): eCls = erA<erRange ? 0 : erA<erTrend ? 1 : (sign(erS)==side ? 2 : 3); vCls = vState. New arrays rgN/rgK (int[7]) and rgPE/rgPV (float[7]); update index eCls and 4+vCls in f_book (1461) beside stN/stK/stPE/stPV. Full view adds two rows (RNG/MIX/TR+/TR− and CMP/NRM/EXP) with hit%, EDGE pp and z, shown once n≥20. Terminal adds 'REGIME TREND ▲ · ER .52 · VOL CMP'. Clean gets an optional 4th table row 'Regime | TREND ▲' in the reference table style, off by default. Data window: plot(erS), plot(vState).
proposals.risk: Thin cells (hence Wilson intervals and minimum n). Users may over-read labels; the tooltips disclose base rates. Negligible CPU.

proposals.title: Efficiency-gated draw: D steers selection only in an efficient trend that agrees with it; zero drift in every regime
proposals.rationale: An engine-like structure D used for side choice loses 9-12 pp of first-touch accuracy and 5-8 pp of hit-within-H intraday (5/3 pp daily) against race geometry, on 23 series and the null. Gating by ER20≥0.40 plus agreement recovers geometry within 0.2 pp; an ADX gate still loses 2.5-3.5 pp. In efficient trends geometry already points with the trend 76-82% of the time, so the trader-visible 'draw follows trend' survives. Drift hurts in every regime, including efficient trends. This is the minimal fallback if BIAS-1/2 is not adopted.
proposals.spec: Input regGate (0..1, default 1.0; 0 = classic). Step 14 (after 1894): gE = f_clamp((erA−0.25)/0.20,0,1); agr = math.sign(drawD)==math.sign(erS); dSel = drawD·(1−regGate+regGate·(agr ? gE : 0)); dirSide uses dSel (1895). evaluate call (1948) becomes lv.evaluate(close, atr, anchors, confTol, dSel, nz(potSig), 0.0), so the Draw pillar, ctrMult and activeCtr (2029) follow dSel and drift is zero. drawD is kept for the panel, the Draw Flip alert and the data window. driftW default 0.0 (QPOT-01), with a tooltip saying regime drift was tested and lowers accuracy. Panel shows 'DRAW ▲ +0.62 (gated: RANGE)' when |drawD|≥dGate but dSel≈0. O(1).
proposals.risk: Defers to the nearer pool when a far with-trend pool is the trader's intuition; the data back that choice. The draw-flip alert semantics are unchanged.

proposals.title: Scope and soften the counter-draw penalty to efficient trends
proposals.rationale: ctrMult 0.50 halves every level opposite D whenever |D|≥0.35. The only support for a counter-trend handicap is in efficient trends at 1H/D: counter-trend pools are touched about 5 pp less than the null, on a ~50% base, which implies about ×0.85-0.90. In RANGE/MIXED there is no side preference.
proposals.spec: With REG-3, dirD = dSel already confines the penalty to gated trends. Change the ctrMult input default (line 162) from 0.50 to 0.85. Require an efficient trend for the label: activeCtr := not na(activeLv) and dirSide != 0 and activeLv.side != dirSide and eState != 0 (2029); the ⚠ COUNTER-DRAW head (2237) follows. Hold and eviction logic (2006-2007) are unchanged. Measured by REG-2's TREND-AGAINST cell EDGE; users can lower ctrMult if it stays ≤ −1σ.
proposals.risk: Low; a slightly higher chance of showing a counter-trend near target in a strong trend.

proposals.title: Compression/expansion readout: graded 'stop-run risk' and an expansion alert (claim C2 done right)
proposals.rationale: Both sides get raided when volatility is compressed, not when price is ranging: P(both within H) OOS −0.97% (1H), −2.95% (15m), with higher ATR reach on both sides. The engine's race WIN≤H is a martingale race and is blind to whether the stop beyond the opposing pool will be run around the target.
proposals.spec: HUD (Terminal) and the Clean label tooltip: 'STOP-RUN ≈ p%', where p = f_potModel(risk, −side, 0.0), the empirical P of reaching the invalidation distance on the opposite side within H from the REG-1 surface (O(1)). Add a SQZ/EXP tag from vState. Grading: on booking a trial whose target hit before H, push the invalidation price, side, end bar (bar0+H) and pStopRun to small arrays srInv/srSide/srEnd/srP. Each confirmed bar, loop the arrays (≤ H+64 entries, O(H), far below the 500 ms per-loop limit) and resolve a stop touch (low≤inv or high≥inv) or expiry. Accumulate the Brier score and show 'STOP-RUN cal' in the Full view. Optional alert 'Volatility Expansion' on bar close when vState moves from 0 to 2 within ≤10 bars or a TTM-style squeeze releases, latched once per state; the message says direction is not forecast.
proposals.risk: One more HUD line. Alert noise if the transition rule is too loose. A small bookkeeping array lifecycle to get right.

proposals.title: Regime features for the learned side model (only with BIAS-1)
proposals.rationale: Weak, timeframe-specific signals exist: 1H with-trend excess +6.1±2.5 pp in efficient trends, 5m continuation of trend-aligned sweeps +5 pp vs null, and a counter-trend pool handicap at 1H/D. None replicates across timeframes, so they belong in a per-chart learned model with zero prior weight, not in fixed rules.
proposals.spec: Add to BIAS-1's online logistic (over the geometry logit, L2 shrinkage toward 0) the features, oriented to the buy-side candidate: x1 = gE·sign(erS); x2 = gE·sign(erS)·[last bar swept a pool on that side]; x3 = clip(vz,−2,2)/2 (expected ≈0); x4 = sign(erS)·[erA≥0.4]·[with-trend pool farther than counter pool]. Zero initial weights. Full view shows the learned weights ± SE, and 'regime: no skill on this chart' if the side-ledger Brier skill vs geometry is ≤0 after n≥200. O(1) per update.
proposals.risk: Overfitting, controlled by shrinkage and prequential scoring. Depends on BIAS-1.

result.summary: I tested this on 14 datasets (CME ES/NQ/CL/GC/RTY/YM at 5-min and 1-hour, EURUSD 1-hour, S&P 500 daily, about 76k level probes) with an engine-like replica. The replica is simplified: no OBs, breakers, iFVGs, killzones or volume-profile path cost, and only approximations of the pillars. The engine's distance-matched random-level baseline (f_potBase) is already a well-calibrated touch probability: calibration slope 0.93-1.04 on every clean dataset. No learner beat it out of sample, each predicting before it learned from the outcome, on the 13 clean sets. Bayesian online probit: -0.15 to -0.79% log-loss. Naive-Bayes lifts: -0.6 to -2.1%. Unregularised SGD: -3.6 to -5.5%. The engine's own f_calMult formula: -0.2 to -1.8%. A gated learner, or a two-expert mixture with the baseline, costs at most 0.26% / 0.32% on clean data and gains +8.8% / +10.5% when the base is broken (GC 1h roll gaps). So the learner's job is protection and honest measurement, not hidden edge. f_calMult (1376-1382) is mostly noise. With an effective prior of only 2 expected hits, an n>=10 cliff and a [0.8,1.2] clamp, it sits 10% or more off 1 in 47-66% of families under a true null at n = 10-40. That is enough to move scores past the 4-point hysteresis, and it learns only from selected targets (bandit feedback). The EDGE verdict (2390) is subject to peeking: it shows a false "EDGE" 10-20% of the time and a false "WEAK" 45-65% under the null. A normal-mixture confidence sequence keeps that at 1.4% or less. Pooled feature lifts are real but small and unstable. Equal highs/lows +0.29 logit (t +3.6, 1h). External pools -0.27 (t -2.9). Confluence -0.25 (t -2.7, 5m). Draw alignment 0 or below. The confluence and tier assumptions are contradicted. A leave-one-dataset-out cross-market prior hurt by -1.17%, so lifts must be measured per chart with shrinkage, never hard-coded. Target choice is a utility decision: every picker's hit rate matched its baseline. Maximising expected reach d*PoT(d), which peaks near 0.75*sigma*sqrt(H) at about 45% PoT, delivered 1.10-1.43 ATR per target against 0.86-1.09 for the hand score. The key infrastructure is a candidate (shadow) ledger. It turns bandit feedback into full information (SE about 1 pp per 5,000 bars) and enables comparison with nearest-pool and random-candidate baselines. Firecrawl credits ran out midway, so the rest of the research used WebSearch.

concepts.name: Distance-matched random-level baseline (offset)
concepts.definition: p0(d,side,regime) = P(random level d ATR away is touched within H) from the empirical excursion surface (3 HTF regimes x 61 bins of bStep) blended with the driftless analytic first-passage prior, priorM=30, nEff=n/(0.6H).
concepts.dolRole: The null model: a liquidity concept has value only if targets are hit more than p0. It is the offset for all learners.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: calibration slope 0.93-1.04 on 13/14 datasets (76k probes); GC 1h broken by roll gaps.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potBase 1313-1322, f_empPoT 1284-1300, surface 1527-1532; well calibrated.

concepts.name: Offset (lift-over-baseline) model
concepts.definition: logit P(y|x) = logit(p0) + b'x (or probit Phi(Phi^-1(p0)+mu'x)); b=0 reproduces the baseline, so every coefficient is a lift beyond distance.
concepts.dolRole: Makes 'no information' the default and measures pillar/family value net of proximity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard GLM offset; used by the engine implicitly via k/e ratio.
concepts.engineNotes: Only implicit in f_calMult k/e (1376); no feature-level offset model.

concepts.name: Proper scoring rules (Brier, log-loss, BSS vs p0)
concepts.definition: B=mean(p-y)^2, LL=-mean[y ln p+(1-y)ln(1-p)]; BSS=1-B/B_ref with distance-matched reference.
concepts.dolRole: Only honest way to grade the displayed PoT and compare models prequentially.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gneiting & Raftery 2007.
concepts.engineNotes: Trial (375-396) has no pShow; displayed PoT never graded.

concepts.name: Murphy decomposition / reliability diagram / calibration slope
concepts.definition: B=REL-RES+UNC; 5-10 forecast bins vs observed; ECE; logistic slope of y on logit p (b<1 overconfident).
concepts.dolRole: Shows whether PoT 70% means 70% on this chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Murphy 1973; Broecker & Smith 2007.
concepts.engineNotes: No bins or slope in the panel (2378-2425).

concepts.name: Platt / intercept recalibration
concepts.definition: p'=sigma(a+b logit p) with targets (N++1)/(N++2); intercept-only delta=logit((K+mPbar)/(N+m))-logit(Pbar).
concepts.dolRole: Corrects systematic PoT bias of the selected target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Platt 1999; Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005: hurts already-calibrated models on small sets. Replica: -0.36..+0.28% LL on clean sets, +2.9% on broken base.
concepts.engineNotes: f_raceAdj 1367-1371 does it for races only (m=20).

concepts.name: Isotonic regression / Venn-Abers
concepts.definition: PAV monotone fit; Venn-Abers fits isotonic twice to output a calibrated [p0,p1].
concepts.dolRole: Non-parametric PoT calibration.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Better than Platt only from about 1,000 points (Niculescu-Mizil & Caruana 2005); Vovk & Petej 2014. Not suited to small, overlapping ledgers.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended; Platt or intercept is sufficient.

concepts.name: Poisson-gamma / beta-binomial shrinkage
concepts.definition: Posterior lift = (k + alpha*lambda0)/(e + alpha), with e = sum p0; alpha = prior expected hits (prior sd = lambda0/sqrt(alpha)); divide k,e by deff for overlap.
concepts.dolRole: Stops per-family hit rates from overreacting to small samples.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Our null sim: engine alpha=2 + n>=10 cliff gives |cm-1|>=0.10 in 66%/47%/33% of families at n=10/40/80; EB alpha=60 gives 0%.
concepts.engineNotes: f_calMult 1376-1382 uses alpha=2, ignores deff, hard cliff, clamp [0.8,1.2].

concepts.name: Empirical Bayes / James-Stein partial pooling
concepts.definition: Shrink each family toward the pooled mean by s^2/(s^2+tau^2), with tau^2 = max(0, Var_between - mean s^2).
concepts.dolRole: Principled family/context lifts with few samples.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Efron & Morris 1975 (17.56 -> 5.01). With 4 families tau^2 is unstable; prefer fixed alpha + gate.
concepts.engineNotes: No pooling.

concepts.name: Online logistic regression (SGD/AdaGrad/FTRL)
concepts.definition: w += eta(y-p)x - eta*lambda(w-w0); per-coordinate rates (AdaGrad, FTRL-Proximal).
concepts.dolRole: Could learn pillar weights from the ledger.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: unregularised constant-eta SGD -3.6 to -5.5% LL vs baseline on 13 clean sets; AdaGrad+L2 -0.4 to -0.7%.
concepts.engineNotes: Good that it is absent in unregularised form.

concepts.name: Bayesian online probit (adPredictor)
concepts.definition: Weights N(mu_j,v_j); P=Phi((o+mu'x)/sqrt(1+sum x^2 v)), o=Phi^-1(p0); updates mu_j += t x_j v_j/Sigma v(z), v_j *= 1 - x_j^2 v_j/Sigma^2 w(z); dynamics epsilon toward prior.
concepts.dolRole: Leak-free pillar/family lift learner with built-in shrinkage to a hand-set prior.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Graepel et al. 2010 (RIG 61% vs naive Bayes -42%). Replica: -0.15 to -0.79% LL on clean data (no signal to learn); +8.8% on broken base.
concepts.engineNotes: Proposal CAL-4.

concepts.name: Naive Bayes multiplicative lifts
concepts.definition: P proportional to p0 * product of per-feature lifts, assuming conditional independence.
concepts.dolRole: Simple per-feature calibration (ICT-1, f_ctxMult designs).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ng & Jordan 2002 (fast but higher error); Graepel 2010 (poorly calibrated); replica -0.6 to -2.1% LL.
concepts.engineNotes: Proposed by sibling reports; replace with CAL-4.

concepts.name: Elo / Glicko / Bradley-Terry ratings
concepts.definition: Elo is SGD on Bradley-Terry log-likelihood (K = learning rate); Glicko adds rating deviation (approximate Bayes).
concepts.dolRole: Could rate families or levels by race wins.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kiraly & Qian 2017; equivalent to SGD or Bayesian logistic, so nothing new.
concepts.engineNotes: Subsumed by CAL-4.

concepts.name: kNN / Lorentzian classifier (Pine)
concepts.definition: Popular Pine kNN: 5 oscillator features, distance sum ln(1+|dx|), accepts neighbours with d >= running threshold, skips i%4==0, label = negated past 4-bar move of the same bar.
concepts.dolRole: Analog-based probability estimates.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Code inspection: non-nearest neighbours, contemporaneous labels, O(2000F) per bar. The engine's histogram surface is the principled kNN-like estimator.
concepts.engineNotes: Do not adopt; extend the surface with partial pooling instead (QPOT-03).

concepts.name: Learning to rank (pointwise + utility)
concepts.definition: Pairwise RankNet / listwise ListNet (Plackett-Luce) vs pointwise calibrated P_i with ranking by expected utility P_i*u_i.
concepts.dolRole: Choosing ONE target among candidates.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Decomposable utility implies the Bayes-optimal rank is by expected utility; pairwise/listwise only matter for position-based losses.
concepts.engineNotes: Hand score 694 ranks candidates; no explicit utility.

concepts.name: Expected-reach utility d*P(d)
concepts.definition: E[U]=d*P(hit within H|d); for driftless BM argmax at d=0.752*sigma*sqrt(H), P=0.452.
concepts.dolRole: Principled proximity pillar: trades hit rate against distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: max d*PoT picker 1.10-1.43 ATR delivered vs hand score 0.86-1.09, nearest 0.66-0.93; all pickers calibrated (no info edge).
concepts.engineNotes: prox 662-667 is an ad-hoc lin/reach/taper blend.

concepts.name: Optimizer's curse
concepts.definition: The argmax of noisy unbiased estimates disappoints on average; Bayesian shrinkage before the argmax fixes it.
concepts.dolRole: Selected target's score/PoT is biased upward.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Smith & Winkler 2006; replica selected excess -6.9..+2.8 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Displayed PoT 2066-2067 not corrected for selection.

concepts.name: Bandit feedback / selection bias
concepts.definition: Grading only chosen arms conditions statistics on the policy; down-weighted arms stop being observed.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why active-only calibration cannot learn family/feature lifts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Li et al. 2011; replica: candidate ledger gives about 2,500-3,500 probes per 5,000 bars, SE about 1 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: f_calMult learns only from selected trials (1461-1474, 2037-2046).

concepts.name: Overlapping labels / design effect
concepts.definition: H-bar windows share paths; cluster-robust variance in 2H blocks; deff = V_cluster/V_indep; uniqueness weights.
concepts.dolRole: Honest intervals and effective sample sizes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Lopez de Prado 2018; replica deff 1.4-2.8 (candidates), about 1 (selected), 7.7 broken GC 1h; open- vs booking-block keying differs by <=0.3.
concepts.engineNotes: cluSt 1077, 1463-1469 used in the panel 2385-2387 but not in f_calMult.

concepts.name: Peeking / confidence sequences
concepts.definition: Re-testing z>=2 continuously inflates false positives; time-uniform boundary |S|<sqrt((V+rho)ln((V+rho)/(rho alpha^2))).
concepts.dolRole: Honest EDGE verdict that can be looked at any time.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Howard et al. 2021 eq.14; Johari et al. 2017; our sim: false EDGE 10/15/20% at 100/300/1000 trials vs CS <=1.4%.
concepts.engineNotes: Verdict 2390 uses fixed z thresholds re-evaluated every bar.

concepts.name: Prequential evaluation
concepts.definition: Predict with the pre-outcome state, score after resolution, learn only from resolved outcomes.
concepts.dolRole: Guarantees no look-ahead and gives honest model comparison.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Dawid 1984.
concepts.engineNotes: Ledger is prequential and leak-free (1426-1459, 1549-1557); no model-vs-model scoring.

concepts.name: Safe aggregation (gate / exponential weights / fixed share)
concepts.definition: Mix base and model by weights proportional to likelihood^eta; Bayes regret <= ln N per sequence; fixed share tracks switches; gate = use model only while its cumulative LL beats base.
concepts.dolRole: Lets a learner help when the base is wrong without hurting when it is right.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi 2006; replica: GATE 0.00..-0.26%, MIX -0.32..+0.01% on clean data, +8.8/+10.5% on broken base.
concepts.engineNotes: Proposal CAL-4/CAL-6.

concepts.name: Selection baselines (nearest, random candidate, runner-up)
concepts.definition: Shadow-grade simple rules at each DOL open and compare hit excess and ATR delivered.
concepts.dolRole: Answers whether scoring beats 'nearest pool'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: hand score vs nearest vs random top-1 excess all within about +-2 SE.
concepts.engineNotes: Only the random-level-at-same-distance baseline exists (1313-1322).

concepts.name: Concept drift / forgetting
concepts.definition: Exponential discount of statistics, adPredictor epsilon dynamics, fixed share.
concepts.dolRole: Adapts to regime changes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Replica: epsilon=1e-3 worse on 10/14 sets (all 5-min), better on 4 (incl. broken GC 1h).
concepts.engineNotes: roll50 display only (1478).

concepts.name: Pillar priors vs measured lifts
concepts.definition: Pooled offset-logistic lifts beyond distance for engine-like features.
concepts.dolRole: Whether confluence, tier, draw and EQ raise hit probability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: EQ +0.29 (t+3.6, 1h); external -0.27 (t-2.9, 1h); confluence -0.25 (t-2.7, 5m); draw -0.11 (t-2.4, 1h); LODO cross-market prior -1.17% LL.
concepts.engineNotes: wConf=15 and 1.2*tier in density (683) assume positive lifts; wDraw=30 not supported beyond distance.

proposals.title: Replace f_calMult with an overlap-aware, evidence-gated empirical-Bayes multiplier
proposals.rationale: The current formula ((k+2)/(e+2))/((K+2)/(E+2)), clamp [0.8,1.2] after n>=10, is mostly noise. It sits 10% or more off 1 in 47-66% of families under a true null at n = 10-40, multiplies the whole score past the 4-point hysteresis, learns only from selected targets, and cost 0.2-1.8% log-loss prequentially.
proposals.spec: STATE HELPERS (replace 1376-1382): gl=(K+2)/(E+2); deff=max(1, vCluster/vInd) from cluSt/stPV; post=(k/deff + calPrior*gl)/(e/deff + calPrior), calPrior input default 60. Gate: S=k-gl*e, V=deff*stPV[g]; apply only if |S| >= f_csBound(V,10,0.10) (new PURE helper: sqrt((v+rho)ln((v+rho)/(rho alpha^2)))). cm = gate ? clamp(post/gl, 0.85, 1.15) : 1. Remove the n>=10 cliff. When CAL-3 exists, take k,e,V from the candidate ledger. Full panel family rows show hit% / exp% / cm.
proposals.risk: Slow to detect real family lifts (a true 7% lift reaches about 4% only at n of about 320); acceptable because measured lifts are below the noise floor.

proposals.title: Peeking-safe EDGE verdict with an always-valid band and expected rates in family rows
proposals.rationale: The z>=2 / z>=1 verdict (2390) is re-evaluated every bar: under the null it shows a false EDGE 10-20% and a false WEAK 45-65% of the time. Family rows hide the expected hit rate, so near families look better by distance alone.
proposals.spec: Panel 2383-2397: S=kA-sum pBase, V=vEdge (existing cluster variance), bnd=f_csBound(V,10,0.05). Verdict: nA/deff<30 CALIBRATING; S>=bnd EDGE; S<=-bnd NEGATIVE; else UNPROVEN with band +-100*bnd/nA pp. Keep Wilson as a fixed-time interval. Family rows: hit% / exp% (100*stPE[g]/stN[g]). Optional, low priority: key cluster blocks by trial open bar using map<int,float>.
proposals.risk: Wider band (z about 3.0-3.7) so the verdict will say UNPROVEN more often, which is honest.

proposals.title: Candidate (shadow) ledger with a baseline suite (nearest / random candidate / runner-up) and ATR delivered
proposals.rationale: Full-information grading removes bandit-feedback bias and gives about 2,500-3,500 probes per 5,000 bars (SE about 0.9-1.4 pp). It shows whether the DOL beats simple rules, and it is the data source for CAL-1, CAL-4 and CAL-7. It supersedes ICT-1's mechanics.
proposals.spec: TYPE Probe {lvId, grp, side, liq, edge, bar0, pb, d0, pM, pG, role, array<float> x} after Trial; Level.lastProbe. STATE: var array<Probe> probes (cap 256), cdSt[5*4] = [n,k,e,v] per family+ALL, rlSt[5*5] per role incl. sum y*d0. Snapshot in step 17 after evaluate (inCalc, past warmup): for each lv with bar_index-lastProbe>=H and 0.25<=dA<=maxATR push Probe(pb=f_potBase). Role probes at each new Trial (2045): active, nearest, hash-random (sin-hash index), runner-up; roles excluded from learning. Grading as new step 2b after 1550-1557 (hit: strict for pools, touch for arrays; or H elapsed) -> f_probeBook. Full panel: CANDIDATES hit/exp, DOL vs NEAREST/RANDOM/#2 with CAL-2 band, ATR DELIVERED.
proposals.risk: Shared-path correlation across probes (use 2H cluster blocks keyed by bar0); the cap may bind on huge pools (drop the farthest routine probes first).

proposals.title: Safe online learner: Bayesian probit lift on the candidate ledger with a hand-set prior, gated by prequential log-loss
proposals.rationale: This is the leak-free learner the brief asks for. On clean data it stays dormant (gate 0.00..-0.26%, mixture -0.32..+0.01% LL); it rescues a broken base (+8.8%/+10.5%); and it shows which pillars carry information on this chart. Ungated SGD (-3.6..-5.5%), naive-Bayes lifts (-0.6..-2.1%) and hard-coded cross-market lifts (-1.17%) all fail.
proposals.spec: Inputs G_ACC: lrMode Off/Measure/Apply when proven; lrSd 0.15; lrOmega 0.25. Features F=11 at snapshot: bias, ext, fvg, obk, eq, fresh-0.5, conf, dens-0.5, draw-0.5, kz-affinity, (dA-2.5)/2.5. Prior means 0 except pillars kappa*w/wSum (kappa 0.3); prior sd lrSd. State var arrays lrMu, lrV, lrMix (2 log-weights), pqSt [n, LL base, LL model, LL mix, Brier base, Brier model]. Helpers f_npdf, f_phinv (Acklam), f_lrPred -> [m,s], f_lrUpdate (adPredictor: z=t*m/s, v=phi/Phi, w=v(v+z), mu+=omega*t*x*v_j/s*v, v_j*=max(.05, 1-omega*x^2*v_j/s^2*w)). At open store pM=Phi(m/s), pG=pi*pM+(1-pi)*pb; at resolution update the prequential sums, the mixture (eta .25, fixed share .005), then the weights. Apply only in 'Apply when proven' with n>=200 and LL model < LL base: lv.mult *= clamp(exp(pi*(L_i-Lbar)), .85, 1.20) (replaces f_calMult); PoT = pi*Phi((Phi^-1(pModel)+L)/s)+(1-pi)*pModel, 95% cap display-only. Full panel: LEARN dLL, pi, n; LIFT top-4 mu+-sd.
proposals.risk: Complexity; mostly dormant on clean data, so the visible value is the measurement readout; must be skipped when Off to save CPU.

proposals.title: Expected-reach proximity pillar and an explicit Target Objective input
proposals.rationale: Because PoT is essentially geometry, target choice is a hit-rate versus distance trade-off. d*P(d) encodes it from the chart's own surface (peak near 0.75 sigma sqrt(H), PoT about 45%). Replica: +20-45% more ATR delivered per target than the hand-score pick, with the hit rate still matching its forecast.
proposals.spec: evaluate (661-667) gains params pR (f_potBase(dist, side), computed at the call site 1948 because evaluate precedes STATE) and erMax (once per bar: max_j (j*bStep)*S_j/n of the regime row, else 0.34*sigma*sqrt(H)/atr). erN=clamp(dAtr*pR/erMax,0,1). Input tgtObj Hit Rate/Balanced/Reach: prox = legacy / sqrt(legacy*erN) / erN. Ledger: add sum y*d0 (ATR delivered) per family and CAL-3 roles, plus a data-window plot.
proposals.risk: The headline hit % falls (e.g. 60 to 45%) and users may read that as worse; default Balanced and show both metrics.

proposals.title: One gated PoT-calibration layer for the selected target (optimizer's curse) plus a prequential scorecard
proposals.rationale: The selected target is an argmax, so its PoT is biased by selection, and the displayed PoT is never graded. QPOT-04, SMC-1 and TIME-2 each propose a calibration; this merges them. Ungated recalibration was -0.36..+0.28% LL on calibrated bases and +2.9% on a broken base, so it must be gated.
proposals.spec: Trial gains pShow (uncapped PoT at open) and pCal. Intercept delta=logit((K+20Pbar)/(N+20))-logit(Pbar) on resolved active trials; optional Platt slope (b in [0.7,1.3]) from 10-bin sufficient statistics via 3 Newton steps once N>=150. Two-expert log-loss mixture (raw vs cal, fixed share) chooses the displayed PoT. Scorecard arrays: n, sum (pShow-y)^2, sum (pBase-y)^2, LL sums, 5 reliability bins [n, sum p, sum y]. Full panel: PoT CAL Brier vs base, BSS, slope, gate state, n, reliability strip; Clean: tooltip.
proposals.risk: Few active trials, so the gate stays at the raw PoT for a long time; overlap handled by tempering.

proposals.title: Pillar information readout: which pillars carry information on this chart
proposals.rationale: Lifts are real but differ between symbols (EQ +0.29, external -0.27, confluence -0.25, draw <=0 logit; cross-market transfer fails). Traders want to know which ICT claims hold on their symbol. A measurement-only readout cannot overfit the score.
proposals.spec: At snapshot (CAL-3) record tertiles of fresh/conf/dens/draw and bits EQ/EXT/KZ; at resolution book [n,k,e,v] into pilSt[7*3*4]. Readout = excess(top third) - excess(bottom third) in pp with a CAL-2 confidence-sequence band at alpha 0.01 (7 comparisons) and * when significant. Full panel row PILLARS dens +1.2 · conf -3.4* · draw +0.4 · EQ +4.1*.
proposals.risk: Multiple comparisons (handled by alpha); purely informational.

result.summary: Firecrawl ran out of credits and WebFetch could not reach the vendor sites (edgeful, nexusfi, linnsoft), so external numbers come from search snippets; the core evidence is my own reproducible tests. They cover CME ES/NQ/YM/RTY/CL 1H for 2025-26, EURUSD 1H for 2017-18, BTC 1H for 2017-24, and SPX/NASDAQ/EURUSD/BTC daily data covering 581-1,194 weeks. Each market was tested against a day-bootstrap null: another day's path, rescaled by ADR and started at today's price. This null reproduces the real day-range distribution (GC excluded for roll gaps). Almost every popular session/day/week statistic matches that null within about ±3 pp: PDH/PDL take rates (ES 58.8/44.4% vs 57.0/43.7%), which session first takes PDH, which session prints the HOD/LOD, Asia/London range raids, the weekday of the weekly extreme (arcsine; 'weekly low by Tuesday in up weeks' 72-75% vs null 76-77%), and PWH/PWL during the week. So session/day/week levels are frequent targets but not stronger magnets than geometry says, and fixed session affinities (f_kzAff) and weekday priors have no support. The surviving residuals are small and of one kind: once one side of a PD, PW or NY AM range is taken, the opposite side is taken 2-6 pp less often than random. The exception is the Asia range on index futures, where the opposite side is taken +3.5 to +6.2 pp more often. 'ADR exhaustion' is backwards. A day that has already used ≥1 ADR extends 4-10 pp more than the null (logistic coefficient on log(range used) +0.22 indices, +0.23 BTC, +0.10 CL; neutral on EURUSD 2017-18), and weeks behave the same. ADR is a good unit and a bad cap. Horizon matters as much as distance: an untaken PDH/PDL at 0.2-0.35 ADR is taken by day end 64% if the forecast is made in Asia but only 19% in NY PM. In a causal comparison, a clock plus today-range-factor model beats the engine-like flat σ by 1.8-4.8% Brier after calibration on all four market groups; the ADR-scaled analytic over-predicts BTC by ~11 pp, so the variance level must be learned per chart. Gaps show no magnet beyond distance. BTC 'CME gaps' fill within 4 weeks 86.7% vs 89.4% for a mirror level at the same distance, and gaps >1 ADR continue; EURUSD weekend gaps fill the same as the mirror; index RTH gaps show a small +6.9 pp fill excess (n=204). The ADR profile is consistent across all eight markets: median day range 0.87-0.97 ADR, P(≥1 ADR) 38-46%, median counter-move from the open 0.17-0.20 ADR. Proposals: a day-state 'today factor' with ADR as a unit and never a cap; a learned, Brier-graded key-level day-end surface giving 'PoT today'; replacing fixed affinities with a bounded learned multiplier plus a per-family ledger; a context readout and key-level alerts; a weekly horizon for PW levels; and a day-boundary input.

Day = TradingView daily session (CME 18:00-17:00 ET, FX 17:00 ET, crypto 00:00 UTC). A gap beyond the level counts as taken at the open.

concepts.definition: P(untaken PDH/PDL is traded through by day end | distance now in ADR units, session/clock time of the forecast).

concepts.name: ADR (average daily range) as unit and distribution
concepts.definition: ADR(N) = mean of the prior N full-day ranges (N=14 here). Day range / ADR distribution; max excursion from the open; counter-move from the open.
concepts.dolRole: Symbol- and timeframe-independent distance unit; reach bands; Crabel-stretch-sized counter-move.

Larger-side excursion from the open q50/q80/q95 0.66-0.76 / 1.01-1.12 / 1.41-1.97 ADR. Smaller side q50 0.17-0.20, q80 0.32-0.36. Lag-1 range correlation 0.19-0.41 (EURUSD 0.00). External: DailyForex 2×ATR20 days ≈ 1 in 40 (snippet).

concepts.name: ADR exhaustion / remaining-ADR cap
concepts.definition: Folklore: once the day has used its ADR, further extension is unlikely. Tested as P(extend beyond the running extreme by x·ADR before day end) vs range used so far, against an ADR-scaled null.
concepts.dolRole: Whether to cap reach or eject targets when the ADR is 'used'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own: the sign is reversed. Used ≥1 ADR gives +4 to +10 pp more extension than the null (IDX x=0.10: 26.3 vs 20.4; BTC x=0.25: 15.7 vs 6.6). Used <0.4 gives −2 to −6 pp. Logistic log(used) +0.215 (IDX), +0.230 (BTC), +0.10 (CL), −0.03 (EURUSD). The weekly test agrees (SPX 23.9 vs 15.0).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; it must not be added as a cap.

concepts.name: Day-state 'today factor'
concepts.definition: ratio = range so far / E[range so far at this clock bucket] (both in ADR units), clamped to 0.5-2.5 and shrunk by the share of a normal day already printed. It multiplies the forward variance.
concepts.dolRole: Scales PoT, reach and race to today's activity (volatility clustering); keeps far targets alive on expansion days.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Own causal Brier after recalibration: IDX clock 0.1477 → clock×today 0.1436 (−2.8%; −4.8% vs flat σ); CL −2.0% vs flat; BTC −1.8%; no gain on EURUSD 2017-18. Structure: Engle & Sokalska 2012 (J. Fin. Econometrics 10(1):54-83), daily × diurnal × intraday variance.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(chg, potLen) at 916 feeds f_pot (1303-1322), reach (665) and race (1360-1363) with no day state.

proposals.title: Day-state variance ('today factor') and ADR as a unit; never an ADR cap
proposals.rationale: A day that has already moved more than normal for this hour keeps moving, and a quiet one stays quiet. The 'ADR exhaustion' folklore is backwards: logistic coefficient on log(range used) +0.22 (indices), +0.23 (BTC), +0.10 (CL); +4 to +10 pp extension excess at ≥1 ADR used. The engine's trailing σ (line 916) is blind to day state. Causal Brier: indices clock 0.1477 → clock×today 0.1436 (−2.8%; −4.8% vs flat σ); CL −2.0% vs flat; BTC −1.8%. The structure is Engle & Sokalska (2012): daily × diurnal × intraday variance.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_POT): useDay bool (default true), adrLen int 14. ADR is built from the engine's own day tracker with no new request.*: on pdNew (945) push pdH−pdL into a dRng array (keep adrLen); dADR = avg once there are ≥5 days. Running day extremes dHi/dLo reset on timeframe.change("D"). Day bucket: db = int((time−dStart)/(bkMin·60000)), bkMin = max(30, chartMin), NBD = ceil(1440/bkMin)+1. State: expR[NBD] = EWMA (α 0.05) of (range so far at the end of bucket)/ADR, learned at each day rollover from the dPath[NBD] written during the day; expEnd = EWMA of final range/ADR. Factor: ratio = (dHi−dLo)/dADR/expR[db]; f = clamp(ratio, 0.5, 2.5); w = clamp(expR[db]/expEnd, 0, 1); fDay = 1 + w(f−1); after the day end fNext = 1 + 0.25(fDay−1) (measured lag-1 range autocorrelation 0.19-0.41; can be learned). Apply: sigD = potSig·√fDay wherever potSig feeds a probability (f_potModel 1304, f_potBase 1315, evaluate reach 665, f_invalidation 1360). Empirical surface lookup at dAtr/√fDay. With QPOT-02, multiply V(j) by fDay before the day end and fNext after. Never eject, penalise or cap by 'ADR used'. Ledger A/B: store pA0 (fDay=1) and pA1 in Trial at f_openTrial (1426); accumulate the Brier of each in f_book (1461); panel row 'DAY-STATE Brier −x%'. Cost O(1) per bar, one NBD (≤49) loop per day rollover; intraday charts only. var state rolls back on realtime ticks, so the live PoT stays consistent.
proposals.risk: News spikes inflate the ratio (handled by the clamp and the early-day w shrink). No gain on FX periods without range clustering (EURUSD 2017-18), hence the ledger A/B and an optional auto-off. Intraday only.

proposals.title: Learned key-level day-end hazard surface ('PoT today') with a Brier grade
proposals.rationale: For an untaken PDH/PDL at 0.2-0.35 ADR, P(taken today) falls from 64% (forecast in Asia) to 19% (NY PM). The fixed-H PoT cannot express this. The analytic level is mis-calibrated per market (BTC 2-9 pp below an ADR-scaled model), so it must be learned on the chart. A time-aware model beats distance-only by 2.6-5.9% Brier on indices/CL/EURUSD. The sib dimension also learns the after-break residuals (PD/PW/NY AM −2 to −6 pp; Asia on indices +4 pp). This is the empirical, self-grading counterpart of TIME-4/QPOT-05.
proposals.spec: Tracked levels (≤10): aPDH/aPDL (fam 0), aPWH/aPWL (fam 1), today's finished Asia/London/NY AM H/L (fam 2; ONH/ONL if TIME-3 lands); sibling = the opposite side of the same range. Per level lvTk = bar of the first strict through-trade today (−1 if none), updated on confirmed bars. At each new day bucket (SESS-1 db), on a confirmed bar, snapshot each untaken level with d = dist/ADR ≤ 3. tb = min(7, int(8·(time−dStart)/(time_close("D")−dStart))) (time_close per reference/time.md l.378); dBin edges [0,.1,.2,.35,.5,.75,1,1.5,2,3]; sib = sibling taken today. Push the packed cell ((fam·8+tb)·9+dBin)·2+sib plus the level slot, the analytic p (pA) and the surface p at snapshot time. pA = TIME-4/QPOT-05 if present, else f_pot(d·ADR, sigD, 0, barsLeftToday) with barsLeftToday = max(1, int((time_close("D")−time_close)/(chartS·1000))). On pdNew resolve: y = lvTk[slot] ≥ 0; hzN[cell]++, hzK[cell] += y; accumulate Σ(pA−y)² and Σ(pSurf−y)². Estimate pSurf = (K + 20·pA)/(N + 20), linear in d, pooled over fam when N < 30. State: hzN/hzK int[432], snapshot arrays (≤ ~500/day), lvTk int[10], hzBr float[3]. Runs on every bar (not gated by calcBars) so 5m charts accumulate days. Display: Terminal HUD and Clean tooltip 'Today 38% (n=812)'; optional 'PoT Horizon = Day End' for key-level targets. Panel: 'KEY LEVELS day-end Brier model .154 · learned .144'. Fall back to the analytic if the surface is not better after 300 snapshots.
proposals.risk: Thin cells early (m-prior, fam pooling). Holidays and short days distort time_close("D") (use max(1, …)). The day-boundary definition matters (see SESS-6). Memory and loops are trivial.

proposals.title: Replace fixed session affinities and the tier probability bonus with a bounded learned key-level multiplier; per-family ledger
proposals.rationale: f_kzAff (597-602, applied 1941) hard-codes ×1.05-1.20 raid priors. First-take session, HOD/LOD session and session raids match the clock/geometry null within ±2.5-3 pp (own day-bootstrap null; ict_time reached the same with a clock random walk). PD/PW/session take rates equal distance-matched nulls, yet tiers add up to 1.2·0.92 to density (682). The real residuals are small and market-specific, so they must be learned. Grp 1 pools all external liquidity, hiding per-family edge.
proposals.spec: 1) Remove lv.mult *= f_kzAff(kz, lv.src) at 1941 (optional input 'Legacy Session Affinity', default off). 2) For key-level pools (src 3-7): mKey = clamp(pSurf/pA aggregated over dBin in the (fam, tb, sib) cell, 0.85, 1.20) when N ≥ 40, else 1.0; lv.mult *= mKey. This carries the after-break discount and any real session residual. 3) Add a fam field to Trial (0 chart, 1 STF/HTF, 2 PD, 3 PW, 4 session, 5 FVG, 6 OB/BRK); resize stN/stK/stPE/stPV/stMae/stBars to 8; keep f_calMult on the old 4 groups; show per-family hits/expected in the Full view. 4) Keep the tier for magnitude display; cap its density contribution until per-family calibration earns it (coordinate with OF-3/WYK-1). Edits only in the scoring loop (1939-1947) and f_book (1461-1499); no new requests.
proposals.risk: Fewer 'London raids Asia' style picks in killzones (the honest outcome). Without SESS-2 only steps 1 and 3 apply.

proposals.title: Day / week context readout and key-level taken alerts
proposals.rationale: Traders reason in session terms (PDH taken? Asia high taken? how much of the ADR is done?). The engine tracks these levels but shows none of the state. The alert set (2077-2094) has no key-level event, a frequent request in competitor threads.
proposals.spec: Terminal panel rows: 'DAY 0.72 ADR (norm 0.55 by now) ×1.3 · PDH ✓ · PDL 12% today · ASIA H ✓ L 41%' and 'WEEK 0.81 AWR · PWH 22% · PWL 9%' (probabilities from SESS-2/5). Clean label tooltip appends 'Today: 38% (learned, n=812)' for key-level targets; the Clean face stays two lines. alert() with alert.freq_once_per_bar_close when a tracked level is first traded through today (reuses lvTk from SESS-2); the message includes the remaining odds, e.g. 'PDH taken · PDL today 9% · next BSL PWH 0.6 ADR'. HUD distances also in ADR units.
proposals.risk: Panel clutter; keep it to the Terminal style and the tooltip.

proposals.title: Weekly horizon and week state for PWH/PWL
proposals.rationale: PW pools are the top tier but are scored on the generic H-bar PoT. Weekly statistics mirror the daily ones: take rates are geometry; the opposite side after the first PW break is −1.6 to −6.5 pp; a week range used ≥1.1 AWR gives +9 to +12 pp more extension (SPX/NASDAQ); the weekday of the extreme is arcsine.
proposals.spec: AWR from pwNew ranges (946). Week bucket = dayofweek (5 or 7). expW[weekday] = EWMA of week range so far/AWR; fWk = 1 + w(clamp(ratio, 0.5, 2.5) − 1), as in SESS-1. Surface weekday × dBin(AWR) × sib = 90 cells per family, resolved on pwNew with the same estimator as SESS-2. Readout 'PWH this week 22%' and HTF-objective tooltip. Optional fWk in the variance for horizons that cross days.
proposals.risk: About 50 samples per year, so the m-prior dominates for a long time; always show n.

proposals.title: Day-boundary choice and ADR distance units
proposals.rationale: PD levels and the day state use the exchange day (945). On crypto that is 00:00 UTC (19:00/20:00 ET), while ICT-style users anchor the crypto day at NY midnight or NY 17:00, so levels and statistics change with the anchor. This is consistency and UX, not edge.
proposals.spec: Input dayAnchor = ["Exchange" (default), "NY Midnight", "NY 17:00"] in G_KEY. newDay = timeframe.change("D") | dayofmonth(time, tz) != dayofmonth(time[1], tz) | first bar inside session "1700-1701" in tz. Feed f_rangeTrack(newDay) at 945 and the SESS-1 rollover. Show distances as ADR beside ATR.
proposals.risk: Changing the anchor changes the levels; the default keeps current behaviour.

result.summary: No projection method from this domain predicts how far a leg will go better than a random level at the same distance. Across about 39,000 ATR-zigzag legs on 18 series (1h, 5m, daily), successive leg ratios show no clustering at any Fibonacci ratio: bump indices are 0.85-1.11 at the Fibonacci ratios vs 0.85-1.23 at placebo ratios and in a shuffled null. Leg 2 is at least as long as leg 1 in 49-50% of cases, exactly the random-walk value. This replicates Batchelor & Ramyar's DJIA test. AB=CD, ICT -0.27/-0.62/-1/-2 SD extensions and pullback extensions are reached at the engine's random-level rate (-0.5 to +2.7 pp, flat across ratios), with no stall at the measured move. An independent benchmarked study even found the 1.618 extension reached less often than a random walk (67% vs 71%, t = -13.5). The only honest quantitative answer to "how far will this leg go" is the directional-change overshoot law. Once a k-ATR reversal confirms a leg, its further extension is close to Exponential(mean k-ATR): P(>= 1x) is 0.34-0.39 vs e^-1 = 0.368, and the previous leg's size carries no information (corr about 0). That matches Glattfelder et al. on 13 FX pairs and the Taylor/Lehoczky theory, and it gives a calibrated "reach before a pullback" readout (PA-3). Al Brooks's headline probabilities are geometry: the "60% measured move" after a strong breakout appears only with a follow-through bar, and geometry predicts the same 60-67%. H2/L2, the 20-gap-bar rule and the Always-In direction carry no side information (Always-In: +0.2 +/- 0.5 pp, n = 10,169). Only very large (>= 2 ATR) range-breaking bars show a weak, inconsistent +2.5 to +3.4 pp, which motivates tightening the engine's displacement vote (PA-4). The "80% of range breakouts fail" rule is really 53-62% vs a 48-53% null. One Brooks magnet the engine lacks has measurable support: the prior RTH close (gap fill / ICT ORG), +3.4 +/- 1.3 pp over a clock-matched random level at 10:00 ET on CME futures. An all-hours baseline inflates that to +12.7 pp, and on 23-hour ETH charts the level must be captured by session time, because TradingView treats ETH as the regular session for futures (PA-2). Finally, 5-14% of bars have no draw-side liquidity within 10 ATR (price discovery). There the engine shows a counter-draw target or nothing, and a measured-move/EXT projection is a legitimate fallback with an already-calibrated PoT (PA-1, P1). Fibonacci, OTE, Elliott, harmonic, H2, 20-gap-bar, Always-In, follow-through and time-symmetry logic should not be added.

concepts.name: Brooks magnets (prior highs/lows, yesterday's H/L/C, open, MA, measured moves, breakout point, range middle)
concepts.definition: Price levels that 'attract' price: prior swing extremes, PDH/PDL/PDC, the day's open, EMA20, measured-move targets, trend-channel lines, the breakout point, and the middle of a trading range.
concepts.dolRole: Candidate targets: which level is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Liquidity pools and projections are reached at random-level rates (T2 row B: -1.5 to +2.2 pp; WYK). Of Brooks's magnets only the prior RTH close shows an edge (T5: +3.4 +/- 1.3 pp, clock-matched).
concepts.engineNotes: Swings 1753-1789, PDH/PWH 944-961 and 1790-1799 present; opens and EQ are confluence anchors only (964-968, 1931); PDC missing; EMA, breakout point and channel lines missing (correctly).

concepts.name: Brooks breakout-bar measured move (the '60%' claim)
concepts.definition: Strong breakout bar (body >= m*ATR, body/range >= 0.6, close in the outer 25%, close beyond the 20-bar extreme). Target = close + (close - open), or high + (high - low). Stop = trade-through of the bar's low.
concepts.dolRole: Probability that the MM is reached before the failure level: target likelihood after displacement.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3 race vs geometry: m>=1 -0.3 pp (1h), +1.5 (5m); with follow-through 0.664 win vs 0.663 geometry; m>=2 +2.5 +/- 1.2 (1h), +3.4 +/- 1.8 (5m), inconsistent per series (1h positive in 6 of 9 series, BTC-driven; 5m in 4 of 6). The 60% claim is weak (forum and flashcard sources).
concepts.engineNotes: No MM level; displacement only feeds D (897-904, 1536-1541, 1893).

concepts.name: Follow-through bar
concepts.definition: The bar after the breakout is a same-direction trend bar closing beyond the breakout close.
concepts.dolRole: Supposed confirmation that raises the MM probability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: it raises the win rate to 0.59-0.67, but geometry rises identically because the entry moves toward the target (diff -1.7 to +1.7 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Leg 1 = Leg 2 / AB=CD measured move
concepts.definition: After A (low) -> B (high) -> C (higher low, A < C < B), target D = C + f*(B - A) with f = 1 (and harmonic variants 1.272 / 1.618).
concepts.dolRole: Projection target beyond existing liquidity: how far the leg will go.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1: P(leg2 >= leg1) = 0.490 / 0.498 / 0.496 vs null 0.491 / 0.498 / 0.492. T2: MM 1.0 hit 0.451 vs random level 0.448 (1h), no stall (react 0.47-0.50). Bulkowski uses only 60% of leg 1 as his target.
concepts.engineNotes: Correct as a scored source; missing as a price-discovery fallback (selection 1999-2005 picks a counter-draw target) -> PA-1.

concepts.name: Bulkowski measured move up/down and measure rule (range-height MM)
concepts.definition: MMU: corrective low + 60% of the first leg. Measure rule: breakout edge +/- range height.
concepts.dolRole: Target after a range breakout.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bulkowski: 60% meet the 60% target, 31,000+ samples (no random baseline). T4 (1b): range-height MM before the opposite edge is +2.6 to +3.1 pp over geometry for 4-8 ATR ranges, about 0 for narrow ranges; WYK +0.03 +/- 0.02.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly not a level source; small effect is a candidate-ledger feature (PA-5).

concepts.name: Measuring gap (Brooks) / FVG-midpoint projection
concepts.definition: Gap between the breakout point and the first pullback; target = 2*gap midpoint - leg origin.
concepts.dolRole: Projection target from a displacement FVG.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (3): hit vs random level 1h -0.0 +/- 0.6 pp; 5m +3.4 (time-of-day confound); daily +3.8 +/- 1.7; race vs the FVG far edge about +1.7 pp vs a +0.6 to +1.2 pp null.
concepts.engineNotes: FVGs present 1868-1887; the projection is correctly absent.

concepts.name: Fibonacci extensions / ICT standard-deviation projections
concepts.dolRole: Claimed targets beyond the last swing.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1 bumps 0.85-1.11 at Fibonacci ratios vs placebo 0.85-1.23; T2 edges flat across ratios (EXT -0.62: +0.7 pp 1h); Batchelor & Ramyar no clustering; MQL5 1.618 reached 67% vs 71% random walk (t -13.5).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; do not add as confluence anchors (1931).

concepts.name: Fibonacci retracement / OTE
concepts.definition: 0.382 / 0.5 / 0.618 / 0.705 / 0.786 retracement of the impulse leg as entry zones.
concepts.dolRole: Entry location; affects race geometry only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1 retracement bumps 0.95-0.99 at Fibonacci ratios (1h); Tradeify: continuation falls smoothly with depth (via ICTS S10).
concepts.engineNotes: Correct; covered by ICTS 1.10.

concepts.name: Elliott wave target rules
concepts.definition: Wave 3 = 1.618 x wave 1, wave 5 = wave 1, C = A, wave 2 retraces 0.5-0.618, wave 4 retraces 0.382; subjective counts.
concepts.dolRole: Leg-length targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No controlled test; CXO accuracy for Prechter 21% vs 47% average; its ratios are rejected by T1 and L1.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Harmonic patterns (Gartley, Bat, Butterfly, Crab)
concepts.definition: XABCD with Fibonacci ratio windows (e.g. Gartley B = 0.618 XA, D = 0.786 XA); D is a reversal zone.
concepts.dolRole: Reversal zone / targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Only student or blog backtests (7-29 trades per pattern) and a researcher-degrees-of-freedom critique; Fibonacci ratios rejected.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Breakout test / breakout pullback
concepts.definition: After a breakout, price returns to test the breakout point.
concepts.dolRole: Magnet at the broken level.
concepts.evidenceNotes: WYK 2.5: throwback 0.870 vs random level 0.872.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Failed breakouts / Brooks 80% rule
concepts.definition: A close beyond a 20-bar range high/low; failure = a close back inside within 5 bars.
concepts.dolRole: Whether a raid holds (continuation) or fails (reversal): which side is next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (1): close back inside 53-62% (1h, 5m, daily) vs 48-53% null; Brooks's 80% is overstated.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt (1580-1582) treats a close beyond as hold = continuation; that is weak evidence (siblings BIAS-4, ICTS-2, REG own the fix).

concepts.name: Trading range vs trend (Brooks context)
concepts.definition: Range = an area of agreement where breakouts fail; trend = always-in with breakouts that succeed.
concepts.dolRole: Regime that should modulate draw and hysteresis.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Regime labels do not persist (REG finding 1); T4 shows only small breakout effects.
concepts.engineNotes: Covered by WYK-3 and REG-2.

concepts.name: Always In direction
concepts.definition: Sign of the most recent strong two-bar breakout (each body/range >= 0.5, combined body >= 2 ATR, closing beyond the 20-bar extreme), held for 100 bars.
concepts.dolRole: Bias: which side's liquidity is taken first.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (2): AI-side nearest pool first vs geometry +0.2 +/- 0.5 pp (n 10,169, 1h), +0.1 +/- 0.6 (5m), -1.3 +/- 2.0 (daily); null similar.
concepts.engineNotes: drawD (1891-1895) is an always-in-like vote gating selection (1975); the evidence says it adds no side information (REG-3, ICTS-1).

concepts.name: Second entries H2/L2
concepts.definition: In a bull-trend pullback, H1 = first bar with a high above the prior bar's high; after a lower low, the next such bar is H2. Entry at the H2 close.
concepts.dolRole: Which pool first: trend high vs pullback low.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: 20 gap bars / moving-average magnet
concepts.definition: >= 20 consecutive bars entirely beyond EMA20; the first touch is expected to retest the trend extreme (Brooks forum: 70-75%).
concepts.dolRole: Conditional PoT boost for the trend-extreme pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: hit within 30 bars vs random level -1.4 +/- 1.5 (1h), +1.3 +/- 1.7 (5m), +6.5 +/- 4.0 (daily, n 120); raw rate 48-52% intraday, not 70-75%.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; the MA is a moving target.

concepts.name: Dow theory (trend definition, confirmation)
concepts.definition: Trend = HH/HL (LL/LH) until a failure swing breaks the prior low/high; two averages must confirm.
concepts.dolRole: Structural bias / side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brown, Goetzmann & Kumar 1998: positive alpha 1902-29 and +4.4 pp/yr 1930-97 (long horizon only); intraday structure side votes are a coin flip (ICTS 2.2, REG).
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure 708-782 is a sound BOS/CHoCH implementation; confirmation (SMT) needs a second symbol.

concepts.name: Directional-change overshoot law (leg reach before a pullback)
concepts.definition: After a reversal of delta = k*ATR confirms a leg, the further extension before the next delta reversal is about Exp(mean delta). For running extreme M, pullback u and target T beyond M: P = ((delta - u)/delta)*exp(-(T - M)/delta); for T inside, a race.
concepts.dolRole: Calibrated 'will this leg reach the target without a k-ATR pullback' probability.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Glattfelder et al. 2011 (13 FX pairs: overshoot about threshold, E 1.04 / C 1.06; total move about 2x); Taylor 1975 / Lehoczky 1977; T1: P(OS >= delta) 0.34-0.39 vs 0.368, P(>= 2 delta) 0.139-0.160 vs 0.135; previous-leg correlation -0.03 to +0.03.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present; PA-3.

concepts.name: Leg-time symmetry (leg 2 lasts as long as leg 1)
concepts.definition: Time from C to the MM touch is about the time from A to B.
concepts.dolRole: ETA / timing.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4 (4): Spearman +0.24 / +0.32 / +0.42, but the shuffled null gives +0.29 / +0.29, so there is no information.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent; ETA belongs to vol-time (QPOT-05, TIME-4).

concepts.name: Prior RTH close / gap fill (ICT ORG)
concepts.definition: Previous regular-session close (16:00 ET); live from the next RTH open if untouched; filled on touch.
concepts.dolRole: Session target with a measurable magnet effect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T5 (CME six futures, 968 instrument-days): +3.4 +/- 1.3 pp (rest of session) and +3.5 +/- 1.4 (30 bars) over a clock-matched random level; +4.8 / +7.1 pp at 1-2 ATR; naive all-hours baseline overstates it (+12.7 pp). Graded weak-moderate in the report.
concepts.engineNotes: No PDC. ICTPD-6's time-break gap detector cannot see the 16:00 -> 09:30 gap on ETH futures charts (TradingView treats ETH as the regular session for futures) -> PA-2.

concepts.name: Price discovery (no draw-side liquidity)
concepts.definition: No unswept pool within maxATR on the trend side (new highs or lows).
concepts.dolRole: State where a liquidity engine has no draw-side target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T6: 5.0% (1h), 5.8% (5m), 13.7% (daily) of bars; reach toward the blind side is about baseline (median 2.46 ATR in 30 bars).
concepts.engineNotes: Selection 1999-2005 falls back to a counter-draw target or nothing -> PA-1.

concepts.name: Traders' equation / R:R race
concepts.definition: P x reward > (1 - P) x risk; race of target vs invalidation.
concepts.dolRole: Probability the target is hit before the stop.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Races are martingale races (QPOT finding 6); all Brooks setups tested here sit at geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation / f_raceH 1343-1364, HUD R:R / WIN / EV 2240-2245; drift should be removed (QPOT-01).

concepts.name: Displacement / strong breakout as a draw vote
concepts.definition: Engine: body >= 1.2 ATR and body ratio >= 0.6, or a two-leg sum >= 1.8 ATR. Brooks-strength alternative: body >= 2 ATR, close in the outer quarter, beyond the 20-bar extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Direction of the draw vector D (side selection).
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: 1-1.5 ATR bars show no continuation beyond geometry; >= 2 ATR range-breaking bars +2.5 to +3.4 pp, inconsistent across series.
concepts.engineNotes: dispUp/dispDn 902-904 fire mostly in the no-information zone; mV 1893 weight 0.20 -> PA-4.

proposals.title: Price-discovery projection targets (MM 1.0 / EXT 1.0 / MM 1.618) as an honest fallback when the draw side has no liquidity
proposals.rationale: On 5-14% of bars (T6) there is no draw-side pool within maxATR, so selection shows a contradictory counter-draw target or nothing. Projections are reached at random-level rates (T2: -0.5 to +2.7 pp, flat across ratios; MQL5; Batchelor-Ramyar), so the engine's existing PoT is already calibrated for them. The value is coverage and a named objective traders recognise, not edge.
proposals.spec: 1) Add an O(1) ATR zigzag on confirmed bars. Input zzK = 2.0. State zzMode / zzExt / zzExtB / zzOpp / zzOppB plus zzPx and zzTy arrays (max 3) declared in STATE; update in ENGINE step 9b after 1776. A bar that sets a new extreme never confirms. 2) Ladder: when zzTy = [-1, +1, -1] (A, B, C), zzMode == 1 and A < C < B: MM1 = C + (B - A), EX1 = B + (B - A) (ICT -1 SD), MM16 = C + 1.618(B - A). Mirror for bear. Pick the nearest rung >= close + minDistATR*atr. 3) Activation in a new step 16b before step 17, inside inCalc: useProj and dirSide != 0 and no kind 0-7 level on dirSide with 0 <= distance <= maxATR*atr (one pool pass). 4) Level: new kinds 8 (above, side +1) / 9 (below); src 8/9/10 = MM 1.0 / EXT 1.0 / MM 1.618; thin zone of width wPx; qual 0.5; touch semantics via isArray(); exclude from CE partial fill (1566: add lv.kind <= 7); f_newLevel side map 1085 add kind 8; f_tierW src 8-10 -> 0.20; f_levelName / f_shortName labels. At most one per side, updated in place (move openT edge as f_mergeAt does at 1124-1126). Delete it (ghost '⊘ REPLACED' if active) when real draw-side liquidity appears within maxATR. 5) Ledger: grp() -> 4 (PROJ); stats arrays 5 -> 6 with ALL at index 5 (1066-1071, 1380-1381, 1470, 2375-2443, f_grpName 543). Minimal alternative: count in family 1 plus a projSt counter. Expected edge about 0; the coverage metric rises. 6) Clean tooltip: 'projection, not liquidity: reached like a random level at this distance'. Kinds and src codes must be coordinated with ICTPD-6 (gap kinds 8/9 -> use 10/11 for projections if both land).
proposals.risk: Users may over-read the projection label as a magic level; the tooltip states the measured rate. The rung changes when a new pivot confirms (at most once per leg); existing hysteresis and the two-bar challenger rule prevent flicker. If REG-3 replaces D-first selection, base activation on the trend side instead of dirSide.

proposals.title: Prior RTH close (ORG / gap-fill level) captured by session time, so it works on 23-hour futures charts
proposals.rationale: Brooks's 'yesterday's close' magnet and ICT's opening range gap are missing. T5: +3.4 +/- 1.3 pp (rest of session) and +3.5 +/- 1.4 pp (30 bars) over a clock-matched random level at 10:00 ET on six CME futures (968 instrument-days), +4.8 / +7.1 pp at 1-2 ATR. ICTPD-6's time-break detector cannot see this gap on ETH charts, because TradingView treats ETH as the regular session for futures (concepts/sessions.md).
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_KEY): useRTHC bool true; sessRTH input.session '0930-1600'. SERIES (global): f_rthClose(sess, zone) uses inS = not na(time(timeframe.period, sess, zone)), var c and cb; on inS[1] and not inS it sets c := close[1], cb := bar_index - 1; returns [inS and not inS[1], c, cb]. rthOK = useRTHC and intraOK and syminfo.type in {futures, stock, index, fund, dr}. ENGINE step 10 (after 1809): if rthOK and rthOpen and not na(rthC) and the bar has not touched rthC, remove the previous src-8 entry from extReg (guarded by extReg.size() > 0), then f_pushExt(extReg, rthC, rthC > close, 8, rthCB, abs(open - rthC)/atr, 1.0). f_tierW(8) = 0.55; names 'RTH C'. The registry already drops it on trade-through (1592-1596). Ledger: family 1, or a src split via SESS-3; must be graded with a clock-matched baseline (TIME-2), since the naive baseline overstates the edge about 3x. Coordinate src codes with PA-1, ACAD-5 and OF-8.
proposals.risk: One year of data from one market family, with correlated instruments; symbols whose RTH differs from 09:30-16:00 ET need the input changed. Crypto and FX are excluded by the type guard. Keep alongside ICTPD-6: NDOG is the 17:00 -> 18:00 gap, ORG is this level.

proposals.title: Leg-reach probability: 'reaches the target before a k-ATR pullback' from the overshoot law, graded by the ledger
proposals.rationale: This is the honest, closed-form answer to the measured-move / Elliott question 'how far will this leg go'. The leg's further extension is about Exp(mean k*ATR) (Taylor 1975, Lehoczky 1977, Glattfelder et al. 2011), and T1 confirms it within about 2 pp on 18 series with no memory of the previous leg. It complements the horizon PoT, which ignores pullbacks, and its calibration can be graded on-chart.
proposals.spec: PURE HELPERS: f_legReach(tgt, side, M, p, dl): u = max(0, side*(M - p)); q = max(0, dl - u); y = side*(tgt - M); result = y > 0 ? (q/dl)*exp(-y/dl) : q/max(q + side*(tgt - p), 1e-9). Use M = zzExt and dl = zzK*atr from the PA-1 zigzag, only when zzMode == activeLv.side; otherwise show '—'. Terminal HUD row after PoT (about 2238): 'LEG 41% before a 2.0-ATR pullback'; Clean: tooltip only. Ledger: Trial gains pLeg, lgExt, lgDl, lgY = -1. In f_step (1434), while undecided, update the favourable extreme; lgY = 1 on hit; lgY = 0 on a pullback >= lgDl from lgExt (use the existing O-L-H-C same-bar rule, 1441). f_book accumulates legSt [n, sum p, sum y, sum (p - y)^2]. Panel row: 'LEG pred x% · obs y% · Brier z (n)'.
proposals.risk: The exponential factor assumes zero drift (consistent with QPOT-01); fat tails make P(>= 2 delta) 1-2 pp above e^-2, which the ledger reveals. The readout is meaningless when the zigzag leg points away from the target, hence '—'.

proposals.title: Displacement vote in D only for Brooks-strength range-breaking bars
proposals.rationale: dispUp/dispDn (902-904) fire on 1.2-ATR bodies with no requirement to close near the extreme or beyond structure. T3 shows bars of that size carry no continuation beyond geometry (-0.3 +/- 0.8 pp at >= 1 ATR, +0.4 at >= 1.5 ATR on 1h). Only >= 2 ATR bars closing in the outer quarter beyond the 20-bar extreme show +2.5 to +3.4 pp, inconsistently. A noisy D component costs side-selection accuracy (REG finding 4).
proposals.spec: Input brkMult = 2.0 (G_FLOW). Global: hh20p = ta.highest(high, 20)[1], ll20p = ta.lowest(low, 20)[1]. brkUp = close > open and bodyB >= brkMult*atrP and bRat >= 0.6 and close >= high - 0.25*rngB and close > hh20p (mirror for brkDn). Use brkUp/brkDn instead of dispUp/dispDn in step 1 (1536-1541); keep dispMult for FVG quality (912). Optionally lower the wM default 0.20 -> 0.10. Measure via ICTS-1's skill gate or REG-3's efficiency gate (edge and drawFlip count by D component).
