concepts.engineNotes: Correct frequencies (2079-2093), but alertcondition messages carry no DOL values and there are no per-event toggles (see competitors COMP-2).

concepts.name: Live visibility filter stability
concepts.definition: Show or hide decisions should be taken on confirmed bars, with a hysteresis band, so a threshold crossing of a live metric does not toggle visuals intrabar. Live numbers can still update in the text.
concepts.dolRole: A target that flickers in and out reads as 'targets jump around' even though the selection is bar-close stable.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism from the rollback docs (strong); user-perception impact is inferred.
concepts.engineNotes: dolShown is computed from live activePoT (2066-2068) and used for rendering (2202) and secondary targets (2185); announcements are already confirmed-gated (2071).

concepts.name: Non-standard chart handling
concepts.definition: chart.is_standard (simple bool) is false on HA, Renko, Kagi, Line break, P&F and Range charts. Real OHLC comes from request.security(ticker.new(syminfo.prefix, syminfo.ticker, syminfo.session), ...) (official FAQ). ticker.standard also strips the session and dividend adjustment.
concepts.dolRole: On HA charts every pivot, FVG, ATR and sweep uses synthetic candles, so WHERE is wrong and the ledger grades fiction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: reference/chart.md:71; faq/general.md:5-28; reference/ticker.md:167,273. The share of users on HA charts is unknown.
concepts.engineNotes: No chart-type check; requests use syminfo.tickerid (923-982), which inherits the HA context; the ledger runs regardless.

concepts.name: Volume-less symbols
concepts.definition: syminfo.volumetype is 'n/a' when a symbol has no volume, so volume-profile features should be disabled and the user told.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps path-cost and LVN logic from silently doing nothing on FX and indices.
concepts.evidenceNotes: reference/syminfo.md:837.
concepts.engineNotes: nz(volume) makes the profile zero and f_pathVol falls back to neutral 1.0 (1417-1424), but the 1H requests still run and LVN silently shows nothing.

concepts.name: Same-bar double-touch convention
concepts.definition: TradingView's broker emulator assumes O-H-L-C when the open is nearer the high and O-L-H-C otherwise, and fills gaps at the open. Bar detalization 'High' uses real intrabars.
concepts.dolRole: Decides WIN<=H, race R and MAE when one bar spans both target and invalidation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: concepts/strategies.md:204-213 (as a platform convention; neither heuristic's accuracy is measured).
concepts.engineNotes: f_step (1436-1452) uses bull bar = O-L-H-C and bear bar = O-H-L-C, which differs from TradingView on hammer and shooting-star bars; ambiguous races are not counted.

concepts.name: Diagnostics: Pine Logs and chart-data export
concepts.definition: log.info(format, args) writes to Pine Logs, which survive rollback. 'Download chart data' exports OHLC plus indicator plot values to CSV (data-window-only plots per secondary sources). Hidden plots can carry one record per forecast.
concepts.dolRole: Audits WHY a target was chosen and lets HOW LIKELY (calibration, per-family stats) be replicated offline on the forecasts the user actually saw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: reference/log.md:58; execution_model.md:414; TradingView help 43000537255; Pineify guide (secondary).
concepts.engineNotes: Only 5 data-window plots (2444-2448); no per-trial record and no decision log.

concepts.name: Reload-dependent calculation window
concepts.definition: Windows anchored to last_bar_index move on every reload, and dataset starting points vary by plan and timeframe, so path-dependent state (hysteresis, calibration, ledger) differs slightly between reloads.
concepts.dolRole: Explains why the accuracy panel can change after a reload with no new bars.
concepts.evidenceNotes: concepts/repainting.md:268-297 (dataset variations).
concepts.engineNotes: inCalc (1519) and the ledger window (2038) start at last_bar_index - calcBars; inherent, should be documented.

concepts.name: Offline Pine v6 runtime (PineTS)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo PineTS 0.14.0 (AGPL) transpiles native v6 and runs it with Pine time-series semantics. It supports custom OHLCV providers with TF aggregation, request.security/security_lower_tf, drawings, maps and log.info, with a TradingView-parity changelog. Native v6 is labelled experimental.
concepts.dolRole: The only way to execute the engine in CI: runtime smoke tests, repaint regression (full run vs streamed updates) and multi-symbol ledger replay for A/B tests of forecasting changes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: github.com/LuxAlgo/PineTS README, CHANGELOG 0.14.0 (2026-11-13), docs/lang-coverage.md, api-coverage; not executed here because npm install was denied by the session's permission policy.
concepts.engineNotes: Only a syntax parser (pynescript) is available; no runtime testing.

concepts.name: Script size and scope limits
concepts.definition: 100,256 compiled IL tokens (unused code is discarded before counting), 1,000 variables per scope, 5 MB compilation request; the scope-count limit was removed in Feb 2025.
concepts.dolRole: Compile-risk headroom for adding features to a 2,450-line engine.
concepts.evidenceNotes: limitations.md:308-367; release notes Feb 2025.
concepts.engineNotes: No evidence of being near the limits; margin unknown without the TradingView compiler.

concepts.name: behind_chart and drawing z-order
concepts.definition: behind_chart (default true) draws all plots and drawings behind the price display when overlay=true.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps candles readable over zones and iFVG boxes.
concepts.evidenceNotes: core.md indicator() behind_chart; release notes Oct 2024.
concepts.engineNotes: Default true at line 31 is appropriate; the label sits in the empty future area (xR = bar_index + extBars).

proposals.title: Settings hygiene: display.none on 76 inputs, active= dependency map, fix CW10026 inline rows
proposals.rationale: 76 of 104 inputs print their values in the status line and Data Window because input.int/float/string/session/timeframe default to display.all. The reference legend shows only the name, so this is the most visible 'cluttered/ugly' difference. Four inline colour rows raise compiler warning CW10026 and misalign the settings tab. Merges with competitors COMP-1.
proposals.spec: (1) Add the literal display = display.none to all 76 non-bool/color input calls (lines 60-226); reference/input.md:27. (2) active= (input bool; all dependencies are declared earlier): cHTF/cSTF/cEXE <- modeIn == "Custom"; sessAs/sessLo/sessNA <- useSess; obLook/obQMin <- useOB or useBRK; fvgQMin <- useFVG; ifvgMaxIn/ifvgMax <- showIFVG; trackAge <- showIFVG or useBRK; lvnThr/lvnN <- showLVN; lvnHours/lvnRows <- showLVN or usePathVP; ghostMax <- showGhost; hudSize and accView <- uiStyle == "Terminal"; warmup <- accView != "Off" or useCal; priorM <- potModel == "Empirical"; tablePosIn <- showTable; uAbove..uText <- theme == "Custom". (3) CW10026: in each inline pair c1-c4 (230-237) keep the title only on the first input (e.g. "Custom · Buy / Sell-side") and use "" on the second; per errors/CW10026.md. (4) Optional: modeIn display.status_line (default none).
proposals.risk: None functionally; users lose input values in the legend.

proposals.title: Runtime budget pack: calc_bars_count, merged HTF request, lazy iFVG drawing, Clean-mode gating, Profiler protocol
proposals.rationale: Only scoring is limited by Calculation Depth. Level tracking, the empirical surface, trackers and the registry run on every bar (up to 40k on Ultimate) against a 500 ms per-bar loop limit and a 20 s (Basic) / 40 s total budget. Runtime has never been profiled, and 'it is slow / does not load' is the worst possible complaint. The docs measure tuple merging at -33% and setters at about half the cost of re-creation.
proposals.spec: (1) Line 31: add calc_bars_count = 20000 (const int; core.md:183) to get the official 'Calculated bars' input. No change for plans with 20k bars or fewer; it halves the work on 40k. Explain it in the Calculation Depth tooltip. (2) After f_htfFvg (~797), add f_htfPack(len, minAtr, dm) returning the 12 f_structure values plus the 5 f_htfFvg values, and replace the requests at 923 and 939 with one request.security(syminfo.tickerid, f_tfSafe(tfH), f_htfPack(biasLen, fvgMin, dispMult), lookahead=barmerge.lookahead_on). Requests drop from 6 to 5; tuple total stays 52/127; non-repainting is unchanged because both inner functions are already [1]-shifted. (3) Step 5 (1611-1619): create the iFVG box and CE line only when tailBar, otherwise store the Zone with bx=na; in RENDERING (2145) create the missing boxes for surviving zones (na(z.bx) and showIFVG). (4) Add needInv = showInv or not clean and needReach = showReach or not clean, and wrap 2112-2115 and 2116-2130 so Clean style skips f_reachD x4, the medians and f_invalidation (pool loop plus 2 x f_raceH of up to 400 terms) on every tick. (5) Profiler protocol: BTC 1m 20k bars Scalping; ES 5m Day; EURUSD 1h; SPY 4h Swing; each in Clean and Terminal-Full, calcBars 5000 and 20000. Accept under 10 s on the 1m case and under 5 ms per realtime tick; record the top-5 lines. Next levers if needed: registry merge only on regNew or every 10 bars; cache f_pathVol per profile rebuild.
proposals.risk: Low. Tuple order must be exact. calc_bars_count shifts the first bar (state differences are acceptable). Regression test: ledger n, hit % and edge must be identical before and after the merge on the same chart.

proposals.title: Non-standard-chart and data guard (chart.is_standard, real-price requests, ledger off, volume check)
proposals.rationale: On Heikin Ashi (and Renko and others) every chart-level pivot, FVG, ATR and sweep uses synthetic candles. The MTF requests inherit the HA context through syminfo.tickerid, and the ledger grades hits against synthetic highs and lows. The result is silently wrong targets and a fictitious accuracy panel. The official FAQ prescribes ticker.new plus request.security for real OHLC.
proposals.spec: (1) After line 309: bool stdChart = chart.is_standard (simple bool, chart.md:71). (2) string tkr = stdChart ? syminfo.tickerid : ticker.new(syminfo.prefix, syminfo.ticker, syminfo.session) (ticker.md:167; faq/general.md:18-25). Use tkr in all five requests (923-925, 939, 981-982). Do not use ticker.standard, which also strips the session and adjustment. (3) Warning row in both styles, mirroring tfWarn (2305-2307, 2431-2433): '⚠ NON-STANDARD CHART | levels use synthetic candles'. Add ledgerOK = stdChart into the trial-open condition (2038) and show 'LEDGER OFF · use candles'. (4) needVP := (showLVN or usePathVP) and syminfo.volumetype != "n/a" (syminfo.md:837); LVN tooltip 'needs volume'. (5) Optional (M-L): drive the engine from a same-TF real OHLC tuple request on HA charts (invasive); non-time-based charts get the warning only.
proposals.risk: ticker.new without an adjustment argument may differ from the chart's dividend adjustment on stocks; since it is used only on non-standard charts, exposure is small (document it).

proposals.title: Confirmed-bar visibility with hysteresis for the Minimum-PoT filter
proposals.rationale: dolShown (2068) is computed from the live PoT. When PoT hovers around minPoT, the zone, glow, tether and label (and secondary targets at 2185) appear and disappear between ticks, which reads as 'the target jumps around' even though the selection is bar-close stable.
proposals.spec: Add var bool showC=false and var int showId=-1. After line 2067, on barstate.isconfirmed with pp = nz(activePoT)*100: if na(activeLv) then showC := false; else if activeLv.id != showId then showC := pp >= minPoT and showId := activeLv.id; else showC := showC ? pp >= minPoT - 2.0 : pp >= minPoT (a 2.0 pp const band, optionally an input with active = minPoT > 0). Rendering (2202), the Terminal FILTERED cell (2349) and annNow (2071) use showC; the label text keeps the live PoT. Secondary targets use the same rule with their PoT cached at bar close.
proposals.risk: A target whose live PoT drops below the filter stays visible until the bar closes (intended).

proposals.title: Persistent render objects updated with setters (stable tooltip, no per-tick churn)
proposals.rationale: Every realtime tick deletes and recreates 6-10 drawings (2132-2141, 2216-2248) and clears the whole 4x22 table (2296, 2311). The label carrying the score-breakdown tooltip gets a new object every tick. The docs measure box.new at about 2x the cost of setters.
proposals.spec: Declare once: var box rZone = box.new(na,na,na,na, border_style=line.style_dashed); var array<line> rGlow (5 lines created on barstate.isfirst); var line rTeth; var label rLab. On barstate.islast, if showDOL and not na(activeLv) and showC, update with box.set_lefttop/set_rightbottom/set_bgcolor/set_border_color, line.set_xy1/set_xy2/set_color/set_width, and label.set_xy/set_text/set_textcolor/set_tooltip/set_size. Otherwise hide via na coordinates, or transparent colours if na is not accepted (verify once). Clean uses 5 glow layers, Terminal 3 plus 2 transparent. Keep the dB/dLn/dLb pools only for variable-count objects (pool lines, secondary targets, LVN). Table: drop the per-tick table.clear; overwrite rows with table.cell and clear only the rows past the current count when it shrinks (track var int lastRows).
proposals.risk: Moderate: stale-object bugs when switching style or when no target exists, so one hide path is needed. Rollback reverting setter changes on open bars is consistent with the docs (execution_model.md:407).

proposals.title: Forecast telemetry: per-trial export record (data-window plots) and opt-in log.info decision trail
proposals.rationale: The ledger only summarises. Nobody can audit why a target was chosen or switched, or replicate PoT calibration and per-family stats offline on the forecasts the user actually saw. Download chart data exports indicator plot values, and Pine Logs survive rollback. This complements the in-script Brier/reliability work in calib_ml/quant_pot.
proposals.spec: New group 'Diagnostics' with dbgExport and dbgLog (both false, display.none). (1) On the bar where f_openTrial runs (2045), set and plot, after the existing 5 plots so {{plot_0..4}} stay stable: xId, xSide, xEdge, xInv, xD0 (ATR), xPoT (model PoT at assertion), xBase (pBase), xGrp, xScore. All are display=display.data_window and na elsewhere or when disabled (+9 plots, 18 of 64 total). Outcomes (hit within H, first touch, MAE) are recomputed offline from the CSV OHLC, which avoids multiple trials closing on one bar. (2) When dbgLog and inCalc, on each confirmed activeId change (2030), log.info('{0} DOL {1}→{2} {3} score {4,number,0.0} chall {5} side {6} D {7,number,0.00} why {8}', ...) with reason in {sweep, eject, invalid, lead2, counter, none}; also log sweeps/ejections (step 3) and ledger bookings (step 2). Doc: log.md:58; execution_model.md:414.
proposals.risk: Low: hidden plots are na unless enabled. Data-window-only plot inclusion in the CSV must be verified once; plot order must stay stable for alert placeholders.

proposals.title: Offline execution harness with PineTS: smoke tests, repaint regression, multi-symbol ledger replay
proposals.rationale: Only a syntax parser is available; there is no runtime check of na handling, array bounds, buffers or repainting, and no way to A/B forecasting changes across many symbols. PineTS 0.14.0 (Nov 2026) runs native v6 with TradingView-parity fixes and covers every construct the engine uses.
proposals.spec: Dev-only tool (AGPL, never shipped). Custom provider extending BaseProvider: synthetic 1-minute GBM bars with a session volatility profile, or real CSVs; HTFs (5/15/60/240/D/W) via automatic aggregation. Test 1 smoke: every Trading Mode x both styles x accView Full over 20k bars must run without runtime errors and produce non-na DOL plots after warm-up. Test 2 repaint regression: run() on N bars versus N-k bars plus k streamed updates; DOL price, score, target id (PENG-6 export) and ledger plots must match on every confirmed bar. Test 3 ledger replay: hit %, edge z and race win % across 20-50 symbols to A/B other studies' proposals by toggling inputs. Test 4: wall time per 10k bars per commit. Not executed in this study because npm install was denied by the session's permission policy; it needs the user's approval.
proposals.risk: Runtime parity is not guaranteed (native v6 is labelled experimental), so failures need triage against TradingView. AGPL obligations apply only if redistributed.

proposals.title: Time-based anchoring (xloc.bar_time + time(bars_back=-n)) for exact far anchors
proposals.rationale: f_x clamps anchors to 4999 bars back because of the max_bars_back(time,5000) cap. On 1m charts PWH/PDH can be 7,000-10,000 bars back, so the zone starts on the wrong candle, which breaks the 'anchored at the candle that formed it' spec.
proposals.spec: Add int anchorT to Level, Ext and Zone. Chart pivots: time[bar_index - aBH]. MTF pivots: htfPvHT/stfPvHT (exact). PD/PW and session levels: record hiT/loT := time inside f_rangeTrack/f_sessTrack (807-863). OB/FVG/breakers: time[obI] and similar. Draw zones, glows, ghosts and iFVGs with xloc=xloc.bar_time: left = anchorT, right = time(timeframe.period, bars_back = -extBars) (time.md:298, valid -1..-500), tether from time. This removes f_x for drawings; scoring keeps bar-index logic.
proposals.risk: Moderate: every drawing call needs xloc, and mixed-xloc bugs are easy to introduce.

proposals.title: Same-bar double-touch: adopt TradingView's emulator convention and count ambiguous races
proposals.rationale: f_step (1436-1452) orders bull bars O-L-H-C and bear bars O-H-L-C. TradingView's broker emulator orders by whether the open is nearer the high or the low, so the two disagree on hammer and shooting-star bars. WIN<=H, race R and MAE silently rest on this heuristic.
proposals.spec: hiFirst = math.abs(high-open) < math.abs(open-low); advFirst := not tgtOpn and (stpOpn or (t.side == 1 ? not hiFirst : hiFirst)) (strategies.md:204-205). Add raceSt[7] counting races decided by the heuristic (hit and stp on the same bar, no barrier gapped at the open) and show 'AMBIG k%' in the Full view's RACE row. Optional (M): resolve exactly with request.security_lower_tf(tkr, timeframe.from_seconds(math.max(60, timeframe.in_seconds()/10)), [high, low], ignore_invalid_timeframe=true), read only when hit and stp (the dataset still loads on every chart).
proposals.risk: Low. Changes race statistics slightly; accuracy of either heuristic is unmeasured, so the ambiguity share is the main output.

result.summary:
1. The engine's EV readout (lines 2245 and 2359, `EV = invWin*RR - (1-invWin)`) is wrong. It conditions on races decided within H and drops the undecided mass, so in a fair market it reads 0 for near targets and -0.34R to -0.97R for far ones, while the true expectancy of any stop/target/time-stop bracket is 0 (optional stopping; Kaminski & Lo 2014).
2. On 163,249 real records (6 CME futures at 5-min with the real 1-min path, plus CME and BTC 1h), corr(EV shown, realized R) was +0.02. For R:R > 4 the shown EV was -0.39R against a realized +0.03R / +0.06R.
3. The drift term in `f_invalidation` adds noise: the driftless WIN<=H has lower log-loss (0.568 vs 0.582 on 5-min, 0.577 vs 0.593 on 1h), and drift makes the readout over-confident at both ends.
4. With zero drift, P(target first) equals risk/(risk+reward), which is exactly the breakeven win rate. The only honest source of positive EV is the ledger's learned race shift (`f_raceAdj`), so EV should become (WIN - BE)(1 + R:R), shown next to the ledger's realized R for the same R:R bucket.
5. A mechanical sweep -> MSS -> FVG limit entry aimed at the nearest opposing pool (853 setups on 5-min, 1,124 on 1h) won within 1-3 pp of the random-walk race and a random-entry null, for all three stop rules. Mean R was -0.06 to +0.05, which agrees with public tests (Silver Bullet profit factor 0.66-0.94; 0 of 10 variants profitable). Setup alignment should not earn a score bonus.
6. A stop 0.3 ATR beyond the opposing pool is a race barrier, not a protective stop. Once the pool is swept it is hit 64-70% of the time on the sweep bar itself and 92-95% within 12-30 bars; random levels give 57-62% / 90-93%. The wick of a rejected sweep is exceeded later 76-82% of the time, the same as for random levels.
7. Obstacles between price and target (inner pools, unfilled opposing FVGs) add no predictive information beyond distance (residual difference 0-1.7 pp). Partials at the first inner pool cut the spread of R by 16-17% with an inconclusive effect on the mean, and time stops are neutral to expectancy. Show these and measure them in the ledger; do not score them.
8. The geometric fill law d/(d+e) is calibrated: predicted 0.735 vs observed 0.696, and 0.774 vs 0.752. About 20-26% of setups ran to the target without filling.
9. The engine's intrabar race rule (bull bar O-L-H-C) orders the high and low correctly 88% of the time, against 81% for TradingView's own broker-emulator rule. Keep it.
10. The HUD re-runs `f_invalidation` from the live close every tick (line 2127) while the ledger grades a bracket frozen at activation (1426-1431), so R:R, WIN and EV jump and describe no trade anyone took.
11. The default Clean view shows only Target and PoT.
12. The seven proposals: honest race economics (TM-1); a frozen trade plan with progress, time left and status (TM-2); a path map with TP1 candidates (TM-3); an entry zone with fill probability (TM-4); plan-payload alerts (TM-5); a stop-distance expectancy curve in the ledger (TM-6); and correct invalidation labels and modes (TM-7). Each adds a statistic the ledger can measure.

concepts.name: R-multiple, expectancy, SQN, profit factor
concepts.definition: R = side*(exit-entry)/|entry-stop|; expectancy = mean R; SQN = sqrt(N)*mean(R)/sd(R); PF = gross win R / gross loss R. Time-stop exits are marked to market at the vertical barrier.
concepts.dolRole: Common unit for comparing targets at different distances: a 70% PoT target at R:R 0.3 and a 25% target at R:R 3 both break even under a random walk.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard measurement (Tharp). Our realized R for engine-style races: -0.008 (5m, n=57,728) and -0.001 (1h, n=105,521), i.e. about 0 before costs.
concepts.engineNotes: rOut 1457-1458 and raceSt 1489-1498 hold realized R; avg R and PF appear only in the Full panel (2419-2426). They are not tied to the active target's R:R, and there is no SQN.

concepts.name: Breakeven win rate and the martingale identity
concepts.definition: BE = 1/(1+RR). For a driftless martingale, P(target at d before stop at r) = r/(r+d) = BE, so any WIN > BE must come from information beyond geometry.
concepts.dolRole: Answers 'is this target worth trading' (WIN - BE), which PoT and R:R alone cannot.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Optional stopping theorem. Our data: observed win rates sit at or just below BE in every R:R bucket (e.g. 0.333 vs BE 0.412 with an undecided share of 0.144 for R:R 1-2); realized R about 0.
concepts.engineNotes: Not shown anywhere. WIN<=H (1364) is not compared with BE.

concepts.name: Two-barrier race with horizon (triple-barrier labelling)
concepts.definition: Upper barrier = target near edge, lower = invalidation, vertical = H bars. The label is the first touch. Unconditional pW = f_raceH(d,r,sigma,mu,H), pL likewise, P(neither) = 1-pW-pL; the conditional WIN<=H = pW/(pW+pL).
concepts.dolRole: Directly answers which liquidity is taken first (target vs opposing pool) and how often neither is taken within H.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Brownian first-passage maths, MC-verified by quant_pot. Real data: driftless WIN<=H log-loss 0.568 vs 0.582 with the engine's drift (5m), 0.577 vs 0.593 (1h); the drift version is over-confident at the extremes (shown 0.792 vs observed 0.738).
concepts.engineNotes: f_race/f_raceH 447-482 are correct. f_invalidation 1361-1364 injects drift potMu*side (917) and returns only the conditional probability; the readout is recomputed from the live close each tick (2127).

concepts.name: Optional stopping: brackets cannot create expectancy
concepts.definition: For a martingale and a bounded stopping time, E[X_tau] = X_0. Any stop, target, partial, break-even stop or time stop has an expected R of 0 before costs. Kaminski & Lo: the stopping premium is negative for i.i.d. returns and can be positive only with momentum or regime switching.
concepts.dolRole: Edge can only come from selection (which target) or race information (which side first), never from exit mechanics. This defines what the ledger should measure.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kaminski & Lo 2014 J. Fin. Markets 18:234-254; Lo & Remorov 2017 J. Fin. Markets 34:1-15. Our time-stop test: exiting at 5/10/20 bars vs 30 changed mean R by -0.012 to +0.004 (SE about 0.02-0.03).
concepts.engineNotes: The EV readout at 2245 and 2359 implicitly assumes brackets carry expectancy determined by geometry.

concepts.name: Displayed EV formula
concepts.definition: Engine: EV = invWin*RR - (1-invWin), with invWin = conditional P(target first | decided within H) after f_raceAdj.
concepts.dolRole: Supposed to tell the trader whether the DOL trade is worth taking.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T2: under a fair market it shows 0 for near targets and -0.34R to -0.97R for far ones while the true E[R] = 0. T4-B on 163k real records: corr(EV shown, realized R) = +0.02; R:R > 4 shows -0.39R vs realized +0.03/+0.06R. Drift adds about ±0.19R per standard error of the 50-bar mean.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2245-2246 (HUD) and 2359-2363 (panel). Fix in TM-1.

concepts.name: Invalidation beyond the nearest opposing pool (race barrier)
concepts.definition: Stop just beyond the nearest opposing level (a liquidity zone pl - 0.2 ATR, or the far edge of an opposing array) minus a 0.1 ATR buffer. Fallback: exec-TF range extreme, then 1.5 ATR; risk floor 0.25 ATR.
concepts.dolRole: Defines draw failure: if the opposing pool trades first, the draw was wrong. This is the second barrier of the which-side-first race.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: once the pool is swept, a stop 0.3 ATR beyond it is hit 64-70% of the time on the sweep bar, 92% within 12 bars and 95% within 30 bars (random levels 57-62/90/93%). Engine stops: median risk 1.53/1.69 ATR; fallback in 6.6%/5.4% of cases.
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation 1343-1358. The semantics are right for a race but it is labelled 'INVALIDATION' (2212) as if it were a protective stop. The distance gate uses atr while ejection uses atrE (1350).

concepts.name: Sweep penetration depth and stop buffers
concepts.definition: Depth = max excursion beyond the level within N bars of the first trade-through, in ATR. Rejected = the sweep bar closes back inside; accepted = it closes beyond.
concepts.dolRole: Tells whether any stop buffer can survive a sweep; informs how raids are read as continuation or reversal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Median depth 0.43/0.60 ATR on the sweep bar and 2.84/2.87 ATR within 30 bars (5m/1h). Pools close back inside less often than random levels (44.9% vs 52.7%; 46.7% vs 54.8%), consistent with Osler (2005) stop cascades.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed zoneATR 0.2 (93) plus buf 0.1 (1344). The raid outcome read at 1579-1582 treats a rejection as a reversal (see ict_struct ICTS-2).

concepts.name: Post-raid stop beyond the sweep extreme
concepts.definition: After the opposing pool is raided and the bar closes back inside, the stop goes beyond the raid's extreme (updated until the MSS), minus a buffer.
concepts.dolRole: The ICT model's stop. It aligns the R:R with how users trade, but it does not change odds beyond geometry.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T3: rejected sweep extremes are exceeded later within 30 bars 76-82% of the time (random levels 78-81%). T4-A: win minus model +1.2 pp (SE 1.9) on 5m and -2.7 pp (SE 1.5) on 1h. GBB script: best stop variant on ES/NQ, still unprofitable.
concepts.engineNotes: The raid event exists (1579-1582) but its extreme is not stored and not usable as invalidation.

concepts.name: Protected-swing stop
concepts.definition: Stop beyond the strong low/high of the current structural leg (the protected extreme after a BOS).
concepts.dolRole: The ICT/SMC risk anchor; the weak extreme is the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional; ict_struct found weak-before-protected odds follow geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: Used only as the exeRL/exeRH fallback (1354). exeProtL/H are returned at 925 but unused. See ICTS-5.

concepts.name: Sweep -> MSS -> FVG entry model (2022 model / Silver Bullet)
concepts.definition: Rules as coded: an unswept pivot(5) pool is traded through and the bar closes back inside; MSS = close beyond the last fractal(1) within 12 bars; FVG = last gap formed in [s+2, m+1]; limit at the FVG edge for 20 bars; stop at the sweep extreme, the FVG far edge or the engine rule; target = nearest live opposing pool; H = 30.
concepts.dolRole: How traders execute toward a DOL. It does not improve which-liquidity-next prediction.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ours: 853 (5m) and 1,124 (1h) setups. Win vs finite-H model: +1.2/+1.4/+1.1 pp (5m) and -2.7/-1.9/-2.1 pp (1h); random-entry null 0.375/0.370; mean R -0.06..+0.05 (SE 0.03-0.10). Public: PF 0.66-0.94; 0/10 variants profitable; Silver Bullet hours not special; FVG-retest component PF 0.80.
concepts.engineNotes: Components exist (raids 1579-1582, BOS 1542-1547, FVG 1867-1889) but no model. It is correctly not used as a score bonus.

concepts.name: iFVG continuation retest
concepts.definition: An FVG inverted by a body close beyond its far edge; enter on the retest of the inverted zone with a hold; stop beyond the iFVG or the sweep candle; target = first internal liquidity, then the DOL.
concepts.dolRole: Continuation entry toward the active DOL.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published statistics; ict_pd found broken gaps hold on retest about as often as random zones.
concepts.engineNotes: iFVG zones are drawn and maintained (1598-1644) but never offered as entry zones.

concepts.name: Breaker retest / Unicorn
concepts.definition: Breaker = an order block whose leg swept liquidity, then broken; Unicorn = breaker overlapping a same-direction FVG; entry in the overlap; stop beyond the breaker; target = the next liquidity.
concepts.dolRole: Entry inventory behind price toward the DOL.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Only practitioner descriptions; no statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Breakers are created as targets only (1646-1661).

concepts.name: Limit-entry fill probability
concepts.definition: With entry e behind price and target d ahead: P(fill before target) = d/(d+e) (driftless); P(target | fill) = 1/(1+RR_zone), RR_zone = (d+e)/(r-e).
concepts.dolRole: Quantifies the trade-off between a better R:R and missing the move to the DOL.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4-A: predicted 0.735 vs observed 0.696 (5m, 4.0% expired); 0.774 vs 0.752 (1h, 4.7% expired); 20-26% of setups ran to the target unfilled.
concepts.engineNotes: No entry-zone concept; arrays are only targets.

concepts.name: Partials at intermediate liquidity and break-even stops
concepts.definition: Take 50% at the first same-side pool or opposing array between entry and target, then move the stop to entry for the runner.
concepts.dolRole: Manages variance on the path to the DOL; under a martingale it cannot change expectancy.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4-A: sd of R 1.12 -> 0.94 (5m) and 1.01 -> 0.84 (1h); mean change +0.107 (SE 0.040) on 5m and +0.010 (SE 0.028) on 1h, inconclusive. A trend-following test found partials always reduced return.
concepts.engineNotes: No TP1, no partial accounting.

concepts.name: Next obstacles (path map)
concepts.definition: Pool levels on the target's side that are nearer than the target: inner same-side pools and opposite-polarity arrays (e.g. a bear FVG/OB above price for a buy-side target), plus volume walls.
concepts.dolRole: Shows where price must go first (natural TP1, possible stalls), but carries no extra probability information beyond distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4-B residual (observed - driftless model): inner pools -0.018 vs -0.019 (5m) and -0.025 vs -0.024 (1h); opposing FVG -0.025 vs -0.008 (5m, 1.4 SE) and -0.026 vs -0.021 (1h).
concepts.engineNotes: The inner flag penalises inner pools as targets (684-685, 1240-1248); f_pathVol is a multiplier (1945-1947); obstacles are never listed.

concepts.name: MAE / MFE (heat, Sweeney stop method)
concepts.definition: MAE = max adverse excursion before exit, MFE = max favourable excursion; Sweeney puts the stop at the p75-p90 of winners' MAE.
concepts.dolRole: Describes the typical path to the DOL: how much heat hits take and how far misses get.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner only. Ours with the engine stop: winners' MAE p50/p80/p90 = 0.27/0.60/0.76R (5m) and 0.26/0.58/0.75R (1h); losers' MFE median 19-20% of the way to the target.
concepts.engineNotes: t.mae 1442-1443 and maeHit p80 'heat' (2404-2408), in ATR, for hits only; it includes post-stop excursions. No MFE.

concepts.name: Stop-distance expectancy curve
concepts.definition: For each stop distance s in ATR: outcome = -1 if MAE >= s, else d0/s if hit, else MTM/s. Sufficient statistics per trial are MAE, d0 and the mark-to-market at H.
concepts.dolRole: Per-chart empirical answer to stop placement; a positive E[R] at some s would show a real selection edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory: Kaminski & Lo (no stop adds EV under a random walk); measurement method of the ledger.
concepts.engineNotes: t.mae and t.d0 exist; the MTM at H is not stored.

concepts.name: Time stop / vertical barrier
concepts.definition: Exit unresolved trades after T bars; the ledger's H-bar grading window.
concepts.dolRole: Defines the forecast horizon of 'within H bars'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T4-B: early exits at 5/10/20 bars change mean R by -0.012..+0.004 (SE about 0.02-0.03), i.e. EV-neutral. Practitioner: helps only if MFE duration clusters.
concepts.engineNotes: f_step 1455-1456; a long-lived DOL is re-graded in consecutive windows (2038-2045).

concepts.name: Plan time left
concepts.definition: Bars remaining in the current grading window, H - (bar_index - t.bar0), and PoT over the remaining window.
concepts.dolRole: Timing: how much of the forecast horizon is left for this target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Follows from first-passage maths; information only (time stops are EV-neutral).
concepts.engineNotes: The live PoT (2067) is a rolling H-bar window from now and never reflects time already used.

concepts.name: ETA (time to touch)
concepts.definition: Conditional first-passage time given a hit; engine: median bars-to-hit of past ledger hits whose distance at activation was within ±0.5 ATR of the current distance (n >= 5).
concepts.dolRole: Timing of the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: quant_pot: constant-sigma ETA rank-corr -0.09 with realized time; vol-time ETA +0.11..+0.22.
concepts.engineNotes: 2116-2126, HUD 2240; bar count only, no clock time, conditional on a hit.

concepts.name: Intrabar path rule for double touches
concepts.definition: Engine: bull bar O-L-H-C, bear bar O-H-L-C; a gap beyond a barrier settles at the open. TradingView emulator: open closer to the high -> O-H-L-C.
concepts.dolRole: Decides which barrier was first when both are inside one bar, i.e. the race label.
concepts.evidenceNotes: T1 vs 1-min truth: engine rule correct 88.1/88.2/88.7% (5m/15m/60m, n = 93,428/32,377/8,211) vs TV rule 80.6-80.7%; on two-long-wick bars 69.6-72.7% vs 64.4-66.8%.
concepts.engineNotes: f_step 1438-1452; better than the platform default; keep it.

concepts.name: Frozen trade plan and pre-commitment
concepts.definition: Entry reference, stop, target, R:R, BE and horizon frozen at activation and shown with live progress in R, heat and status (target first / opposing pool first / window ended).
concepts.dolRole: Makes the graded forecast visible and stable; avoids numbers that jump each tick.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Disposition effect: Odean 1998, PGR 0.148 vs PLR 0.098 on 10,000 accounts. The display/ledger mismatch is a code fact.
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger freezes the bracket at 1426-1431, but the HUD re-runs f_invalidation on the live close at 2127.

concepts.name: Actionable alerts with a plan payload
concepts.definition: Alerts carrying event, side, target, entry/zone, stop, TP1, R:R, BE, win/EV with sample size, bars left; events: new plan, entry zone tapped, TP1, opposing pool taken, target reached, window ended.
concepts.dolRole: Lets the trader act on the forecast without watching the chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner conventions (competitors.md 1.7); alert budgets are small (Essential plan 20).
concepts.engineNotes: 2077-2093: new target/iFVG/sweep/flip with tag, price, score, PoT only; no plan fields or management events.

concepts.name: Meta-labelling (learned trade filter)
concepts.definition: A secondary model learns P(the primary signal's bracket wins) from features and decides whether to trade; López de Prado ch. 3.
concepts.dolRole: Turns ledger outcomes into calibrated, context-aware race probabilities.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Method reference; feature-based learning is covered by calib_ml.md.
concepts.engineNotes: f_raceAdj 1367-1371 is an intercept-only version (logit shift, m = 20) on a drift-contaminated baseline (pRace 1430).

concepts.name: Kelly position sizing
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting; with p from geometry f* = 0.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Kelly maths; misleading unless p is ledger-measured with confidence intervals.
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented; not recommended.

proposals.title: Honest race economics: driftless race, breakeven win rate, ledger-learned EV
proposals.rationale: The EV shown at 2245 and 2359 is a geometric artefact (0 for near targets, -0.34R to -0.97R for far ones in a fair market) with corr +0.02 to realized R on 163k real records. The drift term worsens WIN<=H log-loss by 2.4-2.8%. With mu = 0, P(target first) = BE exactly, so the only honest edge is the ledger's learned race shift.
proposals.spec:
1. f_invalidation 1343-1364: set mu = 0. Return [inv, d/risk, pInf = f_race(d, risk, sg, 0.0) (= BE), pW = f_raceH(d, risk, sg, 0, H), pL = f_raceH(risk, d, sg, 0, H)]. Update the destructurings at 1428 ([inv, rr, pR, pW0, pL0]) and 2127 ([i0, i1, i2, i3, i4]).
2. STATE 1079: raceSt grows to 8 (index 7 = sum p(1-p) over decided races). Add var array<float> rrSt = array.new<float>(12, 0.0), i.e. [n, sumR, sumR^2] x 4 R:R buckets (<1, 1-2, 2-4, >=4); helper f_rrB.
3. f_book: accumulate raceSt[7] and the rrSt bucket of t.rr0 with t.rOut, via array .set (functions cannot reassign globals).
4. Readouts 2127-2130: invWin = f_raceAdj(i2) (equals BE until the ledger has races); invBE = 1/(1+i1); invDec = i3 + i4; EV = (invWin - invBE)*(1 + RR), shown only when raceSt[0] >= 30, else 'EV —'.
5. HUD 2246: 'R:R 1.8 · BE 36% · WIN 38% · EV +0.06R', plus 'LEDGER R:R 1-2 avg +0.03R ±SE n'. Panel 2358-2363 likewise.
6. Full-view RACE row: 'EDGE (wins - sum p)/n pp, z = (wins - sum p)/sqrt(sum p(1-p))'.
7. Tooltip explaining the breakeven identity.
proposals.risk: EV reads '—' or about 0 until 30 races are decided; that is honest. Changing pRace semantics invalidates the old raceSt sums (var state resets on reload). It must stay consistent with QPOT-01 drift removal elsewhere.

proposals.title: Frozen trade plan with live progress, time left and status
proposals.rationale: The HUD recomputes R:R, WIN and EV from the live close every tick (2127) while the ledger grades a bracket frozen at activation (1426-1431), so the numbers jump and describe no trade taken. Traders need a stable plan and its state; the disposition effect (Odean: PGR 0.148 vs PLR 0.098) argues for visible pre-commitment.
proposals.spec:
1. At barstate.islast, find the open Trial aT with aT.lvId == activeId (loop of up to 64).
2. Plan fields: aT.entry, aT.inv, aT.rr0, BE = 1/(1+rr0).
3. Live values: prog = side*(close - entry)/risk; heatR = mae*atr0/risk; left = H - (bar_index - aT.bar0); PoT(left) = activePoT * f_pot(d, sig, 0, left)/f_pot(d, sig, 0, H); ETA clock = str.format_time(time + int(etaHit*timeframe.in_seconds()*1000), 'HH:mm', tz), prefixed '≈'.
4. Status from aT.race: 1 -> '✓ TARGET FIRST'; -1 -> '✕ OPP. POOL FIRST · draw failed'; left <= 0 -> '⌛ WINDOW ENDED'.
5. Terminal HUD lines 'PLAN ref · stop · R:R · BE' and 'NOW +0.42R · heat · 18/30b · PoT(left) · ETA'; Clean only via a new input cleanPlan (default false).
6. Two dotted lines (plan ref, stop) from f_x(aT.bar0) to xR, replacing the live invalidation line at 2210-2213.
7. Data-window plots 'DOL Plan Stop' and 'DOL Plan R:R' for alert placeholders.
proposals.risk: Two R:R values (plan vs from here) may confuse: default to the plan, with the from-here race in the tooltip. Small drawing cost (+2 lines, +1 label). Status semantics must match f_step exactly.

proposals.title: Path map: next obstacles as TP1 candidates, with ledger-graded partials
proposals.rationale: Traders scale out at the first liquidity or opposing array on the path. The engine knows these levels but never shows them. Data show obstacles add no information beyond distance (residual difference 0-1.7 pp), so show them rather than penalise targets. Partials cut sd of R by 16-17% with an inconclusive mean effect; the ledger should measure this per chart.
proposals.spec:
1. Helper f_obstacles(Level tgt, int nMax): up to nMax pool levels with side == tgt.side and id != tgt.id, 0.25 ATR <= distance < target distance - 0.10 ATR, nearest first. This covers inner same-side pools and opposite-polarity arrays.
2. Inputs: obsN (0-3, default 1, Terminal) and obsClean (default false).
3. Render a dotted tick at nearEdge with a tiny label 'TP1 · code · xR · PoT%' (R = distance/plan risk; PoT = f_potModel).
4. Ledger: Trial fields tp1, tp1Liq, tp1Hit, tp1Bar, beHit. f_openTrial sets tp1 from the first obstacle. f_step marks tp1Hit with the same hit rules and advFirst ordering before the race update; after TP1, a touch of entry sets beHit.
5. f_book: rP = tp1Hit ? 0.5*|tp1-entry|/risk + 0.5*(race==1 ? rr0 : beHit ? 0 : rOut) : rOut; accumulate tpSt [n, tp1-first, sumR, sumR^2, sumRP, sumRP^2].
6. Full panel: 'TP1 1ST x% | PART avg sd | FULL avg sd'.
7. Do NOT add an obstacle penalty to evaluate().
proposals.risk: Clutter (keep the Terminal default to 1 tick). The f_step ordering must mirror the race rule. The cost is an O(pool) loop on the last bar only.

proposals.title: Entry zone with fill probability and R:R from the zone
proposals.rationale: ICT traders enter on a retracement into a draw-aligned array between price and the stop; the engine treats arrays only as targets. The fill law d/(d+e) is calibrated (0.735 vs 0.696 observed; 0.774 vs 0.752), and 20-26% of setups ran to the target unfilled, so the trader needs both the better R:R and the miss risk.
proposals.spec:
1. Helper f_entryZone(Level tgt, float inv): the nearest pool array of draw-aligned polarity (buy-side target: kinds 2/4/6 with side -1, below price; sell-side: kinds 3/5/7 with side +1), with distance e >= 0.1 ATR and near edge beyond inv by at least 0.1 ATR. Also scan ifvgs with dir == tgt.side.
2. Compute pFill = d/(d+e), rrZ = (d+e)/max(r-e, 0.25 ATR), beZ = 1/(1+rrZ).
3. Render a dotted border box on the zone to xR with label 'ENTRY · BUFVG · fill 72% · R:R 2.4 · BE 29%' (Terminal; Clean via cleanPlan).
4. Optional ledger stage: limit trial fields limE, filled, missed, pFill. f_step: the target before the fill means missed; a touch means filled, then the race runs from limE. Book fill rate vs sum pFill and win|fill vs sum BE_zone; panel 'FILL 70% (exp 73%) · WIN|fill 34% (BE 31%)'.
5. Input for the pick rule: Nearest or Best R:R.
proposals.risk: Zone choice is a design decision. Origin-locked arrays (689-690) are valid entries even though they are not targets. +1 box +1 label.

proposals.title: Execution alerts with a trade-plan payload
proposals.rationale: Alerts today carry only tag, price, score and PoT (2079-2093), with no stop, R:R, BE, TP1, entry or time left, and no events for post-entry decisions. This extends competitors.md COMP-2's framework with plan fields and four management events.
proposals.risk: Alert noise and the user's alert budget (defaults off). JSON must stay valid (format.mintick strings).

proposals.title: Stop-distance expectancy curve from the ledger (shadow stops)
proposals.rationale: Traders ask where to put the stop. Under a random walk no stop adds expectancy (Kaminski & Lo); a positive realized E[R] at some distance would be a measurable selection edge. The ledger already holds the sufficient statistics (MAE until the hit or H, d0); only the MTM at H is missing. Since MAE is monotone, 'stopped iff MAE >= s' is exact up to the intrabar rule.
proposals.spec:
1. Trial field endA. In f_step at status 3: endA = side*(close - entry)/atr0.
2. STATE: var array<float> sgSt = array.new<float>(11, 0.0), i.e. [sumR, sumR^2] x grid (0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3 ATR) plus index 10 = n (an array because functions cannot reassign globals).
3. f_book: for [k, s] in the grid, r = mae >= s ? -1 : status == 1 ? d0/s : endA/s; accumulate.
4. Full panel row 'STOP·ATR 0.5 x | 1 x | 1.5 x | 2 x | 3 x (n)', marking cells with |mean| > 2 SE, next to the heat p80 converted to R.
proposals.risk: High variance for small s (show SE). MAE after an early stop-out includes post-stop excursions, which is still correct for the stopped condition. The grid is fixed in ATR at entry.

proposals.title: Invalidation semantics and modes: race barrier, post-raid extreme, protected swing
proposals.rationale: Once the opposing pool is swept, a stop 0.3 ATR beyond it is hit 64-70% of the time on the sweep bar and 92-95% within 12-30 bars (random levels 57-62/90-93%), and rejected-sweep wicks are exceeded 76-82% of the time. The 'invalidation' is a race barrier and should say so. A post-raid stop matches how ICT traders trade, without claiming edge (T4-A: win minus model within ±3 pp).
proposals.spec:
1. Relabel '⊗ INVALIDATION' (2212) to '⊗ OPP. POOL', with a tooltip: 'if this trades before the target the draw failed; once a pool is swept a stop this close is taken about 9 times in 10'.
2. Input invMode = ['Opposing Pool', 'Post-Raid Extreme', 'Protected Swing'] shared with ict_struct ICTS-5.
3. STATE (declared before f_invalidation): var float raidX, var int raidSide, var int raidBar. In step 3 at 1580-1582, when a liquidity pool is hit and the bar closes back inside: set raidSide = lv.side, raidX = bar extreme, raidBar = bar_index; extend raidX while bar_index - raidBar <= raidWin (input, default 20).
4. In f_invalidation, for Post-Raid mode with raidSide == -tgt.side, a recent raid and raidX beyond close: inv = raidX - side*buf; otherwise the current rule.
5. Store the mode on the Trial so race stats are per mode.
proposals.risk: Changing the mode shifts R:R and the ledger race stats (reset or tag by mode). Wider stops show lower R:R, which is honest.

result.summary: The Clean style already reproduces the reference screenshot almost exactly. Composited over black, the engine's fill, the four glow layers (90/80/60/30), the white core, the border, the iFVG fill (#00B478 t75 → #002D1E) and its border, and the label and table colours all match the sampled reference pixels within ±3 RGB units. Text sizes match too: label size.normal is 12 pt and table size.small is 10 pt, consistent with the measured 1.2 ratio of text heights. Treat these constants as the regression baseline and do not re-tune them. The most visible gap is the status line: 76 of 104 input calls are int, float, string, timeframe or session inputs, which default to display.all, so about 76 values print beside the script name while the reference shows only the name. 76 inputs also have no tooltip, and `active` is unused. On a light chart the DOL is invisible: every Clean element composites to 1.04–1.37:1 against white, far below the WCAG 3:1 for graphics. The fix needs two colour roles: dark variants for graphics drawn on the chart, and the neon text kept on the dark label and table, where light variants drop to about 3.1–3.3:1. Lines always render below boxes, so iFVG, LVN and ghost boxes draw over the DOL glow and tether exactly during iFVG retests. Colour is not neutral: red-presented financial data cut risk-taking by about 15–30% in 8 experiments (Management Science 2021), and about 8% of men have red-green CVD (simulated deuteranopia shrinks the bias pair from ΔE 130 to 17). Three proposals communicate WHEN and HOW LIKELY in ways the accuracy ledger can grade: ETA coverage, a counter-draw split and an MTF-alignment split. They rest on evidence that showing uncertainty improves decisions (quantile dotplots reached about 97% of optimal, +5 pp; natural frequencies 7% → 45%). Research limits: the Firecrawl credits and the shared WebSearch budget (5 searches used here) ran out, and WebFetch could not reach w3.org, nature.com or northwestern.edu. A few classic citations are therefore marked unverified; the platform facts come from the local official Pine v6 docs.

concepts.name: Status line (legend) hygiene
concepts.definition: The script status line prints the title plus every input whose `display` includes status_line. Pine default: display.all for int/float/string/timeframe/session/source/price/enum inputs, display.none for bool and color (reference/input.md:27,76; concepts/inputs.md:112). Param is const plot_display, written literally per call.
concepts.dolRole: Indirect: a long legend competes with the single target for attention and wraps over candles; the reference legend shows only the name.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism from official docs (strong); benefit is convention plus the reference look (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 59-216: 76 of 104 input calls lack display=display.none, so about 76 values print in the legend. Data-window plots 2444-2448 are correctly display.data_window.

concepts.name: Input UX (groups, inline, tooltips, active, ordering)
concepts.definition: group headers appear in order of first appearance; inline puts inputs on one row; tooltip adds hover help; `active` (input bool, added July 2025) greys out inputs that depend on other inputs (release_notes.md:506).
concepts.dolRole: Indirect: mis-set sessions or timezone silently mislabel PDH, Asia and killzone levels and so corrupt target selection.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner convention; the Pine manual recommends colour presets (colors.md:400).
concepts.engineNotes: 16 groups (42-57) are good. 76 inputs have no tooltip, including all 10 sessions and tz. `active` is unused. Internals (Scoring, Order Flow) come before display groups.

concepts.name: Reference-fidelity palette and layered glow
concepts.definition: A neon line is N co-linear lines of increasing width and transparency plus a near-white 1 px core. Engine Clean: fill c t92; dashed border c t75; glow (t,w) = (90,10),(80,7),(60,4),(30,2); white t15 w1 core; dashed tether c t30 to the centre at xR = bar_index+20; label #161616 size.normal centred, style_label_left.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: makes the single target the brightest object on the chart.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pixel audit: computed composites #051402/#0A2C03/#135607/#229A0C/#32E112/#E0FADB vs reference #041402/#0A2B04/#135508/#229A0D/#32E113/#DDFCD8. iFVG #002D1E and #00704B exact. The Pine manual endorses layered widths (colors.md:406-410).
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2214-2226, 294-299, 1610-1615 match the reference within ±3 RGB. Treat as the regression baseline.

concepts.name: Visual hierarchy / single focal point
concepts.definition: Visual weight (contrast × area × saturation) ranks elements by importance. Engine on black: core 18.9:1 > glow 11.9 > tether 7.5 > iFVG border 3.4 > DOL border 2.15 > fills 1.1-1.4.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: one committed target, not a menu of levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pine manual: 'When you make everything stand out, nothing does' (colors.md:398). More information raises confidence more than accuracy (Tsai, Klayman & Hastie 2008) [unverified this session].
concepts.engineNotes: Extras (secondary, objective, invalidation, reach, pool, LVN, ghosts) are off by default (162-171, 203, 210).

concepts.name: Contrast and theme adaptivity
concepts.definition: WCAG contrast = (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05): text 4.5:1 (large 3:1), graphics 3:1 (SC 1.4.3, 1.4.11; line charts in scope). Pine: chart.bg_color and chart.fg_color (input color); fg = #0f0f0f on light backgrounds and #dbdbdb on dark; the manual's light test is chart.fg_color == #0f0f0f.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: below 3:1 the target is not perceived.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Computed on white: buy #39FF14 1.36, bias green 2.22, iFVG 2.69, LVN 1.60. Rendered Clean zone 1.04-1.37 for every element. Light variants: #0B7A2E 5.47, #C8102E 5.88. Generic darkening color.from_gradient(0.55,0,1,c,#000000) gives at least 5.08:1 for all 17 theme colours.
concepts.engineNotes: Theme palettes 228-292 are dark-only; no use of chart.bg_color or fg_color. The white core (2223), transparent-bg labels (1256, 2166, 2189, 2212) and LVN text (2278) are unreadable on white.

concepts.name: Colour semantics by draw side
concepts.definition: Colour encodes draw side (above price = buy-side lime, below = sell-side red), not kind, which is why 'Target: BEFVG' above price is green in the reference.
concepts.dolRole: WHERE and direction at a glance; colour also shifts willingness to act.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Bazley, Cronqvist & Mormann 2021 (Management Science 67(9)): in 8 experiments red-presented data lowered risk-taking by about 15-30% vs black and prolonged pessimism; absent in colour-blind subjects; yellow and blue had no effect.

concepts.name: Colour-vision-deficiency safety and redundant encoding
concepts.definition: Hue-only cues fail for about 8% of men (1 in 12; women about 0.4-0.5%) with red-green CVD. Remedy: a blue/orange palette plus redundant cues (position, text, glyph, line style).
concepts.dolRole: WHERE and bias readable for every user.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Birch 2012 (PubMed 22472762), MedlinePlus. Machado-2009 simulation: deuteranopia ΔE bias pair 17 (from 130), DOL pair 37 (from 170); proposed #2F9BFF/#FF8A1F ΔE 134.
concepts.engineNotes: Redundancy exists through position and the BULLISH/BEARISH words. No CVD theme; the bias pair relies on hue.

concepts.name: Typography
concepts.definition: v6 sizes accept size.* or int points. Labels: tiny≈7, small≈10, normal 12, large 18, huge 24. Tables and boxes: tiny 8, small 10, normal 14, large 20, huge 36. text_formatting gives bold or italic; font is default or monospace.
concepts.dolRole: Readability of target name, PoT and bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official docs (text_and_shapes.md:488-500, label.md:177). Measured reference label/table text height ratio 1.2 = 12/10.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean label size.normal (2226), table size.small default font (608-610), Terminal monospace. No size input.

concepts.name: Probability communication (value, precision, horizon, reference class)
concepts.definition: A PoT readout should carry its horizon ('within H bars') and reference class ('K of N similar targets hit'), with precision no finer than the calibration supports.
concepts.dolRole: HOW LIKELY: lets the trader weigh the target correctly.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Natural frequencies 7% → 45% correct (Hoffrage et al. 2015). Uncertainty displays about 97% of optimal, +5 pp vs control, better than text (Fernandes et al. CHI 2018). Precision read as confidence (Jerez-Fernandez et al. 2014, moderate).
concepts.engineNotes: 'PoT: 70.1%' without horizon or n (2225). Shows 95.0% on a reached target (2067). Tooltip 2206-2209 lacks price, horizon and calibration (COMP-4).

concepts.name: Timing communication (ETA)
concepts.definition: Empirical median and p80 of bars-to-hit for past hits from a similar ATR distance (±0.5 ATR, n≥5), conditional on a hit.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: expected time to reach the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Showing time uncertainty improved decisions (Fernandes 2018). ETA validity for this tool is unmeasured, hence the coverage check in UX-4.
concepts.engineNotes: etaHit computed at 2117-2126, shown only in the Terminal HUD (2240). No p80, no calibration; the Clean right edge (extBars=20) carries no time meaning.

concepts.name: Tooltips as progressive disclosure
concepts.definition: Keep the chart minimal and put detail on hover: label.new(tooltip), table.cell(tooltip) (reference/table.md:53,69). Boxes and lines have no tooltips; mobile has no hover.
concepts.dolRole: Answers why this target, at what price, by when and how calibrated, without clutter.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Convention; the idea that recreating an object closes an open tooltip is an untested hypothesis.
concepts.engineNotes: Label tooltip present (2206, 2226, 2248). Table cells have none (604-610, 2294-2307).

concepts.name: Z-order and layering
concepts.definition: Ascending z groups: bgcolor < fills < plots < hlines < linefills < lines < boxes < labels < tables. Within a group, the last created is on top. Only plot, hline and fill can use explicit_plot_zorder (visuals/overview.md:230-246).
concepts.dolRole: WHERE: overlays must not dim the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official documentation.
concepts.engineNotes: Glow and tether are lines (2219-2224), so iFVG boxes (fill t75, 1613), LVN (t91, 2276-2286) and ghost boxes (t94, 1254) draw over them where they overlap, typically during iFVG retests.

concepts.name: Right-edge layout and label collisions
concepts.definition: Labels at xR with style_label_left collide when their price gap is less than the label height (2-line normal ≈ 36 px ≈ 4-7% of the visible range at default zoom). Fix by staggering x or folding into the tooltip.
concepts.dolRole: Legibility when optional targets are shown.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Practitioner convention.
concepts.engineNotes: Secondary (2188), objective (2166), invalidation (2212) and LVN text (2278) all anchor at xR with no de-overlap. Clean default (one label) is unaffected.

concepts.name: Drawing-object lifecycle
concepts.definition: Limits of 500 lines, boxes and labels with GC of the oldest; x ≤ bar_index+500. Setters cost less than delete+new: the manual's profile shows box.new ≈ 2× two setters (profiling_and_optimization.md:1074-1112).
concepts.dolRole: Smooth realtime updates on fast symbols.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official profiler example; UX benefits (tooltip and selection stability) are hypotheses.
concepts.engineNotes: iFVG boxes use set_right (1638-1641, 2145-2149). The Clean zone, 5 glow lines, tether and label (8 objects) are deleted and recreated every tick (2132-2141, 2214-2226). Caps are safe.

concepts.name: Data Window / plot formatting
concepts.definition: plot(format, precision) sets the digits in the Data Window, status line and scale (reference/plot.md:244-245).
concepts.dolRole: Clean numeric readouts for score, PoT and D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Official docs (mechanism); benefit weak.
concepts.engineNotes: Plots 2444-2448 have no precision and inherit the symbol's (e.g. 5 decimals on FX).

concepts.name: Bias table design and alignment cue
concepts.definition: Two-column Timeframe | Bias table. Reference: header #25272C / #D5D5D6, body #1B1F24, grid #3A3C43, frame #303136, BULLISH #00C864, BEARISH #E63C3C, 20 px rows. Usage doctrine: act when the Exec TF bias aligns with the HTF bias.
concepts.dolRole: Bias and direction filter for the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Alignment is practitioner doctrine; BEARISH contrast is 4.00:1 (faithful to the reference).
concepts.engineNotes: The look is exact (294-299, 2294-2307). No alignment cue, no cell tooltips, no size option, no ledger split by alignment.

concepts.name: Autoscale compression
concepts.definition: Drawings far from price widen auto-scale and squash candles; the user fix is 'Scale price chart only'.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps the price action readable around the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView help 43000762934 (via competitors.md).
concepts.engineNotes: LVN (2250-2287), objective and reach bands are not distance-capped (COMP-7).

concepts.name: Target state communication
concepts.definition: States: draw-side active, counter-draw active, reached (intrabar), stale (age > H with no hit), filtered (PoT < min), none; each should be visible without relying on hue.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents silent state changes being read as 'the target jumped'; flags weaker counter-draw picks.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Convention; the counter-draw ledger split in UX-3 would measure it.
concepts.engineNotes: Terminal shows COUNTER-DRAW and SWEPT (2237). Clean shows counter-draw only in the tooltip (2206), reached as 95% (2067), and stale or filtered silently.

concepts.name: Confidence encoded as visual weight
concepts.definition: Map PoT or score to opacity, glow or blur, bounded so low-confidence targets stay visible.
concepts.dolRole: HOW LIKELY, pre-attentively.
concepts.evidenceNotes: MacEachren et al. 2012: transparency and fuzziness judged intuitive uncertainty cues [unverified this session].
concepts.engineNotes: Terminal maps score to zone opacity (2228); Clean uses fixed weights.

proposals.title: Legend and settings hygiene: display.none, active map, group order, tooltips, text-size inputs, Data Window precision
proposals.rationale: About 76 input values print in the status line while the reference legend shows only the name: the most visible clutter and the cheapest fix. Greyed-out irrelevant inputs and tooltips (sessions and timezone first) prevent silent misconfiguration that corrupts PDH, Asia and killzone levels. Same core finding as COMP-1; adds the verified dependency map and precision.
proposals.spec: (1) Add the literal `display = display.none` to all 76 input.int/float/string/timeframe/session calls (59-216); optionally modeIn = display.status_line. (2) active map (usages grepped): cHTF/cSTF/cEXE active = modeIn == "Custom"; sessAs/sessLo/sessNA = useSess; fvgMin/fvgQMin = useFVG; obLook/obQMin/useBRK = useOB; lvnHours/lvnRows = showLVN or usePathVP (both feed needVP at 979, 1009, 1902); lvnThr/lvnN = showLVN; ghostMax = showGhost; hudSize = uiStyle == "Terminal"; priorM = potModel == "Empirical"; tablePosIn = showTable; uAbove..uText = theme == "Custom". Keep dispMult, ifvgMaxIn and ifvgMax always active. (3) Reorder groups (Pine lists them by first appearance): Trading Mode, DOL Display, PoT, Theme, Panel, iFVG, Ghost, Volume Profile, Liquidity, Key Liquidity, Imbalances, Sessions & Killzones, then 'Advanced · Scoring / Order Flow / Engine / Accuracy'. Move the derived tfH/tfS/tfE and theme colours with their inputs to avoid forward references. (4) Tooltips for the 76 inputs without one: sessions 'HHMM-HHMM in Session Timezone (default America/New_York)', tz as an IANA name, weights 'normalised, only ratios matter', potH 'chance of touch within this many chart bars', extBars 'reference look: 20'. (5) lblPt = input.int(12, 'Label Text (pt)', 6, 24) used as size = lblPt in the Clean label (2226); tblPt = input.int(10, 'Panel Text (pt)') used as text_size in f_cell/f_cellC (604-610). Labels take series int/string (label.md:177); 12/10 equal normal/small, so fidelity is kept. (6) Plots 2445-2448: precision = 1 (score, PoT, hit %), 2 (D).
proposals.risk: Users lose inputs in the legend. Reordering about 170 lines risks a forward reference; keep each derived variable next to its inputs and run pine_parse.sh.

proposals.title: Theme-aware rendering for light charts: two colour roles plus a light glow recipe
proposals.rationale: On white every Clean DOL element is 1.04-1.37:1, so the target is invisible; the Pine manual asks authors to test light and dark. COMP-8's single swap would break the dark-backed label and table: light variants on #161616 are 3.1-3.3:1, while the neon text there is 13.35:1. So graphics and text need separate colour roles.
proposals.spec: Global after line 292: bgMode = input.string('Auto', 'Chart Background', ['Auto','Dark','Light'], display.none); lightBg = bgMode == 'Light' or (bgMode == 'Auto' and chart.fg_color == #0f0f0f) (doc test, chart_information.md:431,449; input-qualified). f_onLight(color x) => color.from_gradient(0.55, 0.0, 1.0, x, #000000) gives at least 5.08:1 on white for all 17 theme colours. Graphics roles: gAbove = lightBg ? (classic ? #0B7A2E : f_onLight(cAbove)) : cAbove; gBelow likewise with #C8102E; gIBull #00875A; gIBear f_onLight; gLVN #9A6B00; gGhost #5F6B7A. Use g* for zone, glow, tether, iFVG boxes (1612), ghosts (1253-1257), LVN (2276-2286), and the secondary/objective/invalidation lines and their transparent-bg labels. Keep c* (neon) for the Clean label text (2225), table (2294-2307) and Terminal HUD on dark panels. Light glow (replaces 2219-2223 when lightBg): halo (t85, w8), (t70, w4), core g t0 w2, no white filament; fill t90; border t45; tether t20. On white: core 5.47, tether 3.75, border about 2.6, fill 1.15. iFVG light: fill t80, border t40. cLblBg and table colours unchanged. Mock: study/ux_tools/mock_light_theme.png.
proposals.risk: Gradient backgrounds return the midpoint (the override covers this). Assumes a chart-background change triggers recalculation like an input change; verify in TradingView. About 8 extra colour variables.

proposals.title: Clean label state grammar (counter-draw, reached, stale) with a counter-draw ledger split
proposals.rationale: Clean hides states a trader must know: counter-draw targets look identical to draw-side ones, reached targets read 'PoT: 95.0%', and over-horizon targets look fresh. Showing them, and the measured track record of counter-draw picks, also tests the decision-history rule 'draw-side first, counter-draw fallback' with data.
proposals.spec: Clean branch 2214-2226. Counter-draw (activeCtr, 2029): line 1 'Target: BSL ⚠', tether line.style_dotted, tooltip first line 'Counter-draw: order flow D = -0.42 points the other way'. Reached (sweptNow): line 2 '✓ Reached', core solid c t0 (with COMP-4). Stale (bar_index - activeSince > H and not hit): line 2 'PoT: 41.0% · late', textcolor color.new(c, 35). Ledger: add bool ctr to Trial (375-396), set in f_openTrial (1426). The global var bool activeCtr (1038) precedes it and is assigned at 2029 before the call at 2045; it can be read directly or passed as an argument. In f_book (1461) accumulate var array<float> ctrSt(6): n, k, ΣpBase for draw-side and counter-draw. Tooltip 'Counter-draw targets here: 18 of 47 hit (38%) · edge -2.1 pp vs random'; Terminal Full row CTR/DRAW. ⚠ is already used at 2237 and 2306, so it renders.
proposals.risk: The ⚠ suffix changes the reference text in the counter-draw state only. The stale threshold equals H by choice.

proposals.title: Time projection (WHEN): ETA band in the tooltip or as markers, plus an ETA coverage check in the ledger
proposals.rationale: The engine already computes median bars-to-hit for similar distances (2117-2126) but Clean never shows it, and users ask 'when?'. Showing a p50-p80 band uses the evidence that displayed uncertainty improves decisions. The ledger can verify calibration: about 50% of hits should arrive by p50 and 80% by p80.
proposals.spec: Helper after dHit (1075) and before f_openTrial (1426): f_eta(float dNow) builds sim from dHit/ttHit within ±0.5 ATR; float p50 = na, p80 = na; if sim.size() >= 5, p50 := sim.median(), p80 := sim.percentile_linear_interpolation(80); return [p50, p80] (if-block, not a ternary on tuples). It replaces the loop at 2120-2126. Input etaMode = 'Off'/'Tooltip'(default)/'Marker'. Tooltip: 'Typically reached in 6-14 bars (≈30-70 min) when reached · n 37'. Marker: dotted vertical line at x = bar_index + min(500, p50) spanning zone top to bottom, color.new(c,40), and a second at p80 color.new(c,70); extend the zone's right edge to bar_index + p80 if larger than extBars. Ledger: Trial gets eta50, eta80 set in f_openTrial via f_eta(d0) (loop ≤ 300, only at commit). In f_book on a hit: etaSt += [1, bars <= eta50, bars <= eta80]. Terminal Accuracy row 'ETA cover 48% / 79% (n 63)' (about 50/80 means calibrated).
proposals.risk: The ETA is conditional on a hit and must be labelled 'when reached'. It needs n ≥ 5 similar hits. Bars are not clock time across sessions (use COMP-4's f_dur with '≈'). Marker mode changes the reference look, so the default is Tooltip.

proposals.title: Bias table: alignment cue, cell tooltips, optional accuracy row, and a ledger split by MTF alignment
proposals.rationale: The reference's usage advice is to act when the Exec bias aligns with the HTF bias, but the table never states alignment or ties it to the target, and nobody knows whether aligned targets do better. A ledger split turns the doctrine into per-symbol evidence.
proposals.spec: On confirmed bars at commit (after 2029): bH = htfBias != 0 ? htfBias : htfIB; bE likewise for exe; algn = na(activeLv) ? 0 : (bH == side and bE == side) ? 1 : bH == -side ? -1 : 0. Keep it in var int activeAlgn declared in STATE (1020-1080) or pass it to f_openTrial; add int algn to Trial. In f_book accumulate var array<float> alSt(9): n, k, ΣpBase for aligned/neutral/against. Terminal Full shows 'ALIGN +9.2pp (n 88) · AGAINST -1.0pp (n 41)'. Clean table input tblExtra = 'None'(default)/'Target row'/'Target + Accuracy'. Target row: 'DOL' | '✓ ▲ BEFVG' (✓ aligned, ⚠ against), side colour. Accuracy row: 'Hit 62% · Edge +8pp' from stK, stN, stPE ('calibrating' under 20). f_cellC gains string tip = '' passed as table.cell(..., tooltip = tip). Per-TF tooltip, e.g. 'Swing BULL (body break of X) · internal BEAR · price at 62% of range (premium)', from htfRH/htfRL/htfIB and the other TFs; built only at barstate.islast.
proposals.risk: Extra rows deviate from the 3-row reference, so they are off by default. The split needs enough trials per class (show n).

proposals.title: Colour-vision-safe theme and optional direction glyph
proposals.rationale: About 8% of male traders have red-green CVD. Under deuteranopia the bias pair collapses to ΔE 17 and the DOL pair to ΔE 37. Red also lowers risk-taking by about 15-30% in experiments, so a hue-neutral option is useful even for non-CVD users.
proposals.spec: Add theme 'Colorblind' to the theme options (228) and each colour switch (240-292): above/bull #2F9BFF, below/bear #FF8A1F, LVN #F0E442, ghost #7D8799, panel #0B0F14, text #E6EDF3. Computed: deutan ΔE 134, protan ΔE 119; on the #161616 label 6.25/7.68; on the table 5.72/7.02. Light variants with UX-2: #0072B2/#C25400 (5.19/4.60 on white). Input glyph = input.bool(false, 'Direction Glyph in Label') prefixes '▲ ' or '▼ ' to Clean line 1; auto-on when theme is Colorblind.
proposals.risk: None to the default theme.

proposals.title: Persistent DOL drawing objects updated with setters instead of per-tick delete/recreate
proposals.rationale: Clean deletes and recreates 8 objects (zone, 5 glow lines, tether, label) on every realtime tick (2132-2141, 2214-2226). The official profiler example shows box.new costing about 2× two setter calls. Recreation may also reset hover tooltips or selection on fast symbols (hypothesis).
proposals.spec: type DolGfx (box zone, line teth, label lbl, array<line> glow); var DolGfx gx = DolGfx.new(na, na, na, array.new<line>()). On barstate.islast, if the DOL is shown: create once when na(gx.zone), else box.set_lefttop/set_rightbottom/set_bgcolor/set_border_color/set_border_style, line.set_xy1/set_xy2/set_color/set_width/set_style, label.set_xy/set_text/set_textcolor/set_color/set_tooltip/set_size. If not shown: delete all and reset to na. Recreate on a dark/light layer-count change (5 vs 3 glow lines). Keep the dB/dLn/dLb arrays for the extras. Validate with the Pine Profiler.
proposals.risk: Stale objects if the hide branch is missed. The UX benefit is an unverified hypothesis.

proposals.title: Layering and right-edge collision management (fade overlapping iFVG fills, stagger colliding labels)
proposals.rationale: Lines render below boxes, so iFVG (t75), LVN and ghost boxes dim the DOL glow and tether where they overlap, which is common during the iFVG retests the product promotes. Optional right-edge labels can overprint the DOL label.
proposals.spec: Add color col to Zone (348-359), set to ic at creation (1609-1621). In the barstate.islast loop (2145-2149): dolVis = showDOL and not na(activeLv) and dolShown; for z in ifvgs, if not na(z.bx): ov = dolVis and z.top >= activeLv.bottom and z.bottom <= activeLv.top; onTeth = dolVis and z spans the close-to-price path; box.set_bgcolor(z.bx, color.new(z.col, ov ? 92 : onTeth ? 85 : base)), with base 75 Classic Clean else 85. v6 lazy and/or prevents na access. Skip LVN zones that overlap the active zone (2276-2286). Collision manager when extras are on: global float rng = ta.highest(high,150) - ta.lowest(low,150) (computed every bar); minSep = 0.05*rng. Place labels by priority DOL > invalidation > objective > secondaries; one within minSep of a placed label is staggered to x = xR + 14k bars (k = 1..3, ≤ bar_index+500), with its line extended so the pointer stays on its price. After 3 attempts, fold it into the DOL tooltip ('Also near: PDH 5,131.5'). Do not use chart.left_visible_bar_time: it recalculates on every scroll.
proposals.risk: minSep is a zoom-dependent heuristic. Fading an overlapping iFVG slightly changes the reference look in that case only.

proposals.title: Confidence-weighted glow (bounded; reference look at PoT 70%)
proposals.rationale: Clean renders a 35% PoT target with the same brightness as an 85% one. Transparency is an intuitive uncertainty cue, and a bounded mapping keeps the reference look at about 70% PoT.
proposals.spec: Input confGlow = input.bool(false, 'Confidence-Weighted Glow', group = G_DOL). g = na(activePoT) ? 1.0 : f_clamp((activePoT - 0.40)/0.30, 0, 1). Outer glow transparencies 90+6(1-g), 80+8(1-g), 60+10(1-g); the t30 layer and core are unchanged so the line stays at least 3:1. color.new takes float transp (color.md:116). Applies to the dark recipe at 2219-2221 and to the light halo in UX-2.
proposals.risk: Low-PoT targets look dimmer but never vanish (bounded). Off by default for exact fidelity. The evidence (MacEachren 2012) was not re-verified this session.

result.summary: Almost every tested ICT/SMC "magnet" claim reduces to geometry. Pools, FVGs, order blocks, PDH/PDL and session extremes are reached at the rate of a random level at the same distance (FVG 73.0% vs 72.9%, OB 73.7% vs 73.7%, PDH/PDL within ±3 pp of a clock-matched null). Only small, short-lived effects survive: S/R bounces 60.8% vs 56.2% (Osler 2000), FVG/OB reactions of +2.5-5 pp at minutes, and the stop-cluster mechanism itself. Directional ICT claims (AMD, sweep→reversal, structure-based draw) carry no information beyond the trend regime or gambler's-ruin geometry. Base rates are high: a random level 1/2/3 ATR away is traded through within 30 bars 75-80/54-62/39-47% of the time, and "take the nearer pool" wins which-side-first 64.5-70.6%. Raw hit rates are therefore meaningless. The engine's ledger is leak-free, and its distance-matched, regime-split baseline is the right kind: it even absorbs trend beta, which a model-free mirror comparison would credit as +8 to +11 pp of skill on EURUSD/GC 1h. Four readouts are biased by construction (this study). ETA|hit is 2-3× too optimistic and never says ">H". "Heat" over hits only is about half the real adverse excursion (1.6-2.3 vs 3.2-5.1 ATR). The HUD "EV" is E[R|race decided], which shows −0.3 to −1.0R for fair far targets. L50 is a raw rate that tracks distance. The EDGE z is roughly sized at one look but has three problems: (a) peeking, 10-20% false "✓ EDGE"; (b) baseline miscalibration, which shifts it by −4 to +3 pp on real data (GC roll gaps, clock windows); (c) an uncentred, booking-keyed 2H-block variance, which is conservative under seasonality and detects a real +3.3 pp edge 10% vs 30% of the time. A mirror control (the same ATR distance on the opposite side, same bar, same rule) cuts the bias from mean |z| 0.69 to 0.24 on real data. A martingale R-expectancy test needs no baseline model at all. At default depth the minimum detectable edge is 5.5-9.5 pp (anytime-valid), larger than any supported ICT effect, so "NO EDGE" usually means "not measurable". The proposals make the claims honest: survivorship-free readouts, mirror-controlled anytime-valid edge with MDE, corrected variance, R-expectancy, a paired league against strong naive selectors, null-default ICT modifiers, a forward-only ledger, honest wording, multiple-comparison discipline and an audit trail.

concepts.name: Stop clusters beyond extremes / round numbers (liquidity mechanism)
concepts.definition: Stop-loss orders cluster just beyond round numbers and old extremes (stop-buys at 01-10 above '00', stop-sells at 90-99 below); take-profits cluster at the round number. Crossing a stop cluster triggers a cascade.
concepts.dolRole: Explains WHY pools beyond swing highs/lows are targets and why trade-through accelerates (continuation for 15 min to 2 h).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler 2003 JF: 9,667 orders, 8.7% at 00 vs ~1% uniform; stop-buys 14.4% vs 7.4% (p=0.029). Osler 2005: cascades significant 15 min-2 h, not 1-2 days.
concepts.engineNotes: Pools beyond pivots with strict trade-through (624, 1848); no round-number source (sibling ICT-3).

concepts.name: Pools as magnets (reach beyond geometry)
concepts.definition: Claim: an unswept BSL/SSL/PDH/session extreme is reached within H more often than a random level at the same distance, side and regime.
concepts.dolRole: Would justify ranking pools above plain distance for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: External pools −0.14/−0.27 logit vs random (calib_ml); PDH/PDL take rates within ±3 pp of a day-bootstrap null on 7 markets (session_stats). Geometry explains the outcome.
concepts.engineNotes: The source tier adds density (1.2·tier, 682; f_tierW 506-516) and confluence weight 15 (674-680), both assuming a magnet effect that measures negative.

concepts.name: Equal highs/lows (EQH/EQL)
concepts.definition: Two or more pivots within eqTol (0.10 ATR), merged into one pool that moves to the outermost print.
concepts.dolRole: Small positive modifier on reach for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: +0.08/+0.29 logit (t 0.7/3.6, 5m/1h, calib_ml). A distance-matched open-source test found <1% improvement.
concepts.engineNotes: eqCount ×0.9 in density (682); f_mergeAt. Weight is not learned.

concepts.name: Sweep → reversal (turtle soup / raid-and-reverse)
concepts.definition: Price trades through a pool and closes back inside within 1-2 bars; the claim is that it then runs to the opposite pool.
concepts.dolRole: Would flip the draw side after a raid (WHICH side next).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Post-sweep ±1 ATR race 0.497-0.510 for hold and reject alike (quant_regime). 65/66 walk-forward folds favour continuation (Mahadzva SSRN, secondary confirmation). Mesfin 2026: the liquidity-grab reversal family failed out of sample.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt in D encodes hold→continuation / reject→reversal (1535, 1894) without support.

concepts.name: FVG fill / magnet
concepts.definition: 3-candle gap (low > high[2]); claim: price returns to fill it more than to a random same-size zone at the same distance.
concepts.dolRole: Array targets for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 73.0% vs 72.9% random twins (38k FVGs); S&P daily 69% vs 69%; BTC +3.2 pp; a placebo-control script found no advantage in 14 measurements.
concepts.engineNotes: FVG targets with a quality gate (1867-1887); touch hit rule. Fine as a level source; no magnet bonus beyond the hand-set density.

concepts.name: FVG / CE reaction
concepts.definition: Price reacts (bounces) at the gap or its 50% midpoint.
concepts.dolRole: Timing/turn points, not reach.
