concepts.evidenceNotes: About 5 pp above random, not tradeable (Barot SSRN 7148099); edge ratio +3.7% at 5 min, −0.2% at 1 h (Nordman).
concepts.engineNotes: The engine targets arrays; it does not trade reactions.

concepts.name: iFVG polarity flip
concepts.definition: A body close through an FVG inverts it into opposite S/R; retests are claimed to hold.
concepts.dolRole: Continuation retest zones shown to the trader.
concepts.evidenceNotes: S&P daily: held 38% vs 38% random (bullish), 47% vs 47% (bearish). Single source.
concepts.engineNotes: iFVG tracker and boxes; no statistic of retest success vs random (sibling ICTPD-8).

concepts.name: Order blocks / breakers / mitigation blocks
concepts.definition: OB = last opposite candle before the displacement leg that broke structure; breaker = a failed OB that took liquidity.
concepts.dolRole: Array targets for WHERE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: OB revisit 73.7% vs 73.7% random; next-bar reaction +3-5% at 1-5 min; negative after costs. Breakers and other blocks have no audited stats.
concepts.engineNotes: OB/breaker targets with quality gates; no evidence-based prior.

concepts.name: Killzone volatility (timing)
concepts.definition: Volatility concentrated in session opens: Asia 20-00, London 02-05, NY AM 07-10 ET.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: the speed of reach and the PoT within H depend on the volatility clock.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ES 5m variance 4.7× the mean at 09:30, 0.20× at 23:30; 2.1-4.0× peak/quiet across 10 instruments (Andersen-Bollerslev; quant_pot; ict_time).
concepts.engineNotes: Killzones used for hysteresis (kzHx) and affinity; PoT uses a trailing 50-bar σ (916), not a clock.

concepts.name: Session raid affinities (London raids Asia, NY raids London/PD)
concepts.definition: Fixed multipliers ×1.05-1.20 on session/PD pools during killzones.
concepts.dolRole: WHICH key level is targeted per session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Within ±3 pp of a clock-matched null; exception: the Asia range's opposite side +3.5-6.2 pp on index futures (session_stats).
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff 597-602 applied at 1941, unconditionally and unmeasured.

concepts.name: AMD / Power of 3 / Judas swing
concepts.definition: London breaches one side of the Asia range by ≥δ and closes back inside; NY delivers to the opposite Asia extreme.
concepts.dolRole: Directional bias and timing for the NY session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Taylor 2026 (N=484, NQ 15m): bullish 46.9% (coin flip), bearish 39.9% (inverted); trend-aligned 62-71%, trend-opposed 25-30%; 57% of targets delivered before the 09:40 entry.
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented; the evidence says do not add it as a directional rule.

concepts.name: Structure-based draw vector (BOS/CHoCH)
concepts.definition: D = 0.5·HTF + 0.3·STF + 0.2·exe internal bias, blended with displacement and liquidity events; draw-side-first selection.
concepts.dolRole: Chooses WHICH side's liquidity is targeted.
concepts.evidenceNotes: D-proxy 49.9-51.6% for which side first; D-first selection loses 9-12 pp of first-touch accuracy vs geometry intraday; ER gating recovers it (quant_regime, bias_dol).
concepts.engineNotes: 1891-1895, 1975, 2000-2012 (2× side-flip hysteresis), counter-draw ×0.5 at 693.

concepts.name: Premium/discount
concepts.definition: Above 50% of the dealing range = sell zone; below = buy zone.
concepts.dolRole: Bias for which side to target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No ICT statistics; the academic analogue (52-week high, George & Hwang 2004) shows continuation, the opposite.
concepts.engineNotes: Dealing-range EQ used as a confluence anchor (1931) and shown in the Terminal panel.

concepts.name: S/R tests and bounce memory
concepts.definition: b_prev = number of prior bounces at a level; claim (folk): more tests weaken the level.
concepts.dolRole: Whether a tested pool is more or less likely to be traded through within H.
concepts.evidenceNotes: p(bounce|b_prev) > 0.5 and rising with b_prev (Garzarelli 2014, p<0.0001); decays to 0.5 at ~350-900 min (Chung & Bellotti 2021). Osler 2000: published levels 60.8% vs 56.2% random.
concepts.engineNotes: tests add +0.35 each to density (652-656, 682): the opposite sign for a short-horizon trade-through target.

concepts.name: Random-walk touch probability
concepts.definition: P(touch d within H) = 2Φ(−d/(σ√H)); empirical: random levels at 1/2/3 ATR touched 75-80/54-62/39-47% within 30 bars.
concepts.dolRole: The base rate any PoT must match; HOW LIKELY.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Reflection principle; this study's survivorship.py on 7 datasets; quant_pot: the Empirical model's ECE is 0.004.
concepts.engineNotes: f_pot 434-444, empirical surface f_empPoT 1284-1300; drift term is wrong (QPOT-01).

concepts.name: Gambler's ruin: nearest-first
concepts.definition: P(up level first) = b/(a+b) for any continuous martingale.
concepts.dolRole: Strong naive baseline for WHICH side is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Real races within 0.4-1.2 pp (quant_pot); the nearer-first rule scores 0.645-0.706 (quant_regime).
concepts.engineNotes: f_race 447-461 exists, but the race uses drift (1361-1363) and WIN% has no geometric reference.

concepts.name: Martingale expectancy (optional stopping / Wald)
concepts.definition: For any bounded exit rule, E[R] = side·μ·E[τ]/risk; with no drift, E[R] = 0 for every target/stop choice.
concepts.dolRole: A model-free test of whether targets pay; turns avg R into an edge statistic.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Theory; real races near-martingale (quant_pot).
concepts.engineNotes: rOut computed conservatively (1457-1458), avg R/PF in Full view only (2419-2425), with no band and no beta adjustment.

concepts.name: Arcsine law for timing of extremes
concepts.definition: The time of a Brownian max on [0,T] has density 1/(π√(t(T−t))); window edges are over-represented.
concepts.dolRole: WHEN: separates real timing effects from arithmetic.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Weekday-of-extreme stats equal a day-order shuffle (session_stats, ict_time).
concepts.engineNotes: No timing claims in the engine beyond killzones.

concepts.name: Base-rate trap
concepts.definition: Reporting a hit rate without the expected rate for the same distances.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents mistaking geometry for skill.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Random 1-ATR levels hit 75-80% within 30 bars (this study).
concepts.engineNotes: EDGE pp shown (2398-2401), but the DOL HIT row (2393) and L50 (2395) are raw; family rows have no expected rate (2410-2418).

concepts.name: Survivorship in time-to-hit and adverse excursion
concepts.definition: Statistics computed over hits only, ignoring censored misses.
concepts.dolRole: Honest WHEN (ETA) and pain (heat).
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: ETA|hit 9 bars vs a true median of 19-25 at 2 ATR, and '>30' at 3 ATR; heat|hit 1.6-2.3 vs 3.2-5.1 ATR for all trials.
concepts.engineNotes: ETA 2116-2127 (dHit/ttHit), heat 1481-1483 and 2404 (maeHit only when y=1).

concepts.name: Decided-race conditioning (EV bias)
concepts.definition: EV = P(win|decided by H)·rr − P(loss|decided), which ignores the undecided mass.
concepts.dolRole: Honest trade expectancy.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study's MC: shown −0.62R (a=2R, σ√H=1R) and −0.97R (3R) while the true E[R] = 0.
concepts.engineNotes: tEV at 2359, from f_invalidation (1343-1364) with drift.

concepts.name: Overlap / cluster-robust variance
concepts.definition: Variance of Σ(y − p) for overlapping H-bar windows: blocks keyed by open bar, centred, at least a session wide.
concepts.dolRole: A correct uncertainty for the edge.
concepts.evidenceNotes: This study: engine-style z sd 0.76 under seasonal null; detection of +3.3 pp 10% vs 30% with centred 8H blocks; wide blocks sd 0.99-1.06.
concepts.engineNotes: cluSt 1463-1469: uncentred, booking-keyed, 2H blocks; vEdge 2385.

concepts.name: Baseline miscalibration and placebo/mirror control
concepts.definition: The baseline is a model; its bias for the picker's mix of distances, hours and sides shifts the excess. Control: subtract a no-skill comparator graded on the same bars (mirror level at the same distance, opposite side).
concepts.dolRole: Makes the EDGE test measure skill, not model error.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Real-data placebo excess −4.0 pp (GC 1h) to +1.0 pp; clock windows ±2-3 pp; the mirror control cuts mean |bias z| 0.69 → 0.24; paired placebo z sd 0.96, false alarms 2.6%.
concepts.engineNotes: No placebo, mirror or baseline-calibration check.

concepts.name: Beta masquerading as skill
concepts.definition: A trend-side bias in a trending sample looks like directional skill.
concepts.dolRole: Separates trend beta from the engine's level/side skill.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Always-long vs mirror +8.3±3.9 pp (EURUSD 1h), +10.8±6.2 (GC 1h).
concepts.engineNotes: The regime-split surface (1059-1062, 1287) absorbs it for the hit test; the R test needs a drift adjustment (missing).

concepts.name: Peeking / anytime-valid inference
concepts.definition: A fixed-α test re-checked every bar inflates false positives; the fix is confidence sequences / e-processes.
concepts.dolRole: An honest verdict on HOW LIKELY the engine's edge is real.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Johari et al. 2017; Howard et al. 2021; calib_ml sim: 10/15/20% false ✓ EDGE at 100/300/1,000 trials.
concepts.engineNotes: z≥2 / z≥1 verdict at 2390, re-evaluated continuously.

concepts.name: Multiple testing / forking paths / in-sample tuning
concepts.definition: Many charts × families × settings; the best-looking result is selected; MinBTL; t>3 hurdles.
concepts.dolRole: Prevents users from trusting a lucky chart or setting.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sullivan-Timmermann-White 1999; Bailey et al. PBO/MinBTL; Harvey-Liu; Coqueret (4.5 bootstrap vs 8.2 paths). This study: 10 charts → 21% (80% with peeking) chance of a false EDGE; best of 45 settings E[max z]=2.21.
concepts.engineNotes: Family rows without correction (2410-2418); no forward-only ledger; no in-sample disclosure.

concepts.name: Power / minimum detectable effect
concepts.definition: MDE ≈ (z_crit + z_power)·SE.
concepts.dolRole: Distinguishes 'no edge' from 'not measurable'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Active ledger SE 1.4-2.4 pp per 5,000 bars → MDE 5.5-9.5 pp anytime-valid at defaults.
concepts.engineNotes: The verdict prints '✕ NO EDGE' regardless of MDE (2390).

concepts.name: Destination vs next liquidity
concepts.definition: 'Next taken' is a first-passage question over all pools (nearest first); a destination is the outermost pool of the leg.
concepts.dolRole: Defines what the DOL claims and how the ledger should grade it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitional: inner pools on the same side are necessarily taken first.
concepts.engineNotes: The inner-pool penalty ×0.70 (685) targets the destination; the README claims 'most likely drawing to next'; the ledger metric (touched within H) fits a destination.

concepts.name: Look-ahead / repainting / intrabar order
concepts.definition: Future bars in pivots, HTF leakage without [1], unknown intrabar order, coarse-bar exits.
concepts.dolRole: The validity of every accuracy claim.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gençay 2026: a leaky oracle (Sharpe 35) survives DSR/PBO; Barot: PF 2.4 → 1.0 on 1-minute data; TradingView's intrabar rule is ~80.6% right (trade_mgmt).
concepts.engineNotes: Leak-free ledger (1426-1431, 1549-1557, 1527-1532, 2038); [1]+lookahead_on; f_tfSafe; O-L-H-C / O-H-L-C heuristic (1440-1441).

proposals.title: Survivorship-free and martingale-consistent readouts (ETA, heat, EV, L50, hit/exp)
proposals.rationale: Four trader-facing numbers are biased by construction. ETA|hit is 2-3× too optimistic and never '>H'. Heat over hits is about ½ the real p80 adverse excursion. EV shows −0.3 to −1.0R for fair far targets. L50 tracks distance.
proposals.spec: A time-to-touch histogram ttDist[4 buckets × (H+2)] filled in f_book (slot = bars if hit, else H+1). With no early censoring, Kaplan-Meier = the empirical CDF. f_ttStats(bkt) returns [median or na (>H), P(T≤H), n]; it replaces the dHit loop (2116-2127). HUD: 'ETA 19b · 62%' or 'ETA >30b · 45%'. maeAll (all records) replaces maeHit for heat (1481-1483, 2404). Delete tEV (2359) and show WIN≤H next to the drift-free geo = pW0/(pW0+pL0) via f_raceH with mu=0, plus the SKEP-4 ledger R̄. roll50 stores y−pBase (L50 excess). The hit row prints 'hit / exp' using stPE.get(4)/nA. A swept target reads 'PoT: HIT' (2067).
proposals.risk: The numbers look worse (truthfully); the tooltip must explain. No compile risk beyond new arrays and a helper declared after f_book.

proposals.title: Mirror-controlled, anytime-valid EDGE with a baseline check and a minimum detectable edge
proposals.rationale: The baseline is off by −4 to +1 pp per chart and ±2-3 pp by clock window on real data, comparable to the edges the evidence allows and to the ledger's SE. A mirror control (same ATR distance, opposite side, same bar, same hit rule) cancels miscalibration common to both sides: mean |bias z| 0.69 → 0.24. The regime split still removes beta.
proposals.spec: Trial gets role (0 DOL, 1 mirror). Step 20 (2044-2045) pushes the DOL record plus Trial.new(side=−side, edge=close−side·d0·atr, pBase=f_potBase(d,−side), liq=same, role=1, lvId=−id−1); cap 128. f_book routes role 1 away from the main stats and adds residuals into open-bar blocks: blkD (r − rm), blkP (r + rm), blkE, blkN, via f_blk(bar0) with width blkW (SKEP-3). Panel: f_cluVar(blkD, gMax = f_blk(bar_index − H)) → Δ̄, V = G/(G−1)Σ(D_g − N_gΔ̄)², SE. The anytime bound b(V) = √((V+ρ)ln((V+ρ)/(ρα²))), ρ = 10, α = 0.05, gives '✓ BEATS MIRROR' / '✕ WORSE' / '~ NOT PROVEN (MDE x pp)', with MDE = (b/√V + 0.84)·SE; CALIBRATING while n_eff < 30. Baseline check: ½ pair mean; if |bias| > 2SE and > 2 pp, show '⚠ BASELINE OFF' and mark the one-sample verdict UNRELIABLE.
proposals.risk: Doubles the open records (O(1) each). It credits a real pool-magnet effect as edge (intended). Side-asymmetric miscalibration is not cancelled. Slightly larger variance than the one-sample test.

proposals.title: Correct the overlap variance: open-keyed, centred, session-wide blocks
proposals.rationale: cluSt (1463-1469) is uncentred, booking-keyed and uses 2H blocks. Under intraday seasonality z has sd 0.76 under the null, and a real +3.3 pp edge is detected 10% vs 30% of the time. Centred session-wide blocks are correctly sized (sd 0.99-1.06) in all scenarios tested. It also feeds the Wilson deff and CAL-1's n_eff.
proposals.spec: blkW = max(2H, min(int(86400/chartS), int(calcBars/30))): 166 bars on 1m/5m, 60 on 1h, 2H on daily. Remove cluSt (1077, 1463-1469). In f_book: blkE[f_blk(t.bar0)] += y − pBase; blkN += 1. Panel (2384-2389): [sE, nE, vE] = f_cluVar(blkE, gMax); vEdge = max(vE, 0.25·vInd); deff = vEdge/vInd for the Wilson CI and the z/verdict. Guard loops when size = 0.
proposals.risk: With few blocks (G<15) the variance is noisy; the 0.25·vInd floor and the CALIBRATING gate handle it.

proposals.title: Model-free R-expectancy test with a drift (beta) adjustment
proposals.rationale: Under any martingale every target/stop/time-out rule has E[R] = 0 (optional stopping); the engine's rOut is conservative, so E[R] ≤ 0 under the null. Average R is then an edge test that needs no baseline model and is immune to baseline miscalibration. Wald's identity removes drift: E[R] = side·μ·E[τ]/risk. It answers the trader's question: do these targets pay.
proposals.spec: Trial: add mu0 and rBars. driftSt = [Σ(close−close[1]), n], updated each confirmed bar. f_openTrial sets mu0 = the running mean, and pRace drift-free (f_raceH with m=0). f_step records rBars when the race decides or at H. f_book (role 0): R_adj = rOut − side·mu0·rBars/risk, added to blkR by open block. Panel: [sR, nR, vR] = f_cluVar(blkR, gMax) → R̄ ± band and the anytime verdict; the RACE row moves to Compact: 'R̄ +0.06R ±0.11 · PF 1.12 · long 62%'. f_raceAdj then shifts relative to geometry.
proposals.risk: Intrabar target/stop ordering is heuristic (~80% right) and conservative on gaps. R depends on the invalidation rule (a design choice, which is fine because the test is about this trade definition).

proposals.title: Strong-baseline league table: DOL vs NEAREST, GEO (max d·PoT) and TREND selectors on the same bars
proposals.rationale: Beating a random level is a low bar. Sibling replicas show every picker's hit rate equals its baseline, and pickers differ in ATR delivered (max-reach 1.10-1.43 vs hand score 0.86-1.09 vs nearest 0.66-0.93 ATR per target); D-first loses 9-12 pp to geometry. A paired league on identical bars shows whether the scoring adds value over naive rules, and it is an A/B harness for any scoring change.
proposals.spec: At each DOL opening (step 20), one O(pool) pass picks NEAREST (min distance with dA ≥ minDistATR), GEO (max dA·f_potBase) and TREND (nearest on the htfBias side). Push f_openTrial(level) with role 2/3/4 and lvId = −1000000−role so the has-check ignores them; cap 256. f_book routes by role into per-role open-block arrays (excess, R_adj, y·d0). Full view rows show the paired DOL−role Δexcess, ΔR and ATR delivered with SKEP-3 variances and the anytime bound. Shares mechanism with CAL-3.
proposals.risk: Three extra f_invalidation calls per opening (negligible CPU). The panel is longer (Full view only). Overlaps with CAL-3, so implement one shared probe/role mechanism.

proposals.title: Null-default ICT modifiers: unsupported multipliers start neutral and must earn weight
proposals.rationale: Hard-coded modifiers assert effects the evidence contradicts or never found: drift in PoT, fixed killzone affinities, tests-as-magnitude, tier bonus, confluence 15, ungated draw-first. Each moves scores by more than the 4-point hysteresis, so each is a source of target switching with no measured benefit.
proposals.spec: Defaults: driftW 0.5→0 (QPOT-01). New useKzAff=false gating f_kzAff at 1941. New wTests=0.0 and wTier=0.4 replacing the literals 0.35·tests and 1.2·tier at 682. wConf 15→5. D gated by ER20 ≥ 0.40 and sign agreement (quant_regime), keeping draw-side first when efficient. Keep the old constants as a 'scoreOld' computed in evaluate (O(1)) and run it as a SKEP-5 shadow role; switch defaults back only if the old score wins beyond the anytime bound on most charts.
proposals.risk: Changes which target shows; the brief's 'draw-side first' decision is preserved but gated. The reference product markets session confluence, so keep every option available.

proposals.title: Forward-only (realtime) sub-ledger and in-sample disclosure
proposals.rationale: Historical trials are in-sample with respect to settings tuned on the same chart (best of 45 settings: E[max z]=2.21 under the null). Only records opened on realtime bars after the settings were fixed are out-of-sample; a settings change resets them, which is the right property.
proposals.spec: Trial.fwd = not barstate.ishistory at open; fwSt = [n, k, Σp, ΣR_adj] updated in f_book for role 0. Row: 'FORWARD n 9 · hit 56% / exp 51% · R̄ +0.2' or 'waiting for live bars'. A global nTuned counts key inputs that differ from their literal defaults (wProx, wFresh, wConf, wDens, wDraw, minScore, hyst, maxATR, minDistATR, halfLife, potH, dGate, pivLen, eqTol, fvgQMin, obQMin). The ACCURACY header tooltip states the in-sample caveat.
proposals.risk: Forward n grows slowly (about 1 per H bars) and resets on reload. The literal defaults in nTuned must track the input defaults.

proposals.title: Honest claims: PoT definition, PoT filter = distance filter, DOL = destination, verdict words
proposals.rationale: The words overstate. The DOL is a destination (inner-pool penalty, 685), not 'the next liquidity'. PoT is a distance/regime probability, not the level's quality. The minPoT filter selects nearer targets. '✕ NO EDGE' is printed when the edge is merely not measurable (MDE 5.5-9.5 pp).
proposals.spec: README: 'highest-scoring destination for the current leg; inner pools are usually taken first'. PoT label tooltip and potModel tooltip (142): 'how often price travelled this distance within H bars in the same regime; it measures distance and volatility, not level quality; random levels at 1/2/3 ATR are touched ~75-80/55-60/40-45% within 30 bars'. minPoT tooltip (141): 'filtering by PoT filters by distance'. Verdicts: '✓ BEATS RANDOM' / '~ NOT PROVEN (MDE x pp)' / '✕ WORSE THAN RANDOM'. No verdicts in Clean style.
proposals.risk: None technical; it may feel less impressive, which is the honest outcome.

proposals.title: Multiple-comparison discipline in the Full view; gate per-family learning by the same test
proposals.rationale: Five at-a-glance tests (4 families + race) give an 11% chance of a spurious standout at one look, more with peeking. f_calMult acts on those noisy family rates (≥10% off under the null in 47-66% of families).
proposals.spec: One primary pre-declared verdict: the ALL mirror edge (SKEP-2) plus R-expectancy (SKEP-4). Family rows are labelled 'exploratory', show 'hit / exp · excess ± anytime band' in neutral colour, and use per-family open-block arrays (flat array g·nBlocks + id). f_calMult(g) returns 1.0 unless that family's mirror excess passes the anytime bound at α = 0.05/4 (ties to CAL-1).
proposals.risk: Family multipliers will rarely activate at default depth, which is the honest outcome given the MDE.

proposals.title: Audit trail: plot every past target (including abandoned ones) as a step line
proposals.rationale: Visual evaluation is survivorship-prone: the chart shows only the current target, and ghosts are off by default and capped at 12. A step line of the DOL's near edge exposes every switch, abandonment and hit, so users can audit the ledger and the 'targets jump around' complaint by eye.
proposals.spec: Input showAudit=false (G_GHOST). At 2438-2444: dolEdgeOut = activeLv.nearEdge(), dolSideOut = activeLv.side; plot(dolEdgeOut, 'DOL Price', color = dolSideOut == 1 ? cAbove : cBelow, style = plot.style_steplinebr, linewidth = 2, display = showAudit ? display.all : display.data_window). Docs: display is 'input plot_display' and style is 'input plot_style', so the ternary on an input bool is allowed. Values come from confirmed-bar state, so no repaint.
proposals.risk: Clutter (off by default). The DOL Price data-window value changes from price to near edge; note it in the release notes.

result.summary: A and B combined: distance and volatility decide which pool price reaches next, and ICT labels add almost nothing beyond them. B's engine-faithful replication finds pools are reached as distance implies: +0.1 ± 0.4 pp across 7 hourly datasets (n 52,762) and +0.8 ± 0.6 pp across 5 five-minute datasets (n 30,887). Equal highs/lows, priming, test counts and prominence show no consistent effect, which independently confirms A's "EQ adds under 1 pp" finding. A's claim that continuation dominates after a sweep is overstated. There is no reversal edge after a rejected sweep (continuation +1.5 ± 0.7 pp on 1H, three independent large replications), only a 0-2 pp continuation lean whose sign varies by market (GC +6.1, ES −4.6 pp). The engine's fixed REJECT = reversal mapping at line 1581 is wrong, and the reversal lean holds only for a HOLD against the HTF bias. ICT's context rules fail on data: P/D-conditioned turtle soup continues more, not less (+1.7 / +5.1 pp); the IRL↔ERL alternation is ±2 pp and flips sign between timeframes; the daily-bias close rule matches a shuffle null (sibling study). The one ICT path claim supported is the high-resistance run: each untouched opposing FVG between price and a pool cuts reach by 2-3 pp beyond distance, negative in 11 of 12 datasets and robust within trend strata, while the engine's path cost is volume-only. B also found that the sibling study's strong 1H stack-crowding penalty (−6/−10/−29 pp) comes from a corrupted GC 1H file (two contract months interleaved). On clean data, stacking effects differ in sign by market and timeframe, so neither the engine's inner ×0.70 nor a strong crowding prior is justified. Three engine defects A missed: EQ merges are one-sided (a right-higher print sweeps the left pool before the pivot confirms, so only "primed" or exact pairs merge); liqEvt sums every pool hit per bar and counts 1-tick pokes, so one wide bar can flip D; and the HOLD threshold depends on the display input zoneATR. Round-number evidence is strong for order placement but argues for capping zones at rounds, not A's zone extension. Best changes: fix the raid → D mapping now (ICT-9), then grade every candidate with ICT feature bits on the shadow ledger (ICT-1) so each ICT claim earns or loses weight per chart. The WebSearch budget was used up and papers.ssrn.com and quartersequence.com are outside this session's allowed network, so A's sources were verified through sibling studies that re-read them, and unverified preprints are capped at weak.

concepts.name: Buy-side / sell-side liquidity (old highs/lows)
concepts.definition: BSL = buy stops plus breakout buys above an unswept swing high; SSL = sell stops below an unswept swing low. One old high is enough. Zone = [level, level + depth]. Swept on a strict trade-through (high > level); a wick is enough.
concepts.dolRole: Defines the candidate set: where stops rest. It is not by itself an attractor beyond distance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Supports stop location: Osler JF 2003 (stop-buys 14.4% at 01-10 above 00 vs 7.4% below, p = 0.029) and Kavajecz & Odders-White RFS 2004 (84% cointegrated with depth). Null for extra draw: B's tests give +0.1 ± 0.4 pp on 1H (n 52,762) and +0.8 ± 0.6 pp on 5m (n 30,887) vs a distance-matched S(d); a sibling finds −2.0 pp at 1m.
concepts.engineNotes: pivLen 5 pools 1753-1776; strict touched() 623-624; zone 0.20 ATR (93). Matches ICT and the decision history.

concepts.name: Relative equal highs/lows (EQH/EQL)
concepts.definition: Two or more swing highs within a tolerance (engine eqTol 0.10 ATR; practitioners 0.05-0.1% or 0.10-0.15 ATR) form one pool beyond the outermost print; eqCount++.
concepts.dolRole: ICT treats them as the most obvious liquidity. On data they are reached exactly as distance implies.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. B: EQ +0.3 ± 1.8 pp (1H, n 2,230) and −0.1 ± 2.1 (5m, n 1,350) vs singles +0.2 / +0.9; within noise in every distance bucket. Replicates A's E6 (< 1 pp) and orderflow_micro T3 (equal prints carry no post-sweep information).
concepts.engineNotes: f_mergeAt 1111-1131 is asymmetric. A right-higher print sweeps the pool at step 3 before the pivot confirms, so the outer branch (1116-1126) is dead for chart pivots and only left>=right or exact pairs merge. The density term 0.9*eqCount (682) is unsupported (ICT-10, ICT-11).

concepts.name: EQ 'priming' (left high slightly above right)
concepts.definition: For a relative-equal pair, an earlier high slightly above the later one (lows: earlier slightly lower). ICT 2024 Mentorship L1 calls a run on them 'very very high probability'.
concepts.dolRole: Would raise the draw priority of specific EQ pools.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null and inconsistent (B). Primed +0.1 ± 2.1 pp (1H) and +3.9 ± 2.6 (5m); exact +0.7 ± 3.4 (1H) and −8.0 ± 3.8 (5m). The primed-vs-exact contrast flips sign between timeframes, so it is a multiple-comparison blip.
concepts.engineNotes: Implicitly the only EQ case the engine merges (inner print). No flag; proposed as the PRIMED bit in ICT-1.

concepts.name: Right-beyond relative equal (micro-sweep pair)
concepts.definition: A second high exceeds the first by <= eqTol and the bar closes back inside. ICT calls this relative equal; the engine books a raid plus a new single pool.
concepts.dolRole: Correct labelling of EQ pools, and removal of spurious raid events that feed D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Reach is null: RH pools −1.6 ± 2.1 pp (1H, n 1,553) and −0.8 ± 3.0 (5m). The fix is for logic consistency and noise removal.
concepts.engineNotes: Step 3 (1580-1589) treats it as a full REJECT raid (liqEvt −tier), ghosts it, and the new pivot (1758/1770) creates a single pool without EQ. ICT-11 and ICT-9 address this.

concepts.name: STH/ITH/LTH hierarchy and swing prominence
concepts.definition: STH = 3-candle swing; ITH = STH with lower STHs on each side; LTH = ITH with lower ITHs on each side (ICT 2022 Ep. 8/12). Measurable proxy: prominence = height above the right-side low, in ATR.
concepts.dolRole: ICT says higher-order swings are bigger draws.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Contradicted at 1H: the high-prominence tercile is reached −1.4 ± 0.7 pp vs +1.7 ± 0.7 pp for the low tercile, in both trend strata; no difference at 5m. Prominence does predict a larger run after the take (+0.15 ATR, orderflow_micro T3). For pivLen-5 pools the ITH flag is nearly automatic.
concepts.engineNotes: Tier weights f_tierW 506-516; prom at 1757/1769; density 0.8*min(1,prom/3) (682) is unsupported for reach. A's ICT-8 is dropped.

concepts.name: Key liquidity: PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL, Asia/London/NY highs and lows
concepts.definition: Previous day/week extremes and session-range extremes, anchored to the printing candle. Swept on trade-through.
concepts.dolRole: Widely watched pools and common session raid targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Base rates are real but geometric. PDH taken next day S&P 51.3%, NASDAQ 55.4%, either 87-91% (bias_dol). The edgeful YM PDH-break numbers (67/81%) are explained by geometry. Once one side of a range is taken, the other side is about 10-25% less likely than geometry (session_stats).
concepts.engineNotes: f_rangeTrack/f_sessTrack 807-863, 945-961; registry 1790-1809, re-entry 1824-1852. Registry levels in range but not yet re-entered (re-entry runs every 5 bars, 1825) are removed silently at 1592-1596, with no raid event or ghost.

concepts.name: Stacked pools: low-hanging fruit vs outermost draw (path crowding)
concepts.definition: Same-side pools within a window form a stack. ICT: trade to the lowest-hanging fruit (nearest stops) first and to the major/external pool as the objective. The engine makes the outermost pool the draw (inner x0.70).
concepts.dolRole: Chooses between the next pool (always reached first on that side) and the bigger objective behind it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Heterogeneous. Outer-pool edge for 1/2/>=3 intermediate pools: 1H pooled +1.3/+2.3/+3.2 pp, but NQ −3.0/−8.5/−8.6 and BTC +2.2/+4.9/+8.0; 5m +4.0/+4.3/+5.1; 1m (sibling) −1.5/−3.5/−6.1. The sibling's 1H −6/−10/−29 is reproduced only with the corrupted GC 1H file (−9.6/−18.8/−31.5).
concepts.engineNotes: f_stackSide 1230-1251; inner x0.70 684-685; +0.45*stack in density 682. Fixed magnitudes are far larger than any measured effect. Conceptually the outer pool is ICT's objective, never the next pool. ICT-10 makes it neutral and learned; the HTF objective (1984-1989) stays as a display.

concepts.name: IRL/ERL delivery cycle
concepts.definition: Dealing range = leg low to leg high. ERL = stops beyond the range extremes; IRL = FVG/OB/short-term pools inside. After ERL is taken, price draws to IRL; after IRL is rebalanced, it draws to the next ERL.
concepts.dolRole: Would decide retracement vs expansion as the next draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B's race test (nearest pool vs nearest untouched opposite FVG, excess over driftless gambler's-ruin geometry vs control). After liquidity is taken, IRL first: +1.8 pp (1H, n 3,267) but −2.3 pp (5m, n 2,006). After IRL is tagged: −0.9 / −0.7 pp. Inconsistent, so null. Geometry alone is accurate to within 0.3 pp in the control.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent from scoring. htfEQ/dayEQ (967-968) are anchors only. The dealing range must first be fixed (ICTS-4). ICT-4 adds a display and ledger bits only.

concepts.name: Premium/discount context for sweeps (ICT turtle-soup condition)
concepts.definition: pos = (close − rngL)/(rngH − rngL); premium if >= 0.5. ICT: a run above an old high in premium is a turtle-soup sell; a run below an old low in discount is a buy.
concepts.dolRole: Would condition reversal vs continuation after a raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Contradicted. REJECT sweeps on ICT's reversal side continued more: +1.7 ± 1.4 pp (1H, n 1,369) and +5.1 ± 1.9 (5m, n 770); on the continuation side −1.4 / −3.4 pp. Sibling skeptic C15: premium = sell is contradicted at monthly horizons (George & Hwang 2004).
concepts.engineNotes: Display only in the Terminal ZONE column (2324-2333). Keep display-only.

concepts.name: Sweep vs run (outcome after liquidity is taken)
concepts.definition: Engine bar-close class for BSL: HOLD if close > lv.top (level + zoneATR*ATR at creation); REJECT if close < level; else NEUTRAL. ICT: sweep = shallow run that reverses; run = goes through and continues.
concepts.dolRole: Updates the draw direction after each raid: the core 'what happens next' signal.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No reversal edge after REJECT, replicated: B 1H REJECT +1.5 ± 0.7 pp continuation (n 5,899), all sweeps +1.1 ± 0.5 (n 12,550), 5m −0.2 ± 0.7; ict_struct 52.6% continuation (n 1,402); skeptic race 0.497-0.510. HOLD against the HTF bias leans to reversal (B −2.3 ± 1.6; ict_struct 56%, n 381). Signs are market-specific (REJECT GC +6.1, NQ +4.9, ES −4.6 pp). Osler: cascades last 15 min to 2 h.
concepts.engineNotes: 1580-1582 maps REJECT to −1 (reversal). It also sums every pool hit per bar (a stack can swing D in one bar), counts 1-tick pokes, and its HOLD threshold depends on the display input zoneATR. ICT-9 is the static fix; ICT-2 learns per chart.

concepts.name: Purge + market structure shift (MSS)
concepts.definition: After a sweep that closes back inside, a displacement body close through the last opposite short-term swing within N (about 8) bars. ICT counts an MSS only after a purge.
concepts.dolRole: Would confirm a reversal draw toward the opposite pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null or negative. MSS reversal reads were right 45.6% (n 171) without displacement and 50.5% (n 97) with it (ict_struct). Mahadzva (unverified preprint summary): fade CHoCH+FVG reversal reads.
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure 708-782 and bosUp/bosDn 1542-1547 are independent of sweeps. Proposed only as an alert with measured odds (ICT-2).

concepts.name: Turtle soup (false breakout of an old extreme)
concepts.definition: Connors-Raschke: new 20-bar low; prior 20-bar low at least 4 bars old; entry 5-10 ticks back above the old low; stop 1 tick under the new low. ICT version: in discount, aggressive response, then an MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Reversal draw toward the opposite range extreme.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null or contradicted. bias_dol: Turtle Soup excess over geometry on 9 datasets ranges from −0.129 to +0.082, never reliably positive. B: REJECT of pools >= 50 bars old +1.4 ± 1.6 pp continuation; textbook ERL-against-trend REJECT +2.9 ± 1.7 (1H), −0.2 (5m).
concepts.engineNotes: Sweeps are read at 1580-1582 with no age or context requirement. Nothing to add beyond ICT-9.

concepts.name: High- vs low-resistance liquidity runs (opposing PD arrays in the path)
concepts.definition: A run to a pool through unmitigated opposing PD arrays (bearish FVG/OB above price for a BSL target) is high-resistance and least probable; a clear path is low-resistance ('hot knife through butter').
concepts.dolRole: Adjusts reachability by the structure in the path.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Supported, small. Per untouched opposing FVG (pools 1-4 ATR, no same-side intermediate pool): −2.8 ± 0.8 pp on 1H (n 4,757) and −2.1 ± 1.0 on 5m (n 3,387). With trend −2.4, against −3.2. Negative in 11 of 12 datasets.
concepts.engineNotes: The path term is volume-profile only (1945-1947). ICT-5 adds a bounded x0.95 per opposing undelivered FVG (floor x0.90), plus the OPP ledger bit.

concepts.name: Inducement (IDM, retail SMC)
concepts.definition: The first pullback low after a BOS (follow lower lows until none), taken on a wick. A POI behind it is valid only after the IDM is taken.
concepts.dolRole: The first liquidity met on the retrace (low-hanging fruit).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Community definitions disagree; not an ICT term; no quantitative test.
concepts.engineNotes: induceBar density feature (892-895) and inner pools (1230-1251). No IDM level; not proposed.

concepts.name: Trendline (phantom) liquidity
concepts.definition: Stops beyond an obvious diagonal with 3+ touches; swept when price crosses line(t).
concepts.dolRole: Diagonal pool target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT himself: 'everybody's going to have a different diagonal trend line'. No data.
concepts.engineNotes: Not recommended.

concepts.name: Tests / prior bounces at a level
concepts.definition: Approaches within 0.30 ATR that do not trade through, at least 3 bars apart (engine track()).
concepts.dolRole: Folk ICT view: more stops accumulate. Empirical view: the next approach bounces more in the short run, decaying over hours.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong at high frequency (Garzarelli 2014: p < 0.0001 at 45-90 s, not at 180 s). On bars there is no monotone effect: 1 test +0.8 ± 0.9 (1H) / +2.8 ± 1.2 (5m); >=3 tests +2.4 ± 4.6 / −2.4 ± 4.5; sibling 1m >=3 tests −7.3 ± 3.6.
concepts.engineNotes: Density rewards tests monotonically, 0.35*min(tests,6) (682). Exact touches (high == level) are neither tests (gap > 0, 654) nor sweeps (strict, 624). ICT-10 makes the weight neutral; the TESTED bit is learned.

concepts.name: Stop depth beyond a level
concepts.definition: Stops sit in a band beyond the level. On bars, measured as the penetration of sweeps that close back inside.
concepts.dolRole: Sets zone depth, how 'spent' a shallow sweep is, and the invalidation buffer.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Osler: stop-buys concentrate in the first 10% of the step beyond a round. Bar replication (B): REJECT penetration q25/q50/q80/q90 = 0.12/0.28/0.64/0.91 ATR (1H) and 0.11/0.23/0.51/0.76 (5m); sibling pooled 0.233/0.518. No depth bucket carries direction.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed zoneATR 0.20 (93, about the median) and invalidation buffer 0.10 ATR (1344), which sits inside the stop band. ICT-7 adopts OF-2 learned depth.

concepts.name: Round-number stop and limit clusters
concepts.definition: Take-profits and limit orders cluster at 00/50 levels; stops just beyond them; algos front-run by one tick. Auto step = smallest {1,5}x10^k at or above one daily ATR (OF-4).
concepts.dolRole: Locates where orders rest (geometry). Not a magnet.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Placement is strong (Osler 2003/2005, Bhattacharya et al. 2012, Lallouache & Abergel 2013). Bar level (orderflow_micro): not magnets (mixed sign); a sweep wick stops short of a round just beyond a pool (−4.2 pp, about 3σ), which contradicts A's zone extension.
concepts.engineNotes: No round-number logic (grep). ICT-3 now adopts OF-4: cap zones at the round, place invalidation beyond it, no score bonus by default, RN ledger bit.

concepts.name: When a pool is spent (and what becomes the next liquidity)
concepts.definition: Once traded through, its orders are filled and the next untouched high or low is the target. The new sweep wick is itself fresh liquidity.
concepts.dolRole: Removes the target, triggers re-selection, and creates the next candidate.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 60.8% of REJECT wicks are re-taken within 5 bars, but only 38% become pivLen-5 pivots (orderflow_micro T6). Once one side of a range is taken, the other side is 10-25% less likely than geometry (session_stats).
concepts.engineNotes: Binary removal on trade-through (1583-1589), registry removal (1592-1596). Matches the decision history. The fresh wick pool is in OF-1.

concepts.name: Killzone timing of raids
concepts.definition: London 2-5 am NY raids Asia; NY 7-10 am raids London and the previous day; avoid 12-1 pm; PM session from 1:30 pm.
concepts.dolRole: Timing and source affinity of the next raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor backtest only (Backtrex: 53.2% WR / PF 1.68 in killzones vs 47.1% / 1.21 over 24 h), not re-verified.
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff 597-602 and off-killzone hysteresis 976 are fixed multipliers. KZ bit in ICT-1; SESS-3 learns them.

concepts.name: ICT daily bias from previous-range closes
concepts.definition: Bullish if C(t-1) > H(t-2), or if L(t-1) < L(t-2) and C(t-1) > L(t-2); draw = H(t-1). Bearish mirrors. Inside days, and outside days that close inside, are neutral.
concepts.dolRole: Would pick the PDH vs PDL draw for the session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Equals geometry. Right 69-76%, but a shuffle null scores 68-76% (−2.2 to +1.9 pp on 13 datasets, bias_dol). As a hard rule it is worse than geometry (64-73%).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent from D (1892-1894). A's ICT-6 is dropped; it survives as the BIAS-3 readout and the DBIAS ledger bit.

concepts.name: Which side is taken first (top-down DOL vs race geometry)
concepts.definition: ICT: name the HTF draw and trade the legs toward it. Quant: P(up first) = (C − L)/(H − L) under a driftless race; the engine's f_race/f_raceH add drift and horizon.
concepts.dolRole: Sets the draw side, the central forecasting decision.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Geometry is right 70-81% on 17 dataset/reference pairs (bias_dol). The engine's D scores 0.49-0.54 out of sample (ict_struct). Choosing the side by structure costs 4-10 pp. B's control races: geometry error −0.3 to −0.1 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: D = 0.5 htfBias + 0.3 stfBias + 0.2 exeIB (1892) drives the draw pillar and the counter-draw x0.50. The race math exists (447-482) but does not choose the side. Sibling BIAS-1/2 and ICTS-1/3 cover this.

concepts.name: Level age / decay
concepts.definition: Liquidity matures as stops build, then goes stale; S/R memory decays with time since the last bounce.
concepts.dolRole: Freshness weighting of candidates.
concepts.evidenceNotes: At 1m, stale pools (> 12 h) are reached −7.5 ± 1.1 pp less than distance implies (academic_sr); no age effect at 1H/daily (siblings). Chung & Bellotti decay at about 350-900 min.
concepts.engineNotes: The maturing-then-decaying freshness ramp (668-673) is unsupported. Not this domain's main fix.

concepts.name: Per-chart validation of ICT claims (candidate ledger)
concepts.definition: Grade every candidate level, not only the chosen DOL, against the distance-matched baseline f_potBase. Learn a bounded, evidence-gated lift per ICT feature bit.
concepts.dolRole: Turns ICT heuristics into measured multipliers. This is the only safe design given that effects change sign by market and timeframe.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Method is standard. Motivated by B1-B9: every ICT effect is about zero on average or market-specific (stack NQ −8.5 vs BTC +4.9 pp; REJECT GC +6.1 vs ES −4.6 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger grades only the active DOL (2037-2045); f_calMult has 4 families with no significance gate (1376-1382). ICT-1 is built on CAL-3.

concepts.name: Liquidity voids, NWOG/NDOG, SMT divergence
concepts.definition: Multi-candle one-way voids; week/day opening gaps with a CE magnet; a correlated asset failing to take a pool.
concepts.dolRole: Additional draw sources and reversal tells.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT teaching; outside this domain (PD-array and intermarket studies).
concepts.engineNotes: Belongs to other studies.

proposals.title: Fix the raid → draw mapping now: neutral REJECT, HTF-conditioned HOLD, one event per bar per side, ignore micro-pokes, decouple HOLD from zone depth
proposals.rationale: liqEvt (1580-1582) feeds 30% of D (wL, 157). D drives the draw pillar (weight 30), the x0.50 counter-draw penalty and side selection. Its REJECT = reversal sign is contradicted by three large replications: B REJECT +1.5 ± 0.7 pp continuation (n 5,899), ict_struct 52.6% (n 1,402), skeptic 0.497-0.510. Separately, it sums every pool hit on a bar, counts 1-tick relative-equal pokes as full REJECTs, and its HOLD threshold (lv.top) depends on the display input zoneATR. Together these are a plausible cause of D flips and targets jumping around. Merges ICTS-2 and BIAS-4.
proposals.spec:
Input (G_FLOW): float holdATR = input.float(0.20, "Raid Hold Distance (ATR)", minval = 0.0, step = 0.05).

In the ENGINE block before the pool loop (1559): float evB = 0.0, float evS = 0.0.

Replace 1580-1582:
- if hit and lv.isLiquidity():
  - pen = (side == 1 ? high − price : price − low) / atr
  - back = close back inside the level
  - hold = close beyond price ± holdATR*atr
  - micro = back and pen <= eqTol
  - e = 0; if hold and not micro: e := htfBias == side ? 1.0 : htfBias == −side ? −0.5 : 0.5
  - sv = side * e * lv.tier()
  - keep the larger |sv| per side in evB / evS

After the loop (after 1589): liqEvt := f_clamp(liqEvt + evB + evS, −1, 1).

Result: REJECT and NEUTRAL add 0; HOLD with the HTF bias continues; HOLD against it leans to failed breakout (B −2.3 ± 1.6 pp; ict_struct 56% reversal). Later, ICT-2 replaces the static e with per-chart learned values, and ICTS-1 scales wL by D's skill. All on confirmed bars; no new requests.
proposals.risk: D reacts less to raids, so draw flips become rarer. That is intended and measurable through ICTS-1. 5m evidence for HOLD-with-trend is weaker (−1.5 pp), so keep the magnitudes small.

proposals.title: ICT feature bits on the candidate (shadow) ledger: evidence-gated per-chart lifts for every ICT claim
proposals.rationale: Every ICT effect measured is either about zero on average or changes sign by market or timeframe: stacking NQ −8.5 vs BTC +4.9 pp; REJECT outcome GC +6.1 vs ES −4.6 pp; priming flips between 1H and 5m. Fixed weights are therefore wrong somewhere. The current ledger grades about one trial per H window (active DOL only), and f_calMult has no significance gate. Grading all candidates against f_potBase with block-clustered z-gates lets each ICT claim earn or lose weight on the user's chart, and shows the trader which claims hold there. Built on CAL-3/CAL-4 infrastructure: one ledger, not two.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_ACC): useFeat (true), featN0 (60), featB (0.15), featZ (2.0).

Types and state:
- type Probe {int lvId, int side, bool liq, float edge, int bar0, float pBase, int mask} after Trial (396).
- Level gets int lastProbe = −100000. Cap 128 open probes.
- NF = 16. Arrays fN, fK, fE plus block-cluster accumulators (pattern of cluSt 1077/1464-1469), size NF+1; index NF = all probes.
- Decode bits with math.floor(mask / pow2.get(b)) % 2 == 1 (Pine has no bitwise operators).

Bits:
- 0 EQ; 1 PRIMED (set in f_mergeAt on an inner merge); 2 RH (ICT-11); 3 TESTED; 4 STACKED; 5 INNER
- 6 OPP (ICT-5); 7 PROM >= 1.5 ATR; 8 KEY (src >= 6); 9 SESSION (src 3-5); 10 MTF (src 1-2)
- 11 DRAW (side == dirSide); 12 KZ (f_kzAff > 1); 13 RN (ICT-3); 14 ERL (ICT-4); 15 DBIAS (BIAS-3 state)

Snapshot (step 17 after evaluate at 1948, inCalc, past warmup): for each level with bar_index − lastProbe >= H and 0 < dist/atr <= maxATR, push a Probe regardless of score.

Grading (step 2b after 1557): liquidity = strict trade-through; arrays = touch. Book on a hit or at H bars, then remove the probe.

Lift and gates:
- lift_b = ((K_b+2)/(E_b+2)) / ((K_all+2)/(E_all+2))
- z_b = (K_b − E_b) / sqrt(Σ closed-block residual²)
- m_b = (|z_b| >= featZ and n_b >= 100) ? clamp(1 + n/(n+featN0)*(lift_b − 1), 1 − featB, 1 + featB) : 1.0

Apply in the multiplier loop (1940-1947): lv.mult *= clamp(Π m_b, 0.80, 1.25). Every bit starts neutral.

UX (Terminal, Accuracy = Full): an 'ICT CLAIMS · this chart' block with ×lift, n, z and ✓/~/✕ per bit, plus a SELECTION EDGE row.

Cost: about one new probe per bar, <= 128 checks per bar.
proposals.risk: Probes share one price path; the block-cluster z-gate and shrinkage handle that. Sixteen bits means multiple comparisons; the |z| >= 2 gate and bounds limit it (SKEP-9). Adds a UDT and arrays; memory is fine. Must grade every candidate to avoid selection feedback.

proposals.title: Opposing undelivered imbalances in the path (ICT high-resistance run): bounded reach penalty plus OPP bit
proposals.rationale: The only ICT path claim with consistent support. Each untouched opposing FVG between price and a pool cuts 30-bar reach by 2-3 pp beyond distance: −2.8 ± 0.8 pp on 1H (n 4,757) and −2.1 ± 1.0 on 5m (n 3,387). It is negative in 11 of 12 datasets and holds within both trend strata (with −2.4, against −3.2). The engine's path term is volume-only (1945-1947), and the sibling T5 test found that term unstable.
proposals.spec:
Input (G_SCORE): float oppK = input.float(0.05, "Opposing Imbalance Penalty", 0.0..0.2).

In step 17 before the multiplier loop (1939), collect once per bar from the pool:
- oppUp = bottoms of kind 3 (bear FVG, side +1) with fill == 0 and bottom > close
- oppDn = tops of kind 2 (bull FVG) with fill == 0 and top < close

In the loop, per lv:
- e = lv.nearEdge()
- nOpp = count of oppUp with b < e (if side == 1), else count of oppDn with t > e
- lv.mult *= 1.0 − oppK * math.min(nOpp, 2)
- Set the OPP bit (ICT-1) when nOpp >= 1, so the ledger confirms or reverses the default per chart.

Strict comparisons exclude a target FVG's own edge. Order blocks are untested, so they are not counted by default. Optional: also count fvgTrk zones with a new 'touched' flag, matching the test's unfiltered FVGs.

Cost: <= 40 × ~10 compares per inCalc bar.
proposals.risk: Some overlap with the counter-draw penalty, because opposing arrays are common in counter-trend paths; the effect survives within trend strata. The pool holds only quality-gated FVGs (fvgQMin 0.45) while the test used all FVGs >= 0.15 ATR; ledger calibration covers the difference.

proposals.title: Neutral stack and magnitude defaults: drop the fixed 'outermost is the draw' and unsupported density rewards (amends ACAD-1; aligns OF-3/SMC-3/SKEP-6)
proposals.rationale: Several fixed rewards in density and multipliers back claims that are null or change sign: inner x0.70 (684-685), +0.45*stack, 0.9*eqCount, 0.35*min(tests,6), 0.8*min(1,prom/3) (682). Evidence: EQ null; tests null; prominence −3.1 pp at 1H; stacking heterogeneous. The sibling ACAD-1 would install a strong 1H crowding penalty, but its numbers come from a corrupted GC 1H file: B reproduced −31.5 ± 4.1 pp on that file alone vs −8.6 to +8.0 on clean data. Neutral defaults plus learned bits are the only setting not wrong on some charts. They also make the DOL ICT's 'next' (low-hanging fruit), while the outermost pool stays as the optional HTF objective display.
proposals.spec:
Input (G_SCORE): string magModel = input.string("Evidence", "Pool Magnitude Model", options = ["Evidence", "ICT Classic"]). ICT Classic keeps the current formula.

In evaluate (681-685), with ev = magModel == "Evidence":
- x = ev ? 1.2*tier + 0.4*min(1, prom/3) : (the current formula)
- dens unchanged otherwise
- inner x0.70 only when not ev

Keep f_stackSide (STK tags, STACKED/INNER bits) and showObj (1984-1989).

Tell ACAD-1 implementers to replace the hard-coded 1H crowding prior with the learned STACKED/INNER bits. Update the README line 'the outermost pool in a stack is the draw'.
proposals.risk: Visible behaviour change: inside a 0.75-ATR stack the nearer pool now often wins. If the user prefers the old look, the ICT Classic option can stay the default. Halving the prominence term slightly lowers HTF-objective ranks.

proposals.title: Per-chart raid-outcome learner with control races; bar-close raid alert and Purge+MSS alert with measured odds
proposals.rationale: Average post-sweep effects are 0-2 pp, so the static fix (ICT-9) captures most of the value. Market-specific signs are large, though: REJECT GC +6.1, NQ +4.9, ES −4.6 pp on 1H. A learner turns them into D input where they exist and gives the trader an honest 'what happens after a raid on this chart'. MSS reversal reads are 45.6-50.5% (ict_struct), so the Purge+MSS alert must carry measured odds rather than imply a reversal. Downgraded from A's P1.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_FLOW): swLearn (true), swK (1.0 ATR), swWin (8).

type RaidRec {int side, int cell, float up, float dn, int bar0, float base, float mss}
- cell = cls*3 + align (cls HOLD/REJECT/NEUTRAL; align with/against/none HTF); 9 = control; 10 = PURGE+MSS.
- State: var array<RaidRec> (cap 96); rN, rC, rP float arrays of size 11.

Create:
- One record per side per bar from the strongest-tier liquidity hit (same place as ICT-9).
- up/dn = close ± swK*atr.
- mss = side == 1 ? nz(obSwingL, exeRL) : nz(obSwingH, exeRH), captured now because a BOS resets obSwing at 1667/1710.
- Controls: bar_index % 10 == 0 pushes cell 9.

Resolve (step 2c after 1557):
- Both barriers on one bar: drop. Either barrier: book; continuation = the raided side's barrier (controls: the up barrier). Expire after H bars.
- A REJECT upgrades to cell 10 when, within swWin bars, a displacement body close crosses mss (dispDn/dispUp); this sets purgeEvt.

Estimate:
- pCtl = (rC[9]+10)/(rN[9]+20); base = side == 1 ? pCtl : 1 − pCtl.
- lift_c = logit((rC+40*p̄)/(rN+40)) − logit(p̄).
- eL = clamp((sigm(lift_c) − 0.5)/0.05, −1, 1); blend with ICT-9's static e by n/(n+40).

UX:
- Terminal row with continuation % by cell vs base.
- Bar-close alert when the active DOL is raided, with class and measured odds.
- alertcondition(purgeEvt, "Liquidity Purge + MSS") with cell-10 odds in the alert() text.
proposals.risk: Sparse cells early on; the kappa = 40 blend falls back to ICT-9. Alerts must state 'on this chart, n = …' to avoid implying an edge. Interacts with ICTS-1's skill gate on wL.

proposals.title: Round-number layer per OF-4: cap zones at rounds, stops beyond rounds, no score bonus by default (corrects A's zone extension)
proposals.rationale: Order placement at and beyond round numbers is the strongest evidence in the domain (Osler 2003/2005; Lallouache & Abergel). On bars, rounds are not magnets, and sweep wicks stop short of a round just beyond a pool (−4.2 pp, about 3σ, orderflow_micro T2d). A's original ICT-3 extended zones past the round and added a confluence bonus; both are contradicted. The engine has no round awareness.
proposals.spec:
Adopt OF-4 (orderflow_micro.md) verbatim:
- Step = smallest {1,5}x10^k >= one daily ATR, with atrD = atrSlow*sqrt(86400/chartS), recomputed once per day. timeframe.change("D") is evaluated at global scope (v6 short-circuit).
- Zone cap at 1762/1774/1848: top := R when ph < R < top; mirror for SSL.
- In f_invalidation (1343-1364), place the stop just beyond a round inside the stop band.
- Confluence anchors only with rnConf (default off).
- RN bit for ICT-1.
- Manual step override for exotic symbols.
proposals.risk: The auto step can be off by a factor on exotic symbols (Manual override covers it). Coordinate with the confluence domain to avoid double counting.

proposals.title: Relative-equal symmetry: a micro-poke followed by a right-beyond pivot becomes one EQ pool, not a raid
proposals.rationale: Because step 3 sweeps the left pool before the right pivot confirms, the engine merges only 'left >= right' pairs. A right print 1 tick higher is booked as a raid (liqEvt event, ghost, live alert if active) plus a new single pool without the EQ tag. ICT's 'relative equal' is symmetric. Reach is identical either way (RH −1.6 ± 2.1 pp), so this is a logic and label fix plus a ledger bit, not a score change.
proposals.spec:
State: var arrays msPx (float), msKind, msBar, msEq (int), cap 16.

In step 3, on a liquidity hit with micro (back inside and pen <= eqTol, as in ICT-9): push (price, kind, bar_index, eqCount). Drop entries older than 2*pivLen+1 bars.

In step 9, when a new chart pool is created (1760-1764 / 1772-1776):
- find an entry of the same kind with 0 < (kind == 0 ? ph − msPx : msPx − pl) <= eqPx;
- set nh.eqCount := msEq + 1 and a new Level field bool rh = true;
- remove the entry.

The ghost and the live 'DOL Target Swept' alert are unchanged (decision history: a strict trade-through is a sweep). tag() shows 'EQx2 ⇡'. Sets the RH bit for ICT-1.
proposals.risk: Slightly more EQ tags; no score effect under ICT-10. Must not change the hit definition.

proposals.title: IRL/ERL and premium/discount as a delivery readout and ledger bits only (no multipliers)
proposals.rationale: Traders think in this vocabulary, so the classification is worth showing. But the IRL↔ERL alternation (+1.8 pp on 1H vs −2.3 pp on 5m after liquidity is taken) and the P/D reversal condition (contradicted: +1.7/+5.1 pp continuation on the reversal side) both failed. A's kPhase/kPD multipliers would add noise or a wrong-signed term. Downgraded from A's P2.
proposals.spec:
Requires ICTS-4: f_structure returns the leg's [protected, weak] range.

f_isERL(lv) = liquidity beyond the weak extreme ± 0.1 ATR; everything else is IRL. Phase state (1 = ERL taken, 2 = IRL tagged) expires after H bars.

Display:
- HUD/tooltip tag ERL/IRL.
- Terminal 'DELIVERY' row with ledger-measured odds from ICT-1's ERL/PHASE bits, e.g. 'IRL-first 52% vs geometry 51% (n 140)'.

Advanced inputs kPhase = 0 and kPD = 0 by default. All state on confirmed bars.
proposals.risk: Display could suggest a predictive claim; the measured odds next to it prevent that. Depends on ICTS-4 landing first.

proposals.title: Stop depth from observed sweeps: adopt OF-2 (learned zone depth, sweep classes, invalidation beyond q80)
proposals.rationale: Penetration quantiles of rejected sweeps are stable and chart-specific: q50 0.23-0.28 ATR, q80 0.51-0.64 ATR (B, replicating orderflow_micro T1). The fixed 0.20-ATR zone is about the median, but the 0.10-ATR invalidation buffer (1344) sits inside the stop band. orderflow_micro T4 shows deeper buffers trade win rate for R with expectancy unchanged, so the EV readout stays honest.
proposals.spec:
Adopt OF-2 (orderflow_micro.md):
- Push the penetration (ATR) of each REJECT sweep (computed in ICT-9) into var array<float> penArr (cap 300).
- When size >= 30, set q50/q80 via array.percentile_linear_interpolation.
- New pools use wPx = clamp(q50, 0.05, 0.6)*atr in place of zoneATR at 1520.
- Optional invalidation buffer clamp(q80, 0.05, 0.8)*atr in f_invalidation (1344).
- Terminal 'SWEEP DEPTH q50/q80'.
- The hit definition is unchanged.
proposals.risk: Only REJECT sweeps measure depth (mild survivorship). Zone visuals change slightly, and wider buffers lower the displayed R:R.

result.summary: I merged and corrected both studies, and replicated A's headline result with the engine's own method on local data (CME 1H and 5m, BTC 1H, SPX/NDX daily). The method uses the 3-bar / 1-ATR origin lockout and the distance-matched baseline, the same idea as f_potBase. FVG reach minus baseline: +0.4 pp CME 1H (n 1,756), -0.6 pp CME 5m (n 4,950), -1.6 pp BTC 1H (n 3,337), -2.9 pp daily (n 935). Order blocks: -1.8 to +2.4 pp. 4H FVGs used on the 1H chart: +1.6 pp CME (not significant), -2.8 pp BTC (z -2.3). Whether an array is reached within H bars is a distance question that PoT already answers. I corrected A's size argument: A's raw rates ('big gaps fill less') are mostly distance. What does hold is that the engine's displacement 'quality' is never a positive target signal. On CME 1H, FVGs the engine rejects (q < 0.45) beat the baseline by +7.0 pp (z 3.3), while accepted ones sit at -1.8 pp. On BTC, the top tercile of middle-candle displacement is at -5.5 pp (z -3.8). So array density at line 687 should become neutral. Breakers: A's diagnosis is right. The engine's tookL gate reproduces only 11-24% of ICT/open-source template breakers; removing it reproduces 57-77%, and 20-39% of template breakers are wick-only stop runs the engine never sees. Breakers are also weak targets (-5 to -9 pp on 1H; first retest holds about 50%). The definition must be fixed and breakers down-weighted, with their own ledger family. Respect, disrespect, iFVG retests and the 'first presented FVG' carry no directional information: the +/-1 ATR race lands at 50-52%, and iFVGs hold 49-50% of about 25,000 retests. ICT's IRL-to-ERL alternation and premium/discount rules failed my tests: phase effects are inconsistent and within 3 pp, and the 20-day range shows momentum, not reversion. I dropped A's phase multipliers and P/D prior and turned them into measurement-only panel rows. Opening gaps fill beyond distance only when large (>= 0.5 ATR: +7.4 pp, z 2.2; CE shows no excess). A's ICTPD-6 spec had a src 6/7 collision with PDH/PWH killzone logic. A also missed that the origin lockout applies only to src 0, so HTF FVGs sitting at price can be picked immediately. Caveats: CME history is short (13 months of 1H, 3 months of 5m), and GC was excluded as a suspected data artefact. The vendor studies (Nordman, MarketTrace, Trader Markus, Barot, LuxAlgo) could not be re-fetched this session: the web search budget was used up, Firecrawl was out of credits, and those hosts are outside the network allowlist. Their numbers are kept as A reported them and marked 'not re-fetched'. arXiv 2610.35887 was verified from its full text. Test scripts and raw outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-m/7ce60006-3639-59b1-8cd3-87355409d58a/scratchpad/brief/study/ict_pd_b_tools/.

concepts.name: Dealing range, premium/discount, equilibrium
concepts.definition: Dealing range = swing low to swing high of the most recent leg that swept liquidity or broke structure (ICT: from the protected extreme to the weak extreme, usually 4H/D). EQ = (H+L)/2; premium above, discount below. Quadrants at 0.25/0.75; OTE at the 0.62-0.79 retracement. A close beyond either extreme retires the range. IPDA ranges = highest high / lowest low of the last 20/40/60 trading days.
concepts.dolRole: ICT side prior: from discount the draw is buy-side (premium arrays, BSL); from premium it is sell-side. Target ladder: EQ, then the opposite extreme.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Moderate evidence AGAINST the ICT rule. Test: P(range high reached before range low) minus the gambler's-ruin value p. Engine-like pivot range: about +/-2 pp on CME 1H, about 0 on 5m and daily. IPDA 20-day range shows momentum: in premium, the 20-day high comes first more often than geometry predicts (CME 1H +15.2 pp, z 3.3; BTC deep premium +4.3 pp, z 3.0; daily +2.3 pp). This matches George & Hwang (2004): 52-week-high momentum, 0.45-1.23%/month.
concepts.engineNotes: rngH/rngL = last pivots (727-779), not ICT's leg range (sibling ICTS-4). Shown as PREM/DISC % in the Terminal panel (2323-2333); dayEQ/htfEQ are confluence anchors (967-968). Not used in D or selection, which the data supports. Measurement only via ICTPD-8.

concepts.name: PD array matrix ordering
concepts.definition: From the range extreme toward EQ: old high/low, rejection block, order block, FVG, liquidity void, breaker, mitigation block. Mirrored in discount. Later eras add VI, BPR, iFVG, NWOG/NDOG, propulsion/vacuum blocks and the Unicorn.
concepts.dolRole: Ahead of price, arrays are candidate draws; behind price they are entry inventory. The order is spatial, not a strength ranking. ICT ranks the draw as HTF over LTF, EQH/EQL over single swings, untapped over probed.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Doctrine; it varies by era. Data supports a type prior only for breakers (-5 to -9 pp on 1H). FVG/OB are about random.
concepts.engineNotes: Liquidity has source tiers (f_tierW 505-516). Arrays have no type prior (661-696). ICTPD-1 adds brkPrior only.

concepts.name: Old high / old low
concepts.definition: A prior swing extreme with resting stops beyond it. Swept only when price trades through it.
concepts.dolRole: ICT's primary DOL and the top of the matrix. It is the liquidity mechanism behind the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong for the mechanism and reaction, NOT for reach (corrected from A). Osler 2000: published S/R levels stop intraday trends 60.8% vs 56.2% for arbitrary levels, and firms' strength ratings did not predict. Osler 2003/2005: stops cluster beyond levels and crossing them adds +0.27 to +2.35 bp-hundredths. Kavajecz & Odders-White 2004: S/R = book depth. Reach: the engine's swing pools are hit at -1.5 to +2.2 pp vs random (sibling price_action).
concepts.engineNotes: Chart, STF and HTF pivots, PDH/PWH and sessions (1752-1853). Swept only when traded through (623-624).

concepts.name: Rejection block
concepts.definition: Bearish: from max(O,C) to the high of a swing candle whose long wick ran buy-side liquidity. Bullish: min(O,C) to the low. No fixed wick size; it must sit at a real swing, ideally as a sweep.
concepts.dolRole: Refines where a target at an old high/low realistically completes; take-profits are trimmed to the wick zone.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Pool zones extend beyond the swing by zoneATR (1762, 1774). The body extreme is not stored. ICTPD-9 adds a near-miss statistic.

concepts.name: Order block
concepts.definition: Bullish: the last down-close candle (ICT: 'the lowest candle with a down close that has the most range between open to close') before displacement that breaks structure; validated by trading above its high. Zone = full range (or body). Mitigated = revisited; invalidated = body close beyond the far edge. The smartmoneyconcepts library instead takes the lowest-low candle between the swing and the BOS.
concepts.dolRole: Return-to-origin entry. As a target ahead of price it is reached at the random-level rate.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman (not re-fetched): 73.7% vs 73.7% random. Local replication, reach vs baseline: BTC -1.4, CME 1H -1.8, CME 5m +1.2, daily +2.4 pp. First retest holds 43.7-51.7%. The own-origin sweep (tookL) is inconsistent: -4.9 to +4.8 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: 1663-1748: body-close BOS, first down-close candle from the leg low back up to 5 bars, close > OB high, quality = leg FVG / tookL / leg size, mitigated blocks skipped. Fine as a source; quality must not raise target density (ICTPD-1).

concepts.name: Mean threshold
concepts.definition: 50% of an order block, over the range or the body (conventions differ). A body close beyond it is the first sign of failure.
concepts.dolRole: Validity grading and entry refinement only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Used only to skip already-mitigated OBs (1684, 1696-1700, 1727, 1737-1741).

concepts.name: Fair value gap (BISI/SIBI)
concepts.definition: Bullish: low[0] > high[2], zone [high[2], low[0]]. Bearish: high[0] < low[2], zone [high[0], low[2]]. Typical minimum 0.10-0.25 ATR; middle candle displaces (the smartmoneyconcepts library requires matching colour). 15-34% of FVGs are followed by a same-direction FVG on the next bar.
concepts.dolRole: Internal range liquidity: a candidate target ahead of price, an entry behind it.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Not a magnet. External (not re-fetched): Nordman 73.0% vs 72.9%; S&P daily 69% vs 69%; BTC 75.6% vs 72.4%; Barot about 5 pp reaction, no edge. Local replication with the engine lockout and baseline: +0.4 (CME 1H), -0.6 (5m), -1.6 (BTC), -2.9 pp (daily).
concepts.engineNotes: 907-912, 1867-1889: size gate fvgMin 0.15, quality gate fvgQMin 0.45 (removes about 29% of FVGs, which are as reachable or more), all FVGs tracked for inversion.

concepts.name: Displacement / quality / HTF origin as array target score
concepts.definition: Using middle-candle body/ATR, gap size, BOS proximity or HTF origin to raise an array's attractiveness as a TARGET.
concepts.dolRole: Should be neutral or slightly negative for near-term reach: strong displacement means continuation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Corrected from A: raw size effects (BTC terciles 78.7/61.7/46.0%, SPY gaps) are mostly distance. Distance-controlled local data: engine q < 0.45 +7.0 pp vs q >= 0.45 -1.8 pp (CME 1H, z 3.3); top displacement tercile -5.5 pp (BTC, z -3.8) and -3.1 pp (CME 1H); flat on 5m and daily. Never positive in any dataset. 4H FVG on 1H: +1.6 / -2.8 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: Line 687: dens = min(1, 0.5*qual + 0.3*coil + 0.2*induce + 0.20*[src==2]); qual from 912/1870/1880/1692/1735. With wDens 20 of 100, qual moves the score by up to about 10 points. ICTPD-1 makes it neutral, with dispPri 0.95 for very large middle candles.

concepts.name: Consequent encroachment / fill ladder
concepts.definition: CE = the 50% line of an FVG (also of wicks, gaps, voids). Ladder: tap, then CE, then full fill (far edge).
concepts.dolRole: Partial vs full delivery of an array target; where partial profits are planned.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Local ladder within H: P(CE|touch) 88-92%, P(full|touch) 79-85% (CME 1H 91.2/83.1, 5m 92.1/85.3, BTC 88.4/78.7, daily 92.2/81.6). CE and full-fill reach are at the distance baseline (CE -0.2 to -2.1 pp; full -0.4 to -2.5 pp), so the engine's PoT model prices them correctly. MarketTrace (not re-fetched): BTC 4H 71.8 / 62.3 / 54.2%.
concepts.engineNotes: Non-active arrays delivered at CE by default (123-124, 306, 1565-1577); glow line at the original mid. There is no CE/FULL probability readout (ICTPD-3).

concepts.name: FVG respected / disrespected
concepts.definition: Respected = traded into (often to CE), then continued in the gap direction. Disrespected = body close beyond the far edge, which makes an iFVG. Breakaway gaps are not expected to fill.
concepts.dolRole: ICT reads respect as continuation toward opposite liquidity and disrespect as the draw continuing through.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null result. Race +1 ATR vs -1 ATR from the close of the first touch bar, gap direction first: 50.0% (CME 1H, n 4,283), 50.0% (5m, n 12,717), 52.0% (BTC), 52.3% (daily). After a disrespect close: 50.5-51.2%.
concepts.engineNotes: Disrespect = inversion (1598-1627). Neither event feeds D, which is correct given the data.

concepts.name: Inversion FVG
concepts.definition: A body close beyond the far edge (some use beyond CE). The span then acts with opposite polarity until it is reclaimed.
concepts.dolRole: Retest/entry zone and bias cue; not a target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: First-retest hold, +/-1 ATR race: 49.1% (CME 1H, n 3,857), 50.2% (BTC, n 7,399), 49.5% (5m, n 11,768), 49.7% (daily, n 2,220). Trader Markus (not re-fetched): 38% vs 38% and 47% vs 47% on S&P daily.
concepts.engineNotes: 1598-1644: display and alert only, cleaned after ifvgMaxIn closes or failure. Correct. ICTPD-8 adds an honest hold statistic.

concepts.name: Liquidity void (consecutive FVGs)
concepts.definition: A sudden one-directional run with porous price action; in practice consecutive same-direction FVGs merged into one zone (highest top, lowest bottom) with its own CE.
concepts.dolRole: Internal target after an external raid; thin path.
concepts.evidenceNotes: 15-34% of FVGs are consecutive. Their reach edge does not differ from isolated gaps (within +/-2 pp, except daily -3.7 vs -2.6). No published statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: VP path cost and LVNs (1945-1947). Consecutive FVGs stay separate levels (ICTPD-10).

concepts.name: Opening gaps NDOG / NWOG / RTH gap (vacuum block)
concepts.definition: NDOG = CME 17:00 ET close to 18:00 reopen. NWOG = Friday close to Sunday 18:00 reopen (ICT keeps the last 5, with CE). RTH opening range gap = 16:00 close to 09:30 open (not a time break on 23-hour futures charts). Crypto has none.
concepts.dolRole: Fill targets: the pre-break close is the full fill; S/R at the edges and CE.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Size-gated. CME NDOG (median 0.12 ATR): 96.2% fill vs 95.5% clock baseline, i.e. pure distance. Gaps >= 0.5 ATR: 69.7% vs 62.3% (+7.4 pp, z 2.2; mirror 65.4%). CE shows no excess. Gap-downs +2.1 pp (z 2.0). Sibling NDX gaps >= 0.5 daily ATR +7.9 pp (z 4.5). BTC weekend gaps > 1 ADR fill 43.5% vs a 78.3% mirror (continuation). arXiv 2511.06177: sell-side shocks rebound more.
concepts.engineNotes: No session-break gap targets; session opens are anchors only (964-966). src 6/7 are taken by PD/PW (f_kzAff 597-602). ICTPD-6 adds a unified object: kinds 8/9, src 11-13, shared with sibling CL-4 / PA-2.

concepts.name: Volume imbalance
concepts.definition: Consecutive candles whose bodies do not overlap while the wicks do (bullish: open[0] > close[1]). If the wicks do not overlap either, it is an opening gap.
concepts.dolRole: Micro entry refinement at OB/FVG edges.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Low DOL value; not proposed.

concepts.name: Balanced price range (BPR)
concepts.definition: The intersection of a bullish FVG and a later bearish FVG over the same prices (or the reverse); the newer displacement sets the bias.
concepts.dolRole: Entry zone only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No audited statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed.

concepts.name: Breaker block
concepts.definition: Bearish (ICT): 'a bearish range or Down Close Candle in the most recent Swing Low prior to an Old High being violated'. Sequence: old high H1, swing low L1 (the block), the leg from L1 violates H1 by wick or close, then a close below the block. Bullish mirrors. Open-source template: zigzag C-D-E with E beyond C, then a close through D; the block is the first opposite-colour candle scanning from D back to C.
concepts.dolRole: Retest/entry zone in the new direction. As a target, a retracement destination.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definition from ICT text plus the open-source template. Measured: the engine's breakers match only 11-24% of template breakers, all-BOS-OB breakers match 57-77%, and 20-39% of template breakers are wick-only. As targets after the lockout they are below random on 1H (BTC -7.5 pp, z -4.4; CME 1H -4.9 to -8.3 pp), about 0 on 5m. First retest holds 46-56%.
concepts.engineNotes: 1646-1661, 1691/1706, 1734/1747: obTrk only takes OBs with tookL/tookH (own-origin sweep, the wrong side). Wick-raid breakers are missed. The tooltip (121-122) and README state the wrong rule. Breakers share ledger family 3 with OBs (635). Fixed by ICTPD-2 together with ICTPD-1's brkPrior and family split.

concepts.name: Mitigation block
concepts.definition: A breaker-like role flip with no sweep: the failing swing falls short of the prior extreme (a lower high), then structure breaks; the launching block flips polarity.
concepts.dolRole: Retest/entry zone, graded below a breaker.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics; conventions differ.
concepts.engineNotes: Optional label-only item in ICTPD-2 (default off).

concepts.name: Propulsion block
concepts.definition: A candle that trades into a prior OB (often to MT) without closing through it, then launches away; it becomes a tighter continuation block.
concepts.dolRole: Continuation entry; little target value.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed.

concepts.name: Implied FVG
concepts.definition: UWM = (H + max(O,C))/2, LWM = (min(O,C) + L)/2. Bullish if LWM_t > UWM_(t-2) and L_t <= H_(t-2); zone [UWM_(t-2), LWM_t].
concepts.dolRole: Secondary confluence when a displacement leg left no clean gap.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics.
concepts.engineNotes: Not proposed.

concepts.name: HTF arrays as magnets
concepts.definition: HTF (4H/D) FVGs and OBs are said to be the draw; LTF arrays refine the entry.
concepts.dolRole: HTF targets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Not magnets. 4H FVGs used as targets on the 1H chart: CME +1.6 pp (n 830, z 1.0), BTC -2.8 pp (n 1,496, z -2.3). S&P daily bullish FVG 69% vs 69% (Trader Markus, not re-fetched).
concepts.engineNotes: HTF FVGs only (785-796, 939-942, 1854-1865). They get +0.20 density and slower decay (687, 1864), which is unsupported. They are NOT subject to the origin lockout, which applies to src 0 only (689) — a bug fixed in ICTPD-1.

concepts.name: IPDA 20/40/60-day extremes
concepts.definition: Highest high and lowest low of the last 20, 40 and 60 completed trading days: ICT's HTF external range. Donchian/Turtle stops also cluster there.
concepts.dolRole: External range liquidity and Swing-mode objectives.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Reached at baseline: sibling classic T2 measures 20-day H/L +0.21/+0.72 and 60-day +0.43/+0.30 pp at 5 days. Momentum at the 20-day scale (see the premium/discount concept).
concepts.engineNotes: Only PDH/PDL, PWH/PWL and pivots exist (945-961, 1790-1799). ICTPD-5 (P3) adds them for naming only; tier must not exceed PW; one buffer shared with TIME-8 and ACAD-5.

concepts.name: Internal vs external range liquidity alternation
concepts.definition: After external liquidity is taken with rejection, the next draw is internal (gaps/OBs). After an internal rebalance holds, the draw is the opposite external pool. A genuine breakout breaks the rule.
concepts.dolRole: Would decide the target TYPE next (pool vs array).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null result. Nearest FVG after a raid that rejects vs ordinary bars: phase effect -1.9 to +2.8 pp with inconsistent sign (CME 1H +3.2 vs +0.4, BTC -2.0 vs -0.5, 5m +1.2 vs -0.2, daily -3.0 vs -1.1). Nearest old high/low after a respected FVG vs ordinary bars: +0.1 to +1.5 pp. Raw differences are distance.

concepts.name: Low- vs high-resistance runs (arrays in the path)
concepts.definition: A path through swept swings and same-direction FVGs is low resistance; through fresh swings and opposing imbalances it is high resistance.
concepts.dolRole: Probability and timing of reaching a pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Pools are small barriers (Osler +4.6 pp bounce). Arrays show no reaction at first touch (50-52% race), so an opposing-array path penalty is not supported.
concepts.engineNotes: Inner stacked pools x0.70 (684-685) and VP path cost (1945-1947). Do not add an array path penalty.

concepts.name: Displacement / MSS validation
concepts.definition: Arrays count only if the move away displaced (big-bodied candles closing near their extremes, often leaving an FVG) and broke a swing.
concepts.dolRole: Quality gate for arrays and a structure signal for bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Nordman MSS (not re-fetched): edge ratio about 1.0 at 1 h with or without displacement. arXiv 2610.35887 (full text verified): N 484, trend-aligned 61.6/70.8%, opposed 29.6/24.8%; no information beyond the trend regime.
concepts.engineNotes: dispUp/dispDn (897-904), OBs require a BOS (1666-1681), FVG quality uses BOS proximity (1869-1870). Fine as gates, not as target scores.

concepts.name: First presented FVG
concepts.definition: The first FVG completed after a time anchor (commonly 09:30 NY), ranked highest by ICT.
concepts.dolRole: ICT's preferred intraday array.
concepts.evidenceNotes: CME 5m: reach -2.9 pp (n 139, not significant). At its first touch the gap direction wins only 41.2% of 244 races vs 51.2% for later FVGs — weak evidence against the claim.

concepts.name: Unicorn (breaker + overlapping FVG) and other later terms
concepts.definition: Unicorn = a breaker overlapped by an FVG of the same leg. Later ICT terms (for example the suspension block) were not verified in this session.
