proposals.title: Evidence-based array scoring: neutral density, lockout for every PD array, breaker weight, mild strong-displacement weight, ledger split OB/BRK with expected %
proposals.rationale: All arrays are reached at about the random-level rate (5 external studies and local replication on 4 datasets). The engine's quality and HTF density bonus (687) favours arrays that are never better and sometimes worse: CME 1H q < 0.45 +7.0 pp vs q >= 0.45 -1.8 pp; BTC top displacement tercile -5.5 pp. Breakers are -5 to -9 pp after they form. HTF FVGs escape the origin lockout (689: src == 0 only). OB and BRK share one calibration family, so the ledger cannot learn the breaker deficit.
proposals.spec: (1) evaluate() array branch, replacing 687-690: dens = 0.40 + 0.30*coil + 0.30*induce (no qual, no HTF +0.20); mult *= 1 - 0.5*fill; if kind 6/7, mult *= brkPrior; if disp >= dispHi, mult *= dispPri; lockout `if this.kind <= 7 and (bar_index - this.createdBar < originBars or this.maxAway < awayATR)` mult *= 0.25 (all arrays incl. HTF FVGs; gap kinds 8/9 exempt). (2) Inputs in G_ARR: brkPrior 0.90, dispPri 0.95, dispHi 1.3 (body x ATR). (3) Level field `float disp = 0.0`, set nfu.disp / nfd.disp := fvB1 / fvA2 at 1875/1885 (global series 910-911). (4) fvgQMin stays a clutter gate; update its tooltip. (5) Ledger: grp() = kind<=1 ? (src==0 ? 0 : 1) : (kind<=3 or kind>=8) ? 2 : kind<=5 ? 3 : 4; f_grpName 3 OB, 4 BRK; stats arrays size 5 -> 6 (1066-1071); ALL index 4 -> 5 at 1380-1381, 1470, 2375-2376, 2384, 2388-2389, 2403, 2443 (not raceSt 1494/2420); step 17 adds cm4. (6) Full view loop g = 0 to 4 showing 'hit% vs exp%' (stPE/ng). Optional later: displacement-tercile f_ctxMult. All on confirmed bars; no request calls.
proposals.risk: Low. Arrays are still chosen when best (Clean 'Target: BEFVG' unchanged). Weights are mild and f_calMult corrects them per chart within 10-30 outcomes. The family split requires careful replacement of the literal ALL index.

proposals.title: Correct breaker definition (sweep by the leg leaving the block), wick-raid breakers, dedupe, corrected tooltip/README
proposals.rationale: ICT's breaker needs the old extreme taken by the leg leaving the block; every BOS-created OB satisfies that. The engine's tookL gate (own-origin sweep) reproduces only 11-24% of template breakers (removing it: 57-77%) and misses all wick-only stop runs (20-39%). Wrong labels and tooltip text are visible to ICT users. It must ship with ICTPD-1's brkPrior and family split, because the corrected definition yields 3-4x more breakers and breakers are weak targets.
proposals.spec: (1) 1706/1747: push every BOS OB to obTrk if not f_hasZone(obTrk, bornBar, dir), with tookLiq = tookL kept as metadata; 1654: drop z.tookLiq from the flip condition. (2) New step 8b after 1749: if useBRK and not na(obSwingH) and not raidedH and high > obSwingH (bosUp already reset obSwingH), set raidedH := true; find the lowest low since obSwingHBar (span <= obLook), then the first down-close candle in rI..rI+5; push Zone(dir = +1, qual = 0.5, tookLiq = true) after the dedupe check. Mirror for lows. Reset raidedH/raidedL where obSwingH := ph (1754) / obSwingL := pl (1766). State: var bool raidedH/raidedL (after 1050); helper f_hasZone(array<Zone>, int born, int dir) in STATE HELPERS. Step 7 (1651) flips on close beyond. (3) Tooltip 121-122 and README 'Blocks' row rewritten to the ICT rule. (4) Optional, default off: mitigation blocks (failure swing then break), label BEMB/BUMB, no statistics.
proposals.risk: More candidates; contained by brkPrior, the lockout, poolMax (1951) and the obTrk cap of 30 (1749). History references inside the if already exist in step 8.

proposals.title: Touch / CE / FULL PoT plus a 'then -> next pool' waypoint in the target tooltip; ledger depth stats
proposals.rationale: Traders plan partials at the near edge, CE and full fill. Arrays behave like random levels, so f_potModel at the CE and far-edge distances is already calibrated. The local ladder is P(CE|touch) about 90% and P(full|touch) about 82%. ICT's 'arrays are waypoints to liquidity' is delivered as information, because the multiplier version failed testing.
proposals.spec: Rendering block after `string tip` (2206), for an array target: mid = (oTop+oBot)/2; far = side==1 ? oTop : oBot; pCE = f_potModel(max(0, dist to mid), side, potMu*side); pFar likewise; tip += 'Touch x% · CE y% · Full z%'. Loop pool (<= 40) for the nearest liquidity level on the same side beyond `far`; tip += 'then -> <f_shortName> @ px (PoT n%)'. Same line in the Terminal HUD. Ledger depth: when an array Trial books a hit (f_book 1461), push [ce, far, side, bar0+H] into a var array; update it in step 2; count ladN/ladCE/ladFull; Full view row 'TAP->CE x% -> FULL y%'. Tooltip text is live like PoT; the ledger runs on confirmed bars.
proposals.risk: None to selection; text only. Clean look unchanged.

proposals.title: Large opening gaps (NDOG/NWOG, unified with sibling settlement/ORG) as full-fill targets
proposals.rationale: Small session-break gaps are pure distance (NDOG 96.2% vs 95.5%). Gaps >= 0.5 ATR fill +7.4 pp above a clock-matched baseline (z 2.2); the NDX cash analogue is +7.9 pp (z 4.5). The excess sits at the pre-break close (full fill), not at CE. These are widely watched ICT names. A's spec reused src 6/7 (PD/PW), which would trigger PDH killzone boosts in f_kzAff, and targeted CE.
proposals.spec: Inputs G_KEY: useGap (true); gapMinD 0.10 x prior-day range (about 0.5 x 1H ATR on index futures; TF-independent). Global after 961: sesBrk = timeframe.isintraday and not na(time[1]) and time - time[1] > 1500*timeframe.in_seconds(); wkChg = timeframe.change('W') evaluated every bar. New step 12b: if sesBrk and gap = |open - close[1]| >= max(gapMinD*(aPDH-aPDL), 2*mintick) and the gap is not filled on the break bar, create kind 9 (gap up, target below) or kind 8 (target above), src 12 if wkChg (NWOG) else 11 (NDOG), as a thin zone close[1] +/- 0.05*ATR with price = close[1]; hlMult = sqrt(86400 or 604800 / chartS). Keep the last 3 NDOG / 5 NWOG ids. f_newLevel side map (1085) adds kind 8 -> +1; grp kinds 8/9 -> family 2; f_levelName/f_shortName 8/9 -> NDOG/NWOG/ORG (src 13 reserved for sibling CL-4/PA-2 RTH gap or settlement). Exempt from the lockout (ICTPD-1). The Terminal may draw the full gap box with CE.
proposals.risk: Feed quirks (FX rollover, missing bars) create small spurious breaks; the size gate filters them. Asset-dependent: BTC weekend gaps continue, and crypto has no breaks. On 23-hour futures charts only NDOG/NWOG are visible.

proposals.title: Liquidity-void merge of consecutive same-direction FVGs
proposals.rationale: 15-34% of FVGs come in runs. Separate levels duplicate candidates, risk flicker between adjacent zones, and give a CE of one sub-gap only. Merging does not change edge (consecutive vs isolated within about +/-2 pp), so this is a stability and cleanliness change matching ICT's void and the smartmoneyconcepts join_consecutive convention.
proposals.spec: Step 13 (1868-1886): var int lastBuId/lastBuBar (and the bearish pair). If a new bullish FVG forms at bar_index == lastBuBar + 1 and that level is still in pool with fill == 0: top := max(top, low); oTop := top; price := (oTop+oBot)/2; disp := max(disp, fvB1/fvA2). Otherwise create a new level. fvgTrk stays per gap.
proposals.risk: The merged CE is deeper, so non-active CE delivery takes longer (intended).

proposals.title: Measurement-only 'ICT checks' panel: iFVG hold, premium/discount side, IRL/ERL phase (replaces A's ICTPD-4/7 scoring)
proposals.rationale: The reference product markets iFVG continuation, and ICT traders rely on P/D and IRL/ERL. Local data shows all three are null at the H-bar scale (iFVG hold 49-50%, n about 25k; P/D no ICT effect, momentum at 20 days; IRL/ERL inconsistent within 3 pp). Users should see their own chart's numbers, and nothing should touch the score.
proposals.spec: (a) On the first retest of an active iFVG (step 6, 1630-1644) open a light record: target = touch -/+ 1 ATR, fail = close beyond the far edge, expiry H; expected value p0 = f_race(1.0*atr, far - touch, potSig, -/+potMu) (447); needs a Zone.retested flag and a parallel var array; Full view 'iFVG HOLD k/n vs exp'. (b) Trial.pz = quartile of close in the HTF range (after ICTS-4's fix, else htfRH/htfRL at 923) stored in f_openTrial (1426); book 8 cells (side x zone) in f_book; row 'BUY from DISC k/n vs exp · SELL from PREM k/n vs exp'. (c) Optional: A's ERL/IRL event state tags Trial.ph and reports k/n vs exp per phase, with no multipliers.

proposals.rationale: ICT/RB practice trims targets to the body extreme of an old high/low. The engine's strict 'through the wick' sweep stays. Measuring how often price reaches the wick zone but fails to sweep informs take-profit placement.

proposals.title: IPDA 20/40/60-day extremes as named external-range objectives (one buffer shared with TIME-8 / ACAD-5)
proposals.rationale: They are ICT's canonical HTF range, but they are reached at baseline (sibling T2: +/-0.8 pp), so their value is naming ('20D H') and Swing-mode objectives, not accuracy. Two sibling studies propose the same N-day buffer.

Step 10 after 1799: f_pushExt(extReg, ..., src 8/9/10, anchor bar, prom = range/atr*0.5, hlMult = sqrt(n*86400/chartS)). f_tierW 8 => 0.70, 9 => 0.74, 10 => 0.78 (not above PW, changed from A's 0.84-0.95). f_levelName '20D H/L', '40D H/L', '60D H/L'. result.summary: I merged A's study with my own checks into one final report. Market structure does not predict which side's liquidity is taken first, and the evidence for that is now strong. On 8 markets (NQ, gold, EURUSD, ES, RTY, YM, CL, BTC, hourly) the engine's draw vector D called the first-touched side right 47.4-52.7% of the time, the same as on 8 matched random walks. A found the same on 3 markets. Taylor's AMD paper, which I read in full, agrees, and so do two open-source ICT/SMC backtests: the 2022 model has a profit factor of 0.74-0.87 on ES/NQ over 2014-2026, and a multi-timeframe SMC rule set loses -0.33R out of sample. Yet draw is the engine's heaviest scoring weight (30), counter-draw targets are halved, and selection is draw-side first. I corrected A's fix (ICTS-1). In simulation, A's linear skill ramp switched on 8% of the time on random walks (36% on one), and the periods when it was on were followed by 46-49% accuracy. A significance gate (one-sided lower bound with the measured overlap design effect of about 1.6) never switched on falsely. It also never switched on for any real market, because none had skill. The new 'Measured' mode would drop draw-side-first selection on charts without measured skill. That changes a recorded design decision, so the user needs to confirm the default; 'Always' keeps the classic behaviour. I tested ICT's MSS on 4,032 events. It went the MSS direction 49.4% of the time. With the HTF bias it was 50.0%, so A's 'with-trend resumption' reading is not supported. After an MSS the opposite pool was reached first 55.7% of the time against 56.8% predicted by geometry, so it is not a magnet. Which pool is hit first is geometry: the race from the weak to the protected extreme matched the gambler's-ruin prediction across 8 markets (65.3% vs 65.8%, n 12,148). The engine already has this math, so the Clean label should show it in its tooltip; a third label line would break the reference look. ICT's dealing range should be [protected, weak] of the current leg. Neither that range nor the engine's current one predicts the side (49.1-49.5%), but with ICT's range the premium/discount % equals the geometric weak-first probability, which is calibrated. I found one new robustness gap: the Pine docs do not say how ta.pivothigh treats exact ties. Tied swing windows are common (22% on ES 5m, 40% on 6E 5m), and a leftmost-wins pivot recovers up to 22% of swings, which are exactly ICT's equal highs. Two interaction hints (displacement plus FVG with the HTF swing, and swing-CHoCH continuation) should go on the candidate ledger as measurable bits, not into scoring, because I chose those cells after looking at the results. Several sources could not be reopened (Nordman, Tangirala, Mahadzva, IvanSetuper, Quarter Sequence, Tradeify): web search was used up, Firecrawl was out of credits, and those hosts are blocked. They are marked as not re-fetched. To re-check them, nordman-algorithms.com, ssrn.com, arxiv.org, tradingview.com and luxalgo.com need to be allowed in the session's network settings.

concepts.name: Structure-derived draw vector (bias → DOL side)
concepts.definition: Engine D = clamp(0.5·sV + 0.2·mV + 0.3·liqEvt), where sV = 0.5·htfBias + 0.3·stfBias + 0.2·exeIB, mV is a displacement direction decaying with half-life 12, and liqEvt is the decaying sweep read. |D| ≥ 0.35 sets the draw side (dirSide).
concepts.dolRole: Decides which side the target is chosen from (draw pillar weight 30, ×0.5 counter-draw multiplier, side-first selection, draw-flip alert).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. A, 3 markets: D 49.9-51.6%. B, 8 markets, ±1.5 ATR within 30 bars: D 47.4-52.7%, gated D 41.6-52.7%; random walks 48.4-52.1% and 47.9-54.5%. A's logistic learner was worse than a coin out of sample. Sibling REG-3: side-first selection loses 9-12 pp against geometry. External S1-S5 agree; Taylor was read in full.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed weights at 155-162 and 1891-1898; wDraw 30 (145); ctrMult at 691-693; selection 1964-2035; drawFlip 1896-1898. A's ramp gate false-activates (B4). ICTS-1 adds a significance gate with 'Always' kept as an option.

concepts.name: Market structure shift (MSS, ICT)
concepts.definition: A raid of an old high (a wick is enough), then a close below the short-term (3-candle) low that formed before the run, within about 8 bars, preferably with displacement or an FVG. Defined inside an HTF bias. Algorithm: arm on any raid with level = last ta.pivotlow(low,1,1); the first close through it inside the window is the MSS; a new raid re-arms it.
concepts.dolRole: ICT reads it as a turn of the intraday draw toward the opposite pool (the 2022-model target), or as with-HTF resumption.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. B, 8 markets: 49.4% (n 4,032; random walk 50.3%); with displacement 50.2%; with HTF 50.0% (n 2,031), against 48.7%. Opposite-pool race after an MSS: 55.7% vs geometry 56.8% (-1.2 ± 0.8 pp, n 3,784; control -0.1). A: 45.6% (n 171) / 50.5% (n 97). Nordman edge ratio 0.97-1.13 (not re-fetched).
concepts.engineNotes: Sweeps (1579-1582) and structure (708-782) are independent. Justified only as an alert with a measured follow-through rate (ICTS-6) and a ledger bit (ICTS-8).

concepts.name: Protected (strong) vs weak extremes
concepts.definition: In bullish swing structure, the protected low is the low of the pullback that preceded the last BOS (engine: protL := legL at the break) and the weak high is the running high since that break (legH). Mirror in bearish structure. LuxAlgo's 'Strong Low' is instead the trailing low since the latest swing-low pivot.
concepts.dolRole: Weak extreme = structural target; protected extreme = invalidation. P(weak first) = (C − prot)/(weak − prot) when driftless.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong that the odds are geometry, with no magnet effect. B, 8 markets: 65.3% observed vs 65.8% geometry (n 12,148); random walks 67.3% vs 67.5%. A: NQ 62.8% vs 64.8%, gold 62.4% vs 64.6%.
concepts.engineNotes: Computed at 755-773 (legH/legL at 729-730). protH/protL are returned at 782 but never read after 923-925; legH/legL are not returned. Unused for invalidation (1343-1365), the HTF objective (1984-1989) or the panel. ICTS-4/5/7.

concepts.name: First-passage race (which pool is taken first)
concepts.definition: P(+a before −b) for Brownian motion with drift; driftless = b/(a+b). With a horizon H, eigen-expansion (f_raceH). Corrected by the ledger's decided races (f_raceAdj).
concepts.dolRole: Answers 'which liquidity first' between two known pools.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mathematical result, calibrated empirically: B2 within 0.5 pp across 8 markets; B1b within 1.2 pp after an MSS; control within 0.1 pp. QPOT-06 uses the same math.
concepts.engineNotes: f_race/f_raceH 446-482, f_invalidation 1343-1365, f_raceAdj 1367-1371. Shown only as WIN≤H in the Terminal HUD (2244-2246). ICTS-3 puts it in the Clean tooltip.

concepts.name: Dealing range and premium/discount
concepts.definition: The range of the current meaningful leg. Structure-consistent form: [protL, legH] in bullish bias, [legL, protH] in bearish. Premium above 50%, discount below. LuxAlgo variant: trailing top and bottom of the latest swings.
concepts.dolRole: ICT: from discount, draw to premium liquidity. Reinterpreted: in bullish structure the P/D position equals the geometric P(weak high before protected low).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. B3: the ICT rule 'bull + discount → up, bear + premium → down' scored 49.5% (exec, n 3,001) and 49.1% (HTF, n 2,878); the old range 49.3% / 50.4%; random walks 49.0-50.2%.
concepts.engineNotes: rngH/rngL (727-779) = last pivot high/low, extended while broken. Feeds htfEQ (968, 1931), Terminal P/D (2323-2333), the f_invalidation fallback (1354) and prominence (1783-1789). ICTS-4 returns [prot, weak] with an unchanged tuple shape, plus a W1st readout.

concepts.name: Swing points (3-candle vs N-candle fractal) and tie handling
concepts.definition: ICT: 3 candles with the middle highest, confirmed at the 3rd close. Fractal of strength p: p lower bars on each side, known p bars late. LuxAlgo leg(): right-side-only test plus high/low alternation (swing 50, internal 5). smartmoneyconcepts: centred 2×50-bar window (look-ahead if used in backtests). The ta.pivothigh tie rule is undocumented; tie-safe rule = strictly above the p older bars and at least equal to the p newer bars (leftmost wins).
concepts.dolRole: Unswept swings are where stops rest; the next unswept swing on each side is a candidate draw. Exact ties are ICT's equal highs and lows.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Descriptive measurements. Tied swing windows: 1H futures 3-11%, ES 5m 22%, 6E 5m 40%; a leftmost-wins rule recovers 1.5-5.2% of 1H pivots and 11.5-22.5% of 5m pivots. Pivot lag: 71-75% of raided 3-candle swings never were 5-bar pools (random walks 74-76%, so geometric). EQ density lift is supported (calib_ml +0.29, t 3.6).
concepts.engineNotes: Chart pivots pivLen 5 (90, 879-880); MTF pivots biasLen 3 (65, 709-710); pools created at 1752-1776. Exact double tops may yield no pivot. ICTS-9 adds f_pivHi/f_pivLo with tie counts fed to eqCount.

concepts.name: Break of structure (BOS)
concepts.definition: A candle close beyond the last unbroken swing in the trend direction. Variants: wick vs close, swing strength, minimum distance; smartmoneyconcepts uses a 4-swing pattern. Academic analogue: the trading-range-break rule (close above the N-day max).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed continuation toward the next same-side swing pool.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null intraday. TRB on the DJIA was significant (Brock et al. 1992) but not out of sample after data-snooping correction (Sullivan, Timmermann & White 1999); profits vanish after costs (Zhu et al. 2015, abstract read). Intraday rules fail (Marshall et al. 2008). Tangirala: 44 detectors, none beat random (not re-fetched).
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure upBrk/dnBrk close-based (747-759), protected low re-armed at each BOS; chart BOS for OBs 1542-1547. Correct.

concepts.name: Change of character (CHoCH: internal and swing)
concepts.definition: Internal: the first close through the last swing pivot against structure (LuxAlgo convention; engine ibias). Swing (protected convention): a close through the protected extreme of the leg that produced the last BOS (engine bias).
concepts.dolRole: Claimed reversal toward opposing liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B6: internal CHoCH 50.1% (n 2,467; random walk 50.4%). Swing CHoCH continuation in the new direction 53.7% (n 1,016; random walk 50.1%), at least 52% in 6 of 8 markets, but selected post hoc, so a weak hint. Mahadzva says fade CHoCH+FVG (unverified, weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Swing via protH/protL 760-773; internal ibias 749-753 uses the same 3-bar pivots. Clean table falls back to ibias (2294-2305). Correction: LuxAlgo's swing CHoCH is NOT the protected-extreme break.

concepts.name: Displacement
concepts.definition: An energetic one-sided move. Engine: body ≥ 1.2·ATR[1] with body/range ≥ 0.6, or a two-candle leg with ratios ≥ 0.5 and combined body ≥ 1.8 ATR. Alternatives: body ≥ 1.5·ATR(20) with ≥ 70% of range; body ≫ 20-bar average; leaves an FVG.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed to validate an MSS and imply continuation; 20% of D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null for continuation: B 51.3% (n 4,347; random walk 50.6%); with FVG 50.6%. Hint: FVG + with-HTF 54.0% (n 965) vs against 47.1% (n 946), 7 of 8 markets. Literature: significant intraday reversal after extreme moves (Zawadowski et al. 2006; Heston et al. 2010; Grant et al. 2005). Nordman: no added value to MSS.
concepts.engineNotes: dispUp/dispDn 897-903 good as an FVG/OB gate. wM 0.20 (156), half-life 12 (158), used in D at 1893 with no measured skill. ICTS-1 component skill; ICTS-8 bit DISPHTF.

concepts.name: Sweep outcome read (hold vs reject)
concepts.definition: After a pool is traded through: HOLD = close beyond the zone by holdATR; REJECT = close back inside; NEUTRAL otherwise.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed: hold → continuation, reject → reversal to opposing liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: REJECT → continuation 52.6% (A, n 1,402); +1.5 ± 0.7 pp (ict_liq B7, n 5,899). HOLD against the HTF reverses 56% (n 381); with the HTF continues 53%.
concepts.engineNotes: 1579-1582: REJECT = −1 has the wrong sign, HOLD ignores the HTF, stacked hits sum. Fix with ict_liq.final ICT-9 (= ICTS-2).

concepts.name: ICT 2022 mentorship model
concepts.definition: HTF bias → raid of an obvious pool (killzone) → displacement close through the pre-raid STH/STL (MSS) → FVG retrace entry → stop beyond the raid → target the opposite pool.
concepts.dolRole: Target = the opposite liquidity pool after the raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Null. Opposite-pool race equals geometry (B1b, -1.2 pp, n 3,784). truongxxxx ict-backtest ES/NQ 2014-2026: PF 0.87 (337 trades) / 0.74 (322). SMC multi-TF falsification: -0.329R OOS, 0/42 configs survive BH-FDR. IvanSetuper: ±0.05R before costs (not re-fetched).
concepts.engineNotes: Pieces exist (liqEvt 1579-1582, D flip 1895-1899, opposite-side selection 1964-2035); the sequence is not coded. Rejected for scoring.

concepts.name: AMD / Power of 3 session model
concepts.definition: Asia accumulation range; London false break of one side (breach ≥ δ, close back inside); NY delivery to the opposite Asia extreme. Taylor's outcome is the 4 PM close vs the Asia midpoint.
concepts.dolRole: Target = opposite side of the Asia range after a London raid.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Taylor arXiv 2610.35887, full text read: fires on 44% of days; 57% delivered before 9:40; bullish 46.9%, bearish 39.9%. Regime cells: aligned 61.6% / 70.8%, against 29.6% / 24.8%. 'The trend is doing the predicting.' The regime cells are in-sample labels of a daily close, not evidence that trend forecasts the intraday draw.
concepts.engineNotes: Killzone affinity f_kzAff (597-602): London raids Asia ×1.20; no regime conditioning.

concepts.name: HTF trend regime / trend persistence
concepts.definition: Trend state from HTF swing structure or EMA distance. In the literature, weak trends persist from hours to about 1-2 years and strong trends revert; below about 15 minutes weak trends revert.
concepts.dolRole: The only structure-family variable with consistent directional information, but only at long horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong at 1-12 months (Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen; Lempérière et al., t≈5 since 1960, read). Safari-Schmidhuber 2025 (read): small coefficients at hours to days. Kurth-Eisler-Rej-Bouchaud 2026: short-term trend following failed after 2009. At 30 1H bars, B: HTF bias 48.3-52.4% on 8 markets = none.
concepts.engineNotes: htfBias is 0.5 of sV (1892) and keys the empirical PoT surface (1530-1531, 1284). A called the split 'good'; at this horizon it only dilutes samples (REG-1/BIAS-6 own the change).

concepts.name: STH / ITH / LTH hierarchy
concepts.definition: STH = 3-candle swing; ITH = STH with lower STHs on both sides (or a high made rebalancing an imbalance); LTH = ITH with lower ITHs on both sides, usually daily. Breaking an ITL is significant; breaking an STL is a shift.
concepts.dolRole: Swing order approximates pool size; the ITH/LTH above is the objective, the ITL is protected.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definitions only. The tier proxy adds little beyond distance (ict_liq E6; calib_ml tier lift negative).
concepts.engineNotes: Proxied by timeframe tier f_tierW (506-516); no nested ITH/LTH (ict_liq ICT-8).

concepts.name: ITH/LTH and HTF weak extreme as targets
concepts.definition: Once the ITL forms, the HTF leg's weak extreme (ITH/LTH) is the objective.
concepts.dolRole: HTF objective / ERL target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ICT doctrine; tier adds little beyond distance; the weak extreme is not a magnet beyond geometry (B2).
concepts.engineNotes: STF/HTF pivots register about 4 HTF bars late (1779-1789; hValid 780-781). The current HTF leg extreme is invisible until then. ICTS-7 needs only +1 tuple element (55 of 127) with ICTS-4.

concepts.name: Turtle soup
concepts.definition: New 20-day low below a prior 20-day low at least 4 sessions old; buy stop above the old low (Connors-Raschke). ICT adds discount context and a later MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Claims reversal to opposite liquidity after a false break.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Closes back inside lean to continuation (52.6%, +1.5 pp); the age filter is untested; no published statistics found.
concepts.engineNotes: Sweeps read at 1579-1582 with no age/context filter (ict_liq.final).

concepts.name: Optimal trade entry (OTE 62-79%)
concepts.definition: Entry band at the 62-79% retracement (70.5% sweet spot) of the displacement leg, ideally in discount and overlapping an FVG/OB.
concepts.dolRole: Entry location; for the draw, geometry only (deeper pullback = nearer protected low).
concepts.evidenceNotes: Tradeify (not re-fetched): continuation falls monotonically with depth, no Fibonacci bump. Gurrib et al. 2022 (abstract): Fibonacci system beat buy-and-hold on energy stocks, with no distance baseline.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed; geometry is in the race/PoT models.

concepts.name: Market maker buy/sell model (MMXM)
concepts.definition: Original consolidation → staged run to a sell-side objective (engineering liquidity) → smart money reversal (sweep + MSS/CISD) → retrace taking interior consolidations nearest first, ending at the original consolidation; −2 to −2.5 SD projections beyond.
concepts.dolRole: Target ladder of interior pools after the SMR.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No published test. Its core (sweep → MSS → opposite pool) tests at geometry (B1b).
concepts.engineNotes: Implicit via proximity after D flips; no SMR detector. Rejected for scoring.

concepts.name: Change in state of delivery (CISD)
concepts.definition: A body close back through the open of the first candle of the last consecutive down-close (up-close) series into a swept extreme; fires earlier than an MSS.
concepts.dolRole: Entry trigger only.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No statistics; only uncommented open-source indicators exist.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed by a target engine.

concepts.name: Directional-change overshoot scaling law
concepts.definition: After a reversal of threshold δ, price extends on average about δ beyond confirmation, with an exponential-like tail (median about 0.70δ under a random walk).
concepts.dolRole: Prior for leg extension; a per-chart persistence meter.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Glattfelder-Dupuis-Olsen (13 FX pairs; confirmed to exist). A's simulation shows a random walk gives the same law; Houweling 2025: DC share ≈ 1−1/e (memoryless). Gold and NQ overshoot slightly more than a random walk; leg direction predicts first touch only 47-56%. Strong as a law, none as an edge.
concepts.engineNotes: Not needed; the empirical PoT learns excursions.

concepts.name: Structure-shift alerts and per-chart structure measurement
concepts.definition: Alerts on an HTF swing-bias flip and on an execution MSS after a raid, each with the chart's measured follow-through; structure bits (weak-extreme target, HTF side, recent MSS, with-HTF displacement, swing CHoCH) on the candidate ledger.
concepts.dolRole: Workflow and honesty: shows the trader which ICT structure claims hold on this symbol.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Edge evidence is null (B1, B6). Measurement value: ICT-1/CAL-3 method (moderate).
concepts.engineNotes: Alerts exist only for new DOL, iFVG, sweep and draw flip (2077-2094). The draw-flip alert fires on a skill-less D. ICTS-6, ICTS-8.

proposals.title: Evidence-gated draw: D steers target choice only after this chart shows statistically significant side skill (significance gate replaces A's ramp)
proposals.rationale: The draw pillar (weight 30), the ×0.5 counter-draw multiplier, draw-side-first selection, the 2× flip hysteresis and the draw-flip alert all assume D knows the direction. On 11 markets (A + B) D scored 47.4-52.7%, inside the random-walk band, and REG-3 finds side-first selection loses 9-12 pp against geometry. A's linear skill ramp switched on 8.2% of the time on random walks (35.6% on one) and was followed by 46-49% accuracy. A significance gate never switched on falsely, and it also never switched on for any real market (none had skill). Decision-history note: 'Measured' mode changes draw-side-first selection on skill-less charts, so the user should confirm the default; 'Always' keeps the classic behaviour.
proposals.spec: Inputs (G_FLOW, after 166): drawMode ['Measured','Always','Off'] (default Measured), dSkK 1.5 ATR, dSkEvery 5, dFloor 0.25. Constants: prior 60, design effect 2, z 1.96. TYPE DProbe{float up, float dn, int bar0, int dS, int sS, int mS, int lS, int hS} after Trial (~396). STATE (after 1080): var array<DProbe> dq; var array<float> skN, skK (5 cells: D, sV, mV, liqEvt, htfBias); var float drawRho. Helpers after STATE: f_skill(c) = (skK[c]+30)/(skN[c]+60); f_skLB(c) = f_skill(c) − 1.96·sqrt(0.25·2/(skN[c]+60)); f_skBook(c,s,y). ENGINE step 2b (after the Trial loop ~1557): resolve probes (u = high>=up, d = low<=dn; exactly one → book all cells and remove; both or age>=H → remove unbooked). Step 14 (after 1895): every dSkEvery bars push DProbe(close±dSkK·atr, bar_index, dirSide, int(sign(sV)), int(sign(mV)), int(sign(liqEvt)), htfBias); drawRho := Always ? 1 : Off ? 0 : max(dFloor, clamp((f_skLB(0)−0.5)/0.03, 0, 1)); int dirSel = drawRho >= 0.5 ? dirSide : 0. Step 17 (1948): evaluate(..., drawD·drawRho, ...), so at the floor the draw pillar is ±3.75 pts and ctrMult never fires (|0.25·D| < dGate). Step 19: dirSel in elig (1975), ctrHold (2001), curElig (2004), activeCtr (2029) and the INVALIDATED ghost; the HTF objective keeps dirSide. drawFlip (1897) also requires drawRho >= 0.5. REG-3 factor multiplies in if implemented; BIAS-1's prequential side skill replaces the probe if built. UX: Terminal DRAW row 'skill 51% (n 812) ×0.25'; Full view component skills; data-window plot of drawRho. Cost ≤ 64 probes (≈ 6 live), O(1) each.
proposals.risk: The product spec's 'Draw Direction' becomes mostly neutral on most charts (the floor keeps it visible). A chart with real skill needs about 400-600 resolved probes before the gate opens. The probe label is a direction proxy; the ledger EDGE measures the target-level effect.

proposals.title: Fix the raid → draw mapping in liqEvt: implement ict_liq.final ICT-9 (neutral REJECT, HTF-conditioned HOLD, one event per side per bar)
proposals.rationale: Line 1581 maps REJECT to reversal (−1). Measured: continuation 52.6% (n 1,402) and +1.5 ± 0.7 pp (n 5,899). A HOLD against the HTF swing reverses 56% (n 381). Stacked hits sum and 1-tick pokes count, so one bar can flip D. ICT-9 already merges ICTS-2 and BIAS-4; this domain adds that the MSS built on raids is 49.4% (n 4,032).
proposals.spec: Per ict_liq.final.md ICT-9: input holdATR 0.20 (G_FLOW); before the pool loop (~1559) float evB = 0, evS = 0; replace 1580-1582: pen = penetration/atr; back = close back inside; hold = close beyond price ± holdATR·atr; micro = back and pen <= eqTol; e = hold and not micro ? (htfBias == side ? 1 : htfBias == −side ? −0.5 : 0.5) : 0; sv = side·e·tier; keep the strongest |sv| per side; after the loop liqEvt := clamp(liqEvt + evB + evS, −1, 1). The ICT-2 learner later replaces the static values; ICTS-1 component cell 3 reports liqEvt's skill.
proposals.risk: D reacts less to raids, so draw flips are rarer (intended). The sample is one 1-2 year window per market.

proposals.title: 'Which pool first': show the calibrated first-touch race against the opposing pool in the Clean label tooltip (optional label line)
proposals.rationale: The core question is which liquidity is taken next. Structure cannot call the side, but the race between two known pools is geometry and is calibrated: B2 65.3% vs 65.8% (n 12,148, 8 markets); after an MSS 55.7% vs 56.8%. The engine computes it (f_raceH via f_invalidation, ledger-corrected by f_raceAdj) but shows it only in the Terminal HUD. Correction to A: a third label line would break the reference two-line look, so the default is the tooltip.
proposals.spec: f_invalidation (1343-1365): loop 'for [i, lv] in pool', track int oppI (set when best updates), return [inv, d/risk, p, oppI]. Destructurings: 1428 [inv, rr, pR, oI0]; 2127 [i0, i1, i2, i3], with i3 kept in a global var int invOpp next to invWin. Input raceShow ['Tooltip','Label line','Off'] (G_DOL, default Tooltip). Clean branch (2213-2226): oppTag = invOpp >= 0 ? f_shortName(pool.get(invOpp).kind, pool.get(invOpp).src) : '-1.5 ATR'; rTxt = '1st vs ' + oppTag + ': ' + str.tostring(invWin·100,'0') + '%'; Tooltip mode appends rTxt plus an explanation (decided within H bars; corrected by raceSt n) to tip; Label mode also appends it to the label text. Optional dotted line at the opposing near edge (1 line). Graded by raceSt (1079).
proposals.risk: With no opposing pool within maxATR the barrier is 1.5 ATR, and the tag must say so. The drift term should follow QPOT-01 (zero drift).

proposals.title: Tie-safe swing pivots (leftmost wins) with the tie count fed into the EQ density
proposals.rationale: The ta.pivothigh tie rule is undocumented. Exact ties at the window maximum occur in 3-11% of 1H swing windows on futures and 22-40% of 5m windows on ES/6E. Under a strict rule an exact double top (ICT's equal highs) yields no pivot: no BSL pool, no EQ count, no OB BOS reference and no MTF structure pivot. A leftmost-wins rule recovers 11.5% (ES 5m) to 22.5% (6E 5m) of all pivots, and EQ is the one density input with measured support (+0.29, t 3.6).
proposals.spec: PURE HELPERS, before 699: f_pivHi(float src, int p) => hh = ta.highest(src, p); older = hh[p+1]; if bar_index >= 2p and src[p] > older and src[p] >= hh: pv = src[p]; ties = count k in 0..p−1 with |src[k] − src[p]| <= mintick/2; return [pv, ties]. f_pivLo is the mirror (ta.lowest, <, <=). Replace 879-880 with [ph, phTies] = f_pivHi(high, pivLen), [pl, plTies] = f_pivLo(low, pivLen). Set nh.eqCount := phTies and nlo.eqCount := plTies on the new-level paths (1761-1763, 1773-1775). In f_structure (709-710) use [pvHi, tH] = f_pivHi(high, len) and [pvLo, tL] = f_pivLo(low, len); the tuple is unchanged. Before shipping, check counts against ta.pivothigh with a 10-line TradingView script on ES 5m.
proposals.risk: Slightly more pools on coarse-tick charts (they are real equal highs). If ta.pivothigh already keeps a tied bar, the change only adds explicit semantics and the EQ count. ta.highest must be computed into a variable every bar before taking its history.

proposals.title: Return ICT's dealing range [protected, weak] from f_structure and show the calibrated 'weak-first' odds in the Terminal P/D cell
proposals.rationale: rngH/rngL shrink to a sub-swing after any internal lower high, which corrupts the Terminal P/D %, the htfEQ confluence anchor, the f_invalidation fallback and every sibling dealing-range proposal (ICT-4 IRL/ERL, ICT-1 bit 14, ict_pd items). Neither range predicts the side (B3: 49.1-49.5%), so the value is semantic. With ICT's range, the bullish P/D position equals the geometric P(weak high before protected low), which B2 measured as calibrated: an honest number in place of a folklore label.
proposals.spec: In f_structure after the bias block (ends at 773), before the range extension (775-779): float drH = bias == 1 ? legH : bias == -1 ? protH : rngH; float drL = bias == 1 ? protL : bias == -1 ? legL : rngL; return drH[1], drL[1] instead of rngH[1], rngL[1] at 782 (shape unchanged, no call-site edits; protL/protH are set at every transition, so there are no na holes). Terminal ZONE cell (2327-2332): wf = sb == 1 ? pos : sb == -1 ? 1 − pos : na; zn = PREM/DISC pct + ' · W1st ' + wf pct; tooltip: 'In discount of a bullish leg the protected low is nearer than the weak high'. Non-repainting through the same [1] + lookahead_on read.
proposals.risk: htfEQ values change, so some confluence scores shift; the P/D readout looks more 'premium' right after breaks. Prominence magnitudes (1783-1789) grow slightly in trends.

proposals.title: Structure bits on the candidate (shadow) ledger: per-chart measurement of ICT structure claims (extends ict_liq ICT-1)
proposals.rationale: The only structure effects in B's data are two interaction hints: displacement + FVG with vs against the HTF swing (54.0% vs 47.1%, 7 of 8 markets) and swing-CHoCH continuation (53.7%, 6 of 8). Both were selected after looking, so putting them in scoring would be data-snooping. ICT-1's candidate ledger grades every pool against f_potBase with a block-cluster z-gate and neutral defaults, which is the right home for them.
proposals.spec: Raise ICT-1's NF from 16 to 21. Bits set at snapshot (step 17, after 1948): 16 WEAKX (target within eqTol·atr of the exec, STF or HTF weak extreme, legH in bull / legL in bear, via ICTS-4/7); 17 HTFSIDE (side == htfBias); 18 MSSDIR (an execution MSS toward side within H bars, ICTS-6 state); 19 DISPHTF (dispDir == side == htfBias and bar_index − dispBar <= dispHL); 20 CHOCH (exec swing bias flipped to side within H). Lifts, z-gate (|z| >= 2, n >= 100), shrinkage, bounds and UX ('WEAKX ×1.00 (n 214, z 0.3) ~') exactly as ICT-1. Keep DRAW (bit 11).
proposals.risk: More bits mean more multiple comparisons; ICT-1's gate and bounds plus SKEP-9 discipline apply. Depends on ICT-1 / CAL-3 infrastructure.

proposals.title: Protected-swing invalidation option and a weak-extreme tag on the HTF objective
proposals.rationale: ICT/SMC traders put risk beyond the protected low and aim at the weak high. f_invalidation uses the nearest opposing pool, so the Terminal R:R, WIN≤H and EV describe a different trade. The race odds are geometry (B2), so this is semantic alignment, not edge.
proposals.spec: Input invMode ['Nearest Opposing Pool','Protected Swing (Exec)','Protected Swing (STF)'] (G_DOL). In f_invalidation, when protected mode is on and tgt.side == that TF's swing bias: sw = side == 1 ? exeProtL : exeProtH (or stf*, already returned at 924-925); if sw is on the correct side of close and within maxATR, inv := sw − side·buf, else the current rule. Step 19 (1984-1989): if the HTF objective is within eqTol·atr of htfRH (bull) or htfRL (bear) after ICTS-4, append '· WEAK H/L'. Terminal: one dotted PROT line. raceSt then grades the trader's actual stop logic.
proposals.risk: Wider stops show a lower R:R (honest). Small code surface; shares the f_invalidation signature change with ICTS-3.

proposals.title: Structure-shift alerts (HTF swing flip; execution MSS after any raid) with this chart's measured follow-through
proposals.rationale: ICT users want these alerts, but the MSS measures 49.4% (n 4,032) and the HTF bias is about 50% at the engine horizon. Each alert should carry the chart's own measured follow-through, not an implied promise.
proposals.spec: Globals: stlP = ta.pivotlow(low,1,1), sthP = ta.pivothigh(high,1,1); var lastStl/lastSth, mssArmD/mssLvlD, mssArmU/mssLvlU, mssEvt, var array<float> mssSt (n, wins). Step 3: on any hit of a liquidity pool, a BSL raid arms down (lvl = lastStl, arm = bar_index) and an SSL raid arms up. Each confirmed bar: mssEvt := 0; if bar_index − mssArmD <= mssWin (8) and close < mssLvlD, set mssEvt := −1, disarm, and open a ±1.5 ATR / H probe booked into mssSt; mirror for up; then update lastStl/lastSth. htfShift = barstate.isconfirmed and htfBias != htfBias[1] and htfBias[1] != 0. alertcondition(htfShift, 'HTF Structure Shift', ...) and alertcondition(mssEvt != 0, 'Execution MSS', ...) after 2094, plus alert() text 'MSS ▼ after BSL raid · follow-through here 49% (n 171)'. Terminal row STRUCT.
proposals.risk: Alert noise on low timeframes; mssWin and an optional displacement gate reduce it. A few var states only.

proposals.title: Register the HTF/STF weak extreme in the external registry before pivot confirmation (one extra tuple element with ICTS-4)
proposals.rationale: The current HTF leg's weak extreme, the textbook objective, enters the registry only about 4 HTF bars late (biasLen 3 + [1]). Correction to A: with ICTS-4, drH/drL already equal legH (bull) / legL (bear), so only the print time is needed (+1 element per call, total 55 of 127), not +4. Benefit is labelling and HTF tier/freshness; tier adds little beyond distance.
proposals.spec: f_structure also returns wkT[1] (time when the weak extreme last set a new extreme; 13 elements × 3 calls). Step 10 (1779-1789), confirmed bars: if htfBias == 1 and (htfRH − close)/atr >= minDistATR, call f_pushExt(extReg, htfRH, true, 2, f_barAtTime(htfWkT, anchorMax), prom, hmH); mirror for bear with htfRL; same for STF with src 1. f_pushExt dedups by price; the step-4 raid check (1591-1597) removes it when exceeded, and the new extreme registers when price leaves by minDistATR.
proposals.risk: Registry churn (handled by dedup). Requires ICTS-4. Low forecasting value.

result.summary: I merged and corrected A's study and my first pass, and in this pass I verified A's web sources where I could and ran new tests on CME data. Time changes the odds of a level being taken mainly through the intraday volatility clock. Ederington and Lee (J. Finance 1993) show that scheduled news drives most time-of-day and day-of-week volatility. The engine's PoT ignores the clock, so it is biased by hour: mean absolute bias 7.3 pp on 5m with H 30 (worst at 07-08 ET, where it predicts about 52% and 68-69% happen), 8.4 pp on 1H with H 12, and 3.1 pp on 1H with H 30. One real time effect goes beyond volatility. In the US cash-open drive on ES/NQ/YM/RTY, 20-minute windows starting 09:20-09:59 take out the prior 60-minute high or low 10-15 pp more often than a generous clock predicts (SE 1.6-3.2 pp, 60 days). It is absent at the 08:30 releases, after 10:00 and in CL/GC. This corrects my first-pass claim that the '09:50-10:10 macro' excess came from 10:00 data releases. Taylor (2026, N 484) tests Power of 3 / Judas directly: the swept side does not predict the close beyond the daily trend, and 57% of targets are delivered before the 09:40 NY entry. Macros and Silver Bullet are null on sweep rate and on volatility. The midnight open is no more of a magnet than other recent opens at the same distance. IPDA extremes are reached at the random-level rate; 52-week extremes act as volatility barriers rather than magnets. The overnight and pre-FOMC drifts have decayed, and the FX fix and home-hours drifts are real but only a few bp. Correctness bugs: on the default 1H chart the NY AM range is wrong on 76% of days because session tests use only the bar open, and on 2H/4H charts the killzone label and hysteresis are arbitrary. Also, clock timing alone puts ±2-3 pp of fake skill into the ledger's EDGE. Proposals, best first: exact sessions, killzones only on charts of 1H and below, and London DST; a time-of-day surface (helped Brier on every symbol and setting tested, +0.4 to +3.75%; landmark blocks tested, no better); a robust NY-keyed clock gated by a per-chart scorecard (+3.9 to +5.5% on 5m, but -9.8% on GC 1H); a time-neutral EDGE; neutral killzone affinity; session-end PoT with an ETA; ONH/ONL pools; and event scaling stated in σ units (my first pass wrongly used range ratios as variance multipliers).

concepts.name: Intraday/weekly volatility clock (business time, theta-time)
concepts.definition: r_t = sigma_day * s(tau_t) * z_t, where s(tau) is a deterministic periodic factor by NY time-of-day bucket and weekday, and sigma_day is a slowly varying level (Andersen-Bollerslev; Dacorogna et al. 1993 theta-time). A driftless walk's touch probability depends on z = d / sqrt(V), where V is the clock variance left in the window, not on the bar count.
concepts.dolRole: Sets how far price can travel in the next H bars or before the session ends, which drives PoT, reach, race odds and ETA. It is the quantitative form of 'killzones'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Andersen-Bollerslev 1997/98; Ederington-Lee 1993 (announcements cause most time-of-day and day-of-week volatility patterns); Dacorogna 1993; ES 5m variance at 09:30 is 4.7x the daily mean and 0.20x at 23:30. Engine bias measured on CME data: 5m H30 mean |hour bias| 7.3 pp (07-08 ET predicted about 52% vs 68-69% observed); 1H H12 8.4 pp; 1H H30 3.1 pp.
concepts.engineNotes: potSig = ta.stdev(chg, potLen) (916) is time-blind. It feeds f_potModel (1304), f_potBase (1315), the race (1360-1363) and the proximity reach (665, via sig at 1948). The empirical surface (1059-1062, 1527-1532) is ATR-normalised and pooled over all hours.

concepts.name: Killzones
concepts.definition: Windows in NY time (DST-aware): Asian 20:00-22:00 (ICT original; 20:00-00:00 is the Asian session range); London 02:00-05:00; NY AM 07:00-10:00 (index variants 08:30-11:00 and 09:30-11:00); London close 10:00-12:00; lunch 12:00-13:00/13:30; NY PM 13:30-16:00. A bar is in a killzone if [bar open, bar open + tf) overlaps the window.
concepts.dolRole: Says when raids are likely, i.e. when the forward variance is high. It does not independently select which level is taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong as times of elevated activity. As extra raid probability beyond the clock: none (session_stats ±3 pp), except the cash-open drive (09:20-10:00, index futures). Killzone windows re-verified on innercircletrader.net, TradingFinder and LuxAlgo; the Asian KZ boundary is corrected.
concepts.engineNotes: 223-226, 970-976: Asia, London, NY AM 07-10 and NY PM; no London close. On 1H, OFF-KZ covers 12 of 24 hours with doubled hysteresis (976, used at 2012). On 2H/4H the bar-open label is arbitrary: the 4H 10:00-14:00 bar is OFF-KZ (new G20).

concepts.name: Killzone affinity ('London raids Asia, NY raids London/PD')
concepts.definition: ICT session sequence: Asia builds a range, London takes one side, and NY takes London's or the previous day's extremes. The engine encodes it as fixed score multipliers by session and source.
concepts.dolRole: Claims a session-specific preference for which pool is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A random path on the clock reproduces it. Day-bootstrap null: session take rates are within ±3 pp. The residuals (index-futures Asia two-sided raids +3.5 to +6.2 pp; the cash-open drive, which takes any nearby pool) are not what it encodes.
concepts.engineNotes: f_kzAff (596-602), applied at 1941: x1.05-1.20 regardless of distance or forward variance. It double-counts the clock and clusters DOL choices and ledger trials in killzones.

concepts.name: Session ranges as liquidity (Asia, London, NY AM, NY PM, overnight)
concepts.definition: The high and low printed inside a fixed NY-time window, pushed as pools once the window closes. Overnight/Globex 18:00-09:30 gives ONH/ONL.
concepts.dolRole: Very frequent next targets. Their probability is governed by distance and the remaining variance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The Asian range is broken on at least one side about 99% of days (as reported by A). RTH breaks at least one ON side 94.2% (tradingstats, as reported by A) and 96.4% (NexusFi, independent). Versus the null, 'none' is 3.6-4.0% vs 7.4-8.2% (session_stats).
concepts.engineNotes: Asia, London and NY AM pushed at 1800-1809 (gated to ≤1H by intraOK, 947). ONH/ONL is missing; it also holds the 05:00-09:30 pre-market extremes.

concepts.name: Pine session membership on coarse bars
concepts.definition: time(timeframe.period, sess, tz) returns na unless the bar's OPEN time lies inside the session (docs, concepts/sessions.md line 47). Windows starting at :30 therefore begin at the next bar on charts with bars on the hour.
concepts.dolRole: Determines whether session pools and opens are the true levels.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Measured on 349 instrument-days of 1-min CME data. On a 1H chart the engine's NY AM range is wrong on 76.2% of days, off by 14-16% of the day range. An overlap test cuts that to 34.7% and 6-7%; 30-min intrabars make it exact. The NY open anchor is the 10:00 open, a median 15.6% of the day range away from the 09:30 open. The NY PM range misses its high 25% and its low 36% of the time.
concepts.engineNotes: 798-803, 835-863, 948-950, 964-966, 971-974. On 4H futures charts midOpen stays na forever and nyOpen is the 10:00 open.

concepts.name: US cash-open drive (equity-index futures)
concepts.definition: For ES/NQ/YM/RTY, a 20-minute window starting 09:20-09:59 ET takes out the prior 60-minute high or low far more often than a variance clock with the same-day level predicts. Observed 87-93% vs model 72-79% at the 09:20-09:40 starts.
concepts.dolRole: The only measured time-specific rise in the PROBABILITY that nearby liquidity is taken, beyond volatility. It is a short-horizon effect.
concepts.evidenceNotes: New B2 test (macro_attr2.py), 60 days, day-clustered SE. Start bins 09:20 +10.7 ± 2.5, 09:30 +14.3 ± 1.6, 09:40 +14.8 ± 2.5, 09:50 +10.5 ± 3.2 pp. 10:00 +1.3, 08:30 releases -2.8 ± 3.0, rest of RTH -2.6 ± 1.0; CL/GC not significant. Consistent with Gao et al.'s first-half-hour momentum. It explains the 09:50-10:10 'macro' excess.
concepts.engineNotes: Not modelled. A time-of-day empirical surface (TIME-2) learns it per symbol. At 5m with H 30 it is diluted; landmark blocks with a 09:30-10:00 cell gave no extra Brier gain.

concepts.name: Midnight open / true day open
concepts.definition: The open of the 00:00 NY bar, extended through the day. ICT: on bullish days the low forms below it early, then price distributes above it.
concepts.dolRole: A claimed magnet, and a premium/discount split of the day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Raw RTH retrace rates are 57-74% (edgeful 6-month snapshots by open side, LuxAlgo NQ) and 65.6-68.0% (tradingstats, as reported by A). Against neighbouring hourly opens at equal distance the excess is +0.27 ± 1.14 pp (1,412 instrument-days) and +0.35 ± 2.6 pp on 1-min data. The effect is distance and recency, not the midnight time.
concepts.engineNotes: A confluence anchor only (sessMid 220, f_sessOpen 798-803, midOpen 964, anchors 1931, +0.35 per hit at 677). It is in the feature spec ('Session Opens'). Keep it, but make it exact; it is na on 4H.

concepts.name: 08:30 / 09:30 / weekly / session true opens
concepts.definition: Opens at 08:30 (release time), at 09:30 (cash open), the weekly open (Sunday 18:00, or Monday 18:00 in quarterly theory), and the session true opens at 19:30, 01:30, 07:30 and 13:30.
concepts.dolRole: Bias split lines; 08:30 and 09:30 are volatility times.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong as volatility times, untested as levels. classic_levels: weekly and monthly opens act as barriers (-5 to -7 pp); time anchors give +0.6 pp (not significant) at CME and -3.3 pp at BTC.
concepts.engineNotes: London 02:00 and NY 09:30 opens at 221-222 / 965-966 (09:30 wrong on 1H). No 08:30 or weekly open.

concepts.name: Algorithmic macros
concepts.definition: About 20-minute NY windows: 02:33-03:00, 04:03-04:30, 08:50-09:10, 09:50-10:10, 10:50-11:10, 11:50-12:10, 13:10-13:40, 15:15-15:45. ICT claims price sweeps nearby liquidity and/or rebalances an FVG inside them.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed fine timing of raids.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Tested: sweep residual beyond the clock +0.58 ± 0.48 pp over 21,839 windows. Clock variance in the windows vs their neighbours is 0.39-1.22x, so there is no volatility bump. The 09:50-10:10 excess (+6.1 pp) is index-only (ES +12.5, NQ +12.9; GC -0.5, CL -5.9 pp): it is the cash-open drive, not 10:00 releases. Some windows bracket real flows (WM/R fix 11:00 ET, COMEX gold settle about 13:30, NY option cut 10:00), but 10:50-11:10 is -1.1 ± 2.2 pp on CME.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent, correctly. No scoring term. At most a ledger tag.

concepts.name: Silver Bullet
concepts.definition: Windows 03:00-04:00, 10:00-11:00 and 14:00-15:00 NY. After a liquidity sweep, enter on the first displacement FVG toward the draw and target the next pool.
concepts.dolRole: A claimed high-probability time window for a draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Negative evidence is moderate. tradestar: 38.9% win rate at 1:1 over 108 trades (as reported by A). trade_mgmt: PF 0.66-0.94, 0 of 10 variants profitable. EURUSD mechanical bot: 29.6% win rate, PF 0.81. B's window test: +0.19 ± 0.61 pp; 10:00-11:00 alone -0.83 ± 1.04.
concepts.engineNotes: Absent; not recommended.

concepts.name: Power of 3 (AMD) and the Judas swing
concepts.definition: Accumulation (Asia, 19:00/20:00-00:00), then manipulation (London sweeps one side of the Asia range and closes back inside), then distribution (NY delivers to the opposite pool). The Judas swing is the manipulation leg, measured from the midnight or session open.
concepts.dolRole: Claims the first raid of a session is a reversal pointing at the opposite liquidity, and that delivery happens in NY.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Taylor 2026 (arXiv:2610.35887, N 484 NQ days, δ = 10 pts, robust to 5-20): bullish 46.9% (not significant), bearish 39.9% (inverted, p 0.002); trend-aligned 62-71%, counter-trend 25-30%; 57% of targets delivered before the 09:40 entry. FX Asian first-break fade 49.4% (as reported by A). The one residual is the index-futures Asia two-sided raid, +3.5 to +6.2 pp over the null.
concepts.engineNotes: liqEvt (1580-1582) hard-codes 'close back inside = reversal' at any time. ict_liq ICT-2 should learn its sign.

concepts.name: CBDR / Asian range / Flout standard-deviation projections
concepts.definition: CBDR 14:00-20:00 NY. One 'SD' = the range height; rungs H + k*R and L - k*R for k in {1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4}. The London extreme is expected at 1-3 SD (4 SD on news). The Asian range (20:00-00:00) is used if the CBDR is too wide; Flout = CBDR + Asia.
concepts.dolRole: Claims where the day's high or low forms.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No test found. The '<40 pips' rule is a community convention (scripts cite about 1/3 of ADR as ideal, 40% as the maximum). The size fact is a volatility ratio, which the clock already provides.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Quarterly theory
concepts.definition: The day in 6-hour quarters (18-00, 00-06, 06-12, 12-18 NY), each split into 90-minute quarters, applied recursively to week, month and year. Phases AMDX or XAMD; the true open is the Q2 open. Credited to Daye.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed phase timing of manipulation vs delivery.
concepts.evidenceNotes: LuxAlgo publishes no validation. Cycle identification is discretionary, and the AMDX/XAMD choice makes it close to unfalsifiable.
concepts.engineNotes: Not implemented; not recommended.

concepts.name: Daily/weekly profiles and weekday effects
concepts.definition: Templates such as Tuesday/Wednesday low of week, Wednesday reversal, Consolidation Thursday and Seek & Destroy Friday; London/NY reversal or continuation days.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed day-of-week priors for when the extremes form.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The arcsine null is Mon 29.5 / Tue 14.1 / Wed 12.8 / Thu 14.1 / Fri 29.5%, and real data matches a day-order shuffle. The real effect is volatility: day range / ADR is Tue 0.90-0.98 and Fri 1.08-1.11 (variance factor 0.80-1.23), mostly the release calendar (Ederington-Lee).
concepts.engineNotes: The weekday variance factor belongs in the clock (TIME-3) and event scaling (TIME-8); the profiles are not recommended.

concepts.name: IPDA 20/40/60-day data ranges and quarterly shifts
concepts.definition: The highest high and lowest low of the last 20/40/60 trading days (daily bars; some tools use 50), plus their 50% levels, 'cast forward' as draws. A quarterly shift is a change of daily direction near a quarter turn; definitions vary.
concepts.dolRole: Higher-timeframe objective levels for swing horizons.
concepts.evidenceNotes: classic_levels T2: 20/60/252-day extremes are within ±0.8 pp of the random-level rate at 5 and 20 days. Driessen-Lin-Van Hemert 2013: near 52-week extremes implied volatility and beta fall; after a break, realised variance rises 19% (high) / 43% (low). They are barriers, not magnets.
concepts.engineNotes: PWH/PWL (1795-1799), HTF pivots (1782-1789) and htfEQ (968) cover the HTF objective. Optional at most.

concepts.name: Calendar and time-of-day drifts (overnight, pre-FOMC, FX home hours, FX fix 'W')
concepts.definition: Systematic directional returns at certain clock times or dates: ES 02:00-03:00 ET; the 24 hours before FOMC; currencies weakening in their home hours; the dollar rising before FX fixes and falling after.
concepts.dolRole: A drift tilt toward one side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: All real, all small or decayed. Overnight drift 3.7% a year, about zero since 2021 (NY Fed SR917; Liberty Street July 2026). Pre-FOMC drift +49 bp (1994-2011), about 40 bp on press-conference days only, weaker since 2016. Breedon-Ranaldo 2013. Krohn-Mueller-Whelan 2024: about 2 bp daily swings.
concepts.engineNotes: potMu (917) carries a generic drift that QPOT-01 says to remove. Not worth modelling.

concepts.name: Scheduled releases and the institutional clock (releases, WM/R fix, NY option cut, gold fix, settlements)
concepts.definition: Known flow times that create volatility: 08:30 and 10:00 data and 14:00 FOMC; the WM/R fix at 16:00 London (11:00 ET; 12:00 in mismatch weeks); the NY option cut at 10:00 ET; the LBMA gold PM fix at 10:00 ET; COMEX gold settle about 13:30, crude about 14:30, ES 15:59:30-16:00 ET. NFP is released on the third Friday after the reference week (the week containing the 12th).
concepts.dolRole: Large, foreseeable jumps in reachability on specific days.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Ederington-Lee 1993; Evans 2018 (pre/post-fix reversal in all 21 pairs); Michelberger-Witte (volatility spikes at the fix minute and at 10:00 ET). Release-hour range FOMC 5.2x, NFP 2.7x, CPI 2.1x (as reported by A), i.e. about 27x / 7x / 4x in variance.
concepts.engineNotes: No calendar in Pine. A clock learns only the average bump. TIME-8 adds a manual event input and an NFP rule in σ units.

concepts.name: Intraday momentum / session opening drive
concepts.definition: The first half-hour return (previous close to 10:00) predicts the last half-hour return (SPY, 1993-2013).
concepts.dolRole: A claimed late-session directional tilt for equity indices.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Gao et al. JFE 2018: R² 1.6% in sample, 1.2% OOS (verified). Mesfin 2026: 0 of 14 OHLCV intraday-momentum families on MNQ survive costs. The related cash-open drive is about range expansion, not the close.
concepts.engineNotes: The generic displacement term (1536-1541, 1893) is fine. No session-return tilt.

concepts.name: Arcsine law (timing of highs and lows)
concepts.definition: For Brownian motion on [0, T] the time of the maximum has density 1/(pi*sqrt(t(T-t))), in business time. Window edges are over-represented.
concepts.dolRole: The null any 'the high forms at X' or 'Tuesday low' claim must beat.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ES HOD in the first 15 minutes: 17.2% (mypivots, as reported by A) vs 17.7% from arcsine plus clock. Panas 2005 finds U-shaped timing of daily extremes. The weekly null is 29.5/14.1/12.8/14.1/29.5%. 'Red first hour → red day' is 65-66% by overlap arithmetic.
concepts.engineNotes: Not a feature. It shows that hard-coded time priors are mostly artefacts.

concepts.name: Opening gaps: NDOG / NWOG / ORG
concepts.definition: NDOG = the gap from the 17:00 close to the 18:00 reopen; NWOG = Friday 17:00 → Sunday 18:00; ORG = previous RTH close → 09:30 open; CE = the gap midpoint. ICT claims gaps act as magnets for days or weeks.
concepts.dolRole: Claimed time-anchored magnets.
concepts.evidenceNotes: session_stats gaps.py, fill vs a mirrored placebo: S&P cash daily gaps -26.8 pp (the edge is a barrier); EURUSD weekend gaps +0.2; BTC CME gap -5.8; index-futures ORG +6.9 pp (n 204, not significant).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent as targets (ict_pd covers gaps as PD arrays).

concepts.name: Time-aware ledger baseline and PoT calibration
concepts.definition: Grade target hits against a random-level baseline matched on distance AND forward variance (time of day), or against a mirrored placebo, and score the displayed PoT with Brier and calibration.
concepts.dolRole: Measures whether target choice beats chance net of timing, and whether the displayed PoT is honest.
concepts.evidenceNotes: skeptic §2.3 F: no-skill pickers timed in busy windows show +2-3 pp of fake EDGE, and -2 to -3 pp in quiet windows; a mirror control cuts mean |z| from 0.69 to 0.24.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potBase (1314-1322) is time-blind. Trials open whenever the active DOL has none (2037-2045), so they cluster where turnover is high. The displayed PoT is never stored or graded.

concepts.name: Session-horizon PoT and clock-time ETA
concepts.definition: P(touch before the killzone end / 16:00 / 17:00) from the remaining clock variance. ETA50 = the time when V(tau) reaches (d/0.6745)²; ETA80 uses (d/1.2816)².
concepts.dolRole: Answers 'will it be taken this session, and roughly when' — the ICT 'time stop'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: session_stats: P(PDH/PDL at 0.2-0.35 ADR taken by day end) is 64/57/47/19% from Asia/London/NY AM/NY PM. A vol-time ETA rank-correlates +0.11 to +0.22 with time-to-touch vs -0.09 for constant σ. Taylor: AMD targets are mostly delivered 05:00-09:40.
concepts.engineNotes: ETA|hit is the median bars-to-hit of similar past hits (2105-2126), in bars. H is a fixed bar count (305), shared by Scalping on 5m (2.5 h) and Day Trading on 1H (30 h).

proposals.title: Exact session windows and anchors; London close killzone; killzones only on charts ≤1H; London DST tracking
proposals.rationale: On the default 1H Day Trading chart the NY AM pools are wrong on 76% of days, by 14-16% of the day range. The NY open anchor is the 10:00 open and the NY PM killzone starts at 14:00. Cause: time() tests only the bar open (doc-verified). On 2H/4H charts the killzone label and hysteresis doubling are arbitrary (the 4H 10:00-14:00 bar is OFF-KZ). These are visible errors on the user's chart.
proposals.spec:
(a) Parse each input.session once: f_hhmm(s, at) = int(str.tonumber(str.substring(s, at, at+2)))*60 + int(str.tonumber(str.substring(s, at+2, at+4))); sM = f_hhmm(sess, 0), eM = f_hhmm(sess, 5); eM <= sM means the window wraps midnight. With b0 = hour(time,tz)*60 + minute(time,tz) and chMin = max(1, int(chartS/60)), f_inWin tests the overlap of [b0, b0+chMin) and its copy shifted by -1440 against [sM, eM) or [sM,1440)∪[0,eM). It also returns an exact flag. It replaces not na(time(timeframe.period, sess, tz)) at 799, 836 and 971-974.
(b) Exact bounds when chartS > 1800 and intraOK: one global request, [ltT, ltO, ltH, ltL] = request.security_lower_tf(syminfo.tickerid, "30", [time, open, high, low], ignore_invalid_timeframe = true). f_sessTrackLT and f_sessOpenLT are called every bar, with their bodies on barstate.isconfirmed only. They iterate for [j, t] in ltT, test membership by the intrabar's start minute, extend var hi/lo anchored at bar_index, and keep a var bool wasIn. The emitted tuple is the same as f_sessTrack's. Input exactSess (default true). Fall back to (a) on charts ≤30m.
(c) kzLC = input.session("1000-1200", "London Close Killzone") as kz 5; f_kzName 5 → "LDN CLOSE KZ"; f_kzAff 5 → 1.0.
(d) At 975: kz = not timeframe.isintraday or chartS > 3600 ? -1 : inKzLo ? 2 : inKzNA ? 3 : inKzLC ? 5 : inKzNP ? 4 : inKzAs ? 1 : 0.
(e) ldnDst (default true): offLN = (hour(time,"Europe/London") - hour(time,tz) + 24) % 24. When offLN == 4, shift sM/eM of sessLo, sessLdn, kzLo and kzLC by +60 minutes.
(f) Keep session opens in confluence by default (feature spec), now exact. Add an openConf toggle; mark approximate anchors with '≈'. Inputs use display.none. Non-repainting; 8 of 40 requests.
proposals.risk: Lower-TF arrays differ between realtime and history; consume them on confirmed bars only. Midnight-wrap edge cases need unit checks (Asia 2000-0000, ON 1800-0930, a 23:00 bar). Including a straddling bar in (a) adds pre-session prices; (b) fixes that.

proposals.title: NY time-of-day dimension (8 x 3-hour blocks) in the empirical PoT surface, partially pooled
proposals.rationale: The default PoT is biased by up to 17 pp by hour (mean 7.3 pp on 5m H30; 8.4 pp on 1H H12). This split improved Brier in all 24 symbol x setting tests: +2.2% (5m H30/H60), +3.75% (1H H12), +0.4% (1H H30), ECE ≤0.015. Being empirical, it also learns the effect beyond volatility (the index cash-open drive), which a pure clock cannot. It also makes f_potBase time-aware. Twelve killzone-aligned landmark blocks were tested and are not better.
proposals.spec:
Input todOn (G_POT, default true, display.none). Constants NQ = 8, NQ1 = 9 (row 8 = pooled), TODM = 60.
Series after 920: todQ = todOn and timeframe.isintraday and chartS <= 3600 ? int(hour(time, tz)/3) : NQ.
State at 1061-1062: sUp/sDn = array.new<int>(3*NQ1*NB1, 0); row = regime*NQ1 + q.
Step 0 (1528-1532): with bH = htfBias[H] and qH = todQ[H], bump the pooled rows (bH+1)*NQ1+NQ and (1-bH)*NQ1+NQ. If qH < NQ, also bump the cell rows.
f_empPoT(dAtr, side, bias, q): pooled pP/nP with the existing gate and fallback (nAll from the pooled rows); cell pC/nC; nCe = nC/max(1, 0.6*H); p = (nCe*pC + TODM*pP)/(nCe + TODM); return [p, nP], so the analytic blend weight is unchanged.
Callers f_potModel (1307) and f_potBase (1318) pass todQ (the live bar's block for the live PoT). f_reachD and the reach bands (2108-2111) use the cell row when its n ≥ max(150, 20*H), else the pooled row. O(NB) per bump; 3.3k ints; max_bars_back is fine for H ≤ 450.
proposals.risk: Slower per-cell convergence (handled by pooling). On 1-minute charts hourly blocks might do better; untested. The DST London shift is mostly absorbed by 3-hour blocks.

proposals.title: Robust NY-keyed volatility clock with forward variance and a z-unit empirical surface (Auto-gated)
proposals.rationale: It is the largest PoT gain measured in any study: Brier +3.9% (5m H30), +5.5% (5m H60), +3.9% (1H H12), all 6 symbols positive on 5m; hour bias 7.3 → 2.1 pp. It is the symbol-learned form of killzones, weekday volatility and theta-time, and it supplies the forward variance for TIME-5, TIME-6 and TIME-8. It fails on GC 1H (-9.8%) and does not help 1H with H30, so it must be gated per chart.
proposals.spec:
Inputs clkMode (Auto/On/Off, default Auto), clkMin (15/30/60, default 30), clkMem (40 days). Derived: bkMin = max(clkMin, chMin); clkOK = intraday and bkMin <= 240 and 1440 % bkMin == 0; NBK = 1440/bkMin; bpb = bkMin*60/chartS.
Series: xVar = max(0, 0.5*ln(H/L)² - (2ln2-1)*ln(C/O)²) + ln(O/C[1])² (GK plus gap); cB = (hour*60 + minute)/bkMin; cD = dayofweek - 1, all in tz.
Robust learning on confirmed bars, over all loaded bars: an additive EWMA of the deseasonalised ratio, ratio = min(xVar/clkLs, 50); clkA[cB] += max(1-0.5^(1/(clkMem*bpb)), 1/n_b)*(ratio/clkD[cD] - clkA[cB]), floored at 0.05; clkD likewise with 5x slower memory, floored at 0.2. Slow level clkLs (about 5 days) and fast level clkLf (2/(potLen+1)), with clkLf ≥ 0.2*clkLs. Cell counts clkC[7*NBK]. Daily renormalisation to a bar-weighted mean of 1.
f_fwdVar(h), computed once per bar: walk the rest of the current bucket, then cells open by count (clkC ≥ 0.3*(days/7)*bpb, which skips halts and weekends), with a guard of 7*NBK+8; returns v*clkLf.
Phase B: fwdSd = close*sqrt(fwdV) as a series. zUp/zDn surfaces with TIME-2's row layout, grid 5/NB; bump with (fwdHi - close[H])/fwdSd[H]. Query z = d/fwdSd; driftless erfc prior capped at 0.95; same blend.
potSel (0 ATR pooled / 1 tod / 2 clock) is set by TIME-4 in Auto. Reach (665 via sig at 1948) and the race (1360) use sigH = close*sqrt(fwdV/H) when potSel == 2. No new request; memory under 1k.
proposals.risk: Jump-heavy series and regime shifts (GC 1H). A's multiplicative spec breaks (zeroed buckets) and gains only about +0.9%, so the robust form is mandatory. Holidays and early closes overstate V. It needs 5 days of warm-up.

proposals.title: Per-chart PoT scorecard with model auto-selection, a time-neutral EDGE baseline, and EDGE by killzone
proposals.rationale: The best PoT model depends on timeframe, horizon and symbol (the clock wins on 5m and loses on GC 1H), so only the user's chart can decide. DOL trials are too few to detect 1-4% Brier gaps; cheap probes are not. Clock timing alone puts ±2-3 pp of fake skill into EDGE (skeptic E30), as large as the edges the evidence allows.
proposals.spec:
Probes: at each confirmed bar, 6 probes (k = 1, 2, 3 ATR x side) x 3 models (0 pooled ATR, 1 tod, 2 clock). Ring buffer prb = array.new<float>((H+1)*18, na), index ((bar_index % (H+1))*6 + j)*3 + m. Resolve slot (t-H) % (H+1) with the step-0 window: y = fwdHi - close[H] >= k*atr[H] (or the mirror). Accumulate n, Σ(p-y)², and per-bar Brier differences vs model 0, in 2H-bar blocks for a cluster-robust z (the cluSt pattern, 1463-1469; scSt = array.new<float>(15, 0)).
Selection once a day (timeframe.change("D")): the model with the lowest Brier among those with ≥2,000 resolved bars and z ≤ -2 vs model 0; hold at least 5 days.
Baseline: f_potBase (1314) uses the selected model, driftless. Pair it with skeptic SKEP-2's mirror control to remove the residual clock bias.
Trials (375-395) gain pPot (the displayed PoT at open) and kz0. f_book adds kzN/kzK/kzE arrays (size 7, index kz0+1).
Terminal panel (Accuracy = Full): 'PoT MODEL CLOCK ✓ · Brier -3.9% · z 6.1 · 14k bars'; 'PoT CAL pred 44% · obs 46% · n 212'; 'EDGE by KZ LDN +5.8 · NYAM +6.3 · OFF +1.9 pp'. 18 O(1) evaluations per bar; at most 8.1k floats; confirmed history only.
proposals.risk: Probes grade models at fixed distances, not at the DOL's own distance (QPOT-04's trial calibration covers that). Early noise, gated by n and z.

proposals.title: Neutral killzone affinity by default (Off / Fixed legacy / Learned) and continuous, clock-based hysteresis
proposals.rationale: f_kzAff multiplies session and PD pool scores by 1.05-1.20 in fixed killzones regardless of distance. The clock-matched null puts those raids within ±3 pp. The real time residuals (the cash-open drive; the index Asia two-sided raid) are not what it encodes, and TIME-2 learns the first. With TIME-2/3 the fixed multipliers double-count timing and bias the ledger. The binary off-killzone hysteresis rule is a crude stand-in for 'the next bars are quiet'.
proposals.spec:
kzAffMode = input.string("Off", "Killzone Affinity", options = ["Off", "Fixed (legacy)", "Learned"], group = G_FLOW, display = display.none). At 1941: lv.mult *= mode == Fixed ? f_kzAff(kz, lv.src) : mode == Learned ? f_kzLearn(kz, lv.src) : 1.0. Learned uses session_stats SESS-3 or ict_liq ICT-1 probes, shrunk with w = n/(n+40) and bounded to [0.85, 1.15].
Hysteresis at 976: hystEff = clkUse ? hyst * clamp(sqrt(H / max(fwdSum, 1e-9)), 1, kzHx) : (kz == 0 ? hyst*kzHx : hyst), with fwdSum = f_fwdVar(H)/clkLf. With TIME-1d, charts above 1H have kz = -1, so they are never doubled.
proposals.risk: Users who like the ICT narrative can choose Fixed (legacy). The Learned cell is noisy early (shrinkage and bounds).

proposals.title: PoT by session end (killzone end / 16:00 / 17:00) and an ETA in clock time
proposals.rationale: Traders ask 'will it be taken in NY AM / before the close?'. P(PDH/PDL taken today) falls 64 → 57 → 47 → 19% from Asia to NY PM. A vol-time ETA ranks time-to-touch correctly; a bar-count one does not. Scalping on 5m and Day Trading on 1H share H = 30, i.e. 2.5 hours vs 30 hours.
proposals.spec: Inputs potHor ('Bars (H)', 'Killzone End', 'NY Close 16:00', 'Day End 17:00') and showEta. Use the TIME-3 grid walk to count open-cell bars hS to the end minute (in tz) and V(hS). PoT_S = the z-surface at z = d/(close*sqrt(V)) (horizon-free), else the analytic 2Φ(-z). ETA50: walk until V ≥ (d/0.6745)²; ETA80: (d/1.2816)². On barstate.islast convert with time(timeframe.period, "", tz, -k) (k ≤ 500) and str.format_time(t, "HH:mm", tz). Terminal HUD: 'PoT 30b 41% · →16:00 63% · ETA ≈10:40'. In Clean style the tooltip only, so the reference face is unchanged. In the ledger, trials store hT when the horizon is not Bars, and f_step (1455) uses t.bars >= t.hT. Without the clock, fall back to the ATR surface and the bar ETA.
proposals.risk: Future projection ignores holidays, so the ETA is labelled '≈'. Requires TIME-3.

proposals.title: Overnight (Globex 18:00-09:30) high/low as registry pools (ONH/ONL)
proposals.rationale: These are the most-watched index-futures pools. RTH breaks at least one ON extreme 94-96% of NQ days, somewhat more than the null ('none' 3.6-4.0% vs 7.4-8.2%), and the cash-open drive is the mechanism. They also hold the 05:00-09:30 pre-market extremes, which no current pool covers.
proposals.spec: sessON = input.session("1800-0930", "Overnight Range", group = G_KEY); useON Auto/On/Off, where Auto = on when syminfo.type is futures or index. Track with f_sessTrack using TIME-1a overlap membership, or f_sessTrackLT (TIME-1b); the window wraps midnight. Push at session end like 1800-1809 as src 8 with f_tierW 0.60 (not above PD). f_levelName 'ONH'/'ONL'; update the src comment at 316. f_pushExt de-duplicates prices equal to the Asia/London extremes. Consider raising the registry cap at 1813 from 60 to 64.
proposals.risk: 24-hour FX and crypto have no natural overnight (Auto default). More registry entries.

proposals.title: Scheduled-event scaling of the clock: manual event input plus an approximate NFP rule, in σ units
proposals.rationale: Release hours carry several times a normal hour's variance (release-hour range FOMC 5.2x, NFP 2.7x, CPI 2.1x as reported by A, i.e. about 27x / 7x / 4x in variance). Ederington-Lee show releases drive the time-of-day and weekday patterns, so the average clock under-reaches on release days. Pine has no calendar. Correction: the first pass used range ratios as variance multipliers; the input must be in σ and squared.
proposals.spec:
Inputs (G_POT, display.none): evOn; evT = input.time(timestamp("2026-01-01T00:00:00-05:00"), "Event Time"); evX = input.float(2.0, "Event Volatility x (σ)", minval = 1.0, step = 0.5), applied as variance multiplier evX*evX; evMin = 60.
Optional nfpOn: the release is the third Friday after the Saturday that ends the week containing the 12th of the previous month, at 08:30 ET. Compute in ms, then rebuild with timestamp(tz, y, m, d, 8, 30) to avoid DST drift; if it falls on 1 January, add 7 days. Label it approximate; the manual input overrides it.
In f_fwdVar, buckets whose projected start falls in [evT, evT + evMin*60000) get variance x evX². Ignore the event once timenow > evT + evMin*60000. The HUD shows '⚑ EVENT' while the window lies inside the horizon. Default evX = 2 is below the as-reported NFP ratio because the learned 08:30 bucket already includes release days and the extra variance decays within about 15 minutes.
proposals.risk: User error and stale events (auto-expiry). The NFP rule breaks in holiday or shutdown months. Requires TIME-3.

concepts.name: Race geometry: two-barrier first passage between opposing targets
concepts.definition: Price x, upper target U, lower target D. Driftless: P(U first) = (x−D)/(U−D). With drift: P = (1−e^{k·b})/(e^{−k·a}−e^{k·b}), where k = 2μ/σ², a = U−x and b = x−D (f_race 447-464). Horizon-conditioned form: pW = f_raceH(a, b, σ, 0, H), pL = f_raceH(b, a, σ, 0, H), P(U first | decided within H) = pW/(pW+pL), with P(decided) = pW+pL. Recommended parameters: μ = 0, σ = potSig (50-bar stdev of close changes), and both targets at least minDistATR away.
concepts.dolRole: The single best predictor of which side is reached first, and the right prior for both the side choice and the probability. Every bias feature should be judged by its excess over this baseline.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A: ruin rule right 70-81% on 17 previous-candle combinations; B re-ran race.py and it reproduces byte for byte. B2 (engine-like pool races, 7 datasets, 568-1,430 resolved each): geometry 67-75% and calibrated within a few points (slope 0.90-1.46). The horizon-conditioned ratio beats the infinite race on 6 of 7 datasets (+1.0 to +3.0% Brier; CI excludes 0 on EURUSD 2017-18 and NASDAQ D). Sibling ict_struct: 65.3% observed vs 65.8% predicted, n 12,148 on 8 markets.
concepts.engineNotes: f_race 447-464 and f_raceH 466-482 are correct, but they are used only in f_invalidation 1343-1365 (A wrote 1334; corrected) and f_raceAdj 1367-1371. The side choice (1891-1898, 1975) ignores them. f_invalidation uses drift (m = potMu·side at 1361).

concepts.name: Next-taken vs destination (path continuity)
concepts.definition: Prices move continuously, so the next pool touched is always either the nearest unswept pool above or the nearest below. 'Which liquidity next' is therefore exactly a race between those two. The DOL destination is the best-scored level on a side. Its side question is the race between the two sides' finalists, and intermediate pools do not change a random-walk race.
concepts.dolRole: Separates two questions: the 'NEXT ▲/▼' readout (nearest-pool race) and D (finalist race). The engine currently conflates them through the vote D.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mathematical (path continuity plus the two-barrier result). B2 and sibling replications of the race confirm the calibration empirically.
concepts.engineNotes: There is no nearest-pool race readout (sibling QPOT-06 / ICTS-3), and D is not a finalist race (BIAS-1/2).

concepts.name: Previous-candle range states and base rates (PDH/PDL taken, both, inside)
concepts.dolRole: Base rates and timing for HTF prior-candle liquidity. At least one prior extreme is taken within 1 candle 79-93% of the time and within 2 candles 92-99%. Both are taken 8-12% of the time; inside candles 7-21%.
concepts.engineNotes: PDH/PDL/PWH/PWL exist with exact anchors (f_rangeTrack 807-833, 945-961, registry 1790-1799). Missing: the candle class, prior close/CLV, the 4H/1H prior candle, which-first and neither probabilities, and base rates. BIAS-3 adds them.

concepts.name: Taylor / Raschke close-location follow-through (80-20s)
concepts.definition: If a session closes in the top X% of its range (CLV ≥ 0.8 or 0.9), the next session retests its high '80-90%' of the time, but closes higher only about 50%. The Raschke 80-20 setup requires an open in the bottom 20% and a close in the top 20% of the range. Mirror rules apply for lows.
concepts.dolRole: The best-known 'previous candle high taken next candle' statistic. It gives the trader the chart's own CLV-bucket base rates for HTF prior extremes.
concepts.engineNotes: There is no CLV or prior close. BIAS-3 adds a per-timeframe CLV-bucket base-rate table (5 buckets × n/kHi/kLo/kBoth) shown in the Clean bias-cell tooltip.
