concepts.name: ICT daily bias rule (close through PDH → PDH next; swept and closed back inside → opposite side)
concepts.definition: Bullish if C1>H2, or if L1<L2 and C1≥L2. Bearish mirrors this. Otherwise neutral (inside, or an outside bar closing inside). The weekly version uses PWH/PWL. Variants differ by session day (18:00, midnight or RTH) and by the TTrades 50% filter. An open-source Pine implementation sums six hand-weighted votes, freezes the bias at 09:30, and tracks a hit rate with no baseline.
concepts.dolRole: Traders' standard answer to 'is today a PDH or a PDL day'. It picks the side of the next draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes:
A: bias side first ties a shape-shuffle null (−2.2 to +1.9 pp on 13 datasets).
[CORRECTED] A's 'hard rule 64-73%' counted neutral days as down calls. B1 scored the rule on its own called cases: rule 68.8-76.3% vs geometry on the same cases 71.6-80.3%, so geometry is ahead by +2.0 to +6.5 pp on 12 of 13 datasets (the exception is EURUSD D, n 152). Where they disagree (13-18% of cases) the rule is right only 31-43%.
edgeful YM 'PDH broken → green 67% / 81%' comes from pages that disagree and could not be opened (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent from D (1891-1894). It should enter only as a gated learned feature (BIAS-1 x6) and as an informational class with measured lift (BIAS-3).

concepts.name: Candle Range Theory (CRT)
concepts.definition: Candle 1 = range (high, low, 50%). Candle 2 trades beyond one extreme and closes back inside (a close beyond voids it). Candle 3 targets the opposite extreme, sometimes the 50% first. Variants: strict vs flexible, HTF range candle with an LTF MSS/FVG entry, 'CRT into an HTF key level'. It is Turtle Soup applied to a single candle's range.
concepts.dolRole: A popular next-draw rule: after a sweep and reclaim, target the opposite extreme of the range candle.
concepts.evidenceNotes:
A: target reached first in 39-48% of decided cases, equal to the null (S&P D 0.458 vs 0.458; NQ 1H 0.430 vs 0.411). Swept equity highs are retaken more often than the null (S&P D 0.691 vs 0.639).
[CORRECTED external evidence]
- The Strange Labs 4,200-variant placebo video could not be found: grade none.
- tradingwyckoff's 45-50% / 60-65% figures were not found on its page.
- New: a published mechanical 1H CRT test at 43-49% win rate, 'coin flip' (weak).
- New: a pre-declared EURUSD CRT structural study with a distance-matched null was inconclusive at n 11-30.
concepts.engineNotes: There is no detector. Sweeps feed liqEvt at 1579-1582 with REJECT = reversal, which is the CRT reading the evidence contradicts. Use it only as an informational class (BIAS-3), an alert (BIAS-7) and a gated feature (BIAS-1 x8).

concepts.name: Sweep-and-reverse family: Turtle Soup, Oops, smash day, Hikkake
concepts.definition:
- Turtle Soup: a new 20-day low where the prior 20-day low is at least 4 days old, then a trade back above it.
- Oops: a gap open beyond the prior extreme, then a trade back to it.
- Smash day: a close below the prior low; buy above the smash-day high next day; exit at the first profitable open.
- Hikkake: an inside bar, a false break of one side, then a reversal.
concepts.dolRole: A reversal draw after external liquidity is raided: the opposite side becomes the target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A turtle.py: excess over geometry −0.13 to +0.08, never reliably positive. New: a pre-declared EURUSD H1 failed-breakout rule lost −0.085R (PF 0.87) after costs. [CORRECTED] RogueQuant's smash-day result (80% win, PF 6.94) is single-source, paywalled, and disputed in reader comments, so weak. Bulkowski reports about 60% of hikkakes meeting target (weak).
concepts.engineNotes: Raids of any pool feed liqEvt (1579-1582) with no age rule; induceBar (892-895) feeds density. Nothing further is needed beyond fixing the sign (ICT-9 / BIAS-4) and measuring it (BIAS-1).

concepts.name: AMD / Power of 3 (London sweep of the Asia range)
concepts.definition: Asia range 19:00-00:00 ET. London breaches one extreme by δ = 10 NQ points before 04:00 and closes back inside before 05:00. Bilateral breaches are excluded. [CORRECTED] The directional outcome is the 16:00 close relative to the Asia midpoint; 09:40-10:30 is only the mechanical entry window.
concepts.dolRole: The intraday-session version of CRT, used to pick the NY-session draw.
concepts.engineNotes: Killzone affinity f_kzAff 597-602 (London ×1.20 on Asia pools) is timing only. Direction must not come from the sweep.

concepts.name: Open-relative bias (midnight / weekly open; intraday momentum)
concepts.definition: Price above the period's open → the period's (or prior period's) high is the draw. Anchors: 00:00 NY, 18:00, Sunday open. Decision time is fixed (08:00, after Monday/Tuesday). The academic analogue: the first half-hour return (from the prior close) predicts the last half-hour return.
concepts.dolRole: An intraday or intraweek side filter for PDH/PDL and PWH/PWL.
concepts.engineNotes: Used only as confluence anchors (964-966, 1931), which is correct. Do not add it to D.

concepts.name: Weekly profile templates
concepts.definition: Named weekly shapes: low or high of the week formed Monday/Tuesday, midweek reversal, consolidation then Thursday reversal.
concepts.dolRole: Which of PWH/PWL is taken first, and on which day.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The arcsine law explains most of the 'extreme forms early' effect (ict_time). As a side predictor the profile reduces to the PWH/PWL race (geometry 72-80% vs the open rule 52-64%).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent. The BIAS-3 readout covers the PWH/PWL race in Swing mode.

concepts.name: Taylor 3-day cycle (Book method)
concepts.definition: Buy day (low made first) → sell day (rally exceeding the buy-day high) → short-sale day (exceeds the sell-day high, then declines).
concepts.dolRole: A claimed daily rhythm for which prior extreme is taken next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor webinars claim '84%' or '91% of cycles positive' with undefined criteria. The testable core, 'previous high taken next day', is geometry (§2.10).
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Value-area 80% rule (Market Profile)
concepts.definition: Open outside the prior value area, then two 30-minute periods close inside it → the far side of the value area is reached '80%' of the time.
concepts.dolRole: An auction-theory next-draw rule within the session.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Negative. Sibling amt_profile: own test 61.9% vs a 54.0% matched baseline (n 42, not significant); independent 589-session test 25-28% vs a 27-29% base rate.
concepts.engineNotes: Correctly absent.

concepts.name: Order-flow / structure vote D
concepts.dolRole: Decides the eligible side, the 30% draw pillar and the ×0.5 counter-draw penalty, so it dominates the side choice.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed weights 155-157 and 1892-1894; gate 1895; draw pillar 691; ctrMult 692-693; eligibility 1975; ctrHold 2001; curElig 2004; activeCtr 2029; flip 1896-1898 and 2086-2088. Fix: D := calibrated finalist race (BIAS-1/2), with the vote kept as a gated feature or as the 'Structure Vote' option.

concepts.name: Raid outcome sign (HOLD = continuation, REJECT = reversal)
concepts.definition: After a pool is traded through on a confirmed bar: HOLD = the close stays beyond the zone (continuation); REJECT = the close is back inside the level (reversal). Engine: ±tier added to liqEvt, half-life 24.
concepts.dolRole: Feeds 30% of D, so it pushes the next-draw side after every raid.
concepts.engineNotes: 1579-1582: REJECT pushes D toward reversal. Implement ict_liq ICT-9 (neutral REJECT, HTF-conditioned HOLD) and keep separate liqHold/liqRej accumulators as gated features (BIAS-4, BIAS-1).

concepts.name: Dealing-range position / premium-discount / CLV
concepts.definition: pos = (x − rangeLow)/(rangeHigh − rangeLow) of the HTF dealing range (ICT: buy in discount toward the premium draw). The previous-candle version is CLV = (C1−L1)/(H1−L1).
concepts.dolRole: CLV carries the previous-candle geometry. As an ICT directional prior, HTF position should only be measured.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The CLV logistic weight is +2.3 to +4.7 in every fit (A); this is geometry. The ICT rule 'bull bias + discount → up' scores 49.5% / 49.1% (sibling). B2's learned HTF-position weight ranges from −0.32 to +0.20.
concepts.engineNotes: Terminal premium/discount display 2324-2333; htfEQ/dayEQ confluence 967-968. The range is the last pivots, not ICT's leg (ICTS-4). It enters BIAS-1 as gated feature x7.

concepts.name: Trend regime (daily close vs EMA20 ±0.5%)
concepts.definition: Uptrend if close > EMA20·(1+band), downtrend if close < EMA20·(1−band), otherwise ranging. Bands: D 0.5%, W 1%, 1H 0.1%.
concepts.dolRole: Conditions sweep and bias signals. In the AMD study the regime carries the directional pattern.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Evidence is mixed. AMD's regime cells are 62-71% aligned vs 25-30% opposed, BH-significant. Excess over geometry in A's cells is only ±2-4 pp and changes sign (S&P D uptrend −3.6 pp; NQ 1H +1.5 pp).
concepts.engineNotes: Learned feature only (REG-6 inside BIAS-1).

concepts.name: Momentum vs mean reversion; breakout continuation vs sweep reversal
concepts.definition: Breakout: close beyond the N-bar extreme (N=20) → continuation. Sweep: wick beyond and close inside → reversal. The sign of the follow-through depends on asset, timescale and regime.
concepts.dolRole: Sets the sign of any adjustment after a level is crossed (continuation origin vs magnet back).
concepts.engineNotes: The empirical PoT surface (1526-1532, f_empPoT 1284-1301) splits by htfBias, which has no skill (REG-1 / BIAS-6). There is no breakout-state feature; any such feature must be learned and gated.

concepts.name: Drift in side races
concepts.definition: Adding a per-bar drift μ (the engine's potMu = 0.5·SMA(Δclose, 50)) to the first-passage race between two targets.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether trend tilts the race odds.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: drift makes the side race 0.4-6.9% worse (Brier) on all 7 datasets. This agrees with sibling QPOT-01 and REG-3 ('drift adds error in every regime').
concepts.engineNotes: f_invalidation 1361 uses m = potMu·tgt.side; potMu 917 (driftW 0.5 at 185). BIAS-8 sets the race drift to 0 by default.

concepts.name: Contraction → expansion (Crabel NR4/NR7/inside day)
concepts.definition: NR4/NR7: the narrowest range of the last 4/7 candles. Inside day as in the taxonomy. Premise: contraction is followed by expansion.
concepts.dolRole: Timing and 'both sides' risk: after a narrow candle both prior extremes are near and are often both taken.
concepts.evidenceNotes: A nr.py: P(next range > median) after NR7 is 0.26-0.45, below the 0.48-0.50 base on every dataset, so the expansion claim is false in absolute terms. P(both prior extremes taken) after NR7 is 0.16-0.29 vs a base of 0.08-0.14, which is geometry.
concepts.engineNotes: coilScore 888-891 feeds density only. Use it for the 'both sides' odds in the BIAS-3 readout, not as an expansion prior.

concepts.name: Triple-barrier labelling, meta-labelling and prequential scoring
concepts.definition:
- Triple barrier: label each event by which of an upper, lower or time barrier is hit first.
- Meta-labelling: a primary rule gives the side; a secondary model learns P(primary correct).
- Prequential scoring: freeze each forecast at issue and score it (Brier, log-loss) at resolution.
- Mixture with a safe expert: cumulative-loss weighting bounds the regret against the better expert.
concepts.dolRole: The formal quant framing of 'BSL first / SSL first / undecided within H'. It gives the engine a principled way to let bias features earn weight over geometry without overfitting.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Sources: López de Prado 2018, ch. 3; Joubert 2022 (JFDS 4(3)); Cesa-Bianchi & Lugosi 2006 (theory). B2: a tempered mixture stays within −1.3% to +2.5% of geometry, while ungated SGD loses 1.7-3.0%. Sibling CAL-4 finds the same gating need.
concepts.engineNotes: The ledger (1426-1499) grades only the active DOL's hit within H. BIAS-1 adds the side ledger and the gate.

concepts.name: Side-level ('which side first') ledger
concepts.definition: Every max(1, round(H/5)) bars, record both finalists, the zero-drift horizon-conditioned race probability, the shadow-model probability, the probability used, and the legacy vote. Resolve on the first trade-through: same-bar both = ambiguous; neither within H = undecided. Accumulate Brier, log-loss and accuracy, plus the ΔLL statistics for the gate.
concepts.dolRole: Measures the side forecast itself, the core 'which liquidity next' question, rather than only 'was the chosen target hit'.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Methodological need: a sign-randomised null reproduces about 95% of apparent RankIC (arXiv 2611.12141, B✓); open-source bias trackers report hit rates with no baseline. B2 shows the ledger detects the legacy vote's −15 to −25% Brier and A's SGD's −2 to −3%.
concepts.engineNotes: Add SideTrial records, step 2b resolution and sdSt arrays (BIAS-1). State must live in arrays, because Pine functions cannot reassign fundamental globals (arrays.md 263).

concepts.name: Calibrated previous-candle readout for HTF/STF/EXE
concepts.definition: For each mode timeframe, while both prior extremes are untaken: pw/pl = f_raceH(…, 0 drift, hRem = n1 − n0 bars), pDec = pw+pl, pHi = pw/pDec. Calibrate pDec per timeframe and per third of the period with a gated two-parameter logistic. Show P(high first) = pDec·pHi, P(low first) = pDec·(1−pHi), P(neither) = 1−pDec. Freeze the value at the open and also show the live value.
concepts.dolRole: The honest trader-facing 'daily bias': P(PDH first), P(PDL first), P(neither) for D/4H/1H, together with the class (CRT or close-through) and its measured lift.
concepts.engineNotes: Only D/W ranges are tracked (945-961). BIAS-3 adds f_candleTrack(timeframe.change(tf)) ×3 with no new request.security. The tooltip goes in via table.cell_set_tooltip on the Clean bias cells (2304).

concepts.name: Multi-timeframe bias table (structure)
concepts.definition: For each of HTF/STF/EXE, the swing bias from BOS/CHoCH (f_structure), or the internal bias while the swing is undecided, shown as BULLISH, BEARISH or NEUTRAL.
concepts.dolRole: Traders read it as the directional forecast.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Swing/pivot bias has no side skill: 0.49-0.54 and htfBias 0.502-0.522 (sibling); pivot logistic weight about 0 (A); B2 structure weight −0.31 to +0.12.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean 2293-2305, Terminal 2321-2336. Keep the reference look. BIAS-5 adds measured skill in the tooltip; dimming is off by default.

concepts.name: Gated learning of bias features (measure first, apply when proven)
concepts.definition: Bias features are learned in a shadow model on top of geometry. They are applied only when the prequential log-loss gain is significant: n ≥ 200 and mean(ΔLL) − 2·sqrt(2·var(ΔLL)/n) > 0, using a design effect of 2 for overlapping windows. Until then the forecast stays at geometry.
concepts.dolRole: Makes every bias claim self-measuring on the trader's chart without letting noise move the target choice.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B2: ungated SGD is worse than geometry on 6 of 7 datasets (CI excludes 0 on NQ, GC and EURUSD 1H). Learned weights flip sign between markets. The sibling learned-D test was worse than a coin. Sibling calib_ml: unregularised SGD −3.6 to −5.5% LL, while the gate costs 0 to −0.26%.
concepts.engineNotes: BIAS-1's sdMode input ('Measure' by default) with sdApply computed at the call site in step 2b.

proposals.title: Side ledger + calibrated side model P(best buy-side target before best sell-side target), with gated feature learning
proposals.rationale: The core forecasting question (which side first) is neither measured nor modelled today. Zero-drift horizon-conditioned geometry answers it at 67-75% and is calibrated. Bias features have no stable sign, and ungated learning hurts (B2: −1.7 to −3.0% Brier on 6 of 7 datasets). So: start at geometry, measure every feature prequentially, and apply features only once this chart proves they help. This corrects A's spec: zero drift instead of potMu; f_raceH conditional instead of f_race; a gate instead of always-on SGD; two-phase scoring instead of stale previous-bar scores; a minDistATR finalist floor; array-held state.
proposals.risk:
- Overlapping trials shrink the effective n; the gate uses a design effect of 2.
- The gate may never open, which is expected; the panel says 'measured, not applied'.
- The two-phase split touches evaluate's signature, so every evaluate call site (1948 only) must be updated.
- Finalists use draw-free scores, so there is no circularity.
- CAL-4's adPredictor can replace the SGD step later.

proposals.title: Draw Source = Calibrated: D := 2·P(buy-side finalist first) − 1, with dead band and 2-bar persistence; legacy vote kept as an option
proposals.rationale: Choosing the side by the legacy vote loses 3.8-8.3 pp of first-touch accuracy against geometry, with every block-bootstrap CI excluding 0 (B2), and loses 2-7 pp of hit-within-H (A). This keeps draw-side-first selection (decision history) and changes what the draw is. With the default weights, the draw pillar becomes the calibrated P(this side's target first).
proposals.spec:
In BIAS-1 step 17b:
- if drawSrc == 'Calibrated': drawD := sideOK ? 2·pUp−1 : 0. [CORRECTED: no fallback to the legacy vote.]
- cand = drawD ≥ dGateEff ? 1 : drawD ≤ −dGateEff ? −1 : 0, with dGateEff = 0.20, i.e. P ≥ 0.60 for a side.
- sidePendN counts consecutive bars with the same cand. When cand ≠ sideC for 2 bars: drawFlip := cand≠0 and sideC≠0; sideC := cand; lastDirSide := cand (keeps the alert text at 2087 correct).
- dirSide := sideC. Eligibility 1975, ctrHold 2001, curElig 2004 and activeCtr 2029 are unchanged and read dirSide.
- applyDraw uses dGateEff for the counter-draw test; the panel (2338) uses dGateEff.
- Finalists inside minDistATR are excluded, so a level price is sitting on cannot swing D. This also protects against the overhaul-P1 taper swap.
- After a sweep, the new finalist on the swept side is farther, so D often flips. Geometry reproduces the 'after BSL is taken, the draw becomes SSL' heuristic, and persistence prevents flip spam.
- README: redefine D. State honestly that geometry-chosen sides raise raw DOL HIT % but cannot raise the distance-matched EDGE (1461-1499).
- A/B: toggle drawSrc on the same chart and compare DOL HIT %, EDGE, side skill, and side-switch and drawFlip counts.
- With ICTS-1 or REG-3 built, their gates apply to the 'Structure Vote' option. REG-4's ctrMult 0.85 is worth A/B testing.
proposals.risk:
- Targets are nearer on average; the minDist floor, the proximity taper and minScore limit trivial picks.
- The classic look is one click away.
- ctrMult 0.50 now fires only when the other side is at least 60% likely.
- It changes D's meaning (README and tooltip must explain).

proposals.title: Zero-drift, horizon-conditioned races everywhere sides are compared (f_invalidation, side model, previous-candle readout)
proposals.rationale: B2: adding the engine's drift (potMu = 0.5·SMA(Δclose, 50)) to side races makes Brier 0.4-6.9% worse on all 7 datasets. The conditional pW/(pW+pL) form beats the infinite race on 6 of 7 (+1.0 to +3.0%; CI excludes 0 on 2). Siblings QPOT-01 and REG-3 reach the same conclusion for PoT.
proposals.spec:
- f_invalidation 1361: `float m = raceDrift ? potMu * tgt.side : 0.0`.
- New input `bool raceDrift = input.bool(false, 'Drift in Races', group = G_POT, tooltip = 'Off by default: trend drift was tested and made first-touch odds worse on every market tested.')`.
- BIAS-1/2/3 use f_sideP / f_raceH with μ = 0.
- f_raceAdj (1367-1371) keeps the ledger intercept correction.
- One-line change; no new state.
proposals.risk: Drift may help on a strongly trending chart. f_raceAdj absorbs systematic bias, and the input restores the old behaviour.

proposals.title: Previous-candle module for HTF/STF/EXE: class, calibrated P(prior high first / prior low first / neither), CLV base-rate table, in the Clean bias-cell tooltip
proposals.rationale: It answers the trader's 'PDH day or PDL day?' with honest numbers. After a close in the top 20% of the range, the prior high is exceeded next candle 75-89% of the time (B1, 13 series). The raw f_raceH readout is calibrated for weekly-from-daily periods but over-predicts 'decided' on short intraday periods (B3: 0.86-0.89 vs 0.79-0.83; late in the period P(neither) 0.03 vs 0.16-0.24). So calibration is built in. Class labels are shown with their measured lift, usually about 0. It also supplies BIAS-1 features x6/x8 and BIAS-7 events.
proposals.risk:
- Session conventions differ (exchange day vs 18:00 vs RTH); the tooltip says which is used.
- Small n per class; shrinkage and the gate hold numbers at geometry until data accrue.
- Cost: 6 f_raceH calls per bar plus O(1) bookkeeping.

proposals.title: Raid outcome: implement ict_liq ICT-9 (neutral REJECT, HTF-conditioned HOLD); keep HOLD and REJECT as separate gated features
proposals.rationale: At 1581 a REJECT pushes D toward reversal. The evidence against it: CRT target-first 39-48% = null; Turtle Soup ≤ geometry; swept equity highs are retaken more often than the null; AMD direction follows the regime; REJECT continues 52.6% (sibling); B2's learned REJECT weight ranges from −0.31 to +0.10.
proposals.spec:
- Replace the liqEvt mapping (1579-1582) per ict_liq.final.md ICT-9: REJECT adds 0; HOLD adds +1 with the HTF swing, −0.5 against it and +0.5 when the HTF is neutral, all ×tier; at most one event per side per bar; 1-tick pokes within eqTol are ignored; HOLD uses a holdATR of 0.20.
- Keep BIAS-1's separate liqHold and liqRej accumulators (decayed with liqHL) as side-model features x4/x5, so each sign is measured per chart.
- A's rejW input is dropped once ICT-9 is in.
proposals.risk: On some markets rejections may carry a reversal signal; the gated BIAS-1 feature picks it up. Legacy D behaviour changes, and the README must note it.

proposals.title: Bias table with measured skill in the tooltip (no dimming by default)
proposals.rationale: Traders read BULLISH/BEARISH as a forecast, but its side skill is about 50%. [CORRECTED] A dimmed cells by default, which breaks the reference look, so the default is tooltip-only.
proposals.spec:
- In BIAS-3's per-period records, also store the displayed bias b (swing, else internal) at the period open.
- On a decided resolution with b ≠ 0, book n, k (bias side first) and Σp (geometric P(bias side first) at the open). lift = k/n − Σp/n; se = √(Σp(1−p))/n.
- Tooltip line: 'When D is BULLISH: prior high first 61% (geometry 58%, n 140) → lift +3% ± 4%'.
- Input 'Bias Skill Shading' (default off): text alpha 60 when lift < 1.5·se.
- Terminal adds a SKILL column.
proposals.risk: Small n on HTF rows (show n). Shading is optional, preserving the reference look.

proposals.title: HTF candle-close event alerts (CRT / close-through) carrying calibrated odds and measured class lift
proposals.rationale: CRT and close-through events are what many traders wait for. An alert that states the engine's calibrated probabilities and the measured class lift gives workflow value without implying an edge.
proposals.spec:
- On timeframe.change(tfH) or timeframe.change(tfS) with cls ∈ {±1, ±2} from BIAS-3: alert('DOL Engine ▸ ' + tfLabel + ' ' + clsText + ' · prior high first ' + pH + ' · prior low first ' + pL + ' · neither ' + p0 + ' · class lift ' + lift + ' (n ' + n + ')', alert.freq_once_per_bar_close).
- Add alertcondition(htfCandleEvt, 'HTF Candle Event', …).
- Input 'Alert · HTF candle events' (default off), limited to tfH and tfS.
- Aligns with ICTS-6 and WYK-4 (an event layer with zero forecast weight).
proposals.risk: Alert fatigue is limited to HTF/STF. Users may still read CRT as a signal; the message shows the lift, typically about 0.

proposals.title: Empirical PoT surface regime key chosen by held-out score: merged into sibling REG-1
proposals.rationale: f_bump/f_empPoT (1526-1532, 1284-1301) split the reach surface by htfBias, which has no side skill. f_empPoT pools only when a row is under nMin (1292-1299), never when a full row is uninformative. REG-1 already replaces the key with a volatility state selected by held-out score.
proposals.spec:
- Implement it inside REG-1's key selector.
- Offer two extra candidate keys: pooled (no split), and BIAS-3's previous-HTF class in 3 groups (up-close or bull CRT / down-close or bear CRT / other).
- Choose by held-out Brier at d ∈ {0.5, 1, 2} ATR, with a ≥ 300-window minimum and a 0.002 margin.
proposals.risk: A small per-bar cost; mild selection overfit is limited by the margin. Coordinate with TIME-1/2 (clock-aware PoT).

result.summary:
The engine already matches or beats the open-source SMC and liquidity conventions. It uses body-close BOS/CHoCH, strict trade-through sweeps, touch/CE/full delivery with cropping, iFVG on a close through the whole gap, session pivots kept until swept, and non-repainting MTF reads. Large studies find no forecasting edge in these detectors, so borrow them for robustness and looks, not for score weight.

Corrections to A:
- The Python SMC library's lookahead fix (PR #65) was reverted the same day (PR #73). Its swing and FVG flags still use future bars, so public backtests built on it are biased.
- `gap > 0` in the tests code is not a bug. Exact touches reach `eqCount` through the pivot-merge path.
- The OB volatility filter is dropped. B's replica shows tall OBs are not born nearer to price on 5m and are not touched more often at the same distance.
- Three claims rest on SSRN or LuxAlgo pages B could not open. They are marked as such, and the Tangirala grade is downgraded.

New findings:
- Two Pine-runtime re-implementations (PineTS, PyneCore) show `ta.pivothigh` resolves ties to the newest equal bar. A tight double top never loses its pivot, which overturns the premise of sibling ICTS-9. It does lose its EQ count and its first-print anchor: 12% of pivots on ES 5m, 41% on 6E 1m.
- The engine's iFVG layer forms 130-158 iFVGs per 1,000 bars on 5m/1H futures (268 on 6E 1m), so "New iFVG Formed" fires every 4-8 bars. Tracking only gaps left by the engine's own displacement candle, plus width, close and same-bar-merge filters, cuts this 4-5× to 29-37 per 1,000 bars. iFVG retests carry no edge, so nothing is lost.
- Peer-reviewed evidence (Garzarelli et al. 2014, Sci Rep) confirms that prior bounces predict bounces, but only at seconds-to-hours scales. That supports a neutral tests weight (ICT-10) plus a decayed memory feature.

Top proposals:
- SMC-1: a gated, ledger-calibrated PoT with its sample size, implemented as CAL-6. The Clean label keeps the reference look; n and "building" go in the tooltip.
- SMC-6: displacement-born iFVGs with "show last N per side".
- SMC-2: an optional commitment mode with a switch-rate metric.
- SMC-8: keep the native pivot, add the tie count and the first-print anchor.
- SMC-10: exact origin candles for HTF pivots from per-HTF-bar extreme maps, with no history references. Today those zones start up to 23 bars early for a daily pivot on a 1H chart.

concepts.name: Swing point detection (symmetric pivot vs LuxAlgo leg vs centred window)
concepts.definition: Pine ta.pivothigh(len,len): H[len] is the extreme of a 2*len+1 window, confirmed len bars late (engine pivLen 5, MTF biasLen 3). LuxAlgo SMC leg: candidate when H[size] > highest(H,size) of the following bars, no left test, highs/lows alternate (swing 50, internal 5, EQ 3). py-smc: H equals the max of a centred window (L-1 older, L newer), non-strict ties, consecutive same-type swings pruned (earlier kept on exact ties); uses future bars. PyInd BSL/SSL port uses pivothigh(len,1).
concepts.dolRole: Swings are the BSL/SSL pools; alternation matters for structure, not liquidity.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Definition choices; no study shows one pivot rule forecasts better. The 5-bar lag hiding raids equals random-walk geometry (ict_struct.final).
concepts.engineNotes: 879-880, 709-710; no alternation (correct). Tie handling: see the Pine tie concept (SMC-8).

concepts.name: Pine ta.pivothigh tie rule (newest equal bar wins)
concepts.definition: A bar on the left equal to the candidate does not disqualify it; an equal bar on the right does, so the later equal top becomes the pivot. ta.highestbars returns the oldest bar on ties. The pivot scan stops at the first na. Established by PineTS on TradingView test series and modelled identically by PyneCore; not in the official v6 reference.
concepts.dolRole: Decides whether tight equal highs become one pool or two, where the zone is anchored, and whether EQ is counted.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Two independent Pine-runtime re-implementations validated against TradingView output. B-test: Pine pivots with an exact older tie are ES 5m 12.0%, 6E 1m 40.6%, GC 5m 4.0%, NQ 5m 2.4%, ES 1H 5.5%, NQ 1H 0.6%. A strict-both-sides rule would lose 12-41% of pivots; Pine does not.
concepts.engineNotes: [CORRECTED A's G1 and sibling ICTS-9] No pivot is lost. A tight double top yields one pool anchored at the second top with eqCount 0 (879-880, 1753-1776). SMC-8 adds the tie count and the first-print anchor.

concepts.name: BOS/CHoCH confirmation (body vs wick), internal vs swing
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: first close crossing the pivot, each pivot breaks once; CHoCH if against the prior trend; internal breaks skipped when equal to the swing level; optional wick confluence filter with a precedence slip. py-smc: 4-swing patterns, close_break=True default, hindsight deletion of unbroken or out-of-order patterns. PyInd MSB: close beyond the last pivot (len 7) plus momentum z ≥ 0.5. openalgo: close by default.
concepts.dolRole: Sets bias/draw side and OB creation.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Structure direction ≈ coin flip (49.9-51.6%, ict_struct 2.2); 44 SMC detectors incl. BOS/CHoCH not better than matched random (SSRN 7483658, A, not re-verified). No published body-vs-wick comparison found.
concepts.engineNotes: f_structure 708-782; chart BOS 1542-1547. Matches the open-source consensus and the reference product's body-break rule.

concepts.name: Strong/weak extremes (trailing extremes)
concepts.definition: LuxAlgo SMC: top = max(top, H) since the last swing high, every bar; Strong High if the swing trend is bearish, else Weak High; mirror for lows.
concepts.dolRole: The weak extreme is the open-source 'next target'; the strong extreme is invalidation.

concepts.engineNotes: legH/legL, protH/protL at 713-774, returned at 782, not exposed (ICTS-4/5/7).

LuxAlgo OB Detector: volume pivots (len 5). ICT: last down-close candle before the displacement.

LuxAlgo IFVG (current): 'Min Candle Size (%)' displacement filter. TradingFinder: four aggressiveness levels.

(3) Engine: only OBs whose origin swept a 20-bar extreme.
