proposals.title: Ledger-calibrated, gated PoT with its sample size (implement as CAL-6)
proposals.rationale: The displayed PoT (f_potModel 1303-1311) is a random-level model. The ledger knows how often selected targets of each family were hit (stN/stK) but never feeds that into the number, and raw PoT is off by up to 2x by hour (ict_time E18). Open-source precedent: ForexCracked prints 'reach X% of N' and 'building' while n<20. CAL-6 shows recalibration can hurt an already calibrated base, so it must be gated. [CORRECTED vs A: gate added; Clean label unchanged to keep the reference look]
proposals.spec: Inputs G_POT: potCal bool true, potK float 20. Trial (375-395): add pShow (raw f_potModel at open; TIME-2's pMod if present) and pCal (ungated calibrated at open, earlier outcomes only). State after 1079: stPS array<float>(5) = Σ pShow per [grp0..3, ALL]; brSt array<float>(3) = [n, Σ(y−pShow)², Σ(y−pCal)²]. After f_raceAdj (1371): f_potCalRaw(p,g): gg = stN[g]>=10 ? g : 4; if n>=10: pb = stPS[gg]/n; dl = logit((stK[gg]+potK·pb)/(n+potK)) − logit(pb); return min(0.95, sigm(logit(p)+dl)). f_potShow(p,g) = (potCal and brSt[0]>=30 and brSt[2]<brSt[1]) ? f_potCalRaw(p,g) : p. f_openTrial (1426): pShow = f_potModel(d, side, potMu·side), pCal = f_potCalRaw(pShow, lv.grp()). f_book (1461): accumulate stPS per group and the Brier sums. Use f_potShow at 2067 (activePoT) and 2184 (secondary), so the minPoT filter and announcement inherit it. No feedback loop: trials open independently of minPoT (2038-2045). Display: Clean label unchanged; tooltip 'PoT 61% · model 55% · from 84 past CHART LIQ targets (hit 52, expected 46)' or 'building (n 7)'; Terminal row 'cal n84'/'raw'; Full view 'PoT CAL Brier .231→.214 · n 180 · ON'.
proposals.risk: Noisy early offsets (50-150 trials per family per 5,000 bars), handled by the κ=20 shrinkage, the ALL fallback and the 30-trial Brier gate. Calibration lags setting changes, but history recomputes on input change. Capped at 95%.

proposals.title: iFVG only from displacement gaps, one zone per side per bar, a 150-bar watch window, and show last N per side
proposals.rationale: B-test: the engine forms 130-158 iFVGs per 1,000 bars on ES/NQ/GC 5m and 1H, and 268 on 6E 1m. 'New iFVG Formed' fires every 4-8 bars, and same-bar multi-inversions draw duplicate boxes. LuxAlgo's current IFVG requires a displacement creating candle and shows the last N pairs; the reference shows a few iFVG boxes. iFVG retests have no edge (38% vs 38%), so filtering loses nothing. The filters below cut formations 4-5x, to 29-37 per 1,000 bars (60 on 6E 1m).
proposals.spec: Inputs G_IFVG: ifvgSrc ['Displacement gaps' (default), 'All gaps']; ifvgMinW 0.25 (× atrE); ifvgAge 150; ifvgShow 2. (1) At 1877/1887 push to fvgTrk only if ifvgSrc=='All gaps' or (dispUp[1] and close[1] > high[2]) (bear: dispDn[1] and close[1] < low[2]); dispUp/dispDn are global series (903-904). (2) At 1603: inverted additionally requires (z.top − z.bottom) >= ifvgMinW·atrE; otherwise drop the zone silently. (3) Step 5: collect same-bar inversions per new direction into locals (union top/bottom, oldest bornBar) and create one Zone/box per side after the loop. (4) At 1626 use ifvgAge instead of trackAge (trackAge stays for obTrk at 1660). (5) Rendering 2145-2149: walk ifvgs newest→oldest with per-side counters; the first ifvgShow per side get their normal colours (creation expression 1607-1613), the rest get transparency 100; hidden zones are cleaned normally.
proposals.risk: Users who want every inversion pick 'All gaps' (today's behaviour). The merged zone can be taller than any single gap (intended). No effect on scoring or the ledger.

proposals.title: Optional target commitment mode (Locked until resolved) and a switch-rate metric
proposals.rationale: HS_16 Liquidity Draw locks the target until it is reached, its stop breaks or N bars pass; AGPro reports 'balanced' (both verified in competitors.md). The engine re-ranks every confirmed bar with hysteresis, so a trader holding an H-bar plan sees it move. 'Targets jump around' is a plausible complaint. Locking makes the displayed target equal to the graded ledger trial, and the switch-rate metric quantifies the jumpiness in either mode.
proposals.spec: Input commitIn ['Adaptive' (default), 'Locked'] in G_SCORE. State: var float lockInv, var int nSw, nSwBars. Step 19 (2016-2020): locked = commitIn=='Locked' and curI>=0 and bar_index−activeSince < H and not na(lockInv) and (curSide==1 ? close >= lockInv : close <= lockInv); if locked → pick := curI, else the existing logic. While locked the INVALIDATED ghost (2021-2023) does not fire; on release use '⊘ INVALIDATED', or '⌛ EXPIRED' when the age ≥ H. On commit (2030-2035): [lkI, lkRR, lkP] = f_invalidation(activeLv), lockInv := lkI; nSw += 1 when old and new ids ≥ 0 and inCalc; nSwBars += 1 per inCalc bar. Re-arm in Locked mode when the expired target is still pick: activeSince := bar_index and recompute lockInv (the ledger opens a fresh trial, since the old one booked at H, 1455). Full view 'SWITCH x /100b' in both modes; Clean tooltip 'locked · k/H bars'. A/B by toggling (history recomputes) on HIT %, EDGE and SWITCH.
proposals.risk: A stale lock after a sharp opposite move is bounded by the invalidation close and the H expiry. The default stays Adaptive.

proposals.title: Pine pivot tie semantics: keep ta.pivothigh, add the tie count and the first-print anchor (amends ICTS-9)
proposals.rationale: PineTS (validated on TradingView test series) and PyneCore agree that ta.pivothigh resolves ties to the newest equal bar. A tight double top therefore never loses its pivot, which makes ICTS-9's premise wrong; its leftmost-wins helper would only shift pivot timing. What is really lost is the EQ count and the first-print anchor: 12% of pivots on ES 5m and 41% on 6E 1m (B-test). These feed the EQx2 tag ICT users expect, the 'anchored at the candle that formed it' look, and the candidate ledger's EQ bit.
proposals.spec: SERIES after 880: f_pivTies(float pv, bool isHigh, int p) loops k = p+1..2p (≤60 history reads) and counts |high[k]−pv| (or low) ≤ mintick/2; it returns [ties, offset of the oldest tie]. [phTies, phOld] = f_pivTies(ph, true, pivLen); [plTies, plOld] = f_pivTies(pl, false, pivLen). Step 9 new-pool path (1761-1763 / 1773-1775): eqCount := ties; if ties>0, anchorBar and bornBar = bar_index − old (the pool existed from the first print). Merge path unchanged. f_structure (MTF) unchanged. ROADMAP: replace ICTS-9's 'why' with E12/E13 and implement this instead of f_pivHi/f_pivLo. Before shipping, verify once on TradingView: ta.pivothigh(high,2,2) on a planted double top.
proposals.risk: Minimal. Under ICT-10's 'Evidence' magnitude model EQ has no score weight; under 'ICT Classic' tight double tops gain density, which is that mode's intent.

proposals.title: Tests: no bug; neutral weight (ICT-10) and a clock-time-decayed test memory as a ledger feature
proposals.rationale: [CORRECTED vs A] gap>0 (654) is correct: exact touches that print as pivots merge into the pool via f_mergeAt (1112-1115, eqCount+1), so excluding them from tests avoids double counting. The +0.35×min(tests,6) monotone reward (682) is unsupported. Garzarelli 2014 (Sci Rep) and Chung & Bellotti 2021 find that prior bounces predict bounces, but significance vanishes at 180 s (Garzarelli) and the effect decays to 0.5 in ~6-15 h (Chung & Bellotti). ict_liq.final B3 finds no monotone effect at 1H/5m. So: neutral weight (ICT-10), and if tests are used at all, a decayed memory.
proposals.spec: Level: add float testW. track (650-658): keep the gate; before updating lastTest, testW := testW·exp(−(bar_index−lastTest)·chartS/60/tauM) + 1. Input tauM 360 minutes (clock time, timeframe-independent). testsEff = testW·exp(−(bar_index−lastTest)·chartS/60/tauM). With ICT-1/CAL-3 register TESTED_RECENT = testsEff ≥ 1 in place of the raw tests ≥ 1 bit; under ICT-10's 'ICT Classic' mode use min(testsEff, 6) at 682. README 66: add '…once the touching candle is confirmed as a swing'.
proposals.risk: None under the neutral default; the T tag display is unchanged.

proposals.title: Exact origin candle for HTF/STF pivots via per-HTF-bar extreme maps (no history references)
proposals.rationale: MTF pivots are anchored at the chart bar where their HTF bar opened (tfOpenBar 1165-1176; f_barAtTime at 1783-1789): up to 23 bars early for a daily pivot on 1H, 47 for a 4H pivot on 5m. The user wants zones anchored at the candle that formed them. Scanning history is impossible beyond the 500-bar buffer (indicator max_bars_back = 500, line 31), but recording each HTF bar's extreme as it happens costs O(1) per bar.
proposals.spec: SERIES next to the tfOpenBar block: f_tfExt(int t) holds var curT, rH, rHB, rL, rLB. On a new t it emits [prevT, prevHighBar, prevLowBar] and resets; otherwise it updates with strict > / < (keeps the first print). Call it twice at global scope: f_tfExt(belowH ? time(tfH) : na) and f_tfExt(belowS ? time(tfS) : na). Store results in var map<int,int> hHiB, hLoB, sHiB, sLoB, capped like tfOpenQ (≈2000 keys). Step 10 (1783-1789): aBar = map.contains(pivT) ? map.get(pivT) : f_barAtTime(pivT, anchorMax), then f_pushExt as now (f_x still clamps). Rollback on realtime ticks keeps it consistent. Fallback is today's path.
proposals.risk: Low. Where the HTF bar's session differs from the chart's, the map still holds the chart's own extreme bar in that period, which is the best visual anchor anyway.

proposals.title: Time-anchored, persistent drawings (merged with PENG-8 and PENG-5/UX-7)
proposals.rationale: The 4,999-bar clamp (f_x 404-405 with max_bars_back(time,5000) at 37) moves left edges on 1-3m charts (one week ≈ 6,900-10,080 bars); xloc.bar_index cannot exceed 10,000 bars back in any case (limitations.md 377). LuxAlgo uses xloc.bar_time. Every DOL object is recreated each tick (2132-2141).
proposals.spec: As PENG-8 (anchors) and PENG-5 (setters). B's additions: anchorT sources are time[bar_index−aBH] (or time[phOld] with SMC-8) for chart pivots; time[1] for FVGs; time[obI]/time[obJ] for OBs; hfT for HTF FVGs; time[bar_index−aBar] from SMC-10 when the offset ≤ 450, else the HTF open time; hiT/loT added to f_rangeTrack/f_sessTrack (807-863). One global int rT = time(timeframe.period, bars_back = −extBars), computed every bar and used on the last bar for every right edge (DOL box, glow, label, iFVG, LVN, ghosts), so edges align. Keep the bar-index path when not chart.is_standard. Implement after SMC-6/SMC-8/SMC-10.
proposals.risk: Touches all drawing code (mixed-xloc bugs, label and tether alignment). Holiday schedule changes can shift the right edge by a bar (cosmetic).

proposals.title: Slow-floored ATR for pool geometry (EQ tolerance, zone depth, stack window, test band)
proposals.rationale: B-test: on 5m CME the median ATR14/ATR200 runs from 0.53-0.71 in the quietest hour to 1.34-1.72 in the busiest (≈3x), so EQ merges, stacks, test bands and zone depth change meaning by the hour (Asia equal lows stop merging; tags flicker). Three open-source EQ detectors use 0.1×ATR(200). The engine already uses atrE = max(ATR14, ATR200) for ejection (878). [CORRECTED vs A: OB volatility filter and height cap dropped; B-test found no geometric problem]
proposals.spec: Input geomIn ['Slow-floored' (default), 'Fast (14)'] in G_LIQ; atrG = geomIn=='Fast (14)' ? atr : atrE (after 878). Use atrG at 1520 (wPx), 1522 (eqPx) and 1926-1927 (stack window); pass atrG as a fourth argument to track for the test band only (maxAway stays on atr). Measure by toggling: CHART LIQ / EXT LIQ family EDGE in the Full view.
proposals.risk: Wider tolerances in quiet sessions, so a few more EQ merges and stack memberships; measurable via the toggle.

proposals.title: LVNs as profile troughs instead of an absolute 30%-of-peak cut (adopted by AMT-5)
proposals.rationale: The engine marks any contiguous run below 0.30×peak as an LVN (2260-2269), which in skewed profiles is a shoulder, not the thin node between two acceptance areas. LuxAlgo Node Detection defines a trough as lower than the N rows on each side, plus a minimum-volume threshold (B verified via snippets). amt_profile AMT-5 adopts this detection and adds the barrier/invalidation use; implement it once, there.
proposals.spec: Inputs G_LVN: lvnNbr 8 (% rows), lvnProm 0.15 (× peak). N = max(1, round(rows·lvnNbr/100)). For r in [N, rows−1−N]: v = vpSm[r]; lMax/rMax = max of the N rows on each side; a trough requires v < every neighbour (strict local minimum) and min(lMax, rMax) − v ≥ lvnProm·peak. Grow the zone while rows ≤ v + 0.35·(min(lMax, rMax) − v). Keep tail exclusion and lvnN per side. Compute once per profile rebuild (step 15) so AMT-5's barrier feature can reuse it.
proposals.risk: None to selection unless AMT-5's barrier feature is enabled; display only.

result.summary: The engine is already ahead of the DOL selectors surveyed on substance. Its lead is narrower than A claimed: two open-source placebo-statistics scripts grade order blocks and FVGs against matched random zones (both find no edge), and two tools (MQLSoftware, LunqFX) do commit to one draw with a hit rate or probability, though without a null. B replicated the published competitor selection rules on 14 datasets: nearest pool, ICT-style nearest-on-bias-side, LuxAlgo tier/distance, an engine-like multi-pillar score and expected reach. Every rule's realised hit rate equals its distance-matched baseline (pooled excess −1.0 to +0.1 pp; paired |z| ≥ 2 in about 4 of 78 pairs, the chance rate). The rules differ only in what they deliver. The engine-like score delivers 0.94 ATR per target, against 0.80 to 0.87 for the free rules (ahead on 11 to 12 of 14 sets), but loses to an expected-reach picker at 1.20 (13 of 14 sets). So a shadow benchmark must report ATR delivered, not edge alone, and abstaining in balanced states gives no precision gain. The visible losses are UX and honesty of the readout. 76 of 104 inputs print in the legend and 76 lack tooltips. The Clean label shows 'PoT: 95.0%' on a target already reached, with no horizon, no sample size, and no reason when the chart is blank. B also found that the intrabar sweep alert fires for targets that were never shown or announced whenever Minimum PoT > 0, that alert() text has no timeframe, and that the 'DOL Price' plot reports filtered targets. The communication evidence supports showing PoT with its reference class (Gigerenzer 2005) and with uncertainty (Joslyn & LeClerc 2012), and supports not adding an ACTION row. It also supports showing the expectation next to each on-chart result, because algorithm aversion (Dietvorst 2015) makes bare misses erode trust. The evidence that clutter itself harms decisions is weak (the choice-overload meta-analysis finds an effect near 0). Platform guard rails matter for alert design: TradingView stops an alert after more than 15 triggers in 3 minutes, sends application/json only for valid JSON, and the Pine Screener allows 5 request calls while the engine uses 6. The final proposals, best first: settings hygiene; an alert system v2 with the correctness fixes first; an honest, explanatory Clean label; competitor rules as roles in the shared shadow ledger judged on ATR delivered; a price-scale tag with distance units and an LVN distance cap; outcome stamps that show the PoT at assertion; light-theme contrast via UX-2; a same-side TP ladder; a screener and output contract; honest wording; and a downgraded balanced/coverage split.

concepts.name: Nearest-opposing-pool selection
concepts.definition: Target = argmin distance over untapped pools on the bias side (ICT doctrine; ICT Order Block Pro draws a DOL line from a validated OB to the closest opposing BSL/SSL), or on either side for the plain variant.
concepts.dolRole: Simplest 'which liquidity next' rule. Maximises raw hit rate because targets are close, so it is the natural benchmark for any scorer.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B replication on 14 sets (H 30): nearest any side hit 0.720 vs baseline 0.719 (+0.1 pp, SE 1.6), 0.80 ATR delivered per target; nearest on bias side 0.661 vs 0.671, 0.86 ATR. No information edge; lowest utility. Vendor pages publish no accuracy.
concepts.engineNotes: Not used as a rule or a benchmark. Proximity is one pillar (evaluate 661-697). Added as a role in COMP-3 (shared with SKEP-5 NEAREST/TREND).

concepts.name: Tier-over-distance selection (LuxAlgo-style)
concepts.definition: score = tierWeight / distATR with tiers weekly 4, daily 3, session and equal extremes 2, gaps 1.5, swings 1. The best score on the structure-bias side (structure length 50) is the working draw, with fallback to the other side; re-anchors on a sweep.
concepts.dolRole: Ranks pools by significance per unit of distance. The free alternative users compare against.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Tiers and structure length verified via search; other defaults are A-only. B replication: hit 0.647 vs baseline 0.655 (−0.8 pp), 0.87 ATR delivered; the engine-like score delivers +0.07 ATR more (z ≥ 2 on 11 of 14 sets).
concepts.engineNotes: Tier enters density (f_tierW 506, used at 682) but the rule is never benchmarked. New TIER/DIST role in COMP-3.

concepts.name: Magnet score / most-likely draw with hit rate
concepts.definition: Pools scored 0-100 (Magnet Score) with the strongest shown as NEXT TARGET, a probability and a BUY-/SELL-SIDE PULL bias (LunqFX). Or: the most likely draw is projected with a self-calibrating historical hit rate, marked provisional while the sample is thin (MQLSoftware).
concepts.dolRole: Shows that single-target tools with a self-reported rate exist. It corrects A's claim that measurement-first tools never commit to a target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor descriptions via search; formulas not public; no null comparison.
concepts.engineNotes: The engine commits to one target and grades it against a null, but only in the Terminal panel. Clean shows no rate (COMP-4).

concepts.name: Per-side draw states including Two-Sided / No Draw
concepts.definition: Each side gets a 0-100 score. States: Buy-Side Draw, Sell-Side Draw, Two-Sided (score gap below the balance-gap input), No Draw (no qualifying untapped pool in range; Max Draw Distance input). AGPro also says its score 'is not a probability of profit'.
concepts.dolRole: Explains blanks and balanced conditions. The precision gain from abstaining requires a selector that carries information.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Selective classification (Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017: 2% top-5 error at about 60% coverage) is moderate in ML. B replication: engine-like pick excess −0.1 pp on balanced bars vs −1.1 pp on clear bars, overlapping SEs, so no precision gain here.
concepts.engineNotes: dirSide 0 at 1895; Terminal shows BALANCED (2342) and 'scanning…' (2367); Clean shows nothing for three different reasons. Display moved to the COMP-4 hint; ledger split in COMP-6 (P3).

concepts.name: Target commitment (confirm at close / lock / hysteresis / display modes)
concepts.definition: Targets change only on confirmed bars (ASXLT, AGPro, reference product). 'Liquidity Draw' locks until hit, stop or N bars. The engine requires a challenger to lead by hyst (twice that across sides) for 2 bars. Display filters such as LuxAlgo SMC Historical/Present and TFO 'Until Mitigated' reduce clutter without changing the calculation.
concepts.dolRole: Stability; jumping targets are the main trust killer.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions; no measured benefit published.
concepts.engineNotes: Lines 2011-2020; off-killzone multiplier kzHx (976). Lock belongs to SMC-2.

concepts.name: Theoretical first-passage PoT with explicit horizon (reference class)
concepts.definition: P(max over horizon ≥ level) for a random walk; driftless reflection gives PoT ≈ 2·P(end beyond). Competitors state the horizon ('within the horizon', expiry, 24 min / 1 h / 4 h). A probability must name its reference class: 'touch within the next 30 bars (≈ 2 h 30 m)'.
concepts.dolRole: Chance of reaching the target within a stated time. The horizon is part of the forecast.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Model exact under its assumptions. Gigerenzer et al. 2005 (Risk Analysis 25:623): a '30% chance of rain' is read as time, area or days, and only New York's majority gave the standard meaning. Transfer to trading assumed.
concepts.engineNotes: f_pot (434) and f_potModel (1303), capped at 0.95. H = 30 bars is never shown in Clean (2225) or the tooltip (2206). COMP-4 adds the clock text; TIME-4 refines it.

concepts.name: Measured reach frequency per category with n
concepts.definition: Per pool category × birth distance: reached within a window, median bars, rejected/cut/stall split; printed only above a minimum sample ('building' otherwise). The dashboard lists the nearest pool above and below with ATR distance, reach %, median bars and n.
concepts.dolRole: Empirical base rates of which pool types get taken and how fast.
concepts.evidenceNotes: ForexCracked dashboard fields and 'makes no performance claims' verified via search; thresholds (50 bars, n ≥ 20, 1 ATR / 0.5 ATR) are A-only. Boost counts conflict in A's notes and were dropped.
concepts.engineNotes: Empirical surface is by distance and HTF regime (f_empPoT 1284), not by category. Per-family rates in Full view only. Category lift is ICT-1 / CAL-3.

concepts.name: Placebo / control-zone statistics
concepts.definition: For each real OB or FVG, control zones of the same height, direction and distance from price are placed at bars without the event. Edge = real hit − control hit; z ≈ 2 is a first sign; replication required.
concepts.dolRole: The right null for 'is this array a better target than any level this far?'. It matches the engine's distance-matched baseline.
concepts.evidenceNotes: FVG Statistics with Placebo Control: no detectable advantage in 14 measurements (3 assets × 3 TFs × 2 periods). OB Statistics vs Random Levels: no reliable gap. Author-run, reproducible method; consistent with the sibling ict_pd / calib_ml replications.
concepts.engineNotes: f_potBase (1314) and the edge test (2376-2430). Not unique overall, but unique among DOL selectors. Wording aligned in COMP-11.

concepts.name: Self-measurement ledger against a null
concepts.definition: Grade every asserted target over H bars against the base rate of a random level at the same distance; Wilson interval, cluster-robust z, verdict, bars-to-hit, heat, race.
concepts.dolRole: The honest way to know whether the selected liquidity is taken more often than chance.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Standard forecast-evaluation methodology.
concepts.engineNotes: f_openTrial / f_step / f_book (1426-1500), panel 2376-2430; Terminal only.

concepts.name: Benchmark against simple competitor rules (ATR delivered)
concepts.definition: Run nearest, nearest-bias and tier/distance selectors on the same pool and bars as shadow roles. Report hit %, excess over the distance-matched baseline with block SE, and ATR delivered = mean(hit × distance) per target, with paired differences vs the engine.
concepts.dolRole: Shows whether the multi-pillar score is better than the free rules. Per B, it is no better on hit vs chance, but it targets farther and delivers more distance per target.
concepts.evidenceNotes: B replication, 14 sets: all rules' excess within ±1 pp pooled. ATR delivered: engine-like 0.94, tier/dist 0.87, nearest-bias 0.86, nearest 0.80; engine ahead with z ≥ 2 on 11-12 of 14 sets; max d·PoT 1.20 beats all (13 of 14). M4 principle (complex often fails simple benchmarks) strong.
concepts.engineNotes: Not present. COMP-3 (P2) as roles in the shared SKEP-5 / CAL-3 mechanism.

concepts.name: Natural-frequency display (k of n next to %)
concepts.definition: Show counts beside probabilities ('41 of 63 reached') with a minimum-sample gate; otherwise show 'calibrating' or 'provisional'.
concepts.dolRole: Lets traders judge how much to trust a PoT value.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Strong for Bayesian tasks: McDowell & Jacobs 2017 meta-analysis 4% → 24% correct; Hoffrage et al. 2015 Study 1 +37 pp average. A's '7% vs 45%' was not verified. Transfer to forecast displays is assumed, hence moderate.
concepts.engineNotes: Clean label (2225) and tooltip (2206) show no n; n only in the Terminal header (2379). COMP-4 adds PoT reliability buckets.

concepts.name: Uncertainty communication vs categorical advice
concepts.definition: Forecasts that include probability or uncertainty information, rather than a deterministic value or a 'do X' recommendation.
concepts.dolRole: Supports showing PoT (with horizon) and rejecting an ACTION/STATUS row.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Joslyn & LeClerc 2012 (JEP: Applied 18:126-140): uncertainty forecasts improved decisions and trust and softened the trust loss after errors; categorical advice alone did no better than deterministic forecasts.
concepts.engineNotes: PoT is displayed; no ACTION row by design.

concepts.name: Probability display precision
concepts.definition: Digits and rounding used for displayed probabilities (weather: 10% or 5% steps).
concepts.dolRole: Over-precise displays signal more confidence than the model has.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Jerez-Fernandez, Angulo & Oppenheimer 2014 (Psych Sci 25:633-635), two small studies: precision read as confidence.
concepts.engineNotes: Fixed '0.0' at 2225 (matches the reference). COMP-4 adds a precision option, default unchanged.

concepts.name: Reached-target and blank-chart states
concepts.definition: Once the target trades, the readout says it was reached instead of a probability. When nothing is drawn, the reason is stated (none qualifies / filtered by Min PoT / balanced).
concepts.dolRole: Prevents reading a completed draw as a live forecast, and makes 'no edge right now' an explicit answer.
concepts.evidenceNotes: UX convention (AGPro No Draw, Terminal SWEPT).
concepts.engineNotes: activePoT := 0.95 on a live sweep (2067), so Clean prints 'PoT: 95.0%' and the DOL PoT % plot (2446) reads 95. Clean is blank for three different reasons. COMP-4.

concepts.name: Level lifecycle (rest / swept / broken / mitigated) and ghosting
concepts.definition: Swept = wick through and close back within a confirmation window; broken = close beyond or window expiry; a swept level later closed beyond becomes broken; TFO 'Until Mitigated' ends the line when traded through; ghosts stay at low opacity.
concepts.dolRole: Swept vs broken bears on reversal vs continuation and on which pool is next.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions; outcome statistics belong to ict_liq.
concepts.engineNotes: Strict trade-through (touched 623); raid folded into D (1580-1582); ghosts at 1586 / 2023, off by default (showGhost 210). Logic in ICT-2; stamps in COMP-5.

concepts.name: Outcome stamps with expectation
concepts.definition: On-chart marker of each target's fate (reached in N bars, abandoned with reason) showing the PoT at assertion next to the result; FIFO-capped.
concepts.dolRole: Makes timing and hit rate visible per target and supports replay testing. Showing the expectation counters algorithm aversion.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions. Dietvorst et al. 2015 (strong): seeing an algorithm err reduces its use even when it outperforms; a 2018 study found slight user control reduces this.
concepts.engineNotes: Trials hold bars, mae and status (375-396, 1434-1459); nothing is drawn. COMP-5.

concepts.name: Approach alert
concepts.definition: Fires once per target when the bar's extreme comes within X of the target (ForexCracked 0.25 ATR with reach ≥ 70% and enough n; ProEA 0.15 × daily ATR).
concepts.dolRole: Timing: prepare exits or entries as the draw completes; approach-to-hit conversion is measurable.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions (thresholds A-only).
concepts.engineNotes: Not in 2077-2094. COMP-2 adds nearEvt with nearAnnId, plus the NEAR→HIT ledger.

concepts.name: Alert correctness and event coverage
concepts.definition: Alerts only for targets the user was told about. Events for reached at close with result, approaching, and abandoned (replaced / ejected / invalidated). Ticker and timeframe in every message.
concepts.dolRole: Tells the trader the forecast completed or changed, and with what result.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions; the engine gaps are code-verified.
concepts.engineNotes: liveSweep (1504) is not gated by dolShown/lastAnnId, so the sweep alert (2084-2085, 2092) fires for never-shown targets when minPoT > 0. alert() text has no timeframe (2079-2088). Events exist (1584-1590, 2021-2036) but raise no alert. COMP-2 Part A/B.

concepts.name: Alert selection, throttling and fatigue
concepts.definition: Per-event toggles for one 'Any alert() function call' alert, filters (draw-side only), a minimum bar gap; never alert.freq_all.
concepts.dolRole: Keeps only the high-value draw events, and avoids TradingView auto-stopping the alert.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView: more than 15 triggers in 3 minutes stops the alert (support 43000690939, strong). Override meta-analyses: 90% (95% CI 85-95, 16 studies) and 79.8% (44 studies) in medicine; transfer assumed. Plan budgets: Plus 100, Premium 400, Ultimate 1000; Essential 20 (third party).
concepts.engineNotes: All alert() calls fire unconditionally (2079-2088). COMP-2.

concepts.name: Machine-readable alerts (JSON, {{plot()}} placeholders)
concepts.definition: alert() builds JSON with str.tostring (not str.format, whose default numeric pattern has thousands separators). alertcondition messages are const but may embed {{plot("title")}} or {{plot_0..19}}, also for display.none plots. TradingView sends application/json only when the body parses.
concepts.dolRole: Lets bots and webhooks act on target price, PoT and side.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism documented (concepts/alerts.md; support 43000529348); the benefit is a convention.
concepts.engineNotes: Plain text; static alertconditions (2090-2093) although the DOL Price / DOL PoT % plots exist (2444, 2446). The DOL Price plot reports filtered targets (2441). COMP-2, COMP-9.

concepts.name: Status-line (legend) hygiene and settings UX
concepts.definition: input display defaults to display.all for all types except bool and color, so int/float/string/timeframe/session values print next to the name; display.none removes them. Tooltips on every input; active greys out inputs that do not apply.
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting; the main 'cluttered' impression, and correct session and timeframe configuration.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Mechanism strong (reference/input.md:27-28). Benefit: reference look and user complaints. Clutter evidence is mixed: the choice-overload meta-analysis finds a mean effect near 0 (Scheibehenne et al. 2010).
concepts.engineNotes: 104 inputs; 76 print in the legend; 76 lack tooltips (54 among legend types); no display or active (40-226). A's 95/75/67 corrected. COMP-1 (= UX-1 = PENG-1).

concepts.name: Price-scale target tag and distance units
concepts.definition: Right-axis tag with the target price (plot display.price_scale); distance shown in ATR, points, ticks, pips or %.
concepts.dolRole: Fast reading of where the target is and how far, in trader units.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions (AGPro tag, Flux units).
concepts.engineNotes: DOL Price plot is Data Window only (2444); distance in ATR only (2243, 2351). COMP-7.

concepts.name: Autoscale compression safety
concepts.definition: Drawings far from price make autoscale fit them, squashing candles; fix with 'Scale price chart only' or by capping drawing distance. display.none plots never affect scale; display.price_scale-only behaviour is undocumented.
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting; prevents unusable charts.
concepts.evidenceNotes: TradingView help 43000762934; Reddit complaint.
concepts.engineNotes: LVN zones are the nearest N per side within the 120 h profile, with no ATR cap (2275, 2282). COMP-7 caps them at maxATR.

concepts.name: Light-theme contrast (two colour roles)
concepts.definition: Graphics on the chart background need ≥ 3:1 against it and text ≥ 4.5:1. Detect light charts via the luminance of chart.bg_color (input color). Switch only on-background graphics to dark variants; keep neon text on the dark label and tables.
concepts.dolRole: None for forecasting; legibility.
concepts.evidenceNotes: WCAG 2.1 §1.4.3/§1.4.11; B recomputed #39FF14 on white 1.36:1, #00C864 2.22, #FFC400 1.60, #FF1744 3.85; #0B7A2E 5.47 on white but 3.31 on #161616, hence two roles (UX-2).
concepts.engineNotes: Dark-tuned themes (226-284); transparent-background neon labels (2166, 2189, 2212, 1256, 2278) and the white core (2223) fail on white. COMP-8 → UX-2.

concepts.name: Same-side target ladder
concepts.definition: Secondary targets taken as the next pools beyond the DOL on the same side, ordered by distance, each with PoT (and R if invalidation is shown); TP1/TP2 convention in vendor tools.
concepts.dolRole: Answers 'where to take profit'. The ordering is a theorem: path continuity means a nearer same-side level is always touched first.
concepts.evidenceNotes: The ordering is strong (geometry); the benefit is a vendor convention (Liquidity Radar PRO TP1-TP3, R:R labels).
concepts.engineNotes: Secondary targets (2170-2190) are next-best scores on either side, off by default (secN 0). COMP-12.

concepts.name: Dashboard / bias table
concepts.definition: Compact directional bias per timeframe; richer HUDs add target, PoT, distance, route, last sweep, pool counts, ACTION.
concepts.dolRole: Directional context for which side's liquidity is the draw.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor conventions. An ACTION row is not supported by Joslyn & LeClerc 2012 (categorical advice alone did not help).
concepts.engineNotes: Clean Timeframe | Bias (2294-2310), Terminal panel (2313-2434); cell tooltips unused (COMP-4 adds them).

concepts.name: Pine Screener multi-symbol scanning
concepts.definition: Plots with display.pine_screener become screener columns. The screener calculates the last 500 bars, ignores input.timeframe/symbol/time (uses defaults), supports listed timeframes only, needs Premium or above, and one help page caps request.* calls at 5.
concepts.dolRole: Find the symbols whose draw currently has high PoT aligned with HTF bias.
concepts.evidenceNotes: No DOL competitor offers it; the request limit conflicts between help pages (5 vs the general 40).
concepts.engineNotes: Engine uses 6 request calls (5 request.security at 923-925, 939, 981 + 1 lower-TF at 982; A said 6 + 1). Merging 923 and 939 (same tfH) gives 5. COMP-9.

concepts.name: Liquidation and order-book heatmaps
concepts.definition: Estimated liquidation clusters by leverage (Coinglass, Hyblock), or displayed limit orders (Bookmap, ATAS). Orders can be pulled, stops never appear in the book, and icebergs and spoofing bias the display.
concepts.dolRole: Magnitude of resting orders, but not the sequence in which they are visited.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Vendor documentation and admissions (Coinglass FAQ A-only; Bookmap blog verified via search).
concepts.engineNotes: Data not visible to Pine; not proposed.

concepts.name: Repaint transparency, honest wording and publishing rules
concepts.definition: State which outputs are live and how MTF data is aligned; never call a score a probability; describe the edge as vs a matched random level. TradingView forbids implying that a reverse-engineering attempt reproduces a closed script's behaviour, and bans intentional misleading.
concepts.dolRole: Trust; avoids moderation risk.
concepts.evidenceNotes: Publishing rules verified via search (support 43000590599). Wording conventions: AGPro 'not a probability of profit', ForexCracked 'no performance claims', placebo scripts' 'no detectable advantage'.
concepts.engineNotes: Header 1-29 and README disclose the live PoT and sweep alert. COMP-11 refines the verdict wording ('≈ RANDOM') and the README language.

proposals.title: Status line and settings hygiene (shared with UX-1 / PENG-1)
proposals.rationale: 76 of 104 inputs print their values next to the script name, while the reference shows only the name; 76 inputs lack tooltips, including all 10 session inputs; active is unused. It is the most visible 'cluttered' difference and costs nothing.
proposals.spec: (1) Add the literal display = display.none to all 76 input.int/float/string/timeframe/session calls (59-211); the parameter is const plot_display (reference/input.md:27). (2) active (input bool, input.md:28): cHTF/cSTF/cEXE active = modeIn == "Custom"; sessAs/sessLo/sessNA active = useSess; lvnHours/lvnRows/lvnThr/lvnN active = showLVN; ghostMax active = showGhost; hudSize active = uiStyle == "Terminal"; uAbove..uText active = theme == "Custom". All are declared earlier, so there are no forward references. (3) Tooltips, sessions first (window, 'read in Session Timezone', 'Asia crosses midnight'), then pivLen, eqTol, poolMax, maxATR, wS/wM/wL, and potH ('bars; on 5m, 30 bars ≈ 2.5 h'). (4) tblSz = input.string("Small", "Panel Text", options = ["Tiny","Small","Normal"], group = G_TABLE, display = display.none), mapped to a global string read by f_cell/f_cellC (604-610). Implement once together with UX-1 and PENG-1.
proposals.risk: None functionally; legend values disappear for good (intended).

proposals.title: Alert system v2: correctness fixes first, then reached/approaching/abandoned events, toggles, JSON, {{plot()}} placeholders
proposals.rationale: The intrabar sweep alert fires for targets never shown or announced (not gated by dolShown/lastAnnId) whenever Minimum PoT > 0. alert() text lacks the timeframe, and the DOL Price plot reports filtered targets. There are no approach, abandoned or reached-with-result events, no toggles and no JSON. TradingView stops alerts that trigger more than 15 times in 3 minutes, sends application/json only for valid JSON, and plans give 20-1000 alert slots. Alert-fatigue meta-analyses show 80-90% overrides.
proposals.spec: Part A (ship first): bool sweepAlert = liveSweep and not na(activeLv) and activeLv.id == lastAnnId, used in alert (2084) and alertcondition (2092); append ' · ' + syminfo.ticker + ' ' + timeframe.period to every alert() text (2079-2088); dolPriceOut := dolShown ? activeLv.price : na (2441); DOL PoT % plot = na while sweptNow. Part B: G_ALT group inputs alNew/alHit/alNear/alIfvg/alLive true, alAbd/alFlip false, alNearATR 0.25, alDrawOnly false, alFmt Text|JSON, alGap 0 (numeric/string with display.none). STATE (after 1039): var int nearAnnId = -1, var int lastAlertBar, var float nearN/nearK. Per-bar flags next to newDolEvent (1511): hitEvt, abdEvt, abdWhy, evName, evPx, evSide, evBars, evMae. Step 2 (1551-1555): when a booked trial has lvId == activeId and status 1, set evMae := t.mae. Step 3 (1584): if lv.id == activeId and lv.id == lastAnnId, set hitEvt := hit, abdEvt := not hit ('ejected'), fill ev* and evBars := bar_index - activeSince; if lv.id == nearAnnId, nearK += 1. Step 19 before activeId := pickId (2034): if pickId != activeId and curI >= 0 and activeId == lastAnnId, set abdEvt := true with reason curElig ? 'replaced' : 'invalidated'. Approaching at global scope after annNow: gapX = side == 1 ? bottom - high : low - top; nearEvt = barstate.isconfirmed and activeLv.id == lastAnnId and activeLv.id != nearAnnId and 0 < gapX <= alNearATR*atr; then nearAnnId := id and nearN += 1. Filters: not alDrawOnly or not activeCtr; bar_index - lastAlertBar >= alGap. All via alert.freq_once_per_bar_close, intrabar sweep freq_once_per_bar, never freq_all. Part C: f_msg(ev, nm, side, px, pot, extra) after LEVEL METHODS: text, or JSON {event, symbol, tf, side, type, price, pot, horizon_bars, bars, mae_atr, reason, counter, time} built with str.tostring (never str.format, which groups thousands); validate once. Part D: keep the 4 alertcondition titles with messages like 'DOL Engine: new target on {{ticker}} ({{interval}}) at {{plot("DOL Price")}}, PoT {{plot("DOL PoT %")}}%'; add DOL Target Approaching / Reached (close) / Abandoned. Part E: Full-view row NEAR→HIT k/n and abandonment counts by reason.
proposals.risk: Noise, hence abandoned and flip alerts default to off; JSON validity; replacement events cluster before hits until the overhaul's near-distance taper fix lands.

proposals.title: Honest, explanatory Clean label: reached state, horizon as reference class, k of n, expected reach, runner-up, why-blank hint
proposals.rationale: Clean shows 'PoT: 95.0%' on a reached target (2067). The PoT has no horizon, and a single-event probability without a reference class is misread (Gigerenzer 2005). There is no sample size and no expected reach. The chart goes blank for three different reasons without saying which. Uncertainty information improves decisions and trust (Joslyn & LeClerc 2012). Users ask when, how sure, and where to take profit.
proposals.spec: (1) Clean branch (2225): potTxt = sweptNow ? '✓ Reached' : 'PoT: ' + str.tostring(activePoT*100, potFmt) + '%'; line 1 stays 'Target: X' (UX-3 grammar). (2) potFmt input '0.1%' (default) | '1%' | '5%' (math.round(p*20)/20). (3) Hint: if showDOL and barstate.islast and (na(activeLv) or not dolShown), draw one dim 'No target' label at (bar_index+extBars, close) with a tooltip reason: nothing ≥ Min Score within Max ATR / 'PDH filtered: PoT 12% < 20%' / 'Balanced: BSL 61 / SSL 58' when dirSide == 0 and the side bests are within 5 points; hintOn input default true. (4) Tooltip (≤ 7 lines, built at barstate.islast): tag, score and draw side; price with pts / % / ATR distance; 'PoT 70% = chance of a touch within the next 30 bars (≈ 2 h 30 m)' via f_dur(H*timeframe.in_seconds()); k of n from calibration buckets (float pShow on Trial set in f_openTrial 1426 = f_potModel(...), declared at 1303; var calN/calK size 5; f_book bucket min(4, int(pShow*5)); print when n ≥ 10, else 'calibrating'); 'Expected reach if aimed here: PoT × dAtr'; runner-up name and margin plus held bars (second-best in step 19, 1965-1990; store runS/runName); pillars. (5) f_cellC gains a tip argument → table.cell(..., tooltip = tip) (table.md:53, 69): swing vs internal bias and dealing-range %. If SMC-1 / TIME-2 land, read their calibration arrays.
proposals.risk: Tooltip length; buckets must use the PoT at assertion, not the live tick; the hint label must never appear when a target is shown.

proposals.title: Competitor rules as roles in the shared shadow ledger, reporting ATR delivered next to excess hit
proposals.rationale: Users ask whether the engine beats the free rules. B's replication on 14 datasets shows every rule's hit equals its distance-matched baseline, so an edge-vs-edge verdict reads 'tie' (paired |z| ≥ 2 in about 4 of 78 pairs). ATR delivered does separate them: engine-like 0.94 vs tier/dist 0.87, nearest-bias 0.86, nearest 0.80 (z ≥ 2 on 11-12 of 14 sets), and max d·PoT 1.20 beats all. Downgraded from P1 and merged with SKEP-5 / CAL-3.
proposals.spec: Use the single role/probe mechanism of SKEP-5 (Trial.role) or CAL-3 (Probe.role). Roles: NEAREST (either side) and NEAREST-BIAS (htfBias side), both already in SKEP-5; add TIER/DIST over candidates with minDistATR ≤ dAtr ≤ maxATR: key = tw/max(dAtr, 0.25); tw = 4 for src 7, 3 for src 6, 2 for src 3-5 or eqCount > 0 (max), 1.5 for kinds 2-3, 1 otherwise; side = htfBias if ≠ 0 else dirSide, falling back to the other side. Open on the same bar as an engine trial (step 20, 2037-2045), with lvId offset (-1000000 - role) so the has-check ignores shadows; same f_step; f_book routes by role and never touches the per-family, calibration or main stats. Metrics per role: n, hit %, excess Σ(y-pBase)/n with block SE, ATR delivered Σ(y·d0)/n, paired Δ vs the DOL on shared blocks. Full-view rows after RACE (2422), e.g. 'vs NEAREST hit 72/60% · Δexc +0.4±3.1pp · ATR del 0.80/0.94'. Wording: 'same accuracy vs chance' when |Δexc| < 2 SE; 'delivers more/less per target' when |Δdel| ≥ 2 SE; never compare raw hit. Data Window plots for the Δ ATR delivered values.
proposals.risk: About 150-400 trials per chart gives low power, so show ± bands, not glyph verdicts; extra loop pass and up to 2× trials (test at 20k depth); users confusing hit with value (tooltip explains).

proposals.title: Price-scale target tag, distance units, autoscale safety
proposals.rationale: Competitors show the target price on the axis and offer distance units. Far drawings squash autoscale (TradingView help 43000762934; Reddit complaint). The engine's LVN zones have no ATR cap.
proposals.spec: (1) plot(dolShown ? activeLv.price : na, 'DOL Price', color = side colour, display = tagOn ? display.data_window + display.price_scale : display.data_window); display is input plot_display (plot.md:243); tagOn input bool true. It adds no new autoscale range because the DOL box already spans the target. (2) distUnit ATR | Points | Ticks | Pips (mintick*10 when syminfo.type == 'forex') | %, used at 2243, 2351 and in the COMP-4 tooltip. (3) LVN loops (2275, 2282): add and math.abs((zTop+zBot)/2 - close) <= maxATR*atr; skip the objective and reach bands beyond maxATR*ejectMult; extBars tooltip: 'Squashed candles? Right-click the price scale → Scale price chart only'.
proposals.risk: Axis crowding with many indicators (toggle); display.price_scale autoscale behaviour is undocumented, so test it.

proposals.title: Outcome stamps that show the expectation next to the result
proposals.rationale: The ledger knows every target's fate, but Clean users only see targets vanish. Competitors show results (result display, sweep tracker, purge circles). Bare misses trigger algorithm aversion (Dietvorst 2015); stamping the PoT at assertion makes misses read as expected outcomes.
proposals.spec: stampMode Off | Terminal only (default) | Always; stampMax 8. Reached (COMP-2 hook in step 3): label.new(bar_index, side == 1 ? top : bottom, '✓ ' + evBars + 'b · ' + pAssert% , style label_down/up, transparent bg, side-colour text, size.tiny); pAssert = pShow of the booked trial (COMP-4), captured in step 2. Abandoned: '⊘ replaced · 55%' or '⊘ ejected' in the ghost colour at the old level. Expired while live: none (UX-3 'late' state). var array<label> stampL as a FIFO; create only when inCalc; budget 8 + 12 ghosts + about 8 HUD/hint labels, far below 500.
proposals.risk: Clutter, hence off in Clean (reference look).

proposals.title: Light-theme contrast via UX-2's two colour roles
proposals.rationale: Classic lime is 1.36:1 on white (recomputed). A's single light variant would break the dark Clean label (#0B7A2E 3.31:1 on #161616), so adopt UX-2's two roles.
proposals.spec: lightBg = (0.2126*color.r(chart.bg_color) + 0.7152*color.g(...) + 0.0722*color.b(...))/255 > 0.5 (chart.bg_color is input color). Graphics on the chart background (zone border and fill, glow, core, tether, transparent-label text, LVN, ghosts) switch to buy #0B7A2E, sell #C8102E, LVN #9A6B00, ghost #5F6B7A on light charts; core line = lightBg ? c : color.new(color.white, 15). Text on the dark label and tables keeps the neon colours. Classic stays the default.
proposals.risk: Gradient backgrounds return the midpoint colour (coarse detection).

proposals.title: Same-side target ladder (TP1/TP2) for secondary targets
proposals.rationale: Users ask where to take profit, and vendors sell TP ladders. The engine's secondary targets are next-best scores on either side, not an ordered path. On the same side a nearer level is always touched first, so a distance-ordered ladder is a geometric fact, with a PoT per rung.
proposals.spec: secMode = input.string('By score', 'Secondary Targets Mode', options = ['By score', 'Ladder (same side)'], group = G_DOL, display = display.none). In Ladder mode inside the secondary loop (2170-2190): candidates with side == activeLv.side, distance > activeLv.distance(close) and dAtr ≤ maxATR, sorted by distance; take secN; label 'TP2 · PDH · 41%' (PoT from the existing f_potModel call at 2184) plus ' · 2.1R' when showInv and the invalidation exist.
proposals.risk: None for the default; could read as advice, so the wording stays 'TP2' level naming only.

proposals.title: Output contract plus Pine Screener columns
proposals.rationale: No DOL competitor offers multi-symbol scanning. Stable plot series also serve webhooks ({{plot_n}}, first 20 plots). The screener allows 5 request calls per one help page; the engine uses 6 (A miscounted 6 + 1).
proposals.spec: Plots (display.data_window + display.pine_screener, constants.md:125), the first 20 kept stable: DOL Price (na when not shown), DOL Side, DOL State (0 none, 1 draw, 2 counter, 3 reached, 4 filtered), DOL PoT % (na when reached), DOL Dist ATR, DOL Score, Draw D, HTF Bias, Bars Since Target. Merge the two tfH requests (923 f_structure, 939 f_htfFvg) into one tuple via a wrapper f_htfAll() returning 17 values (PENG-2), giving 5 requests. Document: last 500 bars only, so the empirical PoT falls back to the analytic model and the ledger is empty; input.timeframe ignored (Custom TFs use defaults); Premium and above.
proposals.risk: May still hit time limits or not run; test live first.

proposals.title: Wording honesty: placebo language, score vs probability, publishing rules
proposals.rationale: The placebo-statistics scripts set the honest vocabulary ('no detectable advantage'). B's replication shows PoT is mostly geometry, so users will often see '✕ NO EDGE' and conclude the tool is broken. TradingView forbids implying that a reverse-engineering attempt reproduces a closed script.
proposals.spec: README/description: EDGE = hit rate minus that of a matched random level at the same distance (placebo); state that PoT is mostly distance and volatility, and that the engine's value is which level and how far it delivers (ATR delivered). Terminal verdict: '✕ NO EDGE' becomes '≈ RANDOM' for z < 1 (2397-2398), keeping '~ WEAK' and '✓ EDGE'. Never call a score a probability; keep the 95% cap; never name the closed product or claim parity of results.
proposals.risk: None.

proposals.title: Balanced / no-draw ledger split and coverage (downgraded)
proposals.rationale: Abstention raises precision only when the selector carries information. B's replication found no gain (excess −0.1 pp balanced vs −1.1 pp clear, overlapping SEs). The display part moved into the COMP-4 hint; the measurement stays useful per chart.
proposals.spec: Ledger covN/covK (bars in the window and bars with an asserted DOL) giving coverage %; bool bal on Trial (set when dirSide == 0 and the buy and sell best scores are within balGap = 5), reported as CLEAR vs BALANCED excess and ATR delivered in Full view. Optional balMode 'Show both' draws the other side's best as a thin secondary via the 2170-2190 code; the default stays 'Show best' (decision history).
proposals.risk: balGap is arbitrary; adds ledger complexity.
